# Appendix: the September 2026 audit, all findings as produced

The complete record behind `2026-09-06-audit-report.md`: every finding
that survived deduplication and both skeptics, with the skeptics' own
evidence, then the five findings the skeptics killed, the gaps the
completeness critic considered and rejected, and the twelve lenses'
strategic paragraphs. Text is the agents' own, edited only to remove
scratch-directory paths, personal details and the three retired phrases
the claim guard forbids.

Produced 6 September 2026 against `main` at 8ad1c06.

---

## Verification key

Every finding below was read by two independent skeptics. The REPRODUCE
skeptic opened the cited files and re-ran the numbers, told to default to
refuted. The MATERIALITY skeptic assumed the mechanism and asked whether
it matters against the project's own standards, told to refute anything
already documented as an accepted limit. A finding died if either
refuted it. The severity shown is the lower of the two skeptics' ratings.

Ids: `F-nnn` are the first round's canonical findings (109, from 144 raw
across twelve lenses); `G-...` are the gap round's (six finders chosen by
the completeness critic).

---

## Confirmed findings (154)

### Severity critical (1)

#### G-Stepped--1. A mis-calibrated step silently re-measures frames under fabricated timestamps and inflates the reported rate, opening the 25 fps gate on clips that should be refused

|                             |                                                                                                                             |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **critical**                                                                                                                |
| Category                    | defect                                                                                                                      |
| Effort                      | M                                                                                                                           |
| Raised by                   | Stepped-clip CFR assumption and the corpus exclusion mechanism                                                              |
| Files                       | `src/io/videoStepper.ts:335-337`, `src/io/videoStepper.ts:344-354`, `src/io/videoStepper.ts:38-41`, `src/main.ts:1417-1420` |

**Claim.** One short inter-frame gap anywhere in the first six probed frames sets a step smaller than the clip's true frame period. Every subsequent schedule slot that falls inside a frame already showing is measured AGAIN — same pixels, same landmarks, a new invented timestamp — and counted as a new frame. The run reports stoppedEarly:false and a frame rate equal to 1/step.

**Impact.** This is a fabricated measurement presented as a real one, which is the null-never-zero rule violated in its own house. Worse, it defeats the project's flagship refusal: a 20 fps clip — a rate at which src/core/constants.ts:123 says a blink cannot be measured — is presented to the whole pipeline at 40 fps, so fpsGate passes, and blink rate, PERCLOS, long closures and the score are all published for a recording the instrument has declared unmeasurable. The inputs the next era targets (phones, tablets, external webcams) are precisely the variable-rate ones.

**Fix as proposed.** Make an inexact landing a first-class fact instead of a silent fallback. (1) Count inexact landings in `StepSummary` and return them. (2) Refuse the run, by name, when they exceed a pre-registered fraction (0.02 mirrors STEPPING_DUPLICATE_TOLERANCE at src/core/frameClock.ts:249) — the message already exists in spirit at src/main.ts:1355-1357. (3) In `measureFrameInterval`, compare the minimum gap against the median gap and refuse or witness when they disagree by more than one quantum; probe more than CALIBRATION_FRAMES=6 (:44) before committing a schedule to a ten-minute clip.

**Evidence as filed.** The code states its own premise at src/io/videoStepper.ts:38-41: "A seek that lands on the frame already showing produces no new frame callback." So when the schedule re-lands on the current frame, the landing is INEXACT, the duplicate guard is skipped by construction (`landing.exact &&`, :349), and :335-337 fabricates a time from the schedule (`origin + index * step`). I ran the real `stepThroughVideo` against a fake decoder with an explicit frame-time list (harness: <scratch> copied from test/io/videoStepper.test.ts's fakeVideo). Case F, a genuinely 20 fps clip (200 frames, ~10 s) with ONE 25 ms gap near the start: `{"framesMeasured":399,"frameIntervalSeconds":0.025,"stoppedEarly":false}`, 1/interval = 40.00 fps, and "distinct reported media times = 399 of 399". Case B (one 20 ms glitch in an otherwise 30 fps clip): 60 true frames measured as 99 at 50.0 fps. Case A (33/34 ms phone alternation, 900 true frames): 914 measured. Case C (29.97 fps, ms-quantised 33/33/34): 909 measured. Control D (exact 30 fps): 900/900, correct.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity critical.** Reproduced independently. I wrote my own harness (<scratch>) driving the real `stepThroughVideo` against a decoder double copied from the repo's OWN fakeVideo in test/io/videoStepper.test.ts:36-121, whose comment states the premise verbatim: 'A frame callback only fires when a NEW frame is decoded: empty space decodes nothing, and landing on the frame already showing decodes nothing either' (the `landed !== displayed` guard). Results, `npx vitest run --root /home/user/blinklab`: D control exact 30 fps → true=900 measured=900 interval=0.033333 reportedFps=30.00 (correct). F, genuine 20 fps with ONE 25 ms gap at frame 3 → true=200 measured=399 interval=0.025000 reportedFps=40.00 stoppedEarly=false distinctReportedTimes=399/399. B, 30 fps with one 20 ms glitch → true=60 measured=99 at 50.00 fps. A, phone 33/34 ms alternation → true=900 measured=914. C, 29.97 ms-quantised 33/33/34 → true=900 measured=909. Mechanism confirmed at the cited lines: measureFrameInterval takes `Math.min(...gaps)` (src/io/videoStepper.ts:230), the CFR justification is stated at :221-229; the schedule fabricates a time on an inexact landing at :335-337 (`origin + index * step`); the duplicate guard is gated on `landing.exact &&` at :348-354, skipped by construction for a re-landing, per the file's own premise at :38-41. The gate impact is arithmetic: src/main.ts:1288 stamps `frameTimestampMs('file', 0, mediaTimeSeconds)` = mediaTime*1000, src/main.ts:2943-2945 runs measureFps over a 2 s window of those stamps, and `node -e` on 25 ms-spaced stamps returns exactly 40 — above MIN_BLINK_FPS = 25 (src/core/constants.ts:123), so measurableAtFps (src/main.ts:3559) passes and blink metrics publish for a 20 fps recording.

_Note._ Confirmed as stated, including the reported numbers digit for digit. Two fair qualifications that do not reduce severity: (a) because the fabricated times march at the calibrated step, total span and therefore blink DURATIONS in seconds stay roughly right — what is fabricated is the frame count, the rate, and the gate decision; (b) the status line does say 'Check that rate against your clip' (src/main.ts:1419) and the Eyeblink8 evaluator has a coverage cross-check (evaluate_eyeblink8.py:163-179), so this artefact would be visible on that corpus — but not on UTA-RLDD, which has no such check and is phone-recorded. No test covers it: the only stepped e2e fixture is CFR (test/e2e/videoFile.spec.ts:27, clip-60fps-60frames.mp4), and no doc anywhere acknowledges the failure mode — grep for 'variable frame rate|variable-rate|VFR' across the repo returns only ROADMAP.md:241 (a future row about record-yourself clips) and an unrelated LEARNING.md:611.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity critical.** Reproduced against the real `stepThroughVideo`, twice. I re-ran the auditor's harness (case F, 200 true frames at 20 fps with one 25 ms gap early): {"framesMeasured":399,"frameIntervalSeconds":0.025,"stoppedEarly":false}, 1/interval = 40.00 fps, "distinct reported media times = 399 of 399". I then wrote my own realistic phone case (<scratch> 2 s at 30 fps then 6 s at 20 fps, i.e. a clip that drops rate in dim light — no glitch frame, just a rate change): true 180 frames, true mean 22.50 fps; measured {"framesMeasured":239,"frameIntervalSeconds":0.033333,"stoppedEarly":false}, reported 30.00 fps, 239 of 239 distinct fabricated timestamps. Chain verified in source: the min-gap rule at src/io/videoStepper.ts:222-231 makes the step the clip's FASTEST period; a schedule slot inside a frame already showing produces no frame callback by the file's own premise (:38-41); the landing is then inexact and the time is fabricated from the schedule, `origin + index * step` (:335-337); the last-frame duplicate guard is skipped by construction because it requires `landing.exact` (:344-354, comment at :340-343); the fabricated times are strictly increasing so `acceptFrame` (src/core/frameClock.ts:47-58) accepts every one, and `stampModelClock` never nulls (src/core/modelClock.ts:59-60 refuses only non-increasing stamps). Reachability into published territory: both corpus preparers stream-copy rather than re-encode to CFR (analysis/tools/prepare_eyeblink8.py:77-108 `-c:v copy`; analysis/tools/prepare_rldd.py:250-262 `-c:v copy`), and UTA-RLDD is self-recorded phone video. Eyeblink8 is NOT affected in fact — docs/eyeblink8-result.txt:25-33 shows measured within one frame of annotated on all eight clips.

_Note._ Severity holds at critical. It satisfies two of the rubric's own tests outright: it FABRICATES a measurement (59 of 239 rows in my case G are the same decoded frame re-measured under invented timestamps, exported as stepped-mode data), and it BLOCKS the project's flagship refusal (a clip whose true mean rate is 22.5 fps — below MIN_BLINK_FPS = 25, src/core/constants.ts:119-123 — is handed to the whole pipeline as 30.0 fps, so the gate never fires and blink rate, PERCLOS, long closures and the score are all published for a recording the instrument has declared unmeasurable). It is exactly the failure this module was rewritten twice to prevent, in its own words: "A wrong number that looks right is worse than no number" (src/io/videoStepper.ts:270-278). It is not an accepted limit — the nearest thing is the comment at :322 claiming the fallback is "correct for constant frame rate video and honest for the rest", and 'honest for the rest' is precisely what is false. It reaches the public demo (file-upload mode publishes 'Measured 239 frames at 30.0 frames per second', src/main.ts:1416-1418, plus an export whose header measured_fps is equally inflated, src/core/frameClock.ts:159-178). ONE CAUTION ON THE FIX, or it will break a strength: parts (1) and (2) — count inexact landings in StepSummary and refuse above a pre-registered fraction — are sound and sufficient. Part (3), 'compare the minimum gap against the median gap and refuse when they disagree', would resurrect the estimator the min-gap rule was introduced to kill (src/io/videoStepper.ts:222-231 records WebKit on a Linux runner skipping half its probes, median 2.2x too large, a 60-frame clip measured as 27): on a healthy CFR clip probed with skips, min and median legitimately differ by a whole quantum, so that rule would refuse good clips. Probing more than CALIBRATION_FRAMES=6 before committing a schedule is the safe half of (3).

### Severity high (16)

#### F-001. Peak closing velocity and A/V on the camera path scale with display-refresh over camera-delivery ratio

|                             |                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Severity after verification | **high**                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Category                    | defect                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Effort                      | M                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Raised by                   | core-numeric, performance                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Files                       | `src/core/blinkShape.ts:84-96`, `src/main.ts:3904-3911`, `src/main.ts:3607-3616`, `src/core/deliveryRate.ts:12-17`, `src/core/score.ts:150-165`, `docs/validation-round.txt:47-54`, `docs/blink-sample-rate.txt:599-603` |

**Claim.** peakClosingVelocityMmPerS and amplitudeOverVelocityMs in exports, the shape readout and the score's sluggish-lid ramp are functions of the viewer's display, not the lid, on every live session where processing exceeds delivery; blinkShape.ts:3-4 promises the opposite.

**Impact.** Cross-device shape comparisons and the A/V penalty (150-300 ms) act on a hardware artefact: on a 120 Hz Mac the penalty can essentially never fire. Stepped corpus runs are unaffected.

**Fix as proposed.** Push one sample per distinct delivered frame (tag samples with deliveredCount and collapse, or drive from rVFC); return null shape when delivery is unreported; pre-register on existing exports that dry-run A/V scales inversely with processing/delivery ratio; re-derive the LID_SLUGGISH ramp and MANUAL item 26 afterwards.

**Evidence as filed.** analyzeClosing divides the max adjacent drop by the adjacent timestamp gap; every rAF tick pushes a stabilitySample, and the camera frame is re-read ~4x on a fast machine (120/30 M5 Max, 55/30 iPhone 17). Reproduced with the repo's function: the same 30 fps blink read at 30/60/120 Hz gives 69/138/276 mm/s and A/V 79.7/39.9/19.9 ms. Round-I P2/P5/P6 ran at 40-46 fps processing on 30 fps cameras.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity high.** Wiring: src/main.ts:4590-4599 drives processFrame from requestAnimationFrame with only a monotonic acceptFrame check (src/core/frameClock.ts:47-58); src/main.ts:2983-2993 calls detectForVideo on every tick; src/main.ts:3904-3911 pushes a stabilitySample per tick stamped with the rAF wall clock; src/main.ts:3607-3616 builds the shape window from those samples; src/core/blinkShape.ts:84-96 divides the max adjacent drop by the adjacent tick gap. Reproduced with the repo's analyzeClosing (vitest probe in scratchpad importing src/core/blinkShape.ts): one 30 fps raised-cosine blink read sample-and-hold at 30/60/120 Hz -> peak closing 101.3 / 202.5 / 405.0 mm/s, A/V 41.5 / 20.7 / 10.4 ms, amplitude 4.20 mm at all three. Ratios reported in the repo: docs/blink-sample-rate.txt:599-603 (processing 120, sampled 30), :631-639 (iphone17promax 55 processing / 30 delivered); docs/validation-round.txt:50,53,54 P2/P5/P6 at 45.2/40.0/46.0 processing on declared 30. Consumers: src/core/blinkLog.ts:89-97 exports peakClosingVelocityMmPerS and amplitudeOverVelocityMs; src/main.ts:3829-3831 writes them into FeatureRecords; src/core/score.ts:150-165 prices the sluggish-lid ramp from them. src/core/blinkShape.ts:3-4 and LEARNING.md:296 promise rate independence.

_Note._ Holds as stated. One caveat the finding does not carry: the 2x/4x factor assumes the model returns the same aperture on a re-read of the same frame; docs/blink-sample-rate.txt:449-456 flags VIDEO-mode smoothing as an untested assumption. Smoothing could spread the drop across ticks but cannot remove the inflation, because the divisor is the display tick either way. The finding's absolute numbers (69/138/276) depend on its blink profile; the scaling is what reproduces.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity high.** src/core/blinkShape.ts:84-96 divides the max adjacent drop by the adjacent timestamp gap; src/main.ts:3904-3911 pushes one stabilitySample per processFrame call, and processFrame runs on every rAF tick (src/main.ts:4590-4599, acceptFrame only requires a monotonic wall clock; src/io/frameLoop.ts:66-79 says the camera path 'cannot tell a fresh photograph from the same one read again'). Reproduced with the repo's own analyzeClosing on a 30 fps step read at 30/60/120 Hz: 120/240/480 mm/s (probe run under vitest, then removed; tree clean). The column is exported per blink (src/core/blinkLog.ts:89-97), shown on the page (src/main.ts:3618-3621) and priced by the score (src/core/score.ts:150-165, ramp 150-300 ms taken from MANUAL item 26 at test/MANUAL.md:26, observed on the owner's ~30 fps Air). Sessions with processing above delivery already exist in the record: pcsony 126.7, iphone17promax 55.0 (docs/validation-dry-run.txt:60,213), P2/P5/P6 at 40-46 (docs/validation-round.txt:53-58), M5 Max 120/30 (docs/blink-sample-rate.txt:599-603). No doc mentions velocity in this context: deliveryRate.ts:12-17, LEARNING.md:913 and ROADMAP.md:40/226 discuss re-reads only for the rate.

_Note._ Materiality holds against the contract: blinkShape.ts:3-4 promises the unit was chosen 'so frame rate cannot silently rescale it', and the promise is broken on the era's target devices without any condition on the column. Two corrections to the framing: no COMMITTED corpus number moves (DROZY/RLDD shape columns come from stepped clips, one read per decoded frame), and the inflation is recoverable post hoc because the export header carries sampled_fps/camera_delivered_fps and the per-second fps column (src/core/sessionMetadata.ts:174-182) — so this is a live-export and demo-score defect, not a retraction. Fix is proportionate except one clause: 'return null shape when delivery is unreported' would over-refuse on a browser without rVFC whose processing rate is near the camera's; record the driver and the read ratio as the column's condition instead, and null only when processing exceeds delivery by more than the existing 5 fps band. Row 12.8 (reopening velocity) must not land before this, or it publishes a second display-scaled column.

#### F-005. The guided midpoint line sits above the passive line, so 'blink duration' means two quantities differing 30-50% and one column carries both

|                             |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **high**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Category                    | science                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Effort                      | M                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Raised by                   | oculometric, blink-closure                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Files                       | `src/core/guidedCalibration.ts:111`, `src/core/longClosure.ts:28-33`, `src/core/constants.ts:154-157`, `src/core/constants.ts:188`, `src/core/blink.ts:106-113`, `src/core/blinkLog.ts:89-97`, `src/core/score.ts:41-48`, `docs/blink-line-adoption.txt:86-93`, `docs/validation-dry-run.txt:203-228` |

**Claim.** For the one atypical case the guided line was built for, calibrating makes the droop-reads-closed failure worse and freezes the count during reading; and the duration definition itself shifts with calibration type and device floor, invisibly in the export.

**Impact.** Row 10.9's phone-vs-Mac duration gap is investigated on a quantity whose definition moves with the floor; the score's slow-blink ramp receives guided durations 1.3-1.5x longer than priced; DROZY/RLDD correlations mix definitions; the adoption doc's hypothesis is refuted by the repo's own numbers.

**Fix as proposed.** Derive guided placement from the measured gap (closed + k x (open - closed), k pre-registered from the noise floor); record line mm and origin on every blink-log row and FeatureRecord; name the two quantities; run the owner's recorded droop session through both lines and publish; add the floor-shift arithmetic as a committed 10.9 candidate testable from existing shutBaselineMm/apertureMm columns.

**Evidence as filed.** The shut floor reads ~33% of baseline, not zero, so the passive 0.5x line sits at 25% of the descent above shut while the guided (open+closed)/2 sits at 50%; with p90/median 1.12 the guided line lands at ~0.61 B, above the passive 0.5 B and above the owner's documented 0.45-0.50 B relaxed droop. Probe against the real reducers: a 5 s droop at 0.47 B reads closed under the guided line (blink.count 0, long.count 0). Raised-cosine blink through blinkStep: closed phase 114 ms passive vs 151 ms guided (x1.32; x1.48 for a 60/0/120 profile). Phones' floor at ~38% moves the passive line to 19% of amplitude, shortening durations ~14% with no lid change. The export has no line column; score.ts prices the 250-450 ms ramp from passive durations.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity high.** Lines: src/core/guidedCalibration.ts:111 personalLineMm = (open+closed)/2; src/core/baseline.ts:107-111 and src/core/constants.ts:152 passive = 0.5 x p90; src/core/longClosure.ts:28-33 'fully shut eyes still report about a third of baseline', droop 45-50%; src/core/constants.ts:15-16 fixture floor 2.2 mm on a ~7 mm open (31%); src/core/constants.ts:189 p90/median ~1.12. Reproduced with the repo's blinkStep (B 7.78 from docs/blink-sample-rate.txt:23): passive 3.89 mm, guided 4.76 mm = 0.611 B; closed phase for a 100/0/200 ms raised cosine 112 ms passive vs 150 ms guided (x1.34), same ratio for 60/0/120 and 50/0/100; a 0.38 B floor (docs/validation-dry-run.txt:224-226: 2.79-3.01 mm against a 3.04 mm shut line) shortens the passive closed phase 112 -> 97 ms (-13%) with no lid change. Export: src/core/blinkLog.ts:89-97 has no line column; grep of src/core/sessionMetadata.ts finds no guided-line field; src/core/score.ts:41-48 prices the 250-450 ms ramp from passive 117-133 ms blinks. docs/blink-line-adoption.txt:57-61 assumes 'closed ... near zero' so guided ~ passive, which the repo's own 31-38% floors contradict.

_Note._ The core claim holds: guided sits above passive (guided < passive would need a closed median under ~0.11 B, far below every floor the repo has measured), and one duration column carries two definitions. One overstatement: the finding's own droop probe at 0.47 B does not discriminate the lines. Under BOTH the passive and guided line blinkState reads closed for the entire 5 s droop with blink.count 0 and long.count 0 (probe output); the band where guided is worse than passive is 0.50-0.61 B (at 0.55 B: passive open, guided closed for all 151 frames). The finding's 114/151 ms numbers come from a probe (left in the scratchpad) that sets guided open = passive baseline; with open = resting median the ratio is still 1.34.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity high.** Guided line = (openMedian + closedMedian)/2 (src/core/guidedCalibration.ts:111); passive line = 0.5 x p90 baseline (src/core/baseline.ts:107-111, constants.ts:152). The instrument's own measured floor: fully shut eyes read about a third of baseline (src/core/longClosure.ts:28-32, src/core/perclos.ts:13), and the owner's fixture bottoms near 2.2 mm with an open median near 7 (constants.ts:14-18), i.e. 31%. So on the owner: guided ~ (7+2.2)/2 = 4.6 mm versus passive 3.89 mm (docs/blink-sample-rate.txt:23), ABOVE the passive line and above the 45-50% relaxed droop that already read as closed under the passive line (longClosure.ts:26-32, ROADMAP amendment 5). The adoption doc's premise 'a TYPICAL subject, whose closed eye really does read near zero' (docs/blink-line-adoption.txt:63-67) contradicts those measurements, and the benefit is explicitly a hypothesis (blink-line-adoption.txt:86-96). No export row records that a guided line was used: sessionMetadata.ts:209-212 carries only the passive window's calibration_* rows; storedBlinkCalibration never reaches an export (src/main.ts:1692,3477,3538-3546); BLINK_CSV_COLUMNS (blinkLog.ts:89-97) and FeatureRecord (featureRecord.ts:34-35) have no line column, while the clip-only frame trace does record blinkLineMm per frame (src/main.ts:3578-3588). score.ts:41-48 prices the 250-450 ms duration ramp from passive-line durations. The calibration is stored per device (guidedCalibration.ts:14-16), so the owner's own future live sessions (11.6-11.8, 10.9's phone-vs-Mac comparison) would silently run on the other definition.

_Note._ Material on three counts of the contract: a design premise refuted by the repo's own measured floor, a duration definition that moves with calibration type and device floor, and an export that omits the condition — the one thing the repo says every number must carry. No committed number is built on the guided line yet (it landed 2 September, corpus-neutral by construction), so the damage is prospective, but the era's live and n-of-1 rows would mix two definitions invisibly. The proposed fixes are proportionate and cheap: record line mm and origin per blink row and per FeatureRecord (the frame trace already sets the precedent), name the two quantities, and pre-register k for a gap-relative placement (matching the passive line at the owner's floor means k near 0.3, not 0.5). Protect the strength: the guided path must stay corpus-neutral and its three refusals unchanged.

#### F-007. A stored guided line is invisible to every export, follows the browser not the face, and lifts the refusal for blinks but not PERCLOS/score; round II's frozen plan cannot read it

|                             |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **high**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Category                    | defect                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Effort                      | M                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Raised by                   | blink-closure, wiring, roadmap                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Files                       | `src/main.ts:1692-1693`, `src/main.ts:3538-3542`, `src/main.ts:3569`, `src/main.ts:3653-3654`, `src/main.ts:3683-3697`, `src/main.ts:3825-3827`, `src/main.ts:3848`, `src/main.ts:3877-3878`, `src/core/guidedCalibration.ts:118-122`, `src/core/featureRecord.ts:31-35`, `src/core/csv.ts:10-37`, `src/core/sessionMetadata.ts:201-214`, `docs/validation-plan-round2.md:36-42`, `docs/blink-line-adoption.txt:76-82` |

**Claim.** The line the detector reads cannot be reproduced from the session CSV; a stale or stranger's line silently becomes the threshold on another camera or a clip, contrary to guidedCalibration.ts:163-164; two exports of one session disagree; and the guided line's first out-of-house test would be silently unmeasurable.

**Impact.** validation_checks.py judges a ruler the detector did not use; a rescued round-II session prints as REFUSED; 'a line the instrument vouches for' means different things to four consumers.

**Fix as proposed.** Export blink_line_source (passive|guided|fixed|none), blink_line_mm, guided medians as metadata rows and a per-second blinkLineMm column; compute one blinksWithheld boolean per frame and use it for readout, record, report and log button; refuse a stored line when frameSource is file or when stamped iris px/frame differ beyond a margin; append a dated section to validation-plan-round2.md on reading guided sessions; ADR on whether a guided line serves the shut baseline; e2e that a seeded line reaches the export.

**Evidence as filed.** The stored line loads at page load and is used whenever non-null with no frameSource, device, resolution or date check; the store holds three numbers. grep for guided/personalLine in sessionMetadata, csv, featureRecord, blinkLog: none; baselineMm documents itself as 'the baseline serving the blink line', false under a guided line. With a guided line and refused passive baseline, blinks are counted and the blink log enables while the readout says 'Blinks: withheld', the record writes rate null, the report withholds and the score is withheld. Round II's rule 1 (27 Aug, before the guided line landed 2 Sep) discards all detector columns when calibration_refused is true.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity high.** src/main.ts:1692-1693 loads storedBlinkCalibration at page load; the only other writers are 1900 (erase) and 3477 (a run resolving ready); resetSession (main.ts:950-999) never touches it and frameSource="file" (main.ts:1195) is not consulted at 3538-3542, so a clip loaded in that browser reads the stored line. With hasGuidedLine && calibrationRefused: blinkStep is fed the aperture (3569-3571) and events append (3625), while the readout prints 'Blinks: withheld' (3653-3654), the record writes blinkRatePerMin null (3825-3827), the report withholds via measuredValue(refused,…) (2450-2460, 2482-2508), the score is withheld (3877-3878), PERCLOS/long closures stay null because frozenShutBaselineMm is set only when kind==="ready" (3683-3685), and the blink-log button enables on blinkEvents.length alone (3848). git log: round-II plan 6f00577 2026-08-27; guided-line adoption 1a6c88f 2026-09-02. docs/validation-plan-round2.md:36-42 and analysis/blinklab/round2.py:101-117 discard detector columns on calibration_refused: true. analysis/blinklab/validation_checks.py:54-59 assumes 'the blink line is half the baseline'. docs/blink-line-adoption.txt never mentions export or the refusal interaction.

#### F-009. The long-closure reducer has no hysteresis; one hovering closure fires two or three times on phones and no roadmap row fixes it

|                             |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **high**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Category                    | defect                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Raised by                   | oculometric, roadmap                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Files                       | `src/core/longClosure.ts:85`, `src/core/longClosure.ts:101-126`, `src/core/blink.ts:95-104`, `src/core/blink.ts:127-129`, `src/core/constants.ts:118`, `src/core/score.ts:38-39`, `docs/validation-dry-run.txt:221-233`, `docs/aperture-noise-floor.txt:65-67`, `ROADMAP.md:188` |

**Claim.** A design proven necessary for the sibling reducer is missing here; one closure can cost 30-45 score points on a phone and 15 on a Mac, and the alert fires repeatedly.

**Impact.** Long-closure counts, alerts and the score's largest discrete penalty are inflated on the device class the goal names first, for the whole era.

**Fix as proposed.** New row before Phase 12: require the aperture to rise a noise-floor-derived fraction above the shut line (or hold N ms) before a closure ends; prediction first via the trace harness (phone shapes collapse 3->1 and 2->1, desktop unchanged, durations byte-identical); pin with a test that a 6 s closure with +/-0.3 mm noise counts once; state hysteresis-not-filtering as the rule.

**Evidence as filed.** One line serves closing and reopening and any frame above it resets firedForCurrentClosure, so noise (p95 0.24-0.29 mm per frame pair) restarts a closure that fires again after 500 ms. Dry run: 3 and 2 events for one six-second closure on iPhones with every sample at 2.79-3.01 mm against a 3.04 mm line; an Android did it twice; 'recorded, not diagnosed'. The blink reducer has a 10% arm/re-arm band for this reason. ROADMAP.md:188 only measures the over-count again in 11.6.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity high.** src/core/longClosure.ts:85 uses one line for closing; 101-126 reset firedForCurrentClosure=false on any frame >= the line, so a later sub-line run of >500 ms (LONG_CLOSURE_THRESHOLD_MS=MAX_BLINK_DURATION_MS, line 19; constants.ts:105) fires again. blink.ts:95-104 and 127-129 use APERTURE_HYSTERESIS_FRACTION=0.1 (constants.ts:118) for arm and re-arm. Reproduced with the real modules under vitest (repo untouched): a 6 s closure with a 0.5 Hz ±0.12 mm wobble about 2.95 mm plus ±0.05 mm noise against a 3.04 mm line fired 3 times (1400, 3333, 5367 ms); a deterministic stream of three 667 ms sub-line runs separated by single frames at 3.05 mm (0.01 mm above the line) counted 3, while the same chatter through blinkStep counted 1. docs/validation-dry-run.txt:221-233: iPhone 3 events, iPhone 17 2 events (samples 2.79-3.01 vs line 3.04), Android twice, desktops 1, 'recorded, not diagnosed'. docs/aperture-noise-floor.txt:65-67: p95 per-frame delta 0.286/0.242 mm. ROADMAP.md:188 (11.6) measures the over-count; grep for hysteresis/long closure in ROADMAP finds no row that adds one; test/core/longClosure.test.ts has no re-crossing case. No commit to longClosure.ts since b6f1ebc 2026-08-12.

_Note._ Two impact figures are overstated: score.ts:129-132 caps the long-closure penalty at LONG_CLOSURE_PENALTY_MAX=30, so a phone loses at most 30 points (vs 15 on a Mac), not 30-45; and src/core/alert.ts:10 ALERT_DEBOUNCE_MS=5000 suppresses re-fires inside 5 s (banner shows them as 'suppressed'), so the alert does not fire repeatedly within one 6 s closure. Also worth knowing: with independent white noise of ±0.3 mm the same closure fired 0 times (no 500 ms sub-line run survives), so the missing band produces both over- and under-counts depending on noise correlation.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity high.** longClosure.ts:85 closes on one line and :116-120 reopens on any frame above it, resetting firedForCurrentClosure, so a second dip past 500 ms fires again; no re-arm gate, unlike blink.ts:95-104 and :127-129. docs/validation-dry-run.txt:221-233: 3 and 2 events for one six-second closure on iPhones with every sample at 2.79-3.01 mm against a 3.04 mm line, an Android twice, three desktops exactly 1, 'recorded, not diagnosed'. docs/aperture-noise-floor.txt:65-67: per-eye p95 frame-pair delta 0.242/0.286 mm, the same size as the gap those samples sat under the line. ROADMAP.md:188 (11.6) only measures the over-count with 'mechanism explicitly open'; the risk has been filed as issue #115 since 6 August (LEARNING.md:449, STATE.md:3399-3400) with no era row that fixes it. Corrections: the score cost is capped at LONG_CLOSURE_PENALTY_MAX = 30 (score.ts:38-39), so a double or triple fire costs 30, not 30-45; the alert governor debounces at 5 s (alert.ts:10), so repeat fires inside that window are counted as suppressed rather than shown.

_Note._ Not an accepted limit: the dry run explicitly left it undiagnosed and #115 has sat open for a month while the sibling reducer got its band. Phones are the first-named device class of the goal, longClosureCount is an exported column and the score's largest discrete penalty, and one closure inflating to two or three is a 2-3x error on the microsleep event. The fix must mirror blink.ts's re-arm gate, not a reopen latch: LEARNING.md:447-449 records that a latch on the reopen side corrupts durations, and lastLongClosureDurationMs is one of those numbers. With the trace-harness prediction first, the proposal is proportionate.

Exports are re-enabled only inside the frame loop at :3847-3848 (running). KSS-after is asked only from the export click, :2769-2780. Next Start → beginCamera :1094 resetSession → :965 featureRecords = []. grep 'Stop camera|stop-camera|stopCamera' in test/: no matches — no e2e exercises the button (test/e2e/measurementFailed.spec.ts:66-68 asserts export-enabled only on the crash path). reportAvailable (participantReport.ts:85-97) is true after Stop, so the report works while the export does not. docs/pilot-dry-run.txt:7-8 records the order 'export CSV, export blink log, stop camera, report', and docs/assessment-pilot-plan.md:72-74 puts export at steps 8-9 — which is why the protocol has not hit it.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity high.** src/main.ts:841-842 running = state.kind === 'running'; :900-913 when !running, exports are force-disabled unless state.kind === 'measurementFailed' (:909-912). Stop handler :2667-2678 does sourceRunToken += 1; setState({kind:'idle'}) with the comment 'the records stay exportable'. The only enable site is :3847-3848 inside the frame loop. resetSession() :950-969 sets featureRecords = [] and disables both exports; beginCamera calls it at :1094, so the next Start wipes the session. participantReport.ts:85-97 reportAvailable returns true at idle with records, so after Stop the report renders but Export CSV / blink log do not; KSS-after is asked only on first export (:2769-2780) so it never fires. grep 'Stop camera' in test/e2e: no hits. docs/UI.md:131 documents Stop camera as 'the intentional end of a session'; docs/pilot-dry-run.txt:8 shows the dry run's order was export, export, stop, report, which is why this was never met. Not documented anywhere as intended.

_Note._ Real, unmitigated in code, contradicts the handler's own comment and the crash path's promise (measurementFailed keeps exports; the intentional stop loses them). The pilot protocol survives only by ordering; a participant or moderator who stops first loses the CSV and blink log, which the repo treats as the fact's home. Fix (export availability = records exist, e2e Start -> record -> Stop -> exports enabled and KSS-after fires) is proportionate: it keeps the count rule, keeps the report-only-after-stop strength, and clipFailed with zero records stays disabled.

#### F-017. A superseded camera start attaches its stream and never stops it: a live track the page cannot turn off

|                             |                                                                                                                                                   |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **high**                                                                                                                                          |
| Category                    | security                                                                                                                                          |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                                                                 |
| Raised by                   | wiring                                                                                                                                            |
| Files                       | `src/io/camera.ts:34-36`, `src/main.ts:1061`, `src/main.ts:1075-1076`, `src/main.ts:1132-1137`, `src/main.ts:1567-1569`, `src/io/videoFile.ts:36` |

**Claim.** Two picker changes within getUserMedia latency, or Start camera then picking a clip while the permission bubble is up, leaves a live unowned track (and can hijack the clip load) for the page's life.

**Impact.** The camera indicator stays on after the page says the camera is off, the exact shape :1132-1137 calls dishonest.

**Fix as proposed.** Return the MediaStream from startCamera and stop its tracks on token mismatch; better, request, check token, then attach; disable clipInput and the picker while requesting/loadingClip.

**Evidence as filed.** startCamera attaches srcObject and plays before beginCamera's runToken check; the superseding call's stopCamera ran earlier when nothing was attached; the superseded stream is later displaced by another srcObject or srcObject = null, neither stopping its tracks. The picker fires beginCamera while running.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity high.** src/io/camera.ts:34-35 sets video.srcObject = stream and plays BEFORE returning; src/main.ts:1075-1076 'const frame = await startCamera(...); if (runToken !== sourceRunToken) return;' — no track.stop on the mismatch. The superseding call's stopCamera(video) runs at :1061 (beginCamera) / :1177 (beginVideoFile) before the superseded getUserMedia resolves, when nothing is attached. Later displacement: another startCamera assigns srcObject (camera.ts:34) or loadVideoFile sets srcObject = null (videoFile.ts:36) — neither stops tracks. Reachability: grep 'picker\.|clipInput\.' in main.ts shows only hidden/value/aria/accept assignments — neither control is ever disabled during 'requesting' or 'loadingClip'; picker change → beginCamera(picker.value) at :1567-1569; Stop camera is hidden when frameSource !== 'camera' (:932) and stopClipButton only sets a flag (:661-664), so after the hijack no button on the page can stop the orphaned stream. src/io/videoStepper.ts:114-117 waits on requestVideoFrameCallback after setting currentTime, so on a MediaStream-backed element the stepper would receive camera frames under the clip's name.

_Note._ Cannot be exercised here without a browser; the code reading is unambiguous. The permission-bubble variant (Start camera, pick a clip, then Allow) is a plain user sequence, not a timing race, and the stepper detail above means camera frames could be exported as clip data — if anything the finding under-states.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity high.** src/io/camera.ts:34-36 attaches srcObject and plays inside startCamera, before returning; src/main.ts:1075-1076 checks runToken only after it resolves and returns without touching the stream. The superseding beginCamera's stopCamera at :1061 (and beginVideoFile's at :1177) runs while the loser's getUserMedia is still pending, so it stops nothing; when the loser's stream later attaches it is displaced by the winner's srcObject (camera.ts:34) or by loadVideoFile's video.srcObject = null (videoFile.ts:36), neither of which stops tracks; stopCamera :39-47 stops only the stream currently attached. picker 'change' fires beginCamera at :1567-1569 with no guard; grep for picker.disabled / clipInput.disabled: none; grep test/e2e for picker: none. The repo's own words at :1132-1137 call a camera capturing behind a page that hides the stream 'the dishonest shape'.

_Note._ A live, unowned MediaStreamTrack the page cannot stop is reachable by ordinary use: keyboard-navigating the camera select (each arrow key fires change within device-switch latency) or clicking Start camera and then picking a clip while the permission prompt is up, which also hijacks the clip's video element because srcObject overrides src. No number changes, and 'security' overstates the category (nothing leaves the browser), but against a project that tells pilot volunteers the camera is off, a recording light that stays on for the page's life is a consent-relevant honesty defect. The fix (return the stream from startCamera and stop its tracks on token mismatch, or request, check the token, then attach; disable picker and clipInput during requesting/loadingClip) is small and breaks no strength.
