_Note._ Two asides are wrong: tools/mutationCheck.mjs DOES list BASELINE_MIN_SAMPLES (→1, →10000, lines 83-94) and PERCLOS_STALE_MS (→1, →2000000, lines 125-136), so 'none is in' is false for those two — but only at order-of-magnitude extremes, and the finding's 50 and 9000 pass it; MIN_BLINK_FPS, BLINK_RATE_MIN_OBSERVATION_MS and GUIDED_CALIBRATION_MIN_SAMPLES are absent. The title's 'six other floors' is four in the evidence. The central claim — every named refusal floor drifts with 962 green — is reproduced exactly.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity high.** Reproduced on two scratch copies of the tree (node_modules symlinked, no .git; the real repo was never modified, git status clean throughout). Scratch baseline: 6 failed / 956 passed of 962, all six in git-dependent tool tests (claimGuard.test.ts, exportsAreIgnored.test.ts). Each of MIN_BLINK_FPS = 28, MIN_BLINK_FPS = 23, BLINK_RATE_MIN_OBSERVATION_MS = 1, PERCLOS_STALE_MS = 9000, BASELINE_MIN_SAMPLES = 50, GUIDED_CALIBRATION_MIN_SAMPLES = 6 produced the identical 6 failed / 956 passed: zero new failures. Probe derivation confirmed: test/core/fpsGate.test.ts:23-27 uses MIN_BLINK_FPS +/- 0.1; blinkRate.test.ts:33-44 uses BLINK_RATE_MIN_OBSERVATION_MS +/- 1; perclos.test.ts:170-178 uses PERCLOS_STALE_MS +/- 1; sessionVerdict.test.ts:96-99 uses literals 22 (refused) and 30 (warned), bounding the floor only to (22, 30]; guidedCalibration.test.ts:31 ENOUGH = 40 and :69-81 refusal probes at 5 samples; baseline.test.ts:51-56 probes at 10 samples. tools/mutationCheck.mjs:20-161 lists BASELINE_MIN_SAMPLES only at 1/10000 and PERCLOS_STALE_MS only at 1/2000000, and omits MIN_BLINK_FPS, BLINK_RATE_MIN_OBSERVATION_MS and GUIDED_CALIBRATION_MIN_SAMPLES entirely. Partial mitigation: tools/detectorRatchet.mjs:47 watches src/core/constants.ts, so a change is a red build until a dated 'DETECTOR CHANGED, not yet re-measured' caveat (:72-75) is added to docs/eyeblink8-result.txt. That ratchet is file-level and ties only to Eyeblink8; it would not connect the change to the 24 docs quoting the 25 fps floor or to the separate Python literal MIN_USABLE_FPS = 25 at analysis/blinklab/drozy.py:38 (imported by rldd.py:53), which would silently desynchronise the DROZY/UTA-RLDD filters from the app.

_Note._ Every claim in the finding holds and the reproduction matches its numbers (962 tests, 0 new failures per mutant). This is not a re-find of the accepted 25 fps limit: the limit is honoured in code today, but nothing except a caveat-satisfiable file hash pins WHERE it sits, and the same 'tests derive inputs from the constant' pattern that remediation C1 (mutationCheck.mjs:1-9) was built to close has recurred on every constant added since. The floor is the most-quoted number in the accepted-limits list and decided 16 of 36 DROZY exclusions, so a drift is material to published claims. The fix (one literal boundary probe per constant in its owning test, each listed in mutationCheck.mjs) is the repo's own established remedy, cheap, and breaks nothing; a sixth line pinning the TypeScript MIN_BLINK_FPS to the Python MIN_USABLE_FPS would close the cross-track gap the finding did not name.

#### F-020. drozyGuard watches one file while four of the seven DROZY rows depend on code that has since changed; the guarded caveat is now false

|                             |                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **high**                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Category                    | overclaim                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Effort                      | M                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Raised by                   | test-quality                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Files                       | `tools/drozyGuard.mjs:3-8`, `tools/drozyGuard.mjs:30`, `test/tools/drozyGuard.test.ts:121-151`, `README.md:478-490`, `docs/drozy-result.txt:19-33`, `docs/eyeblink8-result.txt:205-213` |

**Claim.** The guard enforces a caveat scoped to 2026-08-12 and cannot see that the four 'unaffected' rows are also measured by superseded code.

**Impact.** Blink duration (rho 0.444, the closest row to the bar) and three others are presented as current-code numbers; the sentence saying which rows are stale is itself stale.

**Fix as proposed.** Per-feature source map in drozyGuard requiring the caveat to name every feature whose sources moved since the measuring commit; reword README.md:482-485 and drozy-result.txt:26-28; feed owner decision 10.3 the true stale list.

**Evidence as filed.** Since bd2a98d, blink.ts (re-arm gate), baseline.ts (refusal, ruler freeze) and constants.ts changed; SHAPE_SOURCE is only blinkShape.ts and the caveat is required only for three shape labels. README.md:482-485 says re-measuring returns duration, long closures, rate and PERCLOS byte for byte identical, true of PR #225 on 12 Aug; the freeze alone moved Eyeblink8 recall 87.7 -> 83.6.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity high.** tools/drozyGuard.mjs:30 `export const SHAPE_SOURCE = "src/core/blinkShape.ts"` is the only path the guard asks git about (test/tools/drozyGuard.test.ts:125 `commitsTouchingSince(SHAPE_SOURCE, measuringCommit, root)`). `git log bd2a98d..HEAD -- <file>`: src/core/blink.ts moved (003184a 2026-08-21 re-arm gate; b6f1ebc), src/core/baseline.ts moved four times (092a13f 2026-08-26 calibration refusal, 89658cb 2026-08-23, 171b5f4 2026-08-20 ruler freeze, b6f1ebc), src/core/constants.ts moved four times. The repo's own record contradicts the caveat: docs/eyeblink8-result.txt:205-213 lists 87.7% recall / F1 85.4 'ruler still moving' -> 83.6% / 82.5 'ruler frozen at calibration (2026-08-20)' -> 83.6 / 83.8 're-arm gate (2026-08-21), 13 false alarms removed'. So which blinks are detected, and their starts and ends, changed after bd2a98d. analysis/tools/analyse_drozy.py reads measured-dir CSVs produced by that TS core, so blink duration, long closures, blink rate and PERCLOS all come from the moved code.

_Note._ The scope claim is what is stale, and it is stated flatly in three places: README.md:478 '**Three of these rows were measured by code that has since changed.**', README.md:482-485 'It does not move blink duration, long closures, blink rate or PERCLOS ... re-measuring returns those byte for byte identical', docs/drozy-result.txt:26-28 'Blink intervals re-measure byte for byte identical, so blink duration, long closures, blink rate and PERCLOS are unaffected', and the guard's own premise at tools/drozyGuard.mjs:4-6. Seven of seven rows were measured by code that has since changed; only three are declared stale. Blink duration (rho 0.444, docs/drozy-result.txt:31) is the largest-magnitude row. Mild counterweight, not enough to downgrade: read narrowly the sentences are scoped to PR #225 and remain true of #225, and the published NULL verdict is unaffected (the shuffle control reaches 0.75, README.md:494-496). But the block is headed 'MEASURING COMMIT, read this before the correlations' and closes 'Read those three rows as produced by code this repository has since corrected' — it exists to tell a reader which numbers are current, and that answer is now wrong.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity high.** tools/drozyGuard.mjs:30 scopes the whole guard to one file: `export const SHAPE_SOURCE = "src/core/blinkShape.ts"`, and test/tools/drozyGuard.test.ts:121-151 requires the caveat only while commitsTouchingSince(SHAPE_SOURCE, measuringCommit) is non-empty, checking only the three SHAPE_FEATURE_LABELS. But the DROZY rows are built from blinklab's own exports (analysis/blinklab/drozy.py:162-171 loads `<subject>-<session>.seconds.csv` and `.blinks.csv` — the whole detector chain, not just blinkShape). Since the measuring commit bd2a98d, `git log bd2a98d..HEAD -- src/core/blink.ts src/core/baseline.ts src/core/perclos.ts src/core/constants.ts src/core/aperture.ts` returns ten commits, including 171b5f4 'The ruler freezes at birth' (2026-08-20) and 003184a 'the re-arm gate' (2026-08-21). Both demonstrably move which blinks are detected: docs/eyeblink8-result.txt:205-213 records recall 87.7 -> 83.6 at the freeze and 13 false alarms removed at the gate. So README.md:483-485 ('It does not move blink duration, long closures, blink rate or PERCLOS ... re-measuring returns those byte for byte identical') and docs/drozy-result.txt:26-28 ('Blink intervals re-measure byte for byte identical, so blink duration, long closures, blink rate and PERCLOS are unaffected') are now false. docs/drozy-result.txt contains no mention of the freeze or the gate (grep: zero hits).

_Note._ Confirmed at high. This is exactly the class the repo's contract makes load-bearing: every published number carries its conditions, and here the stated condition is false for four of seven rows, including the strongest (blink duration rho 0.444, docs/drozy-result.txt:35). A reader relies on the caveat rather than doing their own git archaeology, and the guard built to keep that caveat honest is scoped so it cannot see the falseness. Mitigations that keep this from being critical: the commit binding itself is present and correct ('built from bd2a98d', drozy-result.txt:23), and the published conclusion is a null that no re-measure would rescue, so no headline moves. The fix is proportionate and must preserve the strength — drozyGuard's self-retiring design (it reads the measuring commit out of the result file, so re-measuring lifts the requirement with no human memory involved, tools/drozyGuard.mjs:11-20) is one of the best mechanisms in the repo. Extend the source set per feature; do not replace the design. Note the honest end state is that all seven rows are now superseded-code rows, which is a sentence, not a re-extract — DATASETS.md forbids recreating the derived video, so text plus guard scope is the whole cost.

#### F-023. README Privacy section says two localStorage keys; the app writes four, including a pseudonym and a personal blink line

|                             |                                                                                                                       |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **high**                                                                                                              |
| Category                    | overclaim                                                                                                             |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                                     |
| Raised by                   | security-privacy                                                                                                      |
| Files                       | `README.md:589`, `src/io/calibrationStore.ts:29-45`, `src/core/storedData.ts:24-53`, `test/e2e/storedData.spec.ts:49` |

**Claim.** The Privacy section understates storage by half and omits the identity-bearing items; the stamp guard blesses it because it checks dates, not content.

**Impact.** The same class as August's 'the retired telemetry denial': a privacy sentence true when written and silently false; a shared-machine user is told nothing about a stored pseudonym.

**Fix as proposed.** Generate the storage paragraph from STORED_ITEMS (resultsBlock pattern) or at minimum correct it to four named items and add a guard that every storedData key appears in README's Privacy section.

**Evidence as filed.** README.md:589: 'those two keys are the only storage this app touches'; ALL_KEYS has four; the e2e asserts 'Stored on this device now: 3 of 4'. The sentence dates from 2026-08-15; the pseudonym key landed 29 Aug and the blink line 2 Sep; README was re-stamped 5 Sep with the sentence unchanged.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity high.** README.md:589 '**Two things are kept on your device, and the page now lists both and offers to erase them.** ... Nothing else is stored: those two keys are the only storage this app touches.' src/io/calibrationStore.ts:29-32 declares four keys — STORAGE_KEY, PROFILE_KEY, PSEUDONYM_KEY ('blinklab-participant-pseudonym-v1'), BLINK_CALIBRATION_KEY ('blinklab-blink-calibration-v1') — and :40-45 puts all four in ALL_KEYS. src/core/storedData.ts:24-53 enumerates the same four to the visitor, including 'Your personal blink line' (:43) and 'Your chosen pseudonym' (:51). test/e2e/storedData.spec.ts:49 asserts the page prints 'Stored on this device now: 3 of 4.' Dating: the sentence entered at 7656196 (2026-08-15, `git log -S`), PSEUDONYM_KEY at 2918f78 (2026-08-29), BLINK_CALIBRATION_KEY at d44aca8 (2026-09-02); README.md was last touched 8ad1c06 (2026-09-05) with the sentence unchanged.

_Note._ Nothing to soften. The page, the store and the e2e all say four; the Privacy section says two and adds the exclusive 'Nothing else is stored'. Same failure class the repo already catalogued in August, and unlike F-024 this one errs toward understating what is kept — including an identity-bearing pseudonym on a possibly shared machine. The ALL_KEYS comment at src/io/calibrationStore.ts:35-39 explicitly reasons that a key missing from the enumeration is 'the exact E3 defect'; the README paragraph is the enumeration nothing holds to the code.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity high.** README.md:589: '**Two things are kept on your device, and the page now lists both** ... Nothing else is stored: those two keys are the only storage this app touches.' src/core/storedData.ts:24-53 declares four STORED_ITEMS: the calibration profile, its samples, 'blinklab-blink-calibration-v1' ('Your personal blink line') and 'blinklab-participant-pseudonym-v1' ('Your chosen pseudonym'); src/io/calibrationStore.ts:40 ALL_KEYS carries the same four and :98,:122 iterate them. The app agrees with the code, not the README: test/e2e/storedData.spec.ts:49 asserts the page renders 'Stored on this device now: 3 of 4.' grep of README.md for 'pseudonym', 'blink line' and 'blinklab-' returns zero hits, so the two newer items appear nowhere in the README at all.

_Note._ Confirmed at high. This is a categorical privacy claim ('the only storage this app touches') that is false by half on the document outsiders read first, and the two omitted items are the identity-bearing ones — a chosen pseudonym and a personal blink line. It repeats, exactly, the failure mode the project already publicly apologised for in the paragraph immediately below it (README.md:591, 'This page previously denied any reporting of any kind, which was false'): a sentence true when written, silently false after a feature landed, with a date-stamp guard that blesses it because it checks stamps and not content. Real mitigation, which is why this is high and not critical: the instrument itself is honest — STORED_ITEMS drives both the on-page list and the erase, so a visitor at the page sees all four and can erase all four; only the README lies. The proposed fix is proportionate and points the right way: generate the paragraph from STORED_ITEMS the way resultsBlock generates the results block, so the guard is structural rather than another sentence somebody has to remember. Protect the strength while doing it — storedData.ts is pure and hands the interface its sentences; keep the generation in tools/, not in src/core.

#### F-028. Light-response overlay has no touch exit and, without Element.requestFullscreen, throws and leaves a black, textless, unclosable screen

|                             |                                                                           |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **high**                                                                  |
| Category                    | defect                                                                    |
| Effort                      | S                                                                         |
| Raised by                   | demo-ux                                                                   |
| Files                       | `src/main.ts:4144-4173`, `src/main.ts:4118-4127`, `src/main.ts:4175-4194` |

**Claim.** A phone user who taps Light response can be trapped with a z-index-20 black overlay; the only way out is reload, which discards the session.

**Impact.** A hard trap with silent data loss on the device class the owner wants to reach.

**Fix as proposed.** Guard on typeof requestFullscreen; add a touch-reachable exit and touch wording; add the no-fullscreen path to lightResponse.spec.ts via addInitScript.

**Evidence as filed.** startLightStimulus unhides the overlay then calls requestFullscreen().catch(); an absent method throws synchronously so step() never runs; exits are Escape keydown and fullscreenchange only; the finished screen says 'Press Esc'. Reproduced with requestFullscreen undefined: black overlay, empty message, pageerror, still visible after a tap. iPhone Safari lacks requestFullscreen on non-video elements.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity high.** REPRODUCED end to end in headless chromium against the built page with `delete Element.prototype.requestFullscreen` injected via addInitScript, a fake camera, and a real started session. After clicking Light response: overlay `hidden:false`, computed background `rgb(0, 0, 0)`, `z-index: 20`, `dataset.phase` null (step() never ran), message textContent empty, `document.fullscreenElement` null, and one pageerror: 'TypeError: ix.requestFullscreen is not a function'. A tap at (180,300) left `overlay.hidden === false`; only `page.keyboard.press('Escape')` closed it. Code matches: /home/user/blinklab/src/main.ts:4151 sets `lightOverlay.hidden = false` BEFORE :4155 `void lightOverlay.requestFullscreen().catch(...)`, so the synchronous TypeError (verified independently with `node -e`) aborts startLightStimulus before `step()` at :4170. Exits are only the Escape keydown (src/main.ts:4183-4187) and fullscreenchange (:4189-4193), which never fires because fullscreen was never entered; `grep -n lightOverlay src/main.ts` shows no pointer/click/touch listener. The finished screen wording is keyboard-only: src/main.ts:4123 'Finished. Press Esc, then export your session.' test/e2e/lightResponse.spec.ts exercises only `page.keyboard.press('Escape')` (line 40).

_Note._ Nothing to refute — the trap reproduces in a browser, including the empty message and the failed tap-to-exit. Session loss on reload also holds: featureRecords live in memory only (roadmap 14.7, local session history, is unbuilt), so the only exit available to a keyboard-less phone user discards the session. The premise that iPhone Safari lacks Element.requestFullscreen for non-video elements is correct.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity high.** src/main.ts:4152-4155: lightOverlay.hidden = false is set, THEN void lightOverlay.requestFullscreen().catch(...). An absent method throws TypeError synchronously before .catch is reached, so step() at src/main.ts:4157-4170 never runs and paintLightPhase never fires. The overlay is left at its constructed state: src/main.ts:4075-4088 sets position fixed, inset 0, zIndex 20, background #000000, with lightMessage textContent unset. Exits are only Escape keydown (src/main.ts:4181-4185) and fullscreenchange (src/main.ts:4188-4193), the latter dead when fullscreen never engaged. The finished screen text is literally 'Finished. Press Esc, then export your session.' (src/main.ts:4122). Reachable by any visitor: refreshLightResponseButton (src/main.ts:4172-4175) enables it whenever a camera session is running. grep for 'Light response' in test/MANUAL.md and docs/UI.md returns nothing.

_Note._ Confirmed, and there are TWO independent traps, not one — the finding under-states it. The absent-method path is the black-screen version, but even the graceful path (fullscreen present, promise rejects) leaves a touch user with no exit at all, because there is no touch handler anywhere and the terminal screen instructs 'Press Esc'. So every touch device is trapped, not only iOS; only Android is rescued incidentally, by its system back gesture firing fullscreenchange. The code comment at src/main.ts:4149-4151 shows exactly what was reasoned about — 'best effort... a permission, a headless run' — a REJECTED promise, never an absent method. Aggravating: this control has no MANUAL item and no UI.md row, so it has never been hand-walked on a phone, and it ships enabled to every visitor of a public demo for an experiment the repo's own docs/pupil-light-result.txt reports dead at this optics. High is right: it is the only finding in this set that destroys user data (reload discards the session) and it blocks the device class the era goal names. The fix is proportionate and small; the addInitScript e2e slots into the existing test/e2e/lightResponse.spec.ts and needs the same phone-viewport project F-027 asks for. Worth adding to the fix: guard the click handler in try/catch as well, so any future throw cannot again leave an unhidden overlay behind.

#### G-Guided b-4. The guided line has no soundness ceiling and by construction always sits higher, as a fraction of the open eye, than the passive line it replaces

|                             |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **high**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Category                    | risk                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Effort                      | M                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Raised by                   | Guided blink calibration as a measurement PROCEDURE: how the personal ruler is captured, cued, confirmed, and carried — not its arithmetic                                                                                               |
| Files                       | `src/core/guidedCalibration.ts:101-112`, `src/core/constants.ts:167`, `src/core/constants.ts:152`, `src/core/constants.ts:174-193`, `src/core/longClosure.ts:29-35`, `src/core/constants.ts:118`, `docs/blink-line-adoption.txt:113-117` |

**Claim.** The guided line can legitimately be placed up to 0.85 of the person's own open median — above the droop band the instrument itself documents — and nothing at resolve time checks it against the resting eye. The one hard-won soundness ceiling in the codebase guards only the ruler the guided line now supersedes.

**Impact.** The failure mode is the one the baseline freeze was built to prevent: a line above the resting aperture makes closures start at rest, inflating durations and flattening shapes, or (with the 1.1 rearm) stalling the counter entirely. It lands directly on the device-conditioned duration numbers the repo has published and cannot explain (phones 96 ms vs Macs 149-166 ms), adding a second uncontrolled source of duration variance right where an explanation is being sought.

**Fix as proposed.** Add a resolve-time soundness check symmetric to BASELINE_MEDIAN_CEILING_FACTOR: refuse (or warn and refuse to store) when the line exceeds a stated fraction of the open-phase distribution's lower tail — for example when personalLineMm > p10 of the open samples, or when it exceeds the concurrently learned passive baseline's own half-line by more than a committed factor. Pre-register the factor before reading any guided data, exactly as constants.ts:155-167 did for the first two.

**Evidence as filed.** resolveGuidedCalibration accepts any closed median up to 0.7 x open (constants.ts:167) and places the line at the midpoint (guidedCalibration.ts:107-112), so line/open_median = (1 + c/o)/2 lies in (0.50, 0.85]. Using the repo's own healthy p90/median ratio of about 1.12 (constants.ts:188), that is 0.45-0.76 of the passive baseline, against a passive line fixed at 0.50 (BASELINE_THRESHOLD_FRACTION, constants.ts:152) and a shut line at 0.40 (longClosure.ts:35). The relaxed reading droop this repo measured sits at 45-50 percent of baseline (longClosure.ts:29-33) — so a guided line at the top of its permitted range sits well ABOVE the droop band, and the reducer's rearm needs aperture >= line x 1.1 (constants.ts:118), i.e. up to 0.94 of the open median. The passive path acquired exactly this protection after it burned the owner: BASELINE_MEDIAN_CEILING_FACTOR exists because 'once half the baseline exceeds the resting aperture, the blink line sits ABOVE the open eye, every closure is timed from a crossing that happened at rest, durations inflate and shapes flatten' (constants.ts:174-193). The guided path, which overrides the passive line and lifts its refusal, shipped with no analogous ceiling. docs/blink-line-adoption.txt:113-117 pre-registers this precise risk: 'new false positives from a higher guided line arming on ordinary droops... the guided midpoint is too generous'.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity high.** resolveGuidedCalibration (src/core/guidedCalibration.ts:84-113) has exactly three gates: two length checks (:87, :90) and the separation check `closedMedianMm > openMedianMm * (1 - 0.3)` (:101-104). The line is the bare midpoint (:111). No resting-eye or soundness check anywhere. constants.ts:167 = 0.3, :152 = 0.5, :118 = 0.1, :193 = BASELINE_MEDIAN_CEILING_FACTOR 1.25. `grep -rn BASELINE_MEDIAN_CEILING_FACTOR src/` returns ONLY src/core/calibrationWindow.ts:2,67 — the passive path — never guidedCalibration.ts. Arithmetic (node): c/o in (0,0.7] gives line/openMedian in (0.50,0.85] and, at the repo's own p90/median 1.12, line/baseline in (0.446,0.759]; rearm at line*1.1 reaches 0.935*openMedian. The rearm gate is real: src/core/blink.ts `rearmed = ... || apertureMm >= thresholdMm * (1 + APERTURE_HYSTERESIS_FRACTION)`. Droop band 45-50% of baseline: longClosure.ts:29-33. docs/blink-line-adoption.txt:113-117 pre-registers verbatim: 'new false positives from a higher guided line arming on ordinary droops... the guided midpoint is too generous'. test/core/guidedCalibration.test.ts has 24 tests, none about a ceiling (its only 'ceiling' at :25,:83 is the iris-occlusion recall ceiling).

_Note._ Confirmed, and the mechanism is stronger than the finding claims at TYPICAL values, not just the permitted extreme: longClosure.ts:29-31 records fully shut eyes at ~33% of baseline, so a normal person's c/o is ~0.37, putting the guided line at ~0.61 of baseline — already above the 0.45-0.50 droop band and well above the passive 0.50. One overstatement in the impact paragraph: parseBlinkCalibration:187 enforces closed < line < open, so the passive path's exact catastrophic mode (line above the open eye, closures timed from rest) is bounded away by construction. The real exposure is the line sitting inside/above the droop band and, in the c/o->0.7 tail, a rearm gate at 0.935 of the person's own open median. Structural gap and pre-registered risk both hold; severity stands.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity high.** resolveGuidedCalibration (src/core/guidedCalibration.ts:101-112) refuses only when closedMedian > open*(1-0.3), then returns the midpoint; no other check exists. parseBlinkCalibration (guidedCalibration.ts:187) checks only the bracket closed<line<open — an ordering test, not a soundness test. I grepped every 'ceiling' in src/core and src/io: the only one is BASELINE_MEDIAN_CEILING_FACTOR (constants.ts:193) on the passive learner, and the only live soundness monitor, rulerFit, is fed readyBaselineMm and never the guided line (src/main.ts:3775-3780). So line/open_median ∈ (0.50, 0.85] with nothing checking it, and re-arm needs aperture ≥ line*1.1 (blink.ts:127-129, APERTURE_HYSTERESIS_FRACTION=0.1) = up to 0.935*open_median. The finding's arithmetic checks out and its strongest evidence is one it did not use: the repo's OWN measured shut floor. longClosure.ts:29-33 and perclos.ts:11-16 both state that fully shut eyes read about a THIRD of baseline, never near zero. With the repo's healthy p90/median ≈ 1.12 (constants.ts:188), a typical closed median is ~0.33*baseline = ~0.37*open_median, putting the guided midpoint at ~0.61 of baseline — above the entire relaxed reading droop band of 0.45-0.50 of baseline that longClosure.ts:32-33 records, and arming at 0.9*0.61 = 0.55 of baseline, still above it. That is not the worst permitted case; it is the expected case, for the very face (the owner's low lids, ROADMAP.md:13) the feature was built for.

_Note._ Material and correctly rated high. It also refutes a premise of the pre-registered doc: docs/blink-line-adoption.txt claims 'for a TYPICAL subject, whose closed eye really does read near zero, the guided midpoint is approximately half of open', but the repo's own committed measurement (amendment 6, longClosure.ts:29-33) killed 'near zero' — the instrument reads shut at a third of baseline. Guided and passive do NOT nearly coincide; the guided line sits systematically higher. This is not an accepted documented limit: the risk is named at docs/blink-line-adoption.txt:113-117, but the refutation route it names is a corpus precision run, and the same doc argues the corpus can never reach the guided path ('neutral by construction'), so the one pre-registered check for this risk cannot fire. Two corrections to the fix. (1) The proposed test 'refuse when personalLineMm > p10 of the open samples' is ineffective: for a tight open distribution p10 ≈ 0.93*median, far above a 0.685*median line, so it would pass every case including the failing one. The check has to be against the droop band the instrument measured — a committed ceiling on line/open-median (or line/baseline) placed below 0.45 — and it should also reopen the midpoint RULE, since a midpoint between an open median and a non-zero shut floor is structurally biased upward. (2) Refusing outright would deny personalisation to exactly the atypical-eyelid population it exists for, so the honest shape is a ceiling that refuses plus a stated reason, not a silent clamp. Pre-registering the factor first, as the fix says, is the right discipline and matches constants.ts:155-193.

Both steps of the analysis CI job (ci.yml:111-113) stay green. The docstring at :14-26 names exactly these three as the properties the file "deliberately has".

Its docstring at :14-26 names the three deliberate properties. #### G-Stepped--3. UTA-RLDD's 25 fps exclusion is a property of the stepper's calibration on each file, not of the file — and nothing anywhere cross-checks it against the container

|                             |                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **high**                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Category                    | risk                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Effort                      | M                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Raised by                   | Stepped-clip CFR assumption and the corpus exclusion mechanism                                                                                                                                |
| Files                       | `analysis/blinklab/rldd.py:195-198`, `analysis/blinklab/rldd.py:120`, `docs/uta-rldd-plan.md:63-68`, `analysis/tools/prepare_rldd.py:250-275`, `analysis/tools/evaluate_eyeblink8.py:163-179` |

**Claim.** The pre-registered claim that the exclusion is a property of the frame rate alone is not supported by the code: it is a property of what the stepper's six-frame calibration made of that file's opening. The repo holds no container-side witness that could tell a true sub-25 fps recording from a mis-calibrated one, in either direction.

**Impact.** The exclusion decides who is in the published 148-video, 54-subject result. If any of the 30 were mis-measured, the headline (BA 0.498/0.732, p 0.001) is computed on a sample selected by an instrument artefact rather than by the pre-registered rule — and the pre-registration language would then be an overclaim rather than a protection.

**Fix as proposed.** Port the Eyeblink8 instrument. (1) analysis/tools/prepare_rldd.py writes one ffprobe line per clip into a manifest (`r_frame_rate`, `avg_frame_rate`, `nb_read_packets`) — about fifteen lines, the same shape as prepare_eyeblink8.count_frames. (2) analysis/blinklab/rldd.py gains a coverage check: frames_measured against container nb_frames, refusing or flagging above a stated tolerance, exactly evaluate_eyeblink8.py:163-179. (3) Restate uta-rldd-plan.md:66-68 as "the rate this instrument measured", which is what it is.

**Evidence as filed.** analysis/blinklab/rldd.py:195-198 takes `measured_fps` as the MEDIAN of the exported per-second `fps` column, and :120 gates usability on it. That column is `measureFps` over frame timestamps (src/core/fps.ts:9-19, src/main.ts:2943-2945), and in stepped mode those timestamps are the media times the stepper reports — i.e. 1/step, the stepper's own calibrated interval, not an independent reading of the file. The export header's `measured_fps` is no help either: src/core/frameClock.ts:168-178 computes framesMeasured/clip_duration_s, which in my run F is 399/9.95 = 40.1, inflated by exactly the duplication. `grep -rn ffprobe` over analysis/ returns nothing; analysis/tools/prepare_rldd.py remuxes with `-c:v copy` (:250-275) and never counts a frame, while the Eyeblink8 sibling does (analysis/tools/prepare_eyeblink8.py:48-77,:112) and its evaluator flags coverage MISMATCH (analysis/tools/evaluate_eyeblink8.py:163-179). docs/uta-rldd-plan.md:66-68 nevertheless pre-registers the exclusion as "a property of the frame rate alone".

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity high.** analysis/blinklab/rldd.py:195-198 sets `measured_fps = statistics.median(fps)` over the export's per-second `fps` column, and :120 gates usability on `self.measured_fps >= MIN_USABLE_FPS` (imported from blinklab.drozy at :53). That column is measureFps (src/core/fps.ts:9-19) over the stamps main.ts:1288 derives from the stepper's reported media times, so its value is a property of the stepper's schedule and calibration on that file. The export header is no independent witness either: coverageMetadataRows (src/core/frameClock.ts:159-179) writes `measured_fps` as framesMeasured/clip_duration_s, which in my run F is 399/9.975 = 40.0, inflated by exactly the duplication. `grep -rn ffprobe analysis/` returns nothing, and prepare_rldd.py:250-280 remuxes with `-c:v copy` and never counts a frame — while the Eyeblink8 sibling does (prepare_eyeblink8.py:48-75 decodes and counts, :112 returns source and target counts) and its evaluator flags a gap as '<-- MISMATCH' (evaluate_eyeblink8.py:163-179). docs/uta-rldd-plan.md:66-67 nevertheless pre-registers 'the exclusion is a property of the frame rate alone'. The stakes are as stated: docs/uta-rldd-result.txt:31-34 records 178 measured, 30 excluded ('the 25 fps floor, and one short recording'), 148 analysed, 54 of 60 subjects, with :37 noting 'The 25 fps floor is aggressive on this phone-recorded data' — phone recordings being exactly the quantised/variable-interval case G-Stepped--1 mis-calibrates on. Headline BA 0.498 / 0.732 at :45 and :69.

_Note._ Confirmed, with one mechanism correction the finding overstates: the per-second fps column is NOT simply 1/step. On an exact landing the stepper reports requestVideoFrameCallback's own mediaTime (src/io/videoStepper.ts:335-336), a real decoder reading; it degrades to the fabricated schedule only on inexact landings. The conclusion is unaffected, and in fact the exclusion can err in BOTH directions as the finding says: measureFrameInterval's `Math.min(...gaps)` (:230) understates the interval on a short gap (inflating the rate, wrongly INCLUDING a sub-25 fps file), while systematically skipped probes make every observed gap a multiple and the minimum too large (deflating the rate, wrongly EXCLUDING a 30 fps file) — the exact failure the same comment records from WebKit on Linux at :227-229. Also note in fairness that 'property of the frame rate alone' sits beside 'fixed before a single label is read', so its intent is label-blindness; the literal wording is still an overclaim, since no container-side witness exists to make it true.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity high.** Chain verified end to end. analysis/blinklab/rldd.py:194-198 sets measured_fps = statistics.median of the per-second `fps` column and :115-120 gates usability on it (`measured_fps >= MIN_USABLE_FPS and reached_window_end`). That column is measureFps over frame timestamps (src/core/fps.ts:9-19 via src/main.ts:2942-2945), and in stepped mode those timestamps ARE the stepper's own schedule (frameTimestampMs("file", ...) = mediaTimeSeconds * 1000, src/core/frameClock.ts:181-187), so the column equals 1/step, not an independent reading of the file. My case G shows the consequence concretely: a clip whose true mean rate is 22.5 fps exports fps = 30.0 and would be INCLUDED. The header offers no second opinion either — measured_fps is framesMeasured/clip_duration_s (src/core/frameClock.ts:159-178), inflated by the same duplication (239/7.97 = 30). No container witness exists: `grep -rn ffprobe analysis/` returns nothing, prepare_rldd.py remuxes with `-c:v copy` (:250-262) and never counts a frame, while the Eyeblink8 sibling decodes and counts both sides (prepare_eyeblink8.py:48-77, :108) and its evaluator flags coverage MISMATCH above max(5, 1%) (evaluate_eyeblink8.py:163-179). The plan nevertheless pre-registers the exclusion as "a property of the frame rate alone" (docs/uta-rldd-plan.md:63-68). What it selects is published: 178 measured, 30 excluded, 148 analysed, 54 of 60 subjects (docs/uta-rldd-result.txt:30-34), carrying BA 0.498 / 0.732 at p 0.001, and no per-video fps is recorded anywhere in the repo, so the exclusion is unauditable after the fact (the source video is deleted by design).

_Note._ Confirmed at high, and the dangerous direction is worse than the finding states. Because the calibration takes the SMALLEST gap, the reported rate is the clip's PEAK rate, so the error runs toward false INCLUSION: a self-recorded phone video that drops below 30 fps in a dim room still reports 30 and passes the floor. That is label-correlated on this corpus — the drowsy sessions are the late, dim ones — so an instrument artefact could bias the very contrast the published headline rests on, not merely thin the sample. Two things keep this at high rather than critical: no evidence in the repo shows it actually fired (the exclusion count and class balance are plausible on their face, and the physiologically-correct feature loadings at docs/uta-rldd-result.txt:108-117 argue against a gross framing confound), and the direction of the wording error is narrow — "the rate this instrument measured" is the honest restatement. The fix is proportionate and, better, it ports a mechanism this repo already owns and trusts: an ffprobe manifest at prep time plus a coverage/rate check in rldd.py mirroring evaluate_eyeblink8.py:163-179. Protect the strength while doing it: the Eyeblink8 coverage check is the reason that corpus's numbers survive G-Stepped--1 untouched (docs/eyeblink8-result.txt:25-33, measured within one frame of annotated on all eight clips), which is the strongest argument that the same instrument belongs on the RLDD track.

The two neighbours at src/main.ts:2431-2442 ARE routed through asExported with the comment naming the reason. The asExported docstring (src/core/participantReport.ts:56-62) names this exact class: 'a page computing an input from a raw float while the file carries the rounded form lets the two sides disagree at a rounding boundary' — the paid-for lesson of docs/pilot-dry-run.txt:47-55, whose fix shipped as 'the one-capture fix and the asExported round-trips' (:88-90). I checked the escape hatches and there are none: the processing-rate fallback is safe because src/core/csv.ts:79 writes fps with `String(value)` at full precision, so sampled_fps really is the only verdict input the file rounds; deliveryRate.ts:142-143 computes it as ((distinct-1)*1000)/spanMs, a continuous quantity that can land anywhere; the fixtures carry only sampled_fps 60.0 (test/fixtures/verdict/good-session.csv:17, refused-session.csv:17) and unknown (degraded-session.csv:17), so no boundary case is pinned. analysis/blinklab/pilot.py:66-78 then raises InstrumentDefect and halts the cohort on the mismatch, exactly as it did on the real dry-run file.

_Note._ Material and correctly rated. For a measured rate in [59.95,60.0) — the likeliest band, a nominal-60 camera — the page says WARNED and the mirror says OK, and pilot.py stops the whole cohort calling a formatting artefact an instrument defect; docs/pilot-dry-run.txt:82-86 notes a kept session keeps refusing forever, so such a file is permanently mis-diagnosed. In [24.95,25.0) the page also prints a self-refuting sentence ('was 25.0 ... below the 25'). The fix is proportionate and breaks no strength: rounding the verdict input does not touch the live blink gate, which by documented design runs off the PROCESSING rate and whose evidence-rate wiring is an explicitly held stage (src/core/fpsGate.ts:16-27), so no gate loosens. Worth adding to the fix: the boundary fixture is the load-bearing half, since without it the same class can return through any future rounded input.

### Severity medium (62)

#### F-002. Inference and the whole per-frame pipeline run at display rate, 2-4x per photograph; 13.8 is a correctness lever, not a performance row

|                             |                                                                                                                                           |
| --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **medium**                                                                                                                                |
| Category                    | wrong-priority                                                                                                                            |
| Effort                      | M                                                                                                                                         |

**Claim.** Three of four inferences, canvas draws, buffer rebuilds and DOM writes on a fast machine carry no information; on phones ~45% of the inference budget re-reads the same photograph, the thermal load phones throttle under. Gating only detectForVideo would leave F-001 in place.

**Impact.** Cheapest source of phone throttling and battery drain the project controls, and the re-reads corrupt a published column.

**Fix as proposed.** Drive processFrame from requestVideoFrameCallback/observeVideoDelivery (one per presented frame, rVFC timestamp), leave rAF to repaint; keep the rAF fallback and record the driver in the export. Pre-register: stepped Eyeblink8 unchanged, processing rate equals sampled_fps, inference time down by the old ratio. Move 13.8 ahead of Phase 11/12 signal rows.

**Evidence as filed.** The camera path is rAF only; every tick draws the video and calls detectForVideo with no check that a new frame arrived, though deliveredCount is tracked on the same page. Measured re-read ratios 120/30, 55/30, 126.7/30. ROADMAP.md:40 calls 13.8 one of two real levers; Phase 13 has zero ticks while 20 rows landed in five September days. The played-clip path already measures once per decoded frame.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity high.** src/main.ts:2983-2993 draws and runs detectForVideo on every rAF tick while running; src/main.ts:3016-3025 counts a read and noteRead(deliveryState) but nothing gates on deliveredCount; src/main.ts:4590-4599 is rAF-only for the camera (file mode returns early and is driven per decoded frame via src/io/frameLoop.ts:114-148). src/io/frameLoop.ts:66-79 and src/core/deliveryRate.ts:12-17 state the re-read mechanism in the repo's own words. ROADMAP.md:40 names 13.8 one of the two real levers; ROADMAP.md:226 frames 13.8 as inference-saving with an 'event-level live equivalence' check; ROADMAP.md:219-230 Phase 13 has zero [x] rows; ROADMAP.md:164-177 Phase 10 has 7 ticks; git log --since=2026-09-01 shows 61 commits across roughly 20 roadmap rows in five days. 45% on phones follows from the measured 55 processing / 30 delivered pair (docs/validation-dry-run.txt:212, docs/blink-sample-rate.txt:635-636).

_Note._ The code facts and the roadmap facts hold, and F-001 makes 13.8 a correctness change: its own 'live equivalence' check at ROADMAP.md:226 cannot pass for shape numbers as wired. Two things are inference rather than measurement: the thermal/battery claim (ROADMAP.md:227 notes no browser thermal API exists) and the priority call itself, which is the owner's. The mechanism is already documented in deliveryRate.ts, so the new content is the reframing, not the discovery.

**Materiality skeptic: downgraded, severity medium.** The mechanism is confirmed (src/main.ts:2983-2993 draws and calls detectForVideo on every accepted rAF tick; src/main.ts:3023-3025 counts the read; src/io/frameLoop.ts:66-79 states the limit) but it is already an accepted, scheduled limit: ROADMAP.md:226 specifies row 13.8 as exactly the proposed change ('rVFC-gated detection', driver-level test, stepped Eyeblink8 digit-for-digit, live A/B equivalence) and ROADMAP.md:40 names it one of the two real levers; ROADMAP.md:222 requires 13.4 (frames-missed counter) to land BEFORE 13.8. Phase 13 has zero ticks while Phase 10 rows 10.1a/10.1b/10.2/10.4/10.7a/10.10a/10.10b landed 5 September (ROADMAP.md:164-177). The thermal/battery claim has no measurement in the record: ROADMAP.md:227 (13.9) exists precisely because no browser thermal API exists. The 45% re-read share on the iPhone 17 follows from 55/30 (docs/validation-dry-run.txt:60,213).

_Note._ Not a defect and not news: the repo already documents the mechanism and has the right row with the right checks. What survives is a sequencing argument, and it is real in two places: 12.8 (reopening velocity, ROADMAP.md:203) and the live per-device rows 11.6/11.7 (ROADMAP.md:188-189) would be measured on the rAF driver and inherit F-001's artefact, so 13.4 then 13.8 should precede them. The recommendation to move 13.8 'ahead of Phase 11/12 signal rows' is proportionate only if it keeps 13.4 first (the roadmap's own before/after rule) and keeps the rAF fallback plus a recorded driver in the export. 'Corrupts a published column' is F-001's claim counted twice; the phone-throttling impact is unmeasured until 13.9. Medium: a priority correction to an already-planned instrument row.

#### F-003. The 25 fps refusal judges the processing rate, not the evidence rate; the report can say blink numbers were withheld while printing them

**Claim.** A camera delivering 15-24 distinct frames behind a 60 Hz display passes the gate: blink count, rate, duration, PERCLOS and long closures are computed and exported at full confidence with a body-text warning, and the report then asserts they were withheld. The headline honesty rule is enforced on the wrong number and the tests pin the sentence, not the wiring.

**Impact.** Exactly the phones and dim-room webcams the era targets; the report tells participants and the Python verdict a false fact about the instrument's own behaviour.

**Fix as proposed.** Run one dim-room session (no code) so the pre-registered rule can fire; then gate on min(sampledFps, fps) where delivery is reported, with 60/65-style hysteresis, at main.ts:3559/3693/3758; add a verdict/report fixture with sampledFps 20 and processingFps 60 whose measured rows and verdict agree; re-run the stepped corpus to show it is unchanged.

**Evidence as filed.** blinkMeasurable = measurableAtFps(fps) where fps is the 2 s rAF processing rate; the same flag gates long closure and PERCLOS; evidenceFps (sampledFps) feeds only the warning. The report's verdict is built from sampledFps and prints 'temporal blink numbers were withheld rather than guessed' while its measured rows check only baseline refusal, so 'Blinks detected: N' prints beside it; the sentence is byte-pinned into Python. fpsGate.ts:24-27 admits stage two is held; the pre-decision to move the gate waits on a dim-room observation nobody has sought (blink-sample-rate.txt:333-336 names auto-exposure halving delivery).

**Reproduce skeptic: downgraded, severity medium.** src/main.ts:2943-2945 computes fps from processFrame call timestamps (processing rate); src/main.ts:3559 blinkMeasurable = measurableAtFps(fps); the same flag gates long closure at :3693 and PERCLOS at :3758; src/main.ts:2970-2978 evidenceFps feeds only rateRiskShown. Report: src/main.ts:2420 hands the verdict sampledFps; src/main.ts:2480-2509 measured rows are gated only on calibration refusal. Reproduced with assessSession (sampledFps 20, processingFps 60): headline 'refused', sentence 'The evidence rate was 20.0 frames per second (the measured rate of distinct frames read), below the 25 ... so temporal blink numbers were withheld rather than guessed.' while main.ts:2482-2483 would print 'Blinks detected: N'. analysis/blinklab/verdict.py:216-223 carries the same sentence. Fixtures cover only 60/60, null/30 and refused (test/core/sessionVerdictFixture.test.ts:47-48, 86-87).

_Note._ The gate-on-processing-rate half is a documented, deliberately held limit: MODEL_CARD.md:92 says in bold that a slow camera behind a fast display would not be caught and that the true camera rate is 'deliberately still not wired into the gate'; src/core/fpsGate.ts:24-27 and docs/blink-sample-rate.txt:436-444 pre-register the trigger for moving it. Every delivered rate measured so far is 30 (docs/blink-sample-rate.txt:599-603, 635-636), so the report contradiction has never fired on a real session. What is new and real: a latent verdict-vs-measured-rows contradiction in the participant report and a missing fixture for the sampledFps<25, processing>=25 shape. Latent plus documented-limit is medium, not high.

**Materiality skeptic: downgraded, severity medium.** Gate wiring confirmed: src/main.ts:2943-2945 builds fps from per-tick processFrame timestamps; src/main.ts:3559 blinkMeasurable = measurableAtFps(fps) gates the reducer (3569), long closures (3693) and PERCLOS (3758); evidenceFps (delivery?.sampledFps ?? fps, src/main.ts:2970) feeds only the warning. But this is a documented, pre-registered accepted limit: MODEL_CARD.md:92 states the gate reads the processing rate and why the camera rate is 'deliberately still not wired'; docs/blink-sample-rate.txt:436-444 commits the move rule (gate moves only when a device is measured delivering below 25 while processing above it); src/core/fpsGate.ts:24-27 names stage two as held; ROADMAP.md:226 makes 'an owner decision on gate/warning input quantities' row zero of 13.8. The report contradiction is real and not documented: src/core/sessionVerdict.ts:103-123 builds the evidenceRate surface from sampledFps and prints 'temporal blink numbers were withheld rather than guessed', while src/main.ts:2474-2510 withholds measured rows only on calibration refusal, so 'Blinks detected: N' and a rate print beside it; analysis/blinklab/verdict.py:218-224 reproduces the sentence from the file. Fixtures cover sampledFps 22 for the verdict object only (test/core/sessionVerdict.test.ts:96) and the report fixture uses sampledFps null/processing 30 (test/core/sessionVerdictFixture.test.ts:86-87); no fixture pins report-versus-rows agreement. The trigger (delivery below 25 behind faster processing) has not occurred in any of the 13 recorded sessions (docs/blink-sample-rate.txt:599-603, docs/validation-round.txt:53-58).

_Note._ The gate-quantity half collides with an accepted limit with a pre-registered move rule and is not a finding; the finding itself concedes the observation must come first. The report half is a genuine latent honesty defect: in the dim-room case the participant report and the Python re-derivation would assert a refusal the page did not make. It changes no published number today and its trigger is unobserved, so medium, not high. Proportionate fix: a report/verdict fixture with sampledFps 20 and processingFps 60 whose section 2 and section 3 agree (either the measured rows consult the same surface, or the sentence states what was actually withheld), plus the one dim-room session the pre-decision already asks for. Moving the gate to min(sampledFps, fps) before that observation would break the repo's own rule (blink-sample-rate.txt:442-444) and refuse sessions that succeed today.

#### F-004. blinkRatePerMin divides by elapsed time, not observed time, diluting the rate after face loss, gate refusal or the learning period

|                             |                                                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **medium**                                                                                                                                          |
| Category                    | defect                                                                                                                                              |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                                                                   |
| Raised by                   | core-numeric, blink-closure                                                                                                                         |
| Files                       | `src/core/blinkRate.ts:41-51`, `src/core/blinkRate.ts:56-65`, `src/main.ts:3590`, `analysis/blinklab/rldd.py:212`, `analysis/blinklab/drozy.py:229` |

**Claim.** Any gap in trusted frames within the last minute lowers the rate in proportion, silently; the comment's 'time actually observed' is not what is measured.

**Impact.** A wrong number in a published column windowed into the UTA-RLDD feature set and DROZY rate row and shown live: missed blinks reading as calm.

**Fix as proposed.** Accumulate observed time only on frames the reducer was fed an aperture, window it like blink times, null below BLINK_RATE_MIN_OBSERVATION_MS of observed time; export the observed fraction beside the rate.

**Evidence as filed.** observedMs = min(now - startedAtMs, 60000); startRate is called on the first processed frame before any line exists; frames fed null (no face, pose refusal, fps<25, refusal) count no blink but count as observed. Reproduced: four blinks in 20 s then 40 s unfed reads 4.0/min against a true 12. The fps gate applies only at read time to the current frame.

**Reproduce skeptic: downgraded, severity medium.** src/core/blinkRate.ts:45-50: observedMs = min(nowMs - startedAtMs, 60000), recent.length*60000/observedMs. src/main.ts:3590 rateState ??= startRate(nowMs) on the first processed frame, face or no face; rateState is reset only in resetSession (src/main.ts:955). Reproduced with the repo's startRate/recordBlink/blinkRatePerMin: blinks at 5/10/15/20 s read 12/min at 20 s and 4/min at 60 s with nothing fed in between. Consumer: analysis/blinklab/rldd.py:211-213 medians the exported blinkRatePerMin column. Live label: src/main.ts:3658-3667.

_Note._ The mechanism is real, but two of the finding's specifics are wrong. (1) DROZY is not a consumer: analysis/blinklab/drozy.py:218-222 computes the rate from the blink-log event count over the window's real length 'rather than from the app's rolling estimate'. (2) The learning period is not a gap: while learning, calibrationRefused is false, so the reducer is fed against the 4 mm fallback (src/main.ts:3569-3572) and blinks are counted; a refused session withholds the rate entirely (src/main.ts:3825-3827). Real dilution sources are no-face/pose-refused frames, sub-25 fps spans once fps recovers, and time before the face is first found.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity high.** src/core/blinkRate.ts:41-51: observedMs = min(nowMs - startedAtMs, 60000); recordBlink (:20-39) is the only input, so frames the reducer was fed null (no face, pose gate at src/main.ts:3081-3089, fps<25 or refusal at src/main.ts:3569-3571) count as observed time with no blink. rateState starts on the first processed frame (src/main.ts:3590) and the gate applies only at read time (blinkRate.ts:56-65). The comment at blinkRate.ts:8-10 and LEARNING.md:289 both claim 'the time actually observed', which is not what is computed. The column is published: blinkRatePerMin is medianed over seconds 60-360 per RLDD video (analysis/blinklab/rldd.py:212), and docs/uta-rldd-result.txt:106-110 names 'blink duration and rate' among the features the published detection leans on; DROZY's rate (analysis/blinklab/drozy.py:226-229) is count over len(rows), the same elapsed-time denominator computed independently. Nothing in docs accepts this limit. Recovery is possible from existing files: pose_valid_fraction and face_detected_fraction are exported (src/core/sessionMetadata.ts:268,334).

_Note._ Squarely against null-never-zero: unobserved seconds are counted as observed-with-no-blink, and in UTA-RLDD the null-fed frames (nodding past the 20 degree pitch limit, face loss) are label-correlated, so the dilution biases a published feature in a direction correlated with the class. Two corrections: the learning period does NOT dilute (the reducer is fed during learning, against the 4 mm line, main.ts:3569-3572), and the magnitude on the RLDD result is unmeasured here — it should be bounded from the exported pose/face fractions before any claim. The S-sized core fix is proportionate; it must keep the 15 s observation floor (constants.ts:141) and route any RLDD re-derivation through the 12.18 single v2 read (ROADMAP.md:39,213) rather than a per-feature dip, and note blinkRate.ts changes a published column so the detector ratchet/uncertainty caveat applies.

#### F-010. Gaze calibration solver has no goodness-of-fit refusal; a garbage axis is stored and labelled '(calibrated)'

|                             |                                                                                                                                                                           |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **medium**                                                                                                                                                                |
| Category                    | defect                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Raised by                   | gaze                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Files                       | `src/core/calibrationProfile.ts:36-59`, `src/core/calibrationProfile.ts:87-92`, `src/main.ts:3410-3419`, `src/main.ts:2152-2156`, `src/core/guidedCalibration.ts:101-106` |

**Claim.** A fit that explains nothing on one axis is accepted with the same confidence as a good one and drives the quadrant, heatmap and scanpath; nothing records fit quality.

**Impact.** The one place gaze claims to be personal and trustworthy is a label, not a measurement, violating the refuse-rather-than-guess rule the blink calibration honours.

**Fix as proposed.** Compute per-axis RMS residual and R^2 on the dot medians; refuse above a pre-stated bound (e.g. RMS > 0.15 or R^2 < 0.8); carry the residual in the profile, button label and export header; pin with the noise-only-axis case.

**Evidence as filed.** fitLine refuses only spread <= 0; no residual is computed. Reproduced: nine targets with a vertical axis of pure jitter (0.03 +/-0.003) solve to slope 493.2, RMS residual 0.239 screen fractions, so an offset of 0.02 maps to y = -4.43 and 0.04 to y = 5.43; the profile is stored and shown as '(calibrated)'. The blink calibration in the same codebase refuses when its phases do not separate.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity high.** src/core/calibrationProfile.ts:36-59 fitLine refuses only when spread<=0 (line 54) and computes no residual; 87-92 is all-or-nothing on null only. main.ts:3410-3419 stores any non-null solve; 2152-2156 labels output '(calibrated)'. guidedCalibration.ts:101-106 refuses the blink calibration on insufficient separation. test/core/calibrationProfile.test.ts:107-122 only tests exactly identical offsets (spread 0). Reproduced with the real solver under vitest: nine targets, clean horizontal axis, vertical samples 0.03±0.003 jitter → solveCalibration returns a profile with vertical slope -118.7, intercept 4.04, RMS residual 0.325 screen fractions on the dot medians; offsets 0.027/0.030/0.033 map to y=0.83/0.48/0.12.

_Note._ The finding's specific digits (slope 493.2, RMS 0.239, y=-4.43/5.43) depend on its own jitter draw; mine differ but the mechanism reproduces exactly: any nonzero jitter defeats the only refusal and the garbage axis is stored and labelled calibrated.

**Materiality skeptic: downgraded, severity medium.** calibrationProfile.ts:36-59: fitLine refuses only spread <= 0, computes no residual; :87-92 all-or-nothing on null only. main.ts:3410-3420 stores any non-null solve; :2152-2156 labels it '(calibrated)'. The profile's consumers are display-only: the quadrant label (:2145-2157) and the heatmap/scanpath accumulator (:3380-3390). The exported columns do not read it: onScreen is the raw isOnScreen(meanOffset) at :3220, and the fixation reducer consumes smoothedGaze.smoothed at :3330-3345. MODEL_CARD.md:36-38 already states everything but blink detection is externally unverified.

_Note._ The mechanism is real and the contrast with resolveGuidedCalibration's separation refusal (guidedCalibration.ts:101-106) is fair, but the finding's impact overreaches: no exported column, no published number and no analysis path inherits a bad axis; the blast radius is a trust label and a demo heatmap. Worth the S fix before 14.9 builds a validation on top of the profile, so medium: a design gap against refuse-rather-than-guess, not a high defect.

| Category                    | missing-capability                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

| Files                       | `src/core/calibrationProfile.ts:18-21`, `src/io/calibrationStore.ts:163-170`, `src/core/calibrationCapture.ts:17-28`, `src/main.ts:1627`, `src/main.ts:1643-1647`, `src/core/validityGate.ts:31`, `src/core/constants.ts:26-28`, `src/core/constants.ts:196-203`, `SPEC.md:136`, `test/MANUAL.md:38` |

**Claim.** Calibrated gaze is silently valid across head movements and setup changes that shift the mapped point by a quarter to half a screen, with no record of the geometry it was solved under, so drift (14.9) cannot be separated from movement.

**Impact.** Every calibrated output, the heatmap, scanpath and exported onScreen/fixation columns inherit an error the instrument cannot see or declare.

**Fix as proposed.** Store median pose, median iris width px, innerWidth/Height, devicePixelRatio, screen size and camera with the profile; null the calibrated point with 'head moved since calibration' beyond ~5 degrees or ~10% iris width; refuse or flag 'calibrated for a different window/camera' on load; 14.9 must log the pose delta beside every error sample; say 'window' not 'screen' in copy.

**Evidence as filed.** The profile is four numbers; POSE_LIMITS are justified by landmark foreshortening, not gaze. Eye-in-head angle changes one-for-one with head yaw; at ~0.007 units/degree and slope 4, 5 degrees of yaw moves the calibrated point ~0.14 screen widths, 10 degrees ~0.28, while the gate says valid; head translation is unmeasured. Targets are viewport fractions on an inset-0 overlay, so dot positions depend on window size and monitor; the profile is loaded at startup and 'works from the first frame' after any resize, monitor or camera change.

**Reproduce skeptic: downgraded, severity medium.** Code facts hold: profile is four numbers (calibrationProfile.ts:18-21); saveCalibrationProfile writes only the profile JSON (io/calibrationStore.ts:163-171); targets are viewport fractions (calibrationCapture.ts:18-28) on an inset-0 fixed overlay (main.ts:1643-1649); the profile is loaded at startup with no context check (main.ts:1627) and MANUAL item 34 (test/MANUAL.md:38) celebrates 'calibrated from the first frame' after reload; POSE_LIMITS 20/25/25 are justified by landmark foreshortening (constants.ts:196-203) and validityGate.ts:31 is a bare abs>limit; gazeOffset.ts:15-56 has no pose compensation; only 'resize' handler is sizeGraphsToBox (main.ts:941). SPEC.md:136 and ROADMAP.md:10 state the head-still assumption and scope gaze to 'reliable quadrant classification… not a precise gaze point'.

_Note._ Real gap, but the magnitude is asserted, not measured: '~0.007 units/degree', 'slope 4', '10x too loose' and 'quarter to half a screen' appear nowhere in the repo (grep for per-degree figures finds nothing); they are anatomical back-of-envelope estimates. The repo already declares the head-still assumption and labels gaze unvalidated/quadrant-level, and 14.9 (ROADMAP.md:244) is the planned drift measurement, so this is a missing capability against an aspiration rather than a broken stated contract. The requested context fields are a sound enhancement; 'high' overstates it for a demo-tier, explicitly unvalidated feature.

**Materiality skeptic: downgraded, severity medium.** calibrationProfile.ts:18-21: four numbers, no context; calibrationCapture.ts:17-28 targets in viewport fractions on an inset-0 overlay (main.ts:1643-1647); main.ts:1627 loads the profile at startup with no check; POSE_LIMITS 20/25/25 (constants.ts:196-203) are justified by landmark foreshortening. SPEC.md:136 already documents 'Gaze features assume the head stays reasonably still' and names the pose gate, so the head-still limit is a stated assumption, not news. As with F-010, the profile feeds only the quadrant label and heatmap/scanpath (main.ts:2152-2156, :3380-3390); the exported onScreen and fixation columns read the raw or smoothed offset (:3220, :3330-3345), so the claim that exported columns inherit the error is wrong. ROADMAP.md:244 (14.9) is unticked and its check list names no pose-delta logging.

_Note._ Half of this collides with an accepted assumption (SPEC.md:136); the other half, no stored geometry, no invalidation on window/camera change, and 14.9 unable to separate drift from movement, is a real missing capability with display-only reach today. Right treatment is medium: fold the stored-context fields and the pose-delta column into 14.9's check list and say 'window' not 'screen', rather than treating it as a high defect in an unvalidated demo feature.

#### F-013. Alertness Bar 2 tests a joint-noise null, not model-vs-heuristic; 'about as good as a fitted one' is unsupported

|                             |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **medium**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Category                    | science                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Raised by                   | statistics                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Files                       | `analysis/blinklab/alertness.py:401-413`, `analysis/blinklab/alertness.py:304-312`, `docs/alertness-score-plan.md:108-112`, `docs/alertness-score-result.txt:20-23`, `docs/alertness-score-result.txt:66-75`, `docs/alertness-score-result.txt:94-95` |

**Claim.** Bar 2 compares against the distribution when neither score carries signal, a null Bar 1 already rejected; at n=95 it can only clear for ~0.14 AUC, yet the result reads p 0.099 as 'not distinguishable from chance' and 'about as good'.

**Impact.** The build-vs-keep decision for a learned score rests on absence of evidence from a mis-specified, underpowered test written up as equivalence; the true edge could be anywhere from slightly negative to +0.2.

**Fix as proposed.** Keep the pre-registered verdict; add a subject-level paired bootstrap or DeLong test with a CI beside p 0.099; replace 'not distinguishable' and 'about as good' with 'no evidence either way; detectable edge ~0.14 at this n'; pre-register before re-reading.

**Evidence as filed.** null_diff = model_shuf - heur_shuf where both are computed on shuffled labels; observed diff +0.083, null 97.5th +0.141, null mean -0.052, p 0.099. Hanley-McNeil SEs (0.054, 0.048) give even an unpaired 95% CI of about [-0.06, +0.22]; the shuffled-difference null (sd ~0.10) is roughly twice as wide as the paired real-label distribution, so the bar demands an edge of ~0.14 AUC. The plan assumed the null centres on 0; it centred at -0.052.

**Reproduce skeptic: downgraded, severity medium.** analysis/blinklab/alertness.py:401-413: one rng.permutation(y) per shuffle feeds BOTH null_heuristic[i] = auc(heuristic, shuffled) and null_diff[i] = model_shuf - heur_shuf with the model refit LOSO on the same shuffled labels — a joint no-signal null. :304-312 Bar 2 = diff > diff_null_975 and diff_p < 0.025. docs/alertness-score-plan.md:111-112 assumed 'both AUCs fall to ≈0.5 and the difference centres on 0'; docs/alertness-score-result.txt:67-68 records mean -0.052, 97.5th +0.141, p 0.0989; :22-23 'not distinguishable from chance'; :94-95 'about as good as a fitted one here' (only occurrence repo-wide). node -e Hanley-McNeil (n_drowsy 45, n_alert 50): SE 0.0540 at AUC 0.701, 0.0478 at 0.784; unpaired 95% CI on +0.083 = [-0.058, +0.224]; null sd implied by mean/97.5th = 0.098 vs unpaired paired-less SE 0.072. UTA-RLDD feature CSVs are not in the repo (only Eyeblink8 evidence .seconds.csv under docs/evidence), so the run itself cannot be repeated here; every quoted number is internally consistent.

_Note._ The mechanism and every number check out, but the finding omits that the equivalence reading was itself pre-registered (plan.md:157-159: 'if it does not [survive], the honest conclusion is that the explainable hand-tuned score is as good as the learned one here'), so the write-up scored the plan rather than spinning after the fact; the decision it feeds is the conservative one (keep the heuristic, src/core untouched); and the public README sentence (README.md:48, 527-535) carries only the AUC 0.70 / p 0.001 claim, not the equivalence. The unsupported 'about as good' lives in one line of the result file. Real statistical mis-specification and overreach, medium consequence.

**Materiality skeptic: downgraded, severity medium.** analysis/blinklab/alertness.py:401-413: null_diff[i] = model_shuf - heur_shuf, both AUCs computed against the same shuffled labels; :304-312 Bar 2 requires diff > diff_null_975 and diff_p < 0.025. docs/alertness-score-plan.md:108-112 pre-registered exactly this null and assumed 'the difference centres on 0'; docs/alertness-score-result.txt:67 records shuffled mean -0.052, 97.5th +0.141, p 0.0989, observed +0.083. Hanley-McNeil SEs recomputed from n=50/45: 0.053 (AUC 0.701) and 0.047 (AUC 0.784); unpaired 95% CI on the difference about [-0.06, +0.22]; the shuffle null's implied sd about 0.10, so Bar 2 needs roughly +0.14 AUC at this n. Wording 'not distinguishable from chance' (:23) and 'about as good as a fitted one' (:95) exist ONLY in the result file: grep of README.md, MODEL_CARD.md, docs/_.md, docs/_.txt finds no propagation; README:48 and tools/resultsBlock.mjs:236 say only 'above chance (AUC 0.70)'. No CI/bootstrap/DeLong code exists (grep of alertness.py and compare_alertness.py empty). The result file itself hedges at :101-102 ('is not "nothing could"').

_Note._ Mechanism is real and the finding's arithmetic checks out: the Bar 2 null is a joint-noise null that Bar 1 already rejected, it is roughly twice as wide as a paired real-label comparison would be, and the plan's own premise (null centred on 0) failed and was narrated rather than flagged. But materiality is limited: no published number is wrong, the verdict reached is the conservative default, adoption of a learned score was pre-declared a separate gated increment (plan :187-190) so the practical build-vs-keep impact is small, and the equivalence overclaim is two sentences confined to one result file. What keeps it above low: the pre-registered 'what would count as this being wrong' clause (result :110-117) inherits the mis-specified null, so any re-run under the same design is near-unreachable at this n and the reversal promise is hollow until the test is respecified. The proposed fix (keep the scored verdict, add a paired CI beside p 0.099, reword to 'no evidence either way; detectable edge ~0.14 at this n', pre-register before re-reading) is proportionate and preserves the predict-then-verify strength.

**Impact.** The exported file is the fact's home; a file naming the wrong source is worse than none.

**Fix as proposed.** Branch first in the catch: if framesMeasured > 0 set measurementFailed leaving frameSource/loadedClipName/measurementMode untouched; extract the decision into core; e2e injecting a throw during a stepped clip asserting '# source: file' and the clip name.
