**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity high.** src/main.ts:1465-1490 shared catch: :1470 frameSource = 'camera', :1474 loadedClipName = null, THEN :1485-1488 if framesMeasured > 0 → measurementFailed; measurementMode ('stepped', set :1244) is never reset. Stepped throws do reach it: the inner try at :1282-1314 has only a finally (clearInterval), so a processFrame throw inside the stepThroughVideo callback propagates to the outer try opened at :1180 — the code's own comment :1479-1484 says so. Export :2341-2359 then writes sourceMetadataRows('camera', null) → '# source: camera', '# clip: none' (frameClock.ts:213-221); coverageMetadataRows(measurementMode) → '# measurement_mode: stepped' (frameClock.ts:174-179); deviceMetadataRows(null) → '# camera: none, not a camera session' (sessionMetadata.ts:121-125; deviceInfo is set only at :1119 in beginCamera and cleared at :1013); deliveryMetadataRows(settledDeliveryRates()) → :590-596 now passes the frameSource check and deliveryRate.ts:126-151 always returns an object, so the three rows sessionMetadata.ts:153-160 says a clip must never carry appear as 'unknown'. Report :2513-2519: frameSource !== 'file' and deviceInfo null → 'unknown'. Exports stay enabled in measurementFailed (:909).

_Note._ Not executed in a browser; the chain is unconditional once the catch is entered with framesMeasured > 0.

**Materiality skeptic: downgraded, severity medium.** src/main.ts:1465-1491 shared catch: :1470 frameSource = 'camera' and :1474 loadedClipName = null run BEFORE the framesMeasured > 0 branch at :1485-1488 sets measurementFailed. measurementMode is only reset at :1087 (beginCamera) so it stays 'stepped'. deviceInfo is nulled in resetSession :1013 and set only on the camera path :1119, so deviceMetadataRows :121-125 writes 'camera: none, not a camera session'. settledDeliveryRates :590-596 now returns rates because frameSource reads 'camera', so deliveryMetadataRows :168-186 writes three rows the module says are null for a clip. sourceMetadataRows :213-222 writes '# source: camera' and '# clip: none'; export assembly :2341-2359. Report Camera line :2513-2519 reads 'unknown'. stepThroughVideo is awaited inside the try at :1283, so its throw lands in this catch. tools/measure_corpus.mjs:159-160 waits only on clipFailed/modelFailed, so a batch run never reaches the export on this path.

_Note._ Mechanism confirmed exactly as described and the fix (branch on framesMeasured first, leave provenance untouched) is correct and small. Downgraded because of reach: it needs a mid-run throw during a STEPPED clip; the corpus runner does not recognise measurementFailed on the clip path and would stall rather than write the file (a gap of its own), so the mis-labelled file reaches only a manual user; and the file's rows contradict each other visibly (source camera + measurement_mode stepped + camera none) rather than forming a plausible wrong record. No published number is touched. Worth fixing in the same PR as the measurementFailed e2e for clips, and measure_corpus.mjs should learn the state too.

But the substantive claim REMEDIATION.md makes — that these constants are pinned — is TRUE, verified by me one mutation at a time: nothing is naked behind the dead gate, so no number, no refusal and no published claim is at risk today. Two pieces of the finding's evidence are wrong and should not be carried forward: the header count is already derived from the array (`All ${String(MUTATIONS.length)} mutations caught.`, tools/mutationCheck.mjs:226) and the '18' at :165 is a comment recounting a past review episode, not a live claim; so 'derive the header count from the array' is already done. The 'six survivors in five minutes' belongs to F-018's constants (not in this list), not to the unexecuted tail. Fix proportionality: 'run it in CI' is disproportionate — 23 x 28 s is about 11 minutes of CI per PR for a check that found nothing. The cheap, proportionate version is a sub-second unit test asserting every MUTATIONS `find` string is still present in its file (that alone would have gone red on 20 August), keeping the full bend-and-run local. 'Run only the test file it expects to redden' is a reasonable speed-up but narrows the check: a mutation that reddens a different file would be reported as SURVIVED, so each entry must then name its file correctly or the tool gains false alarms.

The repo's own newer record disagrees: docs/iris-occlusion.txt:120-129 'The ~49 shallow-aperture misses are a recall CEILING, not a tunable defect ... Route A is closed'; MODEL_CARD.md:141-155 'An awake per-frame trace and a mechanism autopsy now explain why'; ROADMAP.md:35 makes the ceiling the basis for retiring Eyeblink8 to a regression harness. README.md:351-354 is a verbatim duplicate of :340-343 ('These are not faint or borderline blinks ... Finding out why is the next question.') — a real editing defect. resultsBlock.mjs:233's bold 'That table is a property of the machine it was measured on' is indeed overturned later in the same bullet ('So the number above is a measured property of the instrument and the prepared files on two machines').

_Note._ Downgraded from high to medium, and one sub-claim refuted. What is real: two surfaces (the README and the participant report handed to volunteers) say the biggest accuracy limitation is unexplained while three other documents call it a measured ceiling, and that misdirects exactly the priority question the era's ladder turns on. What limits severity: no published number moves; the error runs in the humble direction (understating what is known, not overstating capability), which is outside the stated purpose of the pin mechanism ('rather than letting a report overstate what the instrument can do', src/core/cannotSee.ts:6-8); MODEL_CARD, the document the project points limitations-readers to, is correct; and claim 1 does not misquote its cited sources — docs/miss-character.txt:7 still says 'nobody has explained it yet' and the pin faithfully reflects it. The real structural gap is narrower than the finding states: a pin cannot see a NEWER document that answers the question its source left open. REFUTED sub-claim: 'resultsBlock.mjs:236 is superseded by the min(delivery, processing) correction'. STATE.md:2419-2455 records that two-rates work as a committed prediction with 'NOTHING IS CORRECTED YET' and 'NOTHING IS RETRACTED ... the evidence fits both models', with the four dry-run devices still unread; validation-dry-run.txt:118-124 still supports the published sentence. Rewording it now would break the predict-then-measure discipline, which is a strength. Also trim the fix: delete-the-sentence at :233 would erase the record of the discovery; reword it to lead with what the 26 August re-measure settled. The valuable half of the fix is the generator grep for unpinned sentence literals plus re-deriving claim 1 from docs/iris-occlusion.txt.

#### F-022. SECURITY.md sends reporters to a private-reporting channel that is switched off

|                             |                                        |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **medium**                             |
| Category                    | overclaim                              |
| Effort                      | S                                      |
| Raised by                   | security-privacy                       |
| Files                       | `SECURITY.md:18-23`, `src/main.ts:414` |

**Claim.** The only path the policy offers does not exist and the fallback is forbidden.

**Impact.** A real finding goes unreported or lands in a public issue; for a repo whose privacy claim is 'checkable by anyone' this is the first thing an outside checker meets.

**Fix as proposed.** Enable private vulnerability reporting and re-verify, or rewrite :18-23 to the mailto already on the page; record the verification date as dependabot.yml does.

**Evidence as filed.** SECURITY.md:18-21 directs to GitHub's Security tab 'Report a vulnerability' and :23 forbids public issues; GET /repos/heshipstech/blinklab/private-vulnerability-reporting returns enabled: false. Last touched 2026-08-14.

**Reproduce skeptic: downgraded, severity medium.** SECURITY.md:19-21 'Open a **private** vulnerability report through GitHub: the Security tab -> "Report a vulnerability"' and SECURITY.md:23 'Please do not open a public issue for anything exploitable.' `curl -sS https://api.github.com/repos/heshipstech/blinklab/private-vulnerability-reporting` -> HTTP 200, `{"enabled": false}` (git remote confirms origin is heshipstech/blinklab). `git grep -n mailto|email SECURITY.md` returns nothing across its 53 lines, so the file offers no fallback; the maintainer mailto lives at src/main.ts:414 and is not referenced from the policy. git log: SECURITY.md last touched e186692 (2026-08-14).

_Note._ The factual core is exactly as stated and I verified it against the live API rather than the finding's assertion. Downgraded on impact, not on truth. The blast radius is small: the deployed artefact is static files with no server, no account, no database and no endpoint to upload to (SECURITY.md:11-15), the maintainer's address is one click away on the page itself (src/main.ts:411-416) and throughout git history, and the failure mode is a report arriving by a route the policy did not name rather than an exploitable defect. 'The first thing an outside checker meets' is rhetoric — an outside checker of the privacy claim reads the code, not the reporting section. Real, trivially fixable, medium.

**Materiality skeptic: downgraded, severity medium.** Confirmed live: `curl https://api.github.com/repos/heshipstech/blinklab/private-vulnerability-reporting` returns {"enabled": false} (the repo itself returns 200, so this is the real setting, not an auth artefact). SECURITY.md:19-20 sends reporters to 'the Security tab -> "Report a vulnerability"' and :23 says 'Please do not open a public issue for anything exploitable.' SECURITY.md carries no email; the only contact anywhere is the mailto on the page itself (src/main.ts:414). Last touched by e186692 (2026-08-14). No document accepts this as a known limit: grep for 'private vulnerability' / 'Security tab' across all Markdown returns only SECURITY.md:19.

_Note._ Downgraded from high to medium. It is a genuine defect and undocumented, and for a project whose privacy claim is 'checkable by anyone' a broken front door to the checkers is worth fixing — the fix is one repository toggle or one sentence. But the harm is bounded and does not touch the audit's spine: no published number moves, no reader is misled about a measurement, there is no server, no account and no user data to breach, and a reporter who finds no button has an obvious discoverable fallback (the maintainer's email is on the page and on every commit). Severity high overstates it next to the false published-number and privacy statements in this batch. The fix as proposed is proportionate; the better half of it is the second clause — record the verification date the way dependabot.yml does, so a setting that silently flips is visible next time.

| Raised by                   | security-privacy, process-docs, demo-ux                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Files                       | `src/core/notice.ts:19-24`, `README.md:7`, `README.md:591`, `MODEL_CARD.md:16-17`, `MODEL_CARD.md:319-324`, `PROJECT.md:28`, `CONTRIBUTING.md:19-23`, `docs/UI.md:108`, `test/core/notice.test.ts:24-25`, `test/e2e/calibration.spec.ts:67`, `tools/claimGuard.mjs:22-35`, `decisions/ADR-0004-model-telemetry.md:106-116` |

Only README:591 says 'Since 5 September 2026 that report no longer leaves your browser'; the telemetry e2e proves nothing reaches the network. claimGuard polices only the retired 'sends nothing' direction.

**Reproduce skeptic: downgraded, severity medium.** src/core/notice.ts:23-24 renders 'The face model this page bundles does send anonymous usage statistics to Google.' The block that makes this false landed at 8745468 (2026-09-05): src/io/telemetryBlock.ts wraps fetch/XHR/sendBeacon, src/main.ts:269,285 installs it before the model, src/core/telemetryPolicy.ts:19 blocks googleapis.com, and test/e2e/telemetryBlock.spec.ts:41 drives a real session past the report point. notice.ts and PROJECT.md were both last touched by 61a4d0e (2026-08-10) and not revisited. Live sites: README.md:7, README.md:591 (the only corrected one, 'Since 5 September 2026 that report no longer leaves your browser'), MODEL_CARD.md:16-17, MODEL_CARD.md:319, PROJECT.md:28 ('which no code here can currently prevent'), CONTRIBUTING.md:19-23, docs/UI.md:108, plus three frozen fixtures (test/fixtures/report/*.txt:5). Pinned by test/core/notice.test.ts:25 and test/e2e/calibration.spec.ts:67. tools/claimGuard.mjs:22-35 lists only the retired denials, so nothing polices this direction. decisions/ADR-0004-model-telemetry.md:106-108 states the library 'still _attempts_ the report; it no longer _completes_ it' and :114-116 that 'the disclosure still names the dependency's attempt' — which the seven sites do not do.

_Note._ Confirmed as fact, downgraded on severity. README.md contradicts itself in one file (line 7 vs line 591), and PROJECT.md:28's 'which no code here can currently prevent' is flatly false about the codebase since 8745468 — that clause is not a direction question. But the error runs the safe way: a visitor is told MORE leaves their browser than does, so no privacy decision is made on a rosier picture than reality, which is what made August's six denials serious. Set beside F-023, where the Privacy section understates storage, this one cannot carry the same weight. The finding's own framing concedes it ('false in the conservative direction'); high overstates it. Fix is still warranted and is a one-sentence variant applied to seven sites plus the two pinning tests.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity high.** src/core/notice.ts:19-24 renders 'The face model this page bundles does send anonymous usage statistics to Google', repeated verbatim at README.md:7 and docs/UI.md:108, and in substance at MODEL_CARD.md:16-17 and :319-322, CONTRIBUTING.md:19-23 and PROJECT.md:28 — the last being flatly false now: 'which no code here can currently prevent'. The block exists and is proven: src/core/telemetryPolicy.ts:19 blocks any googleapis.com host, test/e2e/telemetryBlock.spec.ts:41 drives a live session past the report point, and decisions/ADR-0004-model-telemetry.md:95-104 records that the live test was checked for teeth (red with the guard disabled). Only README.md:591 has been updated. tools/claimGuard.mjs:22-35 polices only the retired denial direction ('the retired telemetry denial', 'the retired data-never-leaves sentence'), so nothing catches the now-false assertion.

_Note._ Confirmed at high. The most-read sentence on the page is false, page and README contradict each other, and notice.ts:5-8 exists precisely to stop the disclaimer becoming 'three different promises'. It errs conservative, but a privacy-conscious visitor or a citing paper acts on it wrongly and the project loses credit for the one thing it actually built. Checked against the accepted limit and it does NOT collide: ADR-0004:113-116 ('Not done') forbids a fresh 'sends nothing' sentence and requires the disclosure to keep naming the dependency's attempt — the proposed wording does exactly that, and the ADR's own prose already draws the distinction ('The library still attempts the report; it no longer completes it'). Two corrections that make the fix cheaper than the finding claims: the pinning tests need no change, because both assert a substring — test/core/notice.test.ts:27 and test/e2e/calibration.spec.ts:67 both check `toContain("usage statistics to Google")`, which survives 'tries to send ... to Google; this page blocks it'; and the length budget holds — DEMO_NOTICE is 318 chars against the 400 cap at test/core/notice.test.ts:35, and the corrected sentence measures 343. Worth adding the positive pin the finding proposes (notice.ts's text quoted verbatim in README and MODEL_CARD), since that is the guard that would have caught this drift and the one claimGuard cannot provide.

#### F-025. 60 fps capture has never been requested; 13.2, the era's own 'real lever', sits ~26 rows behind new-signal work

|                             |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **medium**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Category                    | wrong-priority                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Raised by                   | roadmap, performance                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Files                       | `src/io/camera.ts:28-32`, `ROADMAP.md:40`, `ROADMAP.md:196-213`, `ROADMAP.md:220-221`, `docs/blink-sample-rate.txt:176-178`, `docs/blink-sample-rate.txt:230-237`, `docs/blink-sample-rate.txt:661-666`, `docs/validation-dry-run.txt:53-59`, `docs/validation-dry-run.txt:103-106` |

**Claim.** The single measurement that decides whether live blink accuracy is capped at 30 fps on every owned camera costs one constraint plus getCapabilities().frameRate.max, and is scheduled after 26 rows that do not touch the live capture chain.

**Impact.** Every live-session claim of the era inherits the 30 fps catch loss until 13.2 is known; if no camera negotiates above 30 that is the era's ceiling and should be stated before building 18 signals on it.

**Fix as proposed.** Move 13.2 to the front (before 11.1), then 13.4, then 13.8 (F-002): read capabilities, applyConstraints frameRate ideal 60, record declared max, negotiated rate and resolution change; fold one deliberate dim-room session into it so F-003's pre-decision has its observation.

**Evidence as filed.** Constraints carry no frameRate; browsers negotiate 30 by default and every device declared 30. The project's own model moves catch probability from 0.48 to 0.96 at 60 delivered; dry-run catch at ~30 fps was 7/10 and 9/10 versus 10/10 at 55 and 126.7. 'No camera... observed delivering above it' reads as a platform limit when it is an unsent constraint. 13.2 is row 220, after Phases 11 and 12.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity high.** /home/user/blinklab/src/io/camera.ts:28-32 — the only getUserMedia call constrains `width: {ideal:1920}, height: {ideal:1080}` plus an optional deviceId, and nothing else; no frameRate key. `grep -rn 'frameRate|getCapabilities|applyConstraints' src/ test/` returns exactly one hit in src: /home/user/blinklab/src/io/deviceInfo.ts:56-58, which only READS `settings.frameRate` for the export. No getCapabilities or applyConstraints call exists anywhere in src/ or test/. /home/user/blinklab/docs/validation-dry-run.txt:53-59 — all six dry-run sessions report `declared fps` 30.0 (iphone, iphone17promax, iphone2, macbookair, macbookair2, pcsony). /home/user/blinklab/docs/blink-sample-rate.txt:230-237 — the model table gives catch probability 0.48 at 30 delivered vs 0.96 at 60 delivered for a 3.40 mm minimum. /home/user/blinklab/docs/validation-dry-run.txt:103-106 — iphone2 30.7 fps 7 of 10, macbookair2 29.2 fps 9 of 10, iphone17promax 55.0 fps 10 of 10, pcsony 126.7 fps 10 of 10. /home/user/blinklab/docs/blink-sample-rate.txt:664-666 — 'no camera in this project has yet been observed delivering above it'. /home/user/blinklab/ROADMAP.md:220 is 13.2; I counted the unchecked rows between it and 11.1 (ROADMAP.md:183): 11.1-11.8 = 8 and 12.1-12.18 = 18, exactly 26.

_Note._ Every element of the finding held up on inspection. The '~26 rows' is exact, not approximate. The one nuance worth stating: 55.0 and 126.7 in the dry-run table are PROCESSING fps, not delivered camera rate — but the doc itself uses them that way in the same sentence the finding quotes, and the declared-rate column is 30.0 for all six sessions, so the inference (nothing has been asked for above 30, nothing has delivered above it) stands.

**Materiality skeptic: downgraded, severity medium.** src/io/camera.ts:28-32 passes only width/height ideals plus deviceId — no frameRate key. grep across src/ for getCapabilities|applyConstraints|frameRate returns exactly two hits, both reads: src/io/deviceInfo.ts:56-58 rounding settings.frameRate. So nothing has ever asked a camera for a rate, and no capability has ever been read. The 0.48 -> 0.96 model is real (docs/blink-sample-rate.txt:230-237). ROADMAP.md:220 places 13.2 in Phase 13, after Phase 11 (8 rows) and Phase 12 (18 rows).

_Note._ Mechanism confirmed; severity overstated on three counts. (1) The repo already names this: ROADMAP.md:40 calls 13.2 one of the era's two 'real levers' and 13.3 (ROADMAP.md:221) pre-commits BOTH branches including the empty-set 'platform limit, prediction unscored'. This is a scheduling opinion, not an unknown. (2) The 'unsent constraint reads as a platform limit' charge is weaker than stated: docs/blink-sample-rate.txt:178 says in the file's own words that camera.ts 'requests a resolution and no frame rate at all', and line 665-666 says 'observed delivering', not 'capable of'. (3) The field evidence cited (dry-run 7/10 and 9/10 at ~30 vs 10/10 at 55 and 126.7) is retracted by the repo's own second correction, docs/validation-dry-run.txt:167-186: both phones read ~30 distinct frames, so 'the evidence rate cannot explain why one missed 3 of 10 and the other caught 10 of 10'. Using it as support for the 60 fps lever repeats a mechanism the repo already measured false. The model evidence alone still carries the finding. Row order is also not a schedule — STATE.md:17-20 ends with 'Next: the maintainer's decisions, or Phase 12's instrument rows if the maintainer prefers building over deciding.' The real, non-cosmetic cost is narrower than 'every live-session claim': it is that 11.6, 11.7 and especially 11.8 (a ~3-week longitudinal protocol) are expensive human-cost rows that would be run on a capture chain about to change, and 13.6 frames capability per setup so a 30 fps result stays valid rather than being invalidated. Fix is over-scoped: 13.2 alone is S, but 13.8 carries 'an owner decision on gate/warning input quantities is row zero' plus an Eyeblink8 stepped rerun reproducing F1 digit-for-digit, which is not S; and folding a deliberate dim-room session into 13.2 cuts against the era rule at ROADMAP.md:44 ('instrument rows land before their claim rows') and duplicates 13.3's job. Recommend: move 13.2 alone to the front, keep 13.3 as the separate claim row.

#### F-029. PERCLOS counts blink frames; the literature's PERCLOS is a slow-closure measure that excludes blinks

|                             |                                                                                                                                                          |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **medium**                                                                                                                                               |
| Category                    | overclaim                                                                                                                                                |
| Effort                      | M                                                                                                                                                        |
| Raised by                   | oculometric                                                                                                                                              |
| Files                       | `src/core/perclos.ts:3-7`, `src/core/perclos.ts:83`, `src/core/score.ts:28-34`, `test/MANUAL.md:44`, `MODEL_CARD.md:172-177`, `docs/drozy-result.txt:43` |

**Claim.** The quantity diverges from its literature definition on two axes and only one is documented; at rest it IS blink time and inherits blink-rate variance.

**Impact.** Readers compare the 5-15% ramp and exported values to Dinges' thresholds on the wrong quantity; the 40-point weight rests on a literature that validated a different measure; 12.10 would inherit it.

**Fix as proposed.** Export a blink-excluded share alongside; state 'includes blink time' in perclos.ts, MODEL_CARD and the conditions sentence; carry both variants into 12.10.

**Evidence as filed.** Every sample below 0.4x baseline is closed with no blink exclusion; MANUAL item 40 says the resting 1-3% is 'your blinks added up'; Wierwille/Dinges define PERCLOS as pupil >=80% covered reflecting slow droops. MODEL_CARD discloses only the line change. In DROZY PERCLOS ranked last of seven (rho -0.001).

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** /home/user/blinklab/src/core/perclos.ts:83 `const closed = apertureMm < PERCLOS_CLOSED_FRACTION * baselineMm;` — every sample below the line joins the closed side, with no blink exclusion anywhere in the module. perclos.ts:3-7 frames it as 'the most validated drowsiness proxy in the eye tracking literature'. /home/user/blinklab/src/core/score.ts:28-34 gives it PERCLOS_PENALTY_MAX = 40 with a 0.05-0.15 ramp explicitly anchored to the owner's resting reading. /home/user/blinklab/test/MANUAL.md:44 (item 40) states the resting one to three percent is 'your blinks added up'. /home/user/blinklab/MODEL_CARD.md:172-177 discloses the threshold change only ('PERCLOS uses an adjusted threshold, not the literature's'), never the blink inclusion. /home/user/blinklab/docs/drozy-result.txt:43 'PERCLOS, share of the minute 20 -0.001 0.9990 1.0000' — last of seven features. The literature definition (Wierwille; Dinges & Grace FHWA) is the proportion of time the eyes are >=80% closed, explicitly excluding normal blinks.

_Note._ Confirmed on every cited line. Two mitigations the finding does not mention, which I checked and which cap it at medium rather than higher: README.md:31 and src/core/cannotSee.ts:29 already publish 'not comparable to a PERCLOS figure from another system', so the cross-system comparison the impact worries about is fenced in general terms. What is genuinely undocumented is the SECOND divergence — that at rest the quantity is essentially blink time and inherits blink-rate variance — and the tension between a 40-point weight justified by literature validation and this instrument's own rho of -0.001 on the one labelled corpus is real.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** src/core/perclos.ts:83 'const closed = apertureMm < PERCLOS_CLOSED_FRACTION * baselineMm' — every sample below the line counts, no blink exclusion anywhere in the file (grep 'blink' in perclos.ts returns only comment lines 7, 21, 42, 89). perclos.ts:3-7 calls it 'the most validated drowsiness proxy in the eye tracking literature'; src/core/score.ts:28-33 gives it PERCLOS_PENALTY_MAX = 40 of 100 explicitly on that basis. The project's own measurement disagrees: docs/drozy-result.txt:43 ranks 'PERCLOS, share of the minute' last of seven at rho -0.001, p 0.9990. MODEL_CARD.md:172-177 discloses only the threshold change. The on-page conditions sentence (src/core/samplingBounds.ts:142-149) names the shut line and the landmark noise floor — not blink time. test/MANUAL.md item 40 is the only acknowledgement ('your blinks added up') and it is a test instruction.

_Note._ Confirmed and not covered by the accepted limit, which is scoped only to the shut line vs literature P80 — the blink-inclusion axis is a second, undisclosed divergence, and the finding is right that ROADMAP.md:210 (12.10) fixes only the threshold axis and would inherit this one. Held at medium rather than high because two disclosures already blunt the reader-harm: MODEL_CARD.md:176-177 says outright 'It is not comparable to a PERCLOS figure from another system', which covers the compare-to-Dinges scenario, and the README already labels the score unvalidated (ROADMAP.md amendment 14). What is genuinely un-disclosed is the causal justification: a 40-point weight — the single heaviest input — resting on a literature that validated a blink-excluded measure, while this project's own only test of it put it dead last. That is the part worth fixing, and the fix is proportionate and purely additive: it changes no published number, and the conditions sentence is an already-tested mechanism (samplingBounds.ts:142) that can carry 'includes blink time' at the cost of one clause. One implementation note the M estimate should absorb: perclosStep currently takes only aperture and baseline, so a blink-excluded variant needs blink state threaded into a pure module that today has no notion of events — small, but it is a signature change, not a one-liner.

#### F-030. The 40% shut line is a single-face constant that phones' shut floor sits on; the guided calibration measures a personal floor and it is discarded for PERCLOS and long closures

|                             |                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Severity after verification | **medium**                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Category                    | missing-capability                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Effort                      | M                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Raised by                   | oculometric, blink-closure                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Files                       | `src/core/longClosure.ts:21-35`, `src/core/perclos.ts:11-27`, `src/core/guidedCalibration.ts:115-122`, `src/main.ts:3529`, `src/main.ts:3683-3697`, `src/main.ts:3755-3760`, `docs/validation-dry-run.txt:222-232` |

**Claim.** 'Eyes shut' is defined by one face on one camera; a face whose floor is 0.45 B gets PERCLOS 0 forever (P80 again) while its own measured floor sits unused.

**Impact.** The two heaviest score inputs and strongest RLDD features are not device-comparable and can be wrong in both directions on phones.

**Fix as proposed.** Pre-register a guided shut line (closed + k x (open - closed), k from the noise floor), adopt it when a guided line exists, record shutBaselineMm's source, export floor/baseline per session, and let a guided line lift the PERCLOS/long-closure refusal as it does for blinks.

**Evidence as filed.** 40% is the midpoint between the owner's ~33% floor and 45-50% droop on one camera; iPhone closures sat at 2.79-3.01 mm against a 3.04 mm line (floor ~37-39%). closedMedianMm is stored and both shut consumers take only 0.4 x frozenShutBaselineMm; under a refused passive baseline PERCLOS, long closures and score stay withheld even with a guided line.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** /home/user/blinklab/src/core/longClosure.ts:21-35 — the comment derives 0.4 as 'the measured midpoint between the owner's shut floor (about 33 percent) and their relaxed reading droop (45 to 50 percent)', and line 35 is `export const EYES_SHUT_FRACTION = 0.4;`. /home/user/blinklab/src/core/perclos.ts:11-27 aliases it (`PERCLOS_CLOSED_FRACTION = EYES_SHUT_FRACTION`). Both shut consumers read only the frozen passive baseline: src/main.ts:3693-3697 `longClosureThresholdMm(frozenShutBaselineMm)` and src/main.ts:3755-3760 `perclosStep(..., frozenShutBaselineMm)`; frozenShutBaselineMm is set only at src/main.ts:3683 `if (frozenShutBaselineMm === null && baselineState.kind === 'ready')`, so a refused passive baseline leaves it null forever regardless of a guided line. The guided line is wired only into blinks: src/core/guidedCalibration.ts:144-149 effectiveBlinkLineMm, consumed at src/main.ts:3540 and gated at :3568 `blinkMeasurable && (hasGuidedLine || !calibrationRefused)`. Score is withheld on the passive refusal alone: src/main.ts:3877 `calibrationRefused ? 'Alertness score: withheld, calibration was refused'`, and PERCLOS the same at :3763-3764. closedMedianMm IS stored (src/core/guidedCalibration.ts:115-122; written at src/main.ts:3469-3470) and read nowhere but the status string at src/main.ts:3480. /home/user/blinklab/docs/validation-dry-run.txt:222-232 — 'Every per-second sample in the iPhone 17's closure sat between 2.79 and 3.01 mm against a shut line of 3.04', i.e. a measured floor of ~37-40% of that session's baseline (3.04/0.4 = 7.6 mm), sitting on the constant.

_Note._ Confirmed on all six citations, including the asymmetry that is the sharpest part of the finding: a guided calibration lifts the refusal for blinks but not for PERCLOS, long closures or the score, while the closedMedianMm it measured — the one direct observation of that person's shut floor — is stored and never consulted. The 0.45xB face is hypothetical rather than observed, but the arithmetic is right (a floor at or above 0.4xB yields PERCLOS identically 0 and zero long closures), and the measured iPhone floor at ~37-40% shows how little margin the constant has.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** src/core/longClosure.ts:21-35 states the constant's provenance in its own words: EYES_SHUT_FRACTION = 0.4 is 'the measured midpoint between the owner's shut floor (about 33 percent) and their relaxed reading droop (45 to 50 percent)' — one face, one camera. src/core/perclos.ts:27 aliases it. src/core/guidedCalibration.ts:115-122 resolves and stores closedMedianMm, and StoredBlinkCalibration keeps it. src/main.ts:3683-3686 sets frozenShutBaselineMm from baselineState.baselineMm only; both consumers then read 0.4 x that (main.ts:3694-3697 longClosureThresholdMm, main.ts:3755-3760 perclosStep). Refusal asymmetry confirmed: the blink reducer takes hasGuidedLine || !calibrationRefused (main.ts:3569, 3584) while long closures (3715), PERCLOS (3764), exported blinkRatePerMin (3825) and the score (3877) branch on calibrationRefused alone. The phone failure is on the record: docs/validation-dry-run.txt:221-232, 'Every per-second sample in the iPhone 17's closure sat between 2.79 and 3.01 mm against a shut line of 3.04', over-counting on 3 of 3 phone sessions.

_Note._ Confirmed. Materially this governs 70 of the score's 100 points (PERCLOS 40 + long closures 30, score.ts:31,37-38) with a constant derived from one face, and the repo has already measured it failing in the wrong direction on phones. Held at medium not high because the shut-line convention is a documented accepted limit on one axis, the score is already labelled unvalidated, and ROADMAP.md:187 (11.6) already schedules the long-closure over-count for measurement — this finding's real contribution is narrower and sharper: a personal closed floor is ALREADY measured and stored and is thrown away. One correction to the fix's wording: 'let a guided line lift the PERCLOS/long-closure refusal as it does for blinks' overstates the blink precedent — main.ts:3653 still writes 'Blinks: withheld, calibration was refused' on the label even while the reducer at 3569 keeps counting, so the blink path is itself only half-lifted and that inconsistency should be settled in the same row. Otherwise the fix is proportionate and reuses a proven pattern rather than inventing one: the corpus runner starts each clip with no stored calibration (guidedCalibration.ts:139-142 and docs/blink-line-adoption.txt), so a guided SHUT line is neutral to Eyeblink8 and to the detector ratchet by exactly the construction that already protects the guided BLINK line. Two strengths the implementation must not break: (1) amendment 6's invariant that both shut consumers read ONE aliased frozen line (perclos.ts:27 aliasing longClosure.ts:35) — the new source must be aliased, never forked, or the two watchers can drift again; (2) the frozen-once discipline — a personal shut line must freeze at session start like the baseline, never re-open mid-run. Exporting shutBaselineMm's source and the open/closed medians per session is the honest half and should land first, since it is additive and makes the phone claim re-checkable before any line moves.

#### F-031. Blink counting goes silently dead during a droop below the line or below the re-arm line, and the rate then prints 0/min, not null

|                             |                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **medium**                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Category                    | defect                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Effort                      | M                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Raised by                   | oculometric, blink-closure                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Files                       | `src/core/blink.ts:34-37`, `src/core/blink.ts:91-105`, `src/core/blink.ts:127-129`, `src/core/blinkRate.ts:41-51`, `src/core/constants.ts:193`, `src/core/longClosure.ts:24-27`, `src/main.ts:3658-3667` |

**Claim.** Lid-following-gaze is normal physiology; the literature separates blinks from droops by fast descent, not level. Here the zero is a fabricated calm, the failure the fps gate exists to prevent.

**Impact.** Blink rate (an RLDD feature and score input) reads zero for anyone whose posture crosses their line; nothing distinguishes 'no blinks' from 'counting suspended'.

**Fix as proposed.** Null the rate while closed longer than MAX_BLINK_DURATION_MS or while rearmed is false; surface 'blink counting suspended for N s' and a per-record flag; consider arming on closing velocity; export vertical iris offset so downgaze droop is separable.

**Evidence as filed.** Any aperture below the line is 'closed' and a blink counts only on a reopen crossing, so blinks inside a droop are invisible (the owner's reading posture sat below the line for five seconds awake); re-arm requires >= 1.1 x line, and a resting eye at 4.2 on a 4.0 line yields count 1 for five deep blinks (probe E; reachable below 0.55 B after post-calibration relaxation). The page keeps printing 'Blinks: N' / 'rate: 0/min'.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** Code as described: src/core/blink.ts:91-105 treats every aperture below the line as closed and only mints a count on a reopen crossing (line 122/132); src/core/blink.ts:127-129 re-arms only at >= threshold*1.1. Probe through the compiled real reducers (tsc -> node): rest 4.2 mm on a 4.0 mm line, five deep (1.5 mm) blinks -> count=1, rearmed=false, rate=2.8/min; identical script with rest 4.8 -> count=5, rate=13.9/min. Droop probe (20 s at 3.6 mm with five deep blinks inside) -> count=0, eye=closed, blinkRatePerMin=0 (src/core/blinkRate.ts:41-50 returns 0 once observedMs >= 15 s; gatedBlinkRatePerMin only nulls on fps). src/main.ts:3659-3666 then prints 'Blinks: 0 (rate: 0/min)'. The scenario is the repo's own measurement: src/core/longClosure.ts:24-33 records the owner's relaxed reading droop at 45-50% of baseline, i.e. at or below the 50% blink line (BASELINE_THRESHOLD_FRACTION=0.5, constants.ts:152) and inside the 50-55% re-arm band. During the first 30 s the line is the fixed 4 mm fallback (main.ts:3572).

_Note._ One impact clause is wrong: blink rate is NOT a score input — src/core/score.ts scores PERCLOS, long-closure delta, last blink duration and A/V only (score.ts:31-56, 106-140); blinkRatePerMin is a CSV/RLDD/DROZY feature (csv.ts:17, analysis/blinklab/rldd.py:212). The re-arm cost is disclosed at blink.ts:34-37, but the finding cites that; the undisclosed part — a fabricated 0/min with no suspension flag — holds.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** Reimplemented blinkStep faithfully from src/core/blink.ts:67-142 and ran three probes. Droop probe (baseline 8.0, line 4.0, aperture parked at 3.6 with four deep excursions to 2.0): blinkCount 0, eye 'closed' for 5940 ms continuous. PROBE E (resting 4.2 on a 4.0 line, five deep blinks): count 1, rearmed false. That posture is not hypothetical - ROADMAP.md:13 records the owner's own face: 'naturally low eyelids reading at the bottom of the screen sat below the blink line for five seconds while fully awake', and src/core/longClosure.ts:31-32 prices the reading droop at 45-50% of baseline against a blink line at 50%. The rate then prints a number: src/core/blinkRate.ts:41-51 returns recent.length*60000/observedMs = 0 once observedMs clears BLINK_RATE_MIN_OBSERVATION_MS (constants.ts:141, 15000), and src/main.ts:3658-3667 renders it as 'rate: 0/min' (only null renders 'measuring...'). The same zero is written to the exported dataset at src/main.ts:3825-3827 - directly under the comment at src/main.ts:3823-3824 that reads 'null rather than the zero a never-fed reducer would report: null-never-zero'. The 10.10b on-page conditions line (src/core/samplingBounds.ts:156-162) warns only about the sampling channel ('a quick shallow blink can fall between frames'); it names no droop or re-arm channel, and 'a floor' is vacuous applied to a rate of zero.

_Note._ Confirmed at medium, but the finding is two claims and only one is news. The re-arm suppression half (PROBE E) is a PRE-REGISTERED accepted cost, written before the experiment: src/core/blink.ts:34-37 and docs/blink-rearm.txt ('a lid that hovers inside the 10 percent band above the line has its subsequent blinks suppressed until it rises out... it is a real suppression and it is the trade being made'). Do not re-sell that as a discovery. What is new and material is the droop channel plus the fabricated zero: the counter is definitionally unable to count while the eye sits below the line for longer than MAX_BLINK_DURATION_MS, and both the page and the exported column report calm anyway. That is the repo's own flagship rule broken three lines below where the code recites it. One factual correction: blink rate is NOT a score input. src/core/score.ts:29-56 has exactly four penalties - PERCLOS, long closures, blink duration, A/V - and no rate term, so no score moves. Nor does any published number: DROZY blink rate is rho -0.070, verdict 'no' (docs/drozy-result.txt), and lost blinks only add noise to a null. The real stake is forward-looking - ROADMAP.md:246 (14.11) makes read-vs-rest blink suppression 'the era's honest cognitive state claim' and already demands 'a pre-committed droop refusal bound so suppression-versus-masking is visible'. Uncorrected, that row measures an instrument artifact and calls it cognition. On the fix: nulling the rate while closed beyond MAX_BLINK_DURATION_MS is proportionate and in the house idiom (it is exactly what gatedBlinkRatePerMin already does for the fps gate). The 'consider arming on closing velocity' clause is not an M fix - it changes the arm condition of the most adversarially-reviewed component in the repo (fix #114 depth arming, the killed reopen latch, the re-arm gate; LEARNING.md:447 records twenty-two agents killing the first design three ways). That belongs in its own pre-registered row, not folded in here.

#### F-032. headPose reads MediaPipe's column-major packed matrix as row-major and decomposes the transpose; no real matrix is in any fixture

|                             |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Severity after verification | **medium**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Category                    | defect                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Raised by                   | oculometric, gaze, core-numeric                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Files                       | `src/core/headPose.ts:7-8`, `src/core/headPose.ts:22-36`, `test/core/headPose.test.ts:50-60`, `test/fixtures/syntheticFace.ts:20-22`, `node_modules/@mediapipe/tasks-vision/vision.d.ts:2174-2182`, `src/main.ts:3072-3074`, `test/MANUAL.md:23` |

**Claim.** Displayed signs are inverted and combined poses are mis-split by several degrees; the gate survives because limits are symmetric.

**Impact.** 12.5's per-second pitch medians and nod events and 10.7b/c's pose-derived thresholds would embed the wrong convention; pose_valid_fraction is off at the corners.

**Fix as proposed.** One DEV frame: log the 16 numbers with the head turned (translation at indices 12-14 means column-major); read data[col*4+row], pin a real-recording fixture with a matrix, re-run MANUAL 19 for signs, and use the translation for the gaze distance gate.

**Evidence as filed.** m(row,col)=data[row*4+col] per an unsourced comment; the only test builds its matrix the same way; session-01.json has no matrices. Upstream MatrixDataProtoFromMatrix copies Eigen's column-major buffer and the JS copies packed_data verbatim. Through eulerFromMatrix, true 19/24/0 reads -17.3/-25.2/8.0 (gate refuses a valid pose); 0/24/24 reads a phantom pitch of -9.5. MANUAL 19 checked single axes only, where the transpose just flips sign, and tolerates 'small bleed'.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** src/core/headPose.ts:7-8 asserts row-major with no source; :22 reads data[row*4+col]; the only test builds its matrix the same way (test/core/headPose.test.ts:50-58 asData writes data[r*4+c]), so it cannot see the bug. Upstream chain verified: mediapipe/framework/formats/matrix_data.proto declares 'optional Layout layout = 4 [default = COLUMN_MAJOR]'; matrix.cc MatrixDataProtoFromMatrix clears layout and copies the raw Eigen buffer; tasks/.../face_geometry/libs/geometry_pipeline.cc packs an 'Eigen::Matrix4f pose_transform_mat' (column-major by default); the vendored JS copies packed_data verbatim ('facialTransformationMatrixes.push({rows:...,columns:...,data:lr(t,3,...).slice()})' in node_modules/@mediapipe/tasks-vision/vision_bundle.mjs); the wasm carries '.drishti.MatrixData.Layout:COLUMN_MAJOR'. My probe through the real eulerFromMatrix + poseValidity: true 19/24/0 packed column-major reads p=-17.3 y=-25.2 r=8.0 and the gate REFUSES (yaw 25.2 > 25); true 0/24/24 reads pitch -9.5 (phantom); true 15/15/15 reads -18.0/-11.2/-11.2; single axes only flip sign (10/0/0 -> -10). test/MANUAL.md:23 checks single axes and tolerates 'small bleed'. No fixture carries a matrix: test/fixtures/session-01.json holds only landmarkCountPerFrame/frameCount/frames, and grep for facialTransformationMatrix hits src/main.ts:3072 alone.

_Note._ Fully reproduced, including both quoted numbers. 12.5 is still an unticked ROADMAP row (ROADMAP.md:200), so that half of the impact is prospective; the live harm today is the displayed signs and the corner behaviour of pose_valid_fraction.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** The upstream claim checks out, and I verified it rather than inferring it. mediapipe/framework/formats/matrix.cc: 'void MatrixDataProtoFromMatrix(const Matrix& matrix, MatrixData* matrix_data) { ... matrix_data->clear_layout(); proto_ns::RepeatedField<float>(matrix.data(), matrix.data() + rows*cols).Swap(matrix_data->mutable_packed_data()); }' - it CLEARS layout, so the proto default COLUMN_MAJOR stands, and it copies Eigen's raw buffer, which is column-major. geometry_pipeline.cc calls exactly that on pose_transform_mat. The vendored JS then copies packed_data verbatim with no layout consultation: node_modules/@mediapipe/tasks-vision/vision_bundle.mjs, 'facialTransformationMatrixes.push({rows:Or(t,1)??0??0,columns:Or(t,2)??0??0,data:lr(t,3,Jt,cr()).slice()??[]})'. So data is column-major, and src/core/headPose.ts:22 'const m = (row,col) => data[row*4+col]' decomposes the transpose. Reproduced the finding's numbers exactly: true 19/24/0 reads -17.30/-25.21/7.97; true 0/24/24 reads a phantom pitch of -9.52. Swept a 65k-pose grid through POSE_LIMITS (constants.ts:196-200): 1.8% of poses wrongly ADMITTED, 6.5% wrongly REFUSED, and up to 14.1 deg of magnitude error on poses inside the true gate (true 15/20/10 reads -17.4/-18.0/-4.6). The comment at headPose.ts:7-8 asserting 'read row major' carries no source, and test/core/headPose.test.ts:50-60 builds its input with data[r*4+c], the identical assumption, so the suite cannot catch it. test/MANUAL.md:23 (item 19) checks single axes only, where a transpose merely flips sign, tolerates 'small bleed', and instructs the owner to 'Note the SIGNS you observe... they calibrate 3.7 and 3.8' - so the one recorded observation ('tilt toward the left shoulder reads positive roll') was calibrated in the wrong frame.

_Note._ Confirmed at medium, and of these six this is the one I would do first: it is the only finding whose truth is settleable against an upstream source rather than argued, the fix really is S, and it is the cheapest thing in the batch. It does not reach high because no headline number moves - Eyeblink8 F1 is event-level, the aperture itself is rotation-invariant by construction (MANUAL item 20: 'the measurement is built from distances, which rotation cannot change'), head pose appears nowhere in MODEL_CARD's measurement table, and the 1.8%/6.5% figures come from a uniform pose grid that heavily overweights combined-corner poses a seated user rarely visits. But it does cross three of the materiality bars: it misleads a reader (every displayed sign is inverted), it perturbs a published number (pose_valid_fraction, assembled at src/main.ts:2439-2442, surfaced by src/core/sessionVerdict.ts:233-252 and read by analysis/blinklab/verdict.py:346-353), and it blocks accuracy for a named row - ROADMAP.md:200 (12.5) is per-second pitch medians and nod events, which would embed the wrong convention wholesale, and 12.5 is a named rider on 12.18's LOSO (ROADMAP.md:213). The fix is proportionate as written, with one addition the finding gets right and must not be skipped: pin a fixture containing a REAL recorded matrix. Without it the corrected code is as tautologically tested as the current code. Flipping the display sign will also invalidate MANUAL item 19's recorded observation, so re-running item 19 is part of the fix, not an optional follow-up.

#### F-036. One untrusted frame splits a closure into two long closures and can hand its tail to the blink counter, pinned by test as intended

|                             |                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Severity after verification | **medium**                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Category                    | defect                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Effort                      | M                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Raised by                   | blink-closure                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Files                       | `src/core/longClosure.ts:45-46`, `src/core/longClosure.ts:77-84`, `test/core/longClosure.test.ts:291-307`, `src/core/blink.ts:88-90`, `src/core/blink.ts:101-103`, `src/main.ts:3693`, `src/core/score.ts:123-134` |

**Claim.** 'One closure, one count' and the blink/long partition both break on a single untrusted frame.

**Impact.** A microsleep with a head nod is double-charged (30 points), alerts twice and can count as a blink; laptops near 25 fps put every long closure at risk.

**Fix as proposed.** Carry closure state across a bounded gap; do not arm a closure beginning right after a gap unless the eye was seen open; re-pin the test to the physical intent.

**Evidence as filed.** A null frame resets firedForCurrentClosure and closedAtMs; the test pins a second long closure for a 100->1900 ms closure with one null. Probes: 1.9 s closure with one null -> long.count 2; 1.4 s closure with a null at 1.2 s -> long.count 1 and blink.count 1 (267 ms). Nulls arrive from the pose gate (a nod during a microsleep) and fps-gate flicker.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** src/core/longClosure.ts:77-84 resets closedAtMs and firedForCurrentClosure on a null frame; test/core/longClosure.test.ts:291-307 pins count 2 for a 100->1900 ms closure with one null at 1100. Probes through the real reducers at baseline 8 mm (blink line 4.0, shut line 3.2): 1.9 s closure clean -> long.count 1, duration 1900 ms; same closure with one null -> long.count 2 and the recorded duration collapses to 877 ms; 3 s closure with a null at 1500 -> count 2; 1.4 s closure with a null at 1200 -> long.count 1 AND blink.count 1 at 278 ms (finding said 267 ms — same effect, different frame grid), so the 'exactly one time category' partition at longClosure.ts:13-18 leaks. The null source is real: src/main.ts:3088 computes stabilityMm only inside 'if (gate.kind === "valid")', and :3693/:3570 pass null whenever the pose gate or the fps gate refuses. Score double-charge confirmed: score.ts:123-134 charges LONG_CLOSURE_PENALTY_EACH=15 per delta, so a split microsleep costs 30.

_Note._ One impact clause is refuted: it does not alert twice. ALERT_DEBOUNCE_MS=5000 (src/core/alert.ts:10,41-48) swallows a second trigger arriving ~1 s later and books it as suppressedCount, so the person is told once. The count, the CSV column, the recorded duration and the score penalty are all really double-charged.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** Both halves reproduce. The double count is pinned by the repo's own test: test/core/longClosure.test.ts:290-307 walks one physical closure from 100 ms to 1900 ms with a single null at 1100 and asserts count 2, under a comment framing it as intended ('A fired closure interrupted by a lost face must not poison the next cycle'). The mechanism is src/core/longClosure.ts:77-84, where a null clears both closedAtMs and firedForCurrentClosure. The blink-tail half I reproduced against a faithful reimplementation of blinkStep: a 1.4 s deep closure with one null at 1200 ms yields blinkCount 1 with lastBlinkDurationMs 267 - the tail of a microsleep counted and timed as a blink, breaking the 'every closure lands in exactly one time category' partition asserted at longClosure.ts:14-18. The null source that matters is causally tied to the event: src/main.ts:3054 initialises stabilityMm null and only assigns it at :3168 inside the `if (gate.kind === 'valid')` branch (main.ts:3081-3090), so a head nod trips the pose gate, nulls the aperture, and splits the closure - and a nod is what a microsleep looks like. Cost: score.ts:36-37 charges LONG_CLOSURE_PENALTY_EACH 15 with a cap of 30, so one physical event bills the entire cap, and featureRecord longClosureCount (main.ts:3833) carries the inflation into the export.

_Note._ Confirmed at medium. Two impact claims are wrong and should be dropped before this is written up. (1) 'alerts twice' is false: ALERT_DEBOUNCE_MS is 5000 (src/core/alert.ts:10, checked at :43), so a second firing 900 ms after the first is swallowed and recorded as suppressed, exactly as designed. (2) 'laptops near 25 fps put every long closure at risk' overstates the fps channel - measureFps (src/core/fps.ts:9-18) is a rolling-window estimate over many timestamps, not a per-frame reading, so it does not flicker frame to frame. The pose-gate channel is the one that carries the finding, and it carries it well precisely because the null is correlated with the event rather than random. What survives is enough for medium: a stated invariant broken ('one closure, one count', longClosure.ts:46-47), the blink/long partition leaking, the score's long-closure term saturating from a single event, and an exported column inflated. It stays below high because the score is declared 'a heuristic, not a measurement' in MODEL_CARD and DROZY's long-closure verdict is already 'no', so no published claim moves. IMPORTANT caveat on the fix: 'carry closure state across a bounded gap' as written would reconstruct a duration spanning frames nobody watched, which contradicts the rule both detectors state explicitly (blink.ts:86-87 'a blink we could not watch from start to finish is not a blink we may count or time'; longClosure.ts:73-76 'no event may be built on frames nobody saw'). Do not trade one invariant for another. The proportionate version keeps refusing the duration across the gap but stops the second COUNT and stops the tail arming as a blink - remember that a closure was in progress without claiming its span. And re-pin test/core/longClosure.test.ts:290-307 deliberately: it was added by mutation testing, so a fix will redden it and will look like a regression to anyone who does not read the comment.

#### F-039. Droop-then-blink lands in neither bin: the closure clock starts at the line crossing and the two reducers use different lines

| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **medium**                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Category                    | defect                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Effort                      | M                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Raised by                   | blink-closure                                                                                                                                                                                  |

**Claim.** The drowsy phenotype is refused by one reducer for length and by the other for depth and vanishes with no trace.

**Impact.** The instrument is blind to the transition it most wants to see, growing with drowsiness; refused closures leave no event.

**Fix as proposed.** Time the closed phase from the arm-line crossing, or emit a 'refused: over-length' event class; pre-register against Eyeblink8's 9 long-closure misses.

**Evidence as filed.** Probe D (B=8): a 533 ms droop at 3.8 mm followed by a real 100 ms blink to 2.0 -> blink.count 0 (span 633 > 500), long.count 0 (never below 3.2). The partition is stated 'for any one aperture line'; the wiring uses two.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** Probe D reproduces exactly (B=8, blink line 4.0, arm 3.6, shut line longClosureThresholdMm(8)=3.2): 533 ms at 3.8 mm then 100 ms at 2.0 mm then open gives 'D blink.count= 0 everArmed= true long.count= 0'. Blink refusal is src/core/blink.ts:100 (closedAtMs latched at the droop's first sub-line frame) with 110-113 (633 > 500); the long-closure miss is longClosure.ts:85 (never below 3.2). Worse than claimed: probe D2, a 10 s droop at 3.8 mm containing three real deep 133 ms blinks to 2.0 mm, gives 'D2 blinks counted= 0 long closures= 0', while the same three blinks from an open eye give 'D3 blinks counted= 3'. The droop is not hypothetical: ROADMAP.md:13 records 'naturally low eyelids reading at the bottom of the screen sat below the blink line for five seconds while fully awake', and longClosure.ts:30-32 prices the reading droop at 45-50% of baseline against a blink line at 50%. Wiring lines confirmed: main.ts:3572 hands blinkStep `blinkLineMm ?? BLINK_APERTURE_THRESHOLD_MM`, main.ts:3695 hands longClosureStep `longClosureThresholdMm(frozenShutBaselineMm)`.

_Note._ The neither-bin band itself is documented and pinned, so that half is not news: longClosure.ts:33-34 calls it 'deliberately neither a blink nor a long closure', test/core/longClosure.test.ts:338-395 asserts it, MANUAL item 44 records the descent-time cost. What is new and untested is the conjunction the finding names: a genuine deep blink inside or after a sustained droop is counted nowhere, and blink counting is suspended for the whole droop. LEARNING.md:447 shows the project treats exactly this failure as disqualifying — the fix #114 reopen latch was killed partly because 'once chatter latched the eye closed, a real blink arriving mid ride was folded into the ride and swallowed'. ROADMAP.md:246 (14.11's 'pre-committed droop refusal bound so suppression-versus-masking is visible') shows the masking is half-suspected but not yet measured or fixed.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** Probe D reproduces exactly. Re-implementing both reducers and stepping a B=8 mm trace (blink line 4.0, shut line 3.2): 533 ms held at 3.8 mm, then 100 ms at 2.0 mm, then reopen — blinkStep returns count 0 (span 627 ms > MAX_BLINK_DURATION_MS, src/core/blink.ts:100 keeps closedAtMs from the droop crossing, :110-113 refuses), longClosureStep returns count 0 (never below 3.2 for more than 100 ms, src/core/longClosure.ts:97-107). The two lines are genuinely different in the wiring: src/main.ts:3561-3572 hands blinkStep the blink line, src/main.ts:3690-3696 hands longClosureStep longClosureThresholdMm (EYES_SHUT_FRACTION 0.4, longClosure.ts:34). The partition comment itself is scoped 'For any one aperture line' (longClosure.ts:14-18).

_Note._ Confirmed, and it is NOT the accepted droop-band limit. The accepted case (docs/max-blink-duration.txt:154-158, test/core/longClosure.test.ts:338-377) is a lid that settles between the lines and STAYS — it never reaches shut, so it does not cover this. Probe D's closure reaches 2.0 mm, decisively below the 3.2 shut line, and still lands in neither bin — which falsifies a sentence the repo asserts in its own manual: test/MANUAL.md:45 (item 41) ends 'A closure that reaches truly shut lands in exactly one of blink or long closure by its duration.' That makes this the sharpest of the three blink-closure findings: a stated invariant, manually testable, is false, and the failure mode is exactly the drowsy phenotype (blinks inside a droop vanish silently while PERCLOS at 47.5% of baseline still reads 0 and the score reads 100). Held at medium rather than raised because nobody has measured how often it fires on real footage; the 9 long crossed_line Eyeblink8 misses are the place to price it. FIX CAUTION: take the second half only — emit a 'refused: over-length' event class, which is additive and is what null-never-zero already implies for a witnessed closure that produces no row. The first half, timing the closed phase from the arm-line crossing, redefines every published duration and the meaning of MAX_BLINK_DURATION_MS, breaking the 4.3 definition the ratchet's anchor rests on.

#### F-040. Guided calibration's own 3 s closed phase is scored as a microsleep and fed to the passive baseline

**Claim.** The instrument instructs a closure, then alarms at 500 ms, charges 15 points for a minute and, inside the learning window, feeds 90 closed samples into the baseline.

**Impact.** A calibrated user's first minute reads drowsy by design; a protocol participant exports a spurious long closure.

**Fix as proposed.** Feed null to blinkStep, longClosureStep, perclosStep and baselineStep while collecting, show 'paused for calibration', add a wiring test.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** No gating exists: `grep -n blinkCalibrationSession src/main.ts` returns only the block at 3450-3502 — the variable is never read by any reducer feed, and main.ts:3447-3448 states the intent outright ('Nothing here touches the blink reducer below'). blinkStep (3561-3573), baselineStep (3517-3521), longClosureStep (3690-3697) and perclosStep (3755-3760) all receive stabilityMm with no calibration check; GUIDED_CALIBRATION_PHASE_MS=3000 at constants.ts:172. My probe over 60 s at 30 fps with a 3 s closed phase at the repo's measured shut floor (0.33·baseline) through the real reducers: 'G perclos = 0.0500 long.count = 1 alerts fired = 1 blinks = 0' and 'G score = 85 eyes closed share:0 long closures:15 slow blinks:0 sluggish lids:0' (score.ts:38, LONG_CLOSURE_PENALTY_EACH=15). The alert is real, not inferred: alertStep at main.ts:3705-3714 fires the banner. longClosureCount is an exported column (csv.ts).

_Note._ Confirmed as stated, including the exact numbers (PERCLOS 5.0%, one long closure, score 85), plus one the finding did not claim: the alert banner fires during the instrument's own instructed closure. One sub-clause is true but inconsequential — I measured the baseline effect by tiling the fixture's real open apertures into a 900-sample learning window and replacing 90 of them with shut-floor samples: 'H clean : ready baseline=8.053 spread=1.133' versus 'H dirty : ready baseline=8.053 spread=1.145'. The p90 does not move and the 1.25 ceiling is not approached, so 'feeds 90 closed samples into the baseline' is code-true but costs nothing measurable. The PERCLOS/long-closure/alert/score half is the whole harm, and the fix is still S.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** src/main.ts:889 sets blinkCalibrateButton.disabled = !running, so the guided flow only ever runs inside a live measuring session. src/main.ts:3517-3521 steps the session and :3524-3527 instructs 'Now gently CLOSE your eyes and hold them shut' for GUIDED_CALIBRATION_PHASE_MS = 3000 (src/core/constants.ts:172). Nothing between the calibration block and the reducers gates on an active session: baselineStep at :3517, blinkStep at :3561, longClosureStep at :3690, perclosStep at :3755 — the only guards present are blinkMeasurable and frozenShutBaselineMm. 3000 ms > LONG_CLOSURE_THRESHOLD_MS (500, longClosure.ts:19) so the closure fires one long-closure event, which drives alertStep at :3705-3713 and costs LONG_CLOSURE_PENALTY_EACH = 15 (score.ts:38-39); 3 s in the 60 s window is 5.0% PERCLOS, exactly PERCLOS_RAMP_FLOOR (score.ts:32) so 0 points — score 85, matching Probe G. The per-second export row at :3771 has no session gate either.

_Note._ Confirmed. Not cosmetic: it contaminates the exported per-second CSV, and it does so specifically for people who followed the instrument's own instructions — which lands squarely on 11.7 (validation round II) and 11.8 (the n-of-1 longitudinal protocol), where a spurious long_closure and a 5% PERCLOS spike in a participant's first minute is a data-integrity defect an analyst cannot see from the numbers. It also has the app alarm at a closure it just asked for, which costs the demo credibility the era is explicitly building. The 'nothing here touches the blink reducer below' comment at src/main.ts:3444-3448 is true about the corpus path (a file run never starts a session) and false about the live path, which is how this survived. Fix is proportionate and has two in-repo patterns to copy: the `blinkMeasurable ? stabilityMm : null` feeds at :3693 and :3758, and the wiring-test discipline ROADMAP.md:198 (12.5) already names. Best effort-to-benefit ratio of the six, and it should land before any participant data is collected.

#### F-041. Gaze-derived signal rows (12.11-12.13, 12.18 riders) precede the gaze validation instrument (14.9), inverting the era rule
