**Claim.** Gaze signals built on an uncalibrated offset and an owner-setup literal are read once and never again against UTA-RLDD labels.

**Impact.** The final labelled read carries an unmeasured error term.

**Fix as proposed.** Move 14.9 (with F-010/F-011 additions) ahead of 12.11-12.13; gate 12.18's gaze riders on a committed 14.9 number or drop them; add blink-gating to 12.12's refusals.

**Evidence as filed.** 'Instrument rows land before their claim rows'; slow-drift index, look-away share and fixation turnover are built and ride into the one-shot labelled read before 14.9; the off-screen threshold was priced by eye and never re-earned.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** ROADMAP.md:41 states the era rule verbatim: 'instrument rows land before their claim rows'. The gaze signal rows sit at 206 (12.11 slow-drift gaze index), 207 (12.12 look-away events and off-screen share) and 208 (12.13 fixation turnover); 213 (12.18) is 'The one-shot UTA-RLDD v2 re-measure ... carrying the ... slow-drift, and look-away families as named predicted riders', and ROADMAP.md:39 fixes that read as the last one ever ('read exactly ONCE more ... Per-feature dips into the same 148 videos are refused'). The gaze instrument rows land after it: 244 (14.9 'Gaze validation pass and mid-session drift probe ... Instrument only, no claim') and 248 (14.13 'Scripted look-away validation for 12.12'). The threshold is still an owner-setup literal: constants.ts:25-29 prices OFF_SCREEN_OFFSET_THRESHOLD=0.18 from 'Corner glances observed on the owner's setup' and says 'Calibration at 5.4 will earn a better number', while test/MANUAL.md item 34 records that it never did ('off screen keeps its (uncalibrated) tag on purpose, that boundary is still the guessed 5.3 threshold'). MODEL_CARD.md:32 rates gaze as 'nine point calibration, one person | reliable near the centre, degrades at the corners'.

_Note._ The inversion is real for the two rows that actually ride into the labelled read, 12.11 and 12.12, and 14.9's mid-session drift probe bears directly on 12.11: instrument drift and a 'slow-drift gaze index' are the same measurement, so the confound is not hypothetical. Two small overstatements: 12.13 is marked 'permanently demo-only', so lumping it into a claim-row inversion is loose; and 12.12's uncalibrated 0.18 literal would be earned by 14.13, not 14.9, so the proposed fix names one of the two rows that need moving.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** ROADMAP.md:41 states the era rule verbatim: 'instrument rows land before their claim rows'. The gaze signal rows sit at ROADMAP.md:206-208 (12.11 slow-drift, 12.12 look-away/off-screen share, 12.13 fixation turnover); ROADMAP.md:213 (12.18) names 'slow-drift, and look-away families as named predicted riders' into the labelled read; the gaze validation instrument is ROADMAP.md:244 (14.9), thirty-one rows later. ROADMAP.md:40 makes that read irreversible: 'read exactly ONCE more ... Per-feature dips into the same 148 videos are refused'. The threshold was never re-earned: src/core/constants.ts:28-29 still carries 'Calibration at 5.4 will earn a better number' beside OFF_SCREEN_OFFSET_THRESHOLD = 0.18, and test/MANUAL.md:38 still tags off screen '(uncalibrated) ... still the guessed 5.3 threshold'. MODEL_CARD.md:32 rates gaze one-person, 'degrades at the corners'. UTA-RLDD v1 read seven eyelid features only (docs/uta-rldd-result.txt:118), so gaze would be read against those labels for the first and last time.

_Note._ Confirmed as a wrong-priority against an explicitly written contract, on the one read that cannot be repeated. One correction and one addition. Correction: the three riders are not equally exposed — 12.11 (slow drift) and 12.13 (turnover) are relative/temporal and largely survive a constant offset error; the exposed one is 12.12, whose counts are set directly by the 0.18 literal, and `onScreen` is already a shipped export column (src/core/csv.ts:26). Addition the finding understates: landing 14.9 first does not by itself license the riders, because 14.9 measures the OWNER's calibrated screen-fraction error on the OWNER's screen, and no nine-point calibration can exist for 54 strangers' self-recordings — on that corpus the 0.18 literal is applied cross-subject with no calibration at all. So the honest branch is the finding's own second one: restrict 12.18's gaze riders to calibration-free relative measures, or drop them. Worth protecting while fixing: the UI already labels off-screen '(uncalibrated)' rather than hiding the weakness — that honesty layer holds, and the one-shot read has no equivalent label.

#### F-042. Blinks are not excluded from the gaze chain: each blink splits a fixation, truncates it ~330 ms and credits heatmap dwell to the wrong cell

|                             |                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **medium**                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Category                    | defect                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Effort                      | M                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Raised by                   | gaze                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Files                       | `src/main.ts:3193-3221`, `src/main.ts:3293-3297`, `src/main.ts:3341-3349`, `src/main.ts:3380-3385`, `src/core/fixation.ts:14`, `src/core/csv.ts:23-24`, `test/MANUAL.md:40` |

**Claim.** Fixation count inflates by one per blink (2-3 per 10 s at rest) and 12.13's turnover would move with blink rate, itself a drowsiness marker.

**Impact.** Exported fixation columns are confounded with blinking.

**Fix as proposed.** Null the offset below the blink line, let I-DT bridge a blink-length null gap, exclude those frames from the heatmap; pin with the fixture.

**Evidence as filed.** The mean offset enters smoothing, I-DT and the heatmap with no aperture check; on the fixture closed frames sit 0.041 eye widths above open-eye, twice the I-DT box; the live chain breaks fixations around both fixture blinks. MANUAL 40 records the reset as intended.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** No aperture check anywhere in the chain: main.ts:3193-3218 computes irisOffset/meanIrisOffset inside the pose gate only, 3293-3297 smooths it, 3341-3348 windows it and calls detectFixations, 3379-3386 accumulates heatmap dwell on any frame with a non-null smoothed offset. Running the real chain over test/fixtures/session-01.json (300 frames, 2 blinks): 'frames: 300 closed: 15 open: 285 nullOffsets: 0' — every blink frame yields a non-null offset, so nothing upstream ever nulls it. Magnitude confirmed: 'mean vertical offset closed -0.0176 open -0.0569 delta 0.0394' against FIXATION_DISPERSION_THRESHOLD 0.02 (fixation.ts:14), i.e. about twice the I-DT box; the horizontal delta is 0.0217. Splicing the fixture's own 8 closed frames into a steady stare and running the same chain: 'STEADY live : 3 fixations' versus 'STEADY nulled: 1 fixations' — one blink turns one 5.1 s fixation into three, and nulling the blink frames lets I-DT bridge the gap, which is the finding's own fix working. fixationCount/fixationMedianMs are exported (csv.ts:23-24).

_Note._ Mechanism, magnitude and fix all hold, and the heatmap half is worse than documented: MANUAL item 38 tells the reader 'Blink or turn your head: nothing accumulates during untrusted frames', but a blink frame is trusted in that path and does accumulate. One piece of the cited evidence does not carry the load, though: on the fixture itself the live chain and the blink-nulled chain both produce exactly 13 fixations, with the two blinks landing in gaps that a real saccade opens anyway (closed runs 1951-2067 and 2884-2984 versus fixation boundaries 1900/2234 and 2850/3184). So 'fixation count inflates by one per blink' is not shown by the fixture — the fixture's gaze is moving — and only shows on a steady gaze, where I measured +2.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** No aperture check anywhere in the chain: src/main.ts:3193-3218 computes irisOffset (stabilityMm is already in hand from :3168), :3220 sets frameOnScreen from the raw mean, :3293-3297 feeds the smoothing filter, :3341-3349 feeds detectFixations, :3380-3385 feeds the heatmap; `grep -n blink` over src/core/fixation.ts, gazeSmoothing.ts and the heatmap returns nothing. Measured it on the real fixture (test/fixtures/session-01.json, 300 frames): 18 frames sit below 0.6x median EAR in exactly two runs, frames 116-125 and 173-180 — the two fixture blinks — and the mean iris vertical offset there has median -0.0238 against -0.0810 on open frames, a displacement of 0.057 against FIXATION_DISPERSION_THRESHOLD = 0.02 (src/core/fixation.ts:14), nearly 3x the I-DT box. Exported columns fixationCount, fixationMedianMs, fixating and onScreen are src/core/csv.ts:23-26.

_Note._ Confirmed and measured; the finding's 0.041 is if anything conservative on this fixture. Materiality is higher than 'demo panel' because it already reaches shipped export columns (csv.ts:23-26), not only the future 12.13. The reason to fix it before 12.18 rather than after is circularity: blink rate is itself a drowsiness marker, so a blink-split fixation turnover partially re-encodes blink rate, and 12.18 is the read that cannot be repeated — the confound would be baked into a number nobody may re-measure. Not documented anywhere: MODEL_CARD/SPEC/DATASETS/README list fixations only as features, and the repo's own intent points the other way — test/MANUAL.md:39 (item 35) says 'separating blinks and saccades from steady gaze is 5.7's business', and 5.7 (ROADMAP.md:104) shipped without it, while test/MANUAL.md:40 (item 36) presents the blink reset as intended when the actual mechanism is the blink being read as a saccade. FIX CAUTIONS, both cheap to honour: (1) 'let I-DT bridge a blink-length null gap' softens the documented invariant at src/main.ts:3330-3331 ('a fixation that bridged a lost face would be an invented stillness') — the bridge must be conditioned on a blink-caused null with the face still tracked and bounded by MAX_BLINK_DURATION_MS, never on a bare null; (2) the blink line is not computed until src/main.ts:3530-3546, after the gaze chain, so the fix needs the line hoisted or the previous frame's, and test/MANUAL.md:39's 'the vertical trace notches downward' item must be updated in the same PR or a pinned manual expectation goes stale.

#### F-047. UTA-RLDD result omits the pre-registered per-subject scores and coefficients; 'weights load on long closures' has no committed tool behind it

|                             |                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **medium**                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Category                    | process                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Raised by                   | statistics                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Files                       | `docs/uta-rldd-plan.md:99-104`, `docs/uta-rldd-plan.md:125-131`, `docs/uta-rldd-result.txt:44-56`, `docs/uta-rldd-result.txt:95-115`, `analysis/tools/analyse_rldd.py:166-256`, `STATE.md:571-574` |

**Claim.** The sole evidence against a recording-condition confound is an unreproducible observation from an unidentified fold fit.

**Impact.** The anti-confound argument load-bearing for the README's 'yes' cannot be regenerated.

**Fix as proposed.** Add the per-subject table, standardised all-data coefficients and --seed/--shuffles flags to format_report; regenerate the result from stdout.

**Evidence as filed.** The plan promises per-subject scores and reportable coefficients; the pilot printed the per-subject table, the full result does not; nothing in analysis/ prints coefficients; Verification 4 and the two reseed runs cannot be produced from the CLI.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** All four sub-claims hold. (1) docs/uta-rldd-plan.md:130-131 promises "**Per-subject scores are reported**, not only a pooled number, so a result that rides on a handful of subjects cannot hide inside an average". analysis/tools/analyse_rldd.py:199-202 does print it — `lines.append("  per-subject balanced accuracy:")` then a row per subject — but grep -i 'per-subject|per subject' over docs/uta-rldd-result.txt returns exactly one hit, line 127, which is the one-video-per-state caveat. The section headings (:44 PRIMARY, :57 NEGATIVE CONTROL, :68 SECONDARY, :78 VERDICT, :85 VERIFICATION) contain no such block. The committed file also cannot be the tool's stdout: the tool prints "NEGATIVE CONTROL, labels shuffled, three-class" (:204) while the file reads "labels shuffled 1000x from the fixed seed" (:57). (2) Coefficients: analysis/blinklab/rldd.py:337-354 `_fit` returns `weights, bias`, and both call sites (:448-449, :559-562) discard them after predicting inside the fold. grep for 'coef' across analysis/blinklab/_.py and analysis/tools/_.py returns nothing. So Verification 4 (uta-rldd-result.txt:106-115, "the model leans hardest ... on LONG CLOSURES ... then PERCLOS") comes from numbers no committed tool prints. (3) The reseeds at :99-105 ("250 shuffles each, seeds 42 and 2024") are unreachable from the CLI: run_analysis takes shuffles/seed kwargs (analyse_rldd.py:80-81) but main()'s argparse (:244-247) accepts only `measured_dir`. (4) STATE.md:571-574 confirms the weights are load-bearing — "the model's weights, which load hardest ... arguing the signal is drowsiness and not an arbitrary recording confound".

_Note._ Confirmed as written. The one correction is in the finding's favour rather than against it: format_report DOES print the per-subject table, so the omission is in the committed result file, not the tool — the result was abridged on its way to disk, which the mismatched NEGATIVE CONTROL heading independently proves. That makes it a straight pre-registration breach (a promised report element dropped) plus an unreproducible verification, in a repo whose stated contract is that claims are "scored not edited". Medium is right; the fix genuinely is S, since the weights already exist inside _fit.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity high.** Every part verified. The promise: docs/uta-rldd-plan.md:129-131 — 'Per-subject scores are reported, not only a pooled number, so a result that rides on a handful of subjects cannot hide inside an average' — and :101-104 — 'Its coefficients are reportable, so a positive result can be read as a claim about which features carried it rather than an oracle.' The tool honours the first: analysis/tools/analyse_rldd.py:200-202 prints 'per-subject balanced accuracy:' and one line per subject. The NULL pilot published it and reasoned from it: git 725e9f9:docs/uta-rldd-result.txt:60-77 carries the full table and the sentence 'The per-subject scores confirm it rides on nobody.' The POSITIVE full result does not: docs/uta-rldd-result.txt is 155 lines and contains no per-subject section at all (grep 'per-subject' returns nothing). Ordering rules out staleness — git merge-base confirms edc7793 (which added the printing) is an ancestor of e66a290 (which recorded the full result), so the table was in the stdout that result was written from. Coefficients: nothing in analysis/blinklab/ or analysis/tools/ contains 'coef_' or 'coefficient'; _fit (rldd.py:334-354) returns weights but LosoResult (rldd.py:365-390) retains only labels, truth, predicted, subjects, imputed_cells — the weights are discarded every fold, so Verification 4 at docs/uta-rldd-result.txt:113-125 has no committed producer. Reseeds: analyse_rldd.py:244-247 takes only measured_dir, no --seed or --shuffles.

_Note._ Confirmed and raised to high. This is not a documentation slip; it is the project's central honesty mechanism failing in precisely the asymmetric direction pre-registration exists to prevent. The per-subject table was published when the answer was a null (12 subjects, 725e9f9) and dropped when the answer was the positive that now carries the README's 'yes' (README.md:45) — and its stated purpose, in the plan's own words, was to stop a result riding on a handful of subjects from hiding inside an average. Nothing about the result can be checked against that guard as committed. Verification 4 is the load-bearing anti-confound argument in the result file ('An arbitrary recording-condition confound would be unlikely to load specifically onto the right features in the right direction'), and no code in the repository can regenerate the loadings it describes, so the strongest sentence in the evidence document rests on an observation from an unidentified fold fit. One correction to the finding's framing, in the project's favour: the reseeds are not strictly unreproducible — shuffle_control exposes shuffles and seed as parameters (rldd.py:528-529), so a three-line Python call reproduces them; only the committed CLI cannot. Fix is small and exactly right: have format_report print the per-subject table and standardised all-data coefficients, add --seed/--shuffles to the parser, regenerate docs/uta-rldd-result.txt from stdout, and note the regeneration rather than silently replacing the file. This should be done BEFORE 12.18 re-reads the labels, since v2's parity gate compares against a v1 record that currently cannot be reproduced in full.

#### F-051. Baseline and guided-calibration sample floors count processing ticks, not seconds of face

|                             |                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **medium**                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

**Claim.** The frozen ruler every later number is judged against can rest on 25 distinct photographs with no trace on the page.

**Impact.** The validation round's failed criterion was the ruler; this is a route to a bad one nobody sees.

**Evidence as filed.** Ready at elapsed >= 30 s AND samples >= 100 with no restart on face loss; at 120 Hz a face absent until 29.1 s yields a ruler from 0.91 s of face; guided phases accept 0.3 s of face at 120 Hz; re-reads of one photograph count as many samples. '30 samples = one second at 30 fps' is the justification.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** src/core/baseline.ts:70-77: samples are appended once per call whenever apertureMm !== null, and readiness is `elapsed >= BASELINE_LEARN_MS && samples.length >= BASELINE_MIN_SAMPLES` (constants.ts:149-150 = 30000 ms, 100). src/main.ts:3517-3521 calls baselineStep once per processFrame tick with stabilityMm (null when landmarks are missing, main.ts:3168-3169), and baselineState is cleared only in resetSession (main.ts:953), never on face loss — so a face absent for 29 s then present for ~0.9 s at 120 Hz yields ~108 samples and a ready, permanently frozen ruler. That ticks are not photographs is documented by the repo itself: src/core/deliveryRate.ts:14-17 states frameLoop.ts drives from requestAnimationFrame "with no check that a new frame arrived, so a 127 fps session on a 30 fps camera re-reads each delivered frame about four times and counts each re-read" — confirmed at src/io/frameLoop.ts:8-22, a bare rAF loop. 100 ticks at 120 Hz over a 30 fps camera = 25 distinct photographs. The guided half is the same error with its false equivalence written down: constants.ts:159-160 justifies GUIDED_CALIBRATION_MIN_SAMPLES = 30 as "one second at 30 fps", but guidedCalibration.ts:87-91 counts ticks, so at 120 Hz a 3 s phase resolves on 0.25 s of face.

_Note._ Confirmed at medium, with one supporting clause corrected. "No trace on the page" is false for the PASSIVE baseline: calibrationWindow.ts:70 records sampleCount, sessionMetadata.ts:209 exports it as calibration_samples, and sessionVerdict.ts:93-95 prints "Calibration accepted: N samples..." in the participant report — 108 against an expected ~900-3600 would be visible to a reader who knows to look. It is exactly true for the GUIDED path: StoredBlinkCalibration (guidedCalibration.ts:118-122) holds only three millimetre values, and grepping sessionMetadata.ts, participantReport.ts and sessionVerdict.ts for the guided line returns nothing, so a guided line that overrides the passive baseline and lifts its refusal (main.ts:3538, 3569, 3584) reaches neither the export nor the report in any form. Severity held at medium because the guided path is both the less guarded one and the one that governs the detector.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** src/core/baseline.ts:74-77 gates readiness on `elapsed >= BASELINE_LEARN_MS && samples.length >= BASELINE_MIN_SAMPLES` (30000 ms / 100, src/core/constants.ts:149-150); samples accrue one per processing tick with a non-null aperture (baseline.ts:70) and the state is fed per frame at src/main.ts:3517-3521 from stabilityMm, with no restart on face loss (:88-96 documents freeze-on-birth, not restart-on-loss). The tick rate is not the camera rate: src/core/deliveryRate.ts:12-17 states the frame loop is driven by requestAnimationFrame 'with no check that a new frame arrived, so a 127 fps session on a 30 fps camera re-reads each delivered frame about four times', and docs/blink-sample-rate.txt:598-605 measures exactly that on a real device (processing 120, delivered 30, sampled 30). So 100 samples can be 0.83 s of ticks over ~25 distinct photographs. Guided phases have the same shape: GUIDED_CALIBRATION_MIN_SAMPLES=30 justified in-comment as 'one second at 30 fps' (constants.ts:166-172) but collected per tick (src/core/guidedCalibration.ts:62-71). Nothing in docs/baseline-freeze.txt or docs/calibration-refusal.txt accepts this case.

_Note._ Confirmed at medium; one supporting claim is wrong. The birth IS traced: src/core/sessionVerdict.ts:93-95 speaks 'Calibration accepted: N samples, spread ratio X' on the page and src/core/sessionMetadata.ts:209-211 exports calibration_samples/spread/ceiling_bound - so an analyst comparing 100 samples against a 30 s window can catch it after the fact; the person on the page cannot, and a ruler born from 25 photographs can land between the 1.0 short flag and the 1.25 ceiling and pass every existing check (docs/validation-plan-round2.md:66-73). This sits on the component round I indicted, so it is correctly medium and correctly prioritised. Fix is proportionate and stays in pure core: add a trusted-face span (or distinct deliveredCount count) to the readiness rule and to the birth certificate. Two cautions: tightening the floor can turn some corpus clips into refusals, so re-run the ratchet and bind the number to its commit; and the span field belongs in the exported birth certificate, which is what round II's rules read.

#### F-052. Guided blink and gaze calibrations can be run on a clip's face and persist into the visitor's camera sessions

|                             |                                                                                                                                                            |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **medium**                                                                                                                                                 |
| Category                    | defect                                                                                                                                                     |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                                                                          |
| Raised by                   | wiring                                                                                                                                                     |
| Files                       | `src/main.ts:885-889`, `src/main.ts:3403-3420`, `src/main.ts:3450-3486`, `src/main.ts:3538-3542`, `src/main.ts:4147`, `src/io/calibrationStore.ts:199-212` |

**Claim.** Three seconds of a recorded stranger's eye becomes this visitor's stored personal line and lifts their next session's refusal.

**Impact.** A persisted calibration from the wrong face silently changes the threshold across visits.

**Fix as proposed.** Gate both buttons and steps on frameSource === 'camera'; cancel in-flight calibration in resetSession; e2e on the clip fixture.

**Evidence as filed.** Both calibrate buttons enable for any running source; the sessions are fed with no frameSource check, stored, and adopted on every later visit; the light stimulus, by contrast, is gated to camera; on a stepped clip media time completes the phases normally.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** src/main.ts:885 and :889 set calibrateButton.disabled and blinkCalibrateButton.disabled to !running, where running = state.kind === "running" (main.ts:842) and a loaded clip enters exactly that state (main.ts:1221-1222, after frameSource = "file" at :1195). The frame-loop steps have no source check: the gaze capture at main.ts:3398-3440 and the blink calibration at main.ts:3450-3492 both run for any source. The clip clock advances them normally — frameClock.ts:189-195 returns mediaTimeSeconds * 1000 for a non-camera source, and both clip drivers pass that as nowMs (main.ts:1288, :1434) — so the two GUIDED_CALIBRATION_PHASE_MS phases complete on media time. A ready result is stored (main.ts:3477-3479 -> calibrationStore.ts:198-211), reloaded on every later visit (main.ts:1692-1693 `loadBlinkCalibration()` at module init), and then overrides the passive baseline AND lifts its refusal: main.ts:3569 and :3584 gate on `blinkMeasurable && (hasGuidedLine || !calibrationRefused)`. The contrast is in the same file: startLightStimulus refuses outright at main.ts:4147 with `frameSource !== "camera"` and the comment "the stimulus is for a live eye, not a clip". resetSession (main.ts:950-1010) clears captureState at :991 but never touches blinkCalibrationSession or blinkCalibrationRequested. test/e2e/calibrationBlinks.spec.ts drives only the camera path.

_Note._ Confirmed. One mitigating fact the finding does not mention, which bounds the likelihood without excusing the gap: guidedCalibration.ts:100-105 refuses unless the closed median sits at least 30% below the open median, so a clip whose subject never holds a sustained closure resolves to "closure-not-registered" and stores nothing. The clips that would slip through are exactly the drowsiness ones with long closures. That guard is a separation check, not a wrong-face gate, so the defect stands as filed: nothing anywhere asks whether the eye being measured belongs to the visitor, the persisted line is silent in the export (no guided-calibration row exists in sessionMetadata.ts), and the missing resetSession cancel is real.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** src/main.ts:885-889 sets both `calibrateButton.disabled = !running` and `blinkCalibrateButton.disabled = !running` with no source test, and `running` is `state.kind === 'running'` (:842), which a loaded clip reaches (:1195 sets frameSource='file' inside the clip path). The guided session is stepped from the same per-frame aperture with no source check (:3450-3468), stored on success (:3477-3479, src/io/calibrationStore.ts:199-212), and a stored line then WINS over the passive baseline and lifts the calibration refusal on every later visit (:3535-3542 and its comment). The contrast is in the same file: startLightStimulus refuses outright unless `frameSource === 'camera'` (:4145-4149). resetSession clears the gaze capture (:988-990) but not blinkCalibrationSession/blinkCalibrationRequested (declared :1699-1700, cleared only by the overlay click at :1753-1756). No export row records that a guided line was in use or its value - src/core/sessionMetadata.ts:209-212 describes only the passive baseline window.

_Note._ Confirmed at medium. The harm is the repo's own worst class - a silently wrong ruler that also disables a designed refusal - and it persists across sessions, in mm units that look plausible because iris scaling makes a stranger's aperture a believable number. Published corpus numbers are safe (the corpus runner starts in a fresh browser, so storedBlinkCalibration is null, per the comment at src/main.ts:3536-3542). Fix is proportionate and breaks nothing: the blink e2e already runs against a fake CAMERA stream (test/e2e/calibrationBlinks.spec.ts:22-30), so a frameSource==='camera' gate leaves the suite green, and gaze calibration on a clip is meaningless by construction. Worth folding in one adjacent gap the finding did not name: add a metadata row for the guided line actually in force, so a session measured against a stored line leaves a trace in the file rather than only on the page.

#### F-053. Delivery rates are captured at the first consumer, not at session end, so the report's evidence rate depends on click timing

|                             |                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **medium**                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Category                    | defect                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Effort                      | M                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Raised by                   | wiring                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Files                       | `src/main.ts:579-596`, `src/main.ts:2414-2420`, `src/main.ts:2667-2678`, `src/core/deliveryRate.ts:45`, `src/core/deliveryRate.ts:126-151`, `src/core/sessionVerdict.ts:103-107`, `docs/pilot-dry-run.txt:56-62` |

**Claim.** The dry run's fix made consumers agree but the session fact is still a rolling window read at an arbitrary time.

**Impact.** The surface deciding refused/warned/ok is a function of operator speed, with a misattributing fallback sentence.

**Fix as proposed.** Capture at every session end before the observer stops; longer term record sampledFps per second and use its median.

**Evidence as filed.** sessionDeliveryRates ??= deliveryRates(now) over a 5 s window; Stop captures nothing; a report opened >5 s after Stop prints unknown and the verdict says 'this browser does not report delivery', which is false; export-first memoises a mid-session snapshot.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** src/main.ts:590-596: `sessionDeliveryRates ??= deliveryRates(deliveryState, performance.now())` — memoised at whichever consumer arrives first, reset only in resetSession (main.ts:1023). The window is 5 s (deliveryRate.ts:45) and both rates are computed from timestamps inside it (deliveryRate.ts:126-151 with fps.ts:1-19). stopCameraButton (main.ts:2667-2678) stops the observer and the camera and captures nothing. I simulated the exact functions on a 60 s session (30 fps delivery, 60 Hz processing): report opened 0 ms after Stop -> deliveredFps 30.00 / sampledFps 30.10; at 4000 ms -> 30.51; at 5100 ms -> null / null. So the number moves with click timing and then vanishes. Once sampledFps is null, sessionVerdict.ts:102-106 does `const rate = sampledFps ?? processingFps` and attributes it to "the processing rate, because this browser does not report delivery" — false on a browser that reported delivery all session. The flip is not cosmetic: MIN_BLINK_FPS = 25 and BLINK_RISK_FPS = 60 (constants.ts:123,134), so a 30 fps camera read at 30 gives "warned" while its 60-120 Hz processing median gives "ok, above the risk band". Two ordinary orders reach the bad branch: export while running enables at main.ts:3847 and memoises a mid-session window; export after Stop routes through the KSS-after prompt (main.ts:2769-2781) and only calls exportSession — hence settledDeliveryRates — once the person answers. The report itself is reachable only after Stop (participantReport.ts:85-97).

_Note._ Confirmed as filed. docs/pilot-dry-run.txt:49-63 records the earlier fix and states its own scope precisely — "measured ONCE, at the first moment any consumer needs them" — which is exactly the residue the finding names: consumers now agree with each other, but on a rolling five-second window read at an arbitrary moment rather than on a session fact. The guard mentioned there holds main.ts to one live deliveryRates() call site, so the fix (capture at every session end, and longer term a per-second sampledFps median) has to go in at the capture site, not by adding a consumer.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** src/main.ts:588-596: `sessionDeliveryRates ??= deliveryRates(deliveryState, performance.now())` - one memoised read of a rolling 5 s window (DELIVERY_WINDOW_MS, src/core/deliveryRate.ts:45), consumed by the export (:2359), the verdict inputs (:2414) and the report conditions (:2476). The stop handler (:2667-2678) sets idle and calls stopDeliveryObserver() without capturing. After 5 s of no delivery both rates go null by construction (deliveryRate.ts:126-141 filter by nowMs; src/core/fps.ts:9-11 returns null under 2 samples), and the report can ONLY be opened after stopping (src/core/participantReport.ts:85-96 refuses while running), so a report opened more than 5 s after Stop prints unknown and src/core/sessionVerdict.ts:99-107 attributes it to 'the processing rate, because this browser does not report delivery' - false on any Chrome/Edge/Safari session. That fallback is the exact false-silence shape the module exists to kill (docs/blink-sample-rate.txt:546-560, 598-612: processing 120, evidence 30).

_Note._ Confirmed at medium, not higher, for one reason worth recording: the current protocol has participants press Export CSV while the camera is still RUNNING (docs/participant-instructions.md:54-65 - no stop step), so round I/II export files do carry a real sampled_fps and docs/validation-plan-round2.md:44-55 is not standing on a false premise today. The protection is protocol order, not code - one instruction change or one person who stops first turns the round's evidence-rate column into the processing rate with the fallback silently named. The verdict's refusal line is MIN_BLINK_FPS (25), so the defeated case is a 15-24 fps camera on a fast machine: refused becomes ok. Fix is proportionate and does not break the dry run's one-fact invariant: call settledDeliveryRates() in the stop path before stopDeliveryObserver(), which keeps the guard's exact two live deliveryRates( call sites intact (test/core/sessionVerdictFixture.test.ts:129-142). The per-second sampledFps column is the right longer-term answer and matches the repo's own committed rule that the file is the fact's home (docs/pilot-dry-run.txt:48-56). Fix the misattributing sentence with it - that half is shared with F-054 and should ship once.

#### F-055. Interruptions are counted after the session ended and stamped at 0.000 s before its first record

|                             |                                                                                                                                                                            |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **medium**                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Category                    | defect                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Raised by                   | wiring                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Files                       | `src/main.ts:4241-4247`, `src/main.ts:2425`, `src/main.ts:2563-2566`, `src/main.ts:1120-1124`, `src/core/sessionVerdict.ts:144-161`, `src/core/sessionMetadata.ts:327-331` |

**Claim.** Stop, switch to Downloads, come back, open the report: headline warned for events outside the measurement; and a literal zero where null-never-zero requires unknown.

**Impact.** The verdict is degraded by non-events and the export carries a fabricated time.

**Fix as proposed.** Gate on running; record a null stamp exported as unknown; extend the marker tests.

**Evidence as filed.** The visibilitychange listener has no state gate and appends lastRecordAtMs ?? 0; any count makes the verdict warned; a tab switch during model load writes '# interruption_1_seconds: 0.000'.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** src/main.ts:4241-4247 registers `document.addEventListener("visibilitychange", ...)` at module scope with no reference to `state` — it does `visibilityChanges += 1; interruptionTimesMs = [...interruptionTimesMs, lastRecordAtMs ?? 0]`. `interruptionTimesMs` is cleared only in resetSession (src/main.ts:1021-1022), called from session start (1094, 1221), never from the stop path — stopCameraButton at src/main.ts:2667-2678 only does setState({kind:"idle"}). reportAvailable (src/core/participantReport.ts:85-97) returns true once stateKind is idle with records > 0, so the post-stop report reads the post-stop count: src/main.ts:2425 feeds `visibilityChanges: interruptionTimesMs.length` into assessSession, interruptionsFinding (src/core/sessionVerdict.ts:144-161) returns status "warned" for any count > 0, and HEADLINE_PRECEDENCE (sessionVerdict.ts:320-341) makes "warned" the headline. The zero stamp is real: lastRecordAtMs is set only inside processFrame's one-per-second gate (src/main.ts:3773-3775) and is null until the first record, so `?? 0` writes 0, which src/core/sessionMetadata.ts:327-331 renders unconditionally as `# interruption_N_seconds: 0.000`.

_Note._ Both halves reproduce from the source. The 0.000 is a fabricated timestamp in a repo whose contract is null-never-zero — sessionMetadata.ts:334-339 right below it does exactly the right thing for pose_valid_fraction (null when the gate never ran), which makes the interruption line the odd one out rather than a style choice.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** src/main.ts:4240-4247 — the visibilitychange listener has no state gate: `visibilityChanges += 1; interruptionTimesMs = [...interruptionTimesMs, lastRecordAtMs ?? 0]`. Reset happens only in resetSession (src/main.ts:1021-1022), called at session start (1094, 1221), never at end. Stop is src/main.ts:2667-2671 → setState({kind:"idle"}), and reportAvailable("idle", n>0) is true (src/core/participantReport.ts:85-97), so the report is read exactly in the window where post-session tab switches keep accruing. Count reaches the verdict at src/main.ts:2425 (visibilityChanges: interruptionTimesMs.length) and any non-zero returns status "warned" with the sentence "...time(s) during this session" (src/core/sessionVerdict.ts:144-161); warned ranks into the headline (sessionVerdict.ts:318-341). The export writes one row per entry (src/core/sessionMetadata.ts:327-331), so a hide/show round trip after the session adds two false interruption rows stamped at the last record's time. The pre-first-record case is worse: lastRecordAtMs is null during the model download, so `?? 0` writes '# interruption_1_seconds: 0.000' — a fabricated time in an exported dataset, twelve lines below the code that refuses exactly that (sessionMetadata.ts:334-339 renders pose_valid_fraction as null when gated===0 because '0.000 would read as "every frame failed", the exact opposite').

_Note._ Both halves hold and both are contract violations, not cosmetics: a false sentence in the participant report plus a degraded headline, and a fabricated zero where null-never-zero is the repo's own rule and is honoured by the neighbouring field in the same function. Same family as the still-enabled Mark button after stop (src/main.ts:4210-4211 gates only on sessionStartedAtEpochMs), which never clears at session end. Fix is proportionate and breaks no strength: the clip suspension refusal uses a window delta (src/main.ts:1258, 1337), so it is unaffected by gating the global counter.

#### F-056. KSS-after is re-asked on every export after a Skip and is stamped by whichever export comes first, even mid-session

|                             |                                                                                                                                                               |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **medium**                                                                                                                                                    |
| Category                    | defect                                                                                                                                                        |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                                                                             |
| Raised by                   | wiring, demo-ux                                                                                                                                               |
| Files                       | `src/main.ts:2760-2783`, `src/main.ts:2229-2232`, `src/main.ts:2323-2328`, `src/main.ts:3847`, `src/core/kss.ts:61-69`, `docs/assessment-pilot-plan.md:61-62` |

**Claim.** Two files from one session can carry 'skipped' and '6'; a mid-session answer attaches to the wrong moment.

**Impact.** The project's first label can be silently replaced or misplaced.

**Fix as proposed.** Test !kssAfterAsked; export kss_after_at_seconds; consider asking on session end.

**Evidence as filed.** The guard tests kssAfter === null although kssAfterAsked exists and is set on Skip; export enables from the first record, so an answer at 40 s is the final file's label.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** src/main.ts:2760-2783: the export handler guards on `if (kssAfter === null && frameSource === "camera")` and the callback sets `kssAfter = rating; kssAfterAsked = true`. Skip calls `choose(null)` (src/main.ts:2323-2328), so a skip leaves kssAfter null with kssAfterAsked true — the guard re-fires on the next export, and kssAfterAsked (declared at src/main.ts:2232, reset at 977) is never read by it. The two files differ because src/core/kss.ts:61-69 writes `# kss_after: skipped` for null and `# kss_after: 6 (...)` for a rating. Mid-session stamping is real: exportButton.disabled is set to `featureRecords.length === 0` inside processFrame (src/main.ts:3847), and render() forces it off only when !running (src/main.ts:908-914), so Export is live from the first record; nothing in sessionMetadata.ts writes a kss_after timestamp (grep for kss_after finds only kssMetadataRows).

_Note._ Confirmed as stated. The retained kssAfter is also written into every later export in the session, so a 40 s answer labels a 10-minute file — the docs/assessment-pilot-plan.md:61-62 sequence's own 'skip recorded as skipped, never imputed' survives, but 'skipped then answered' produces two contradictory files from one session.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** src/main.ts:2760-2771 — the guard is `if (kssAfter === null && frameSource === "camera")`, although kssAfterAsked exists (src/main.ts:2231-2232) and Skip sets it: skip calls choose(null) (src/main.ts:2326-2328) → onAnswer(null) (2300-2305) → kssAfter stays null, kssAfterAsked = true, exportSession() runs. A second Export click therefore re-asks and a rating can be given, so two files from one session carry '# kss_after: skipped' and '# kss_after: 6'. Timing: exportButton.disabled = featureRecords.length === 0 (src/main.ts:3847), so Export is live from the first record and an answer at 40 s is written as the session's after-label with no timestamp — kssMetadataRows takes only the two ratings (src/core/kss.ts:61-69) and main.ts:2372 passes only kssBefore/kssAfter.

_Note._ Material because the KSS is the project's only label and the file is the dataset row; kss.ts:43-49 states the rule this breaks ('A person who declines is not a 5... put a fabricated label into a training set'). One refinement for the fix: describe(null) returns 'skipped' unconditionally, so a clip session that was never asked also exports '# kss_after: skipped' — not-asked is being written as declined. Testing !kssAfterAsked and passing the asked flags into kssMetadataRows fixes both at once; adding kss_after_at_seconds fixes the placement.

#### F-057. There is no 'ended' state: a finished clip stays 'running', the report is unreachable for every clip session, and consumers guess 'is the session over' differently

|                             |                                                                                                                                                          |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **medium**                                                                                                                                               |
| Category                    | risk                                                                                                                                                     |
| Effort                      | M                                                                                                                                                        |
| Raised by                   | wiring, demo-ux                                                                                                                                          |
| Files                       | `src/main.ts:691-707`, `src/main.ts:885-889`, `src/main.ts:932`, `src/main.ts:1316-1322`, `src/main.ts:2628-2637`, `src/core/participantReport.ts:85-97` |

**Claim.** Session end is modelled three ways; this is the root of F-015, F-055 and the unreachable clip report.

**Impact.** The skeptical scientist is the clip user and never gets the page's most careful output; the visible advice cannot be followed.

**Fix as proposed.** Add an ended state reached from Stop, clip finish/stop and crash paths; make exports, report and KSS-after depend on it and calibrations/markers/light on running && camera; word the gate per source; pin with unit tests and one e2e per transition.

**Evidence as filed.** Finished or stopped clips stay running with clipRunEnded; reportAvailable refuses running; the gate sentence says 'stop the camera first' while the Stop button is hidden for files; calibrate buttons stay enabled on a finished clip; idle/measurementFailed/clipRunEnded each proxy 'ended'.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** The successful clip path at src/main.ts:1316-1322 sets `clipRunEnded = true; render();` and returns through the status line at 1416-1418 without any setState, so state.kind stays "running"; grep shows clipRunEnded is read in exactly one place, `startButton.hidden` at src/main.ts:925. The video 'ended' listener (src/main.ts:691-707) does the same. reportAvailable (src/core/participantReport.ts:85-97) returns false for "running", so refreshReportGate (src/main.ts:2633-2642) keeps both report buttons disabled and prints 'stop the camera first' — while stopCameraButton.hidden = !running || frameSource !== "camera" (src/main.ts:932) hides the only Stop it names, and 'Stop measuring' (src/main.ts:661-663) only sets clipStopRequested, exiting through the same running-state path. calibrateButton/blinkCalibrateButton are `disabled = !running` (src/main.ts:885-889), so both stay enabled on a finished clip.

_Note._ Confirmed, with one boundary the finding overstates slightly: a clip that FAILS (clipFailed at 1353/1370/1385, or measurementFailed) does leave running and does reach the report. It is every clip session that produced a result — finished or deliberately stopped — that cannot. That is the worse half anyway, and the three-way modelling of 'ended' (idle / measurementFailed / clipRunEnded) is exactly as described.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** Both clip end paths set only a flag: src/main.ts:691-706 (video 'ended' → clipLoop.stop(); clipRunEnded = true; render()) and src/main.ts:1316-1322 (stepped run → clipRunEnded = true; render()). Neither calls setState, so state.kind stays "running" and reportAvailable("running", n) returns false (src/core/participantReport.ts:85-97) — the participant report is unreachable for every clip session, and starting a camera to reach 'idle' would call resetSession (src/main.ts:1094) and wipe the records first. The gate then prints 'stop the camera first' (src/main.ts:2628-2637) while stopCameraButton.hidden = !running || frameSource !== "camera" (src/main.ts:932) hides the only button that sentence names. running is defined as state.kind === "running" (src/main.ts:842), so calibrateButton and blinkCalibrateButton stay enabled on a finished clip (src/main.ts:885-889) with no frames arriving, and markButton stays enabled after a camera stop (src/main.ts:4210-4211). CameraState (src/core/cameraState.ts:1-30) has no ended member; idle, measurementFailed and clipRunEnded each proxy it.

_Note._ Confirmed as stated, including that it is the root of F-055's post-session counting. Materiality is a blocked capability, not a wrong number: the clip user is the skeptical reader and cannot reach the page's most careful output, and the on-screen instruction is unfollowable. Fix caution so it does not break strengths: the state machine carries two hard-won behaviours the refactor must preserve — measurementFailed deliberately keeps the exports (src/main.ts:906-917) and clipRunEnded is what brings the start button back (src/main.ts:925). An 'ended' state must be additive to those, not a replacement.

#### F-063. No Content-Security-Policy, and the two recorded objections to one do not survive reading the bundle

|                             |                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **medium**                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Category                    | risk                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Effort                      | M                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Raised by                   | security-privacy                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Files                       | `SECURITY.md:38-42`, `decisions/ADR-0004-model-telemetry.md:79-82`, `decisions/ADR-0004-model-telemetry.md:109-112`, `src/io/telemetryBlock.ts:7-8`, `NEEDS-REVIEW.md:169`, `index.html:3-7` |

**Claim.** connect-src 'self' closes exactly the named residual risk at the network layer; the repo's documents call it impossible on grounds wrong for this bundle.

**Impact.** Dependabot proposes tasks-vision bumps weekly; a transport change is caught only by the 70 s e2e.

**Fix as proposed.** Add the meta CSP, run the full e2e including WebKit stepped clips, add blob: allowances only if needed, correct SECURITY.md and append to ADR-0004; keep the wrapper.

**Evidence as filed.** SECURITY.md calls CSP a hosting limit; NEEDS-REVIEW concedes a meta CSP is the lever; ADR-0004 rejects it over WASM and a stalling POST, but the bundle's send() catches a rejected fetch and clears its interval, the WASM objection is 'wasm-unsafe-eval', and every asset is same-origin. ADR-0004 names the residual risk a CSP closes.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** The bundle refutation holds. In node_modules/@mediapipe/tasks-vision/vision_bundle.mjs the sender is `Eh=class{...async send(t,e,r){...try{let i=await fetch(...);200===i.status?e?.(await i.text()):r?.(i.status)}catch(t){if("AbortError"===t?.name)r?.(408);else r?.(400)}finally{clearTimeout(i)}}}` — a CSP-blocked fetch rejects with a TypeError, is CAUGHT, and calls the error callback. Its caller `Fh` does `this.error=Error(...);this.h=[];void 0!==this.g&&(clearInterval(this.g),this.g=void 0)` — so a blocked send stops the 6e4 ms interval and never retries. Nothing awaits it: the interval calls `this.flush()` with no callbacks. So ADR-0004:79-82's stated grounds ('cannot hand the caller a synthetic success, so a fire-and-forget POST could stall') do not hold for this bundle. index.html:1-11 has no CSP meta and every asset is same-origin: src/io/landmarker.ts:6-11 resolves the WASM fileset and `models/face_landmarker.task` from `import.meta.env.BASE_URL`, and the only absolute http URL in src/ is a LinkedIn href at main.ts:409 (navigation, not connect-src). SECURITY.md:39-42 puts the missing CSP under 'What is out of scope' as 'a hosting limit, not a defect this repository can fix', while NEEDS-REVIEW.md:174 concedes 'the only lever is an in-document `<meta http-equiv>` CSP' — the two documents contradict each other. .github/dependabot.yml sets npm `interval: weekly`, so tasks-vision bumps do arrive weekly, and test/e2e/telemetryBlock.spec.ts:81-106 is the only live tripwire (it sits past the sixty-second mark).

_Note._ Two small overstatements, not enough to downgrade. 'connect-src self closes exactly the named residual risk' is slightly too strong: ADR-0004:109-112 names 'a transport we do not wrap, or a host we do not match', and connect-src covers fetch/XHR/sendBeacon/WebSocket/EventSource but not an <img> or <script> beacon, so it closes the host half completely and most but not all of the transport half. The WASM objection is answerable, but note the minimal proposal (connect-src only, no default-src) never touches script/WASM loading at all, so 'wasm-unsafe-eval' is not even needed — the ADR's objection is irrelevant to the directive being proposed, which is a stronger point than the finding makes. Severity medium is right: the runtime block already works, so this is defense-in-depth plus two documents stating an incorrect technical reason in a repo whose contract is checkable privacy.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** Both recorded objections fail against the bundle. The stall objection (ADR-0004:79-82, echoed at src/io/telemetryBlock.ts:7-8): in node_modules/@mediapipe/tasks-vision/vision_bundle.mjs the logger class `Fh` runs a 60 s setInterval; its transport `Eh.send` is a plain `fetch` wrapped in an AbortController with `la:1e4` (10 s timeout) and a catch mapping failure to `r?.(400)`; `Fh.flush`'s error callback sets `this.error`, empties the buffer, and calls `clearInterval` on the timer. A CSP-rejected fetch fails fast, kills the timer, and never retries — it cannot stall, and it is off the render path anyway. The WASM objection is answered by `script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'`, and every runtime asset is same-origin: the only absolute URLs in dist/assets/*.js are w3.org (SVG namespace), the odml endpoint string, and linkedin.com; the model and WASM live in public/models and public/mediapipe-wasm. Neither bundle creates a Worker (0 `new Worker`); the WASM glue calls createObjectURL twice, so a `blob:` allowance may be needed, which the fix anticipates. The residual risk is also larger than ADR-0004 admits: src/core/telemetryPolicy.ts:19 blocks `googleapis.com` only, and test/e2e/telemetryBlock.spec.ts:86-88 filters the live assertion on `isGoogleApisHost`. So ADR-0004:105-107's 'The live test is the tripwire for that: if the report ever leaves again, it goes red' is false for a host change — a bump moving the endpoint off googleapis.com passes both the wrapper and the tripwire green. Meanwhile SECURITY.md:38-42 tells a public reporter CSP absence is 'a hosting limit, not a defect this repository can fix', which NEEDS-REVIEW.md:169 contradicts in the same repo ('the only lever is an in-document `<meta http-equiv>` CSP').

_Note._ Confirmed at medium, but the material half is the published rationale and the tripwire, not an open leak. Nothing escapes today: the wrapper works and the e2e was watched red with the guard disabled (ADR-0004:99-103), which is a real strength the fix correctly preserves. What is wrong is that two documents state an impossibility that the bundle's own code refutes, and a third names a tripwire that will not trip on the most likely failure mode. For a project whose method is that reasons are checkable, a rejected option rejected on false grounds is the defect. Reorder the fix: the cheapest first move is S, not M — widen test/e2e/telemetryBlock.spec.ts:85-88's live assertion from `isGoogleApisHost(request.url())` to 'no cross-origin request at all'. That closes the host-change gap in one line and is a prerequisite for trusting either mitigation. Then the meta CSP as defence in depth, then correct SECURITY.md:38-42 (which is wrong for connect-src even if frame-ancestors genuinely cannot be expressed in meta) and append to ADR-0004 rather than editing it, per the ADR-0002 precedent.

The contradiction is live, not theoretical: ROADMAP.md:158 (row 9.1, done 4 Sep) adjudicated a learned model against the explainable heuristic on an accuracy-first rule ("KEEP the heuristic" only because Bar 2 was not cleared); had the learned model won it would have been adopted, which PROJECT.md:29 forbids. ROADMAP.md:198 (12.3) queues the same trade again with the model's black-box appearance head.

_Note._ Confirmed at medium: PROJECT.md is the first document README:628 sends a reader to, and it now describes a project that no longer exists, in breach of its own line 3. Two corrections to the finding. (1) The fix item "the 13.1 mobile ADR before Phase 13" is not a gap — ROADMAP.md:219 already opens 13.1 with "a scoping ADR first (citing the five phone sessions already in the record)", so the roadmap honours PROJECT.md:49's gate for phone CODE; what has already outrun the PRD is phone EVIDENCE (MODEL_CARD.md:286-290), which is a PRD edit, not an ADR. (2) The impact "'why is the blink line what it is' cannot be answered from decisions/" overstates: ROADMAP.md:13-14 (amendments 5 and 6) record the 40% shut line with its measured reasoning, its dated acceptance and its deliberate cost, and MODEL_CARD carries it. The record exists; the INDEX is missing. So the proportionate fix is ADR-0005 on the priority plus a PROJECT.md edit (49 lines, cheap) and a decisions/README index pointing at the amendments — NOT a CONTRIBUTING rule minting a one-page ADR per measurement-definition change, which would re-copy the amendments into a second place and feed exactly the duplication F-070 measures. The amendments are a strength; do not replace them, point at them.

**Claim.** A test-retest bound across ~150 commits confounds the person with the detector.

**Impact.** The era's only within-subject claim would be uninterpretable.

**Fix as proposed.** Row zero: a tagged build at a stable path, named in the frozen plan, with intake refusal on differing app_commit; start after 13.2 and the F-009 fix.

**Evidence as filed.** Deploy on every push to main at 8-20 commits/day; no pinned build; app_commit is exported but nothing holds it constant.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** .github/workflows/deploy.yml:3-6 is `on: push: branches: [main]` — every merge redeploys the single Pages URL, with no tagged/pinned path anywhere in the file. `git tag` returns v0.1.0..v0.7.0 only, and ROADMAP.md:141 (8.3) states the position deliberately: "Tags exist to v0.7.0. The v0.8.0 tag is deliberately not cut... a version number is not worth a ceremony" — so the cited line is apt, not a mis-citation. Commit density from `git log --format=%ad --date=short | uniq -c`: 20/13/12/15/8/10/15/8/8/9/19/20/8/13/17 on active days through 2026-09-05, so ~3 weeks lands in the 150-200 range the finding claims. app_commit is exported once per session (src/core/sessionMetadata.ts:355, `line("app_commit", appCommit)`, sourced from the build's meta tag at src/main.ts:2377-2381) and grep for `app_commit` across the repo returns only that emitter, its test, and one result doc — nothing reads it back as a gate. ROADMAP.md:190 (11.8) names only "the expectancy and time-of-day confounds" in its frozen-plan requirement; detector version is not among them, and no n-of-1 plan doc exists (grep "n-of-1|longitudinal|test-retest" hits only ROADMAP.md:190 and STATE.md prose).

_Note._ Holds on every cited fact. One softening: because app_commit is stamped per session, a shifting detector is at least detectable post hoc — sessions could be stratified or the run voided — so "uninterpretable" is the strong end rather than the certain outcome. The gap is real: nothing in 11.8's own check list would catch the confound before the three weeks are spent.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** .github/workflows/deploy.yml:4-6 deploys on every push to main; `git log --pretty=%ad --date=short | uniq -c` gives 19-20 commits/day on 2026-08-29, 09-02, 09-05, so ~3 weeks is 150-300 deploys. No pinned build exists: ROADMAP.md:141 records the v0.8.0 tag as deliberately not cut, and Pages serves exactly one artifact (deploy.yml:32-42). ROADMAP.md:190 (11.8) asks for "same setup, same protocol, ~3 weeks of sessions, test-retest bound as prediction one" and its Check names only a frozen plan, an intake tool and a split analysis row — nothing about instrument constancy. docs/validation-plan.md has zero occurrences of commit/version/build as a session condition. app_commit is written per session (src/core/sessionMetadata.ts:354-355, sourced from the build-stamped meta tag at src/main.ts:2597-2601) but nothing constrains it; it appears as a stated condition in exactly one result, docs/pupil-light-result.txt:5.

_Note._ Material and correctly graded. The confound is the one the repo already institutionalised against elsewhere — tools/detectorRatchet.mjs (ROADMAP.md:164) exists precisely because a detector change without a re-measure is a lie, but it guards corpus numbers only; nothing guards a live longitudinal run. Two corrections to the finding. (1) "Uninterpretable" overstates it: app_commit is in every export, so the confound is detectable and stratifiable post hoc rather than silent — but a test-retest bound with n=1 per stratum is still useless, so the practical impact stands. (2) The fix is proportionate and, importantly, a lighter fix does not exist for the phone leg: getUserMedia needs a secure context, so a locally built pinned copy is not reachable from a phone over LAN, which is what makes "a tagged build at a stable path" the right shape rather than gold-plating. The intake refusal on differing app_commit is the cheap half and should land regardless. The sequencing prescription ("start after 13.2") is a defensible opinion, not part of the defect — it inverts the roadmap's phase order and the owner may reasonably decline it.

**Claim.** The demo surface carries no statement of what THIS camera can measure.

**Impact.** The era's unit of honesty is postponed ~30 rows.

**Fix as proposed.** Split 13.6a now (rate and iris-px verdicts, light unknown) and 13.6b after 12.16; derive boundaries from committed data.

**Evidence as filed.** Two of three inputs (delivered rate, iris px) exist today; a 17.4 px session (one pixel ~0.67 mm against a 0.4 mm band) shows the same confidence as a 58 px one; 13.6 waits on 12.16's light term.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** ROADMAP.md:224 (13.6) is the ladder row, sitting behind 40 open `- [ ]` rows (awk count of unchecked rows above line 224), one of which is 12.16 at ROADMAP.md:211, the light term. Both other inputs exist today: delivered rate is computed and rendered (src/main.ts:2520-2545, three named rate lines in the participant report), and iris width is computed every frame (src/core/aperture.ts:19 irisWidthPx, sampled at src/main.ts:3139-3150) and exported as `median_iris_width_px` (src/core/sessionMetadata.ts:290). The arithmetic checks: IRIS_DIAMETER_MM = 11.7 (src/core/constants.ts:12), so at the P2 session's 17.4 px (docs/validation-round.txt:50) one pixel is 11.7/17.4 = 0.672 mm against the 0.4 mm shallow band, versus P6's 58.3 px = 0.201 mm/px. Nothing in the code distinguishes them: src/core/sessionVerdict.ts:28-36 lists all eight surfaces (calibration, evidenceRate, interruptions, rulerFit, cameraOutcome, pose, modelTrust, markedWindow) — no iris and no light — and the participant report's conditions block (src/main.ts:2508-2565) carries camera, three rates, measurement frame, KSS, interruptions, markers, but NOT iris px, even though docs/assessment-pilot-plan.md:147 specifies "measurement frame, iris px, KSS, interruptions, markers".

_Note._ Confirmed, and the plan-vs-code drift at docs/assessment-pilot-plan.md:147 (iris px specified for the report's conditions, absent from src/main.ts:2508-2565) is extra support the finding did not cite. Two calibrations: the row count is 40, not ~30, so the finding understates its own case; and "carries no statement of what THIS camera can measure" is slightly strong — the rate half already speaks on the page (the sub-60 fps warning, MODEL_CARD.md:113-116, and the 25 fps refusal). It is the resolution half that is mute.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** ROADMAP.md:38 (amendment 16) states the era's own position: "Capability is a property of a SETUP, not a device class... The ladder the era builds (13.6) is measured per setup — delivered rate, iris pixels, light". ROADMAP.md:224 places 13.6 after ROADMAP.md:211 (12.16, the light term), i.e. after all of Phases 11 and 12. The two other inputs exist today: src/core/sessionVerdict.ts:24-64 already assembles eight per-session surfaces including evidenceRate, rulerFit, pose and modelTrust, and docs/validation-round.txt:50-55 records iris px per session (17.4 px on P2, 58.3 px on P6, a 3.35x spread on sessions the page treated identically). The spatial term is real arithmetic, not a hunch: src/core/aperture.ts:109-122 computes apertureMm = openingPx * (11.7 / irisPx), so one pixel of opening is 0.67 mm at 17.4 px against the 0.4 mm shallow-blink band MODEL_CARD.md:113-116 names — while src/main.ts:3128 renders that number to one decimal.

_Note._ Confirmed as a wrong-priority finding, with the claim corrected. "The demo surface carries no statement of what THIS camera can measure" is materially overstated: the page already carries the sub-60 fps rate warning (MODEL_CARD.md:115-118), the 25 fps blink refusal, the Ruler fit line (src/core/rulerFit.ts:181-187) and the two 10.10b conditions sentences (ROADMAP.md:177). What is missing is specifically the SPATIAL term and the consolidation. The overstatement does not sink the finding because the strongest justification is not the demo surface at all — it is Phase 11 intake. Rows 11.6, 11.7 and 11.8 (ROADMAP.md:188-190) all run live protocols on setups whose capability the page cannot state, and a live iris-px verdict would have flagged P2 before its session rather than in the conditions table afterwards. That is a genuine ordering cost against the era's own stated correction. Two notes on proportionality: the split the fix proposes is already routine repo practice (9.3a/b, 9.4a/b, 10.1a/b, 10.7a/b/c, 10.10a/b), so it costs nothing structurally; and an iris-px boundary is derivable today from committed constants (11.7 mm / 0.4 mm band = ~29 px) without waiting on new data, which satisfies the era rule at ROADMAP.md:38 that boundaries be derived rather than chosen. The sharper version of this finding, worth filing separately, is false display precision: 0.1 mm shown where the ruler quantises at 0.67 mm. Do not let 13.6a acquire a light verdict by inference — the repo's own discipline (docs/aperture-noise-floor.txt:49-56, "ONE face, ONE camera, ONE lighting") is the strength to protect here.

(1) It is the repo's own hardest rule bent on the first screen: an instrument that writes blank cells and em dashes rather than zeros in its exports (src/core/blinkLog.ts:99-104, "a blink whose shape could not be analysed must not read as a blink of zero amplitude") opens with "Blinks: 0" for a session that does not exist, and with a no-penalties verdict for a score that was never computed. (2) test/MANUAL.md:64 is a standing acceptance check the shipped page fails today — that is a broken promise, not a drifted document. (3) These exact idle strings have already been shown to disguise a real failure: docs/audit/appendix-chunk-5-all-findings.md:146 records a 404 on the model file leaving "Alertness score: measuring..." / "Blinks: 0" on screen and the page looking healthy. Not already-accepted: the only place the behaviour is defended is a code comment, and the August audit recorded the doc half as an open medium (docs/audit/chunk-5-ui-and-access.md:139-152, "docs/UI.md is void as a compensating control") that is still unfixed. The fix is proportionate and protects the strength it touches: the anti-reflow property (src/main.ts:850-854) depends on the LINE COUNT being constant, not on the sentences being verdicts, so "not measuring" strings preserve it exactly. Fix the strings and the two documents in one PR; do not start hiding boxes, which would break the no-reflow design the comment is defending.

#### F-079. Keyboard users cannot leave the calibration or heatmap overlays, and the KSS dialog has no focus trap with focus landing on rating 1

|                             |                                                                                                                                                 |
| --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **medium**                                                                                                                                      |
| Category                    | ux                                                                                                                                              |
| Effort                      | M                                                                                                                                               |
| Raised by                   | demo-ux                                                                                                                                         |
| Files                       | `src/main.ts:1670-1674`, `src/main.ts:1753-1757`, `src/main.ts:1988`, `src/main.ts:2244-2255`, `src/main.ts:2335-2338`, `src/main.ts:4183-4187` |

**Claim.** WCAG 2.1.2 and 2.4.3 failures plus a data-integrity edge.

**Impact.** A reflexive Enter records the wrong label in the CSV.

**Fix as proposed.** Escape closes the overlays; native <dialog> with showModal() intercepting cancel; initial focus on the prompt or Skip.

**Evidence as filed.** Three overlays close only on click; the sole keydown listener is the light overlay's; KSS has aria-modal but no Tab handling, focus escapes after 12 Tabs, initial focus is '1 Extremely alert' so Enter files it.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** src/main.ts:1670-1674 (calibrationOverlay), :1753-1757 (blinkCalibrationOverlay) and :1988-1993 (heatmapOverlay) each register only a `click` listener to cancel/close; none of the three divs is focusable (no tabindex), so Enter/Space cannot reach the handler. `grep -n 'keydown' src/main.ts` returns exactly one hit, main.ts:4183, guarded by `!lightOverlay.hidden` — the light stimulus only. KSS: main.ts:2244-2247 sets role=dialog + aria-modal=true; there is no Tab/keydown handling anywhere in the file and `grep -rn 'inert' src/` finds only two unrelated code comments in videoStepper.ts, so background controls stay tabbable. main.ts:2306-2331 builds 9 rating buttons from KSS_SCALE plus Skip and then main.ts:2333-2338 focuses `kssButtons.querySelector('button')`, i.e. src/core/kss.ts:18 `{ rating: 1, label: "Extremely alert" }`; its click handler calls choose(1), and describeRating (main.ts:2269-2277) then records "1 Extremely alert" indistinguishably from a deliberate answer while Skip records "skipped". Buttons activate on Enter keydown, so a reflexive Enter files rating 1 into the CSV.

_Note._ Two details are wrong but do not change the substance. (1) The dialog has 10 tab stops, not 12 (9 ratings + Skip; kssPrompt is a <p>). (2) 'cannot leave the calibration overlays' overstates: both calibration overlays self-close when their timed run completes (main.ts:3422 and :3465) — the keyboard user cannot CANCEL (the on-screen text at main.ts:3440 says 'Click anywhere to cancel'), but is not stuck indefinitely. Only heatmapOverlay is an indefinite click-only trap. The fabricated-KSS-label edge is the strongest half and is squarely against the repo's own honesty contract, so medium stands.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** src/main.ts:1988-1993 is the heatmap/replay overlay's ONLY close path (a click listener); it never auto-closes, unlike the two calibration overlays which the run itself hides (src/main.ts:3422, 3465). The sole keydown listener in the file is the light overlay's Escape (src/main.ts:4183-4187, grep for 'keydown' returns one hit). Overlays are position:fixed inset:0 z-index:10 (src/main.ts:1908-1916), so a keyboard-only visitor who opens the heatmap can only get out by reloading, and featureRecords live in memory until Export, so the reload discards the session. KSS: focus lands on kssButtons' first child (src/main.ts:2335-2338), which is KSS_SCALE[0] = {rating: 1, 'Extremely alert'} (src/core/kss.ts:18); a held or repeated Enter files it as a real answer. ROADMAP.md:146 declines row 8.8 on the ground 'keyboard operable, focus visible, all text clears WCAG contrast'; grep for keyboard/Escape/focus in test/MANUAL.md returns nothing, so that clause has no test or manual item behind it.

_Note._ Material against the repo's own contract, not merely WCAG: 8.8's decline is still standing on a ground that is false for the heatmap, which is the exact failure the 8.8 amendment already had to correct once for contrast ('what did not stand was checking a claim like that by eye'). The KSS half also cuts against a deliberate design: the dialog distinguishes skipped (null) from never-asked (src/main.ts:2256-2260, describeRating at 2270-2278), and a reflexive '1' is indistinguishable from a considered answer in the CSV. The proposed fix is proportionate and does NOT break the documented strength: the comment at src/main.ts:2256-2260 deliberately refuses Escape/backdrop dismissal, and the fix preserves that by intercepting <dialog>'s cancel. Two corrections to the write-up: the Tab count is 10 buttons (9 ratings + Skip), not 12, and the calibration overlays are not permanent traps since their timed runs close them — the heatmap is the only true dead end, and it should be the headline.
