#### G-Browser--2. The engine is in no provenance pin: switching measure_corpus.mjs to chromium, or bumping Playwright, reddens nothing

|                             |                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **medium**                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Category                    | risk                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Raised by                   | Browser-engine conditioning of the published detection numbers                                                                                                                                                                |
| Files                       | `tools/detectorRatchet.mjs:37-60`, `tools/modelProvenance.mjs:15-17`, `package.json:30`, `package-lock.json:2216-2219`, `docs/eyeblink8-m5max.txt:249-250`, `tools/measure_corpus.mjs:128`, `docs/eyeblink8-result.txt:34-39` |

**Claim.** The instrument's execution engine is load-bearing for the published numbers by the project's own reasoning, yet it is the only part of the instrument no guard watches. Changing `webkit` to `chromium` at tools/measure_corpus.mjs:128, or letting the Playwright version move, would silently change the instrument and still allow the ratchet's 'Built from commit' line to advance as though nothing had happened.

**Impact.** The ratchet exists because 'twice this project has let the prose and the code drift apart' (tools/detectorRatchet.mjs:8-10). It now covers the model file and the landmarker options but not the runtime that executes them, so the next corpus run could be measured on a different engine and the mechanism would report freshness. That is a false-freshness failure, and the file's own comment says that price is not close to the price of a false staleness.

**Fix as proposed.** Three additions, all cheap. (1) Add `package-lock.json` and `tools/measure_corpus.mjs` to DETECTOR_SOURCES (tools/detectorRatchet.mjs:37-60) — the disk-existence test already covers new entries. (2) Extend tools/modelProvenance.mjs to read the `@playwright/test` version from the lockfile and the engine identifier from measure_corpus.mjs's import, and add both as lines in MODEL_CARD's provenance block beside the model sha. (3) Put the browser and Playwright version into the reproduction command block at docs/eyeblink8-result.txt:34-39, so a third party reproducing on Chromium knows the difference is theirs and not the instrument's.

**Evidence as filed.** DETECTOR_SOURCES lists 18 paths — core detector modules plus public/models/face_landmarker.task and src/io/landmarker.ts (tools/detectorRatchet.mjs:37-60). It contains neither package-lock.json nor tools/measure_corpus.mjs. modelProvenance reads exactly three artifacts: MODEL_PATH, LOCKFILE and LANDMARKER (tools/modelProvenance.mjs:15-17), and from the lockfile it reads only `node_modules/@mediapipe/tasks-vision`. Meanwhile the project's own exoneration of the browser rests on that lockfile: 'package-lock.json is tracked and has not moved since the published run's commit — @mediapipe/tasks-vision 1.0.1 and @playwright/test 1.62.1, and a pinned Playwright version pins the WebKit build with it' (docs/eyeblink8-m5max.txt:249-250). package.json:30 declares `"@playwright/test": "^1.62.1"` — a caret range; the lockfile pins 1.62.1 (package-lock.json:2216-2219) but nothing checks it against the anchor commit. And 'HOW TO REPRODUCE THIS EXACTLY' (docs/eyeblink8-result.txt:34-39) names only the Python evaluator; the browser is named nowhere in any reproduction command.

**Reproduce skeptic: downgraded, severity medium.** DETECTOR_SOURCES at tools/detectorRatchet.mjs:37-60 is exactly 18 paths (16 src/core modules plus public/models/face_landmarker.task and src/io/landmarker.ts); it contains neither package-lock.json nor tools/measure_corpus.mjs, and commitsTouchingSince (:88-101) passes only that list to `git log`, so a change to the engine line or a Playwright bump produces no touching commit and ratchetVerdict (:119-129) returns ok. tools/modelProvenance.mjs:15-17 pins MODEL_PATH/LOCKFILE/LANDMARKER, and lockfileVision (:27-31) reads only `node_modules/@mediapipe/tasks-vision`. package.json:30 is `"@playwright/test": "^1.62.1"` (caret); the lockfile pins playwright-core 1.62.1 at package-lock.json:2216-2219. The project's own exoneration rests on that pin (docs/eyeblink8-m5max.txt:248-250) and on prose at docs/eyeblink8-result.txt:80-82 ("package-lock.json has not moved since the published run's commit") that nothing checks. The "HOW TO REPRODUCE THIS EXACTLY" block at docs/eyeblink8-result.txt:34-39 names only the Python evaluator.

_Note._ The mechanics are exactly as described and the false-freshness path is verifiable. Downgraded because it is a latent risk with no currently-wrong number, and the lockfile is not entirely unguarded: modelProvenance.mjs:27-31 plus the MODEL_CARD provenance test would redden on a @mediapipe/tasks-vision bump — it is specifically the Playwright/engine slice that is unwatched. Two small citation slips: package-lock.json:2216-2219 is the playwright-core entry, not @playwright/test, and the measurement command does appear in the result file at :82, just not inside the :34-39 reproduction block.

**Materiality skeptic: downgraded, severity medium.** DETECTOR_SOURCES is 18 paths — 16 core modules plus public/models/face_landmarker.task and src/io/landmarker.ts (tools/detectorRatchet.mjs:37-60) — and contains neither package-lock.json nor tools/measure_corpus.mjs; commitsTouchingSince git-logs exactly that list (detectorRatchet.mjs:88-93), so an engine swap at measure_corpus.mjs:128 leaves the "Built from commit 65e8e7c…" anchor (docs/eyeblink8-result.txt:297) reading fresh. modelProvenance.mjs:15-17,85-90 reads only MODEL_PATH, LOCKFILE and LANDMARKER, and from the lockfile only `node_modules/@mediapipe/tasks-vision` (:86-88); MODEL_CARD.md:250-261 pins the model sha, tasks-vision 1.0.1 and four landmarker options, and names no browser. package.json:30 is a caret range `^1.62.1`. The repo's own exoneration rests on the unwatched half: docs/eyeblink8-m5max.txt:247-250.

_Note._ Confirmed as a gap against the repo's own doctrine — detectorRatchet.mjs:8-11 exists because prose and code drifted twice, and modelProvenance.mjs:64-70 says a swap leaves the card "describing an instrument that no longer exists" — but medium, not high: nothing is currently wrong, no published number is misstated, and the failure needs a Playwright bump plus no re-measure to bite. One fix-proportionality caution: part (1), adding package-lock.json to DETECTOR_SOURCES, would redden the ratchet on every unrelated dependency bump (9 lockfile commits in history, including a dependabot group bump 28cc0a1 and a font-vendoring commit 10e0c13). That is false staleness on changes that cannot touch the detector, and caveat fatigue erodes the ratchet's credibility, which is a strength. Prefer part (2) alone — modelProvenance reads `@playwright/test` from the lockfile plus the engine identifier from measure_corpus.mjs, pinned as MODEL_CARD provenance lines — and add tools/measure_corpus.mjs to DETECTOR_SOURCES, not the whole lockfile. Part (3) is right as written; note the runner is already named at docs/eyeblink8-result.txt:45, so only the engine and version are missing.

#### G-Browser--4. Clip exports drop user_agent — the one field that would record the engine — for exactly the runs that produce every published number

|                             |                                                                                                                                                        |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Severity after verification | **medium**                                                                                                                                             |
| Category                    | defect                                                                                                                                                 |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                                                                      |
| Raised by                   | Browser-engine conditioning of the published detection numbers                                                                                         |
| Files                       | `src/core/sessionMetadata.ts:120-126`, `src/core/sessionMetadata.ts:145`, `src/main.ts:1119`, `docs/evidence/2026-09-02-awake-autopsy/README.md:11-18` |

**Claim.** The measurement artifact cannot say what browser produced it. The engine and machine identity survive only as a sentence in a README, which is the prose-drifts-from-code failure the ratchet was built to end — and here the code cannot even emit the fact the prose asserts.

**Impact.** Every committed evidence CSV under docs/evidence/ is unfalsifiable at the engine level: nobody can check after the fact which browser measured a given file, and a future run on a different engine would produce artifacts indistinguishable from the current ones. It also blocks the cheapest possible engine claim, which would otherwise be 'diff the two exports' rather than 'trust the run notes'.

**Fix as proposed.** Split the function: camera rows conditional on a camera, machine rows unconditional. `user_agent`, `hardware_concurrency`, `device_pixel_ratio` and (with the previous finding) the webgl2 probe are properties of the browser, not of the camera, and should be emitted in clip mode with the camera line still reading 'none, not a camera session'. This is one branch in src/core/sessionMetadata.ts:121-126 plus reading a minimal deviceInfo on the clip path in src/main.ts.

**Evidence as filed.** `deviceMetadataRows` returns a single line when there is no camera: `return [line("camera", "none, not a camera session")];` (src/core/sessionMetadata.ts:122-126). The full block — including `line("user_agent", info.userAgent)` and `line("hardware_concurrency", …)` (src/core/sessionMetadata.ts:145-146) — is reachable only when deviceInfo is non-null, and deviceInfo is assigned in exactly one place, after a camera stream goes live (src/main.ts:1119). Every corpus measurement is a clip run, so every corpus CSV carries no user_agent, no hardware_concurrency, no viewport. The engine consequently has to be asserted in prose: 'The run drove the real built app through WebKit' (docs/evidence/2026-09-02-awake-autopsy/README.md:11-12).

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** src/core/sessionMetadata.ts:121-126: `export function deviceMetadataRows(info: DeviceInfo | null)` returns `[line("camera", "none, not a camera session")]` and nothing else when info is null. The full block — line("user_agent") at :144, line("hardware_concurrency") at :145, viewport/screen/device_pixel_ratio/orientation at :146-149 — is unreachable without a DeviceInfo. `grep -n deviceInfo src/main.ts` shows it declared null at :568, cleared at :1013, and assigned non-null in exactly one place, :1119 `deviceInfo = readDeviceInfo(video)`, inside the camera-start path (the comment at :1113-1118 says "after the stream is live"). deviceMetadataRows has one caller, src/main.ts:2349 in exportSession. src/io/deviceInfo.ts:13-19 reads the track off `video.srcObject`, so it is camera-shaped by construction. A committed clip export confirms it: docs/evidence/2026-08-09/repeatability/re-run-A/27122013_154548_cam.blinks.csv:1-6 carries source/clip/measurement_mode/frames_measured/clip_duration_s/measured_fps and no browser identity at all. The engine therefore survives only as prose — docs/evidence/2026-09-02-awake-autopsy/README.md:11-12 "The run drove the real built app through WebKit".

_Note._ Confirmed as described, including the fix's shape: user_agent, hardware_concurrency, viewport, screen, device_pixel_ratio and orientation are machine properties sitting behind a camera-null guard, and only `camera`, `camera_resolution`, `camera_declared_fps` and `facing_mode` genuinely need one. One citation slip: user_agent is at :144, not :145 (:145 is hardware_concurrency). This is the substantive member of the browser-engine group — it is the code-level cause that makes the engine claim prose-only, and it is what would have to change before finding G-Browser--3's probe could reach a corpus export at all.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** src/core/sessionMetadata.ts:120-126: the function documented as "The camera and machine rows" returns `[line("camera", "none, not a camera session")]` and nothing else when info is null; user_agent, hardware_concurrency, viewport, screen, device_pixel_ratio and orientation live only in the non-null branch (:140-149). deviceInfo is assigned in exactly one place, after the camera stream is live (src/main.ts:1119), and cleared on every new source (:1013), so every clip run — i.e. every corpus measurement — exports no machine rows. The engine therefore survives only as prose: docs/evidence/2026-09-02-awake-autopsy/README.md:11-12 "The run drove the real built app through WebKit". Two supports for the fix: src/io/deviceInfo.ts:29-40 already tolerates a null track (label null, settings {}), so calling it on the clip path is safe; and analysis/blinklab/validation.py:104-118 and :206-215 distinguish clip from camera by `source == "file"` and by frame numbers, never by the absence of user_agent, so adding machine rows breaks no loader.

_Note._ Confirmed, and it is the repo's own principle turned against it twice over. test/core/sessionMetadata.test.ts:106-110 states the rule — "A missing row is indistinguishable from a field nobody thought of. 'unknown' is a true statement; absence is a gap" — and provenanceMetadataRows exists precisely "so a CSV separated from its page keeps its provenance" (src/core/sessionMetadata.ts:345-355), emitting app_commit unconditionally. The clip export therefore carries which code measured it and not which browser did, for exactly the runs that produce every published number. Medium rather than high: no number is wrong and the engine is recorded in run notes, but this is the cheapest route to the engine claim findings 1-3 want, and it makes committed evidence self-describing instead of README-attested. Two notes for the fix: test/core/sessionMetadata.test.ts:106-112 asserts equal row counts between FULL and EMPTY and will need updating, and user_agent in a clip export is a fingerprintable field in a file a visitor may share — already true of camera exports, so consistent, but worth stating rather than sliding in.

#### G-Browser--5. The only cross-engine table in the repo was measured on pre-fix code, before both defects the same PR fixed, and has never been re-run

|                             |                                                                            |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **medium**                                                                 |
| Category                    | overclaim                                                                  |
| Effort                      | S                                                                          |
| Raised by                   | Browser-engine conditioning of the published detection numbers             |
| Files                       | `README.md:545-583`, `README.md:553`, `README.md:565-573`, `README.md:583` |

**Claim.** The repository's answer to 'Does it give the same answer twice?' across engines was measured by an instrument that, at that moment, did not give the same answer twice on one engine. The Chrome/Safari differences it reports are inside the run-to-run noise the next day's PR removed, so the table cannot separate an engine effect from that noise — and it has never been re-measured on fixed code.

**Impact.** This is the entire cross-engine evidence base, and the August audit already flagged the browser-agreement table as having no evidence anywhere. It is being read as engine independence for detection on a corpus where a preparation change alone moved one clip's false alarms from 19 to 3 (docs/eyeblink8-result.txt:144-158). A 0.02 mm mean aperture agreement on one clip does not bound threshold-hugging detection differences, which is where the 65 false alarms live.

**Fix as proposed.** Date the table and state its provenance in one sentence: measured 8 August 2026, before PR #156's last-frame fix and PR #189's model-clock fix, and not re-measured since. Then either re-run it on current code with both exports committed under docs/evidence/, or demote the section to a historical record and let the engine question be answered by the corpus falsifier below. Do not leave it standing as the current answer.

**Evidence as filed.** `git log -S'Does it give the same answer twice' -- README.md` returns exactly one commit: 1de3ae4, 2026-08-08, 'fix(io): stop counting the last frame twice, and publish the numbers (#156)' — which touched README.md (+29) and src/io/videoStepper.ts (+17). The section has not been edited since. Two defects were live when the table was measured. First, the last-frame double count, which the table displays as data: Safari 4,203 frames against a 4,202-frame file (README.md:553), and the text below admits it — 'Safari's extra frame was the final one counted twice, which is fixed' (:583), fixed by the very commit that published the table. Second, the wall-clock model clock, fixed the next day by 6e89eff, 2026-08-09, 'fix(core): hand MediaPipe a clock derived from the clip, not the machine (#189)'; the README says so two paragraphs under the table — 'For a while that claim was true across browsers and false across runs. The same clip measured twice on the SAME browser gave two different answers' (:565-573). The table carries no date. It reports frames, detected rate, long closures (1 vs 1), PERCLOS peak (34.3 vs 34.5), eyes-shut span, blink rate per minute and a 0.02 mm mean aperture difference — no comparison against ground truth, one 70 s clip, one person, no committed export.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity high.** `git log -S'4,203' -- README.md` and `git log -S'| PERCLOS peak        | 34.3%' -- README.md` each return exactly one commit: 1de3ae4, 2026-08-08, 'fix(io): stop counting the last frame twice, and publish the numbers (#156)' — the table's numbers have never changed. That commit's own body says 'Safari measured 4,203 frames of a 4,202 frame recording' and adds the exact-only duplicate guard now at src/io/videoStepper.ts:348-354, so the table displays the very count the same PR fixed (README.md:553). The model-clock fix is 6e89eff, 2026-08-09, 'fix(core): hand MediaPipe a clock derived from the clip, not the machine (#189)' — the day after. README.md:545-583 carries no date, no commit binding and no export reference; docs/evidence/2026-08-09/repeatability/ holds only same-browser re-runs (published-run, re-run-A/B/C of one clip), and `grep -rni 'safari|chrome|webkit' docs/evidence/2026-08-09/` returns one unrelated line. AUDIT_REPORT_AUG_2026.md:487 already flagged it: 'The browser-agreement table's nine numbers rest on no saved export. **[untested]**', still unaddressed.

_Note._ One factual error in the finding: 'The section has not been edited since' is false — bd2a98d (2026-08-09) edited it, adding the #189 paragraph now at README.md:565-573 and deleting an earlier caveat. The table's NUMBERS were untouched, so the core claim (never re-measured on fixed code) stands. Also worth noting in fairness that README.md:583 and :565-573 do disclose both defects in prose; what is absent is any statement that the TABLE ITSELF predates both fixes, plus a date, a commit binding and a committed export — the project's own standard (tools/detectorRatchet.mjs, 'every published number is bound to a commit and carries its conditions'). Severity held at high.

**Materiality skeptic: downgraded, severity medium.** History verified: `git log -S'Does it give the same answer twice' -- README.md` returns exactly one commit, 1de3ae4 (2026-08-08, "fix(io): stop counting the last frame twice, and publish the numbers (#156)"); `git log -S'PERCLOS peak'` returns the same single commit, so the table body (README.md:545-583, table rows at :553-557) has never been edited. The model-clock fix is 6e89eff, 2026-08-09, one day later, and its own message quantifies the change: "three runs of one clip gave 43 detections with three different sets of blink timings... the count moves to 54" and "Not yet re-measured against the corpus". No conditions or date line was ever added: `grep -n 'Conditions' README.md` returns nothing, and the most recent conditions work (8ad1c06, roadmap 10.10b) touched only the on-page Blinks/Eyes boxes. The table is genuinely the only cross-ENGINE evidence: the corpus runner always launches WebKit (tools/measure_corpus.mjs:128) and the cross-machine reproduction is WebKit-to-WebKit by its own words (docs/eyeblink8-m5max.txt:400, "different WebKit binary"; :247-250 pins the Playwright/WebKit build), so MODEL_CARD.md:29's "different... browser binary" is not an engine claim. The repo's own August audit already filed this table, at MEDIUM: docs/audit/appendix-chunk-6-all-findings.md:132-144 (C6-08, "no evidence file anywhere", severity as filed medium, verification UNTESTED), and REMEDIATION.md contains no entry for it.

_Note._ Mechanism and provenance fully confirmed, and the deviation from the repo's own contract is real: every other published figure in README.md carries a date, a machine and a docs/ link (:33, :45, :46, :479), while these nine numbers carry none and are bound to no commit. Severity is one notch hot for three reasons. (1) The same section already discloses BOTH defects in prose a reader cannot miss — ":583 'Safari's extra frame was the final one counted twice, which is fixed' tells the reader outright that the table shows pre-fix output, and :565-573 says the cross-browser claim coexisted with the run-to-run bug. What is missing is one sentence ('measured 8 August 2026, not re-measured since'), not a suppressed fact. (2) No published number depends on the table; nothing downstream reads it. (3) The project's own auditors graded the identical claim medium. The proposed fix (date it, or demote it and let a corpus falsifier answer the engine question) is proportionate and breaks no strength — but note the honest re-run is cheap only if it is scoped as an instrument measurement, since the corpus runner is WebKit-only today and a Chromium corpus run has never been done.

#### G-Build, d-2. The published Apache-2.0 notice attributes the wrong version of MediaPipe, and has since 14 August

|                             |                                                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **medium**                                                                                                                                          |
| Category                    | defect                                                                                                                                              |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                                                                   |
| Raised by                   | Build, deploy and notice path — how code becomes the published page, and whether a reader of a published number can find the build that produced it |
| Files                       | `public/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt:11`, `package.json:45`, `package-lock.json:344`, `MODEL_CARD.md:253-254`, `test/tools/licenses.test.ts:20-24`      |

**Claim.** The notice served beside the page names a version of Google's library that the page does not ship, and the only tests covering the notice check package names, never versions, so nothing could have caught it.

**Impact.** This is the exact defect the August audit's A4 was created to close, recurring inside the fix itself. It is also the sharpest available demonstration that a guarded claim survives and an unguarded one rots: MODEL_CARD's version is right because tools/modelProvenance.mjs:27-31 recomputes it from the lockfile; the notice's is wrong because nothing recomputes it. On a public page whose standing rests on "published claims are pinned to artefacts", an attribution naming a version the page does not ship is the cheapest possible own goal.

**Fix as proposed.** Two lines in test/tools/licenses.test.ts, reusing code that already exists and is already typed: `import { lockfileVision } from "../../tools/modelProvenance.mjs"` (declared at tools/modelProvenance.d.mts:12, already imported by test/tools/modelProvenance.test.ts:6) and assert `expect(notice).toContain(`@mediapipe/tasks-vision ${lockfileVision(root).version}`)`. Then correct line 11 to 1.0.1. The notice is then pinned the same way the model card is, and the next grouped bump reddens instead of rotting.

**Evidence as filed.** public/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt:11 reads "MediaPipe Tasks Vision, @mediapipe/tasks-vision 1.0.0". package.json:45 pins `^1.0.1`; package-lock.json:344 resolves 1.0.1; node_modules reports 1.0.1; MODEL_CARD.md:253-254 states "@mediapipe/tasks-vision `1.0.1`". Git shows the mechanism exactly: 28cc0a1 (2026-08-14, "chore(deps): bump the minor-and-patch group with 3 updates (#239)") moved the pin from `^1.0.0` to `^1.0.1` touching only package.json and package-lock.json (`git show --stat 28cc0a1`: 2 files). The notice was written by 8aebffd (11 Aug) naming 1.0.0 and last touched by 10e0c13 (16 Aug, the fonts block) without correcting it. test/tools/licenses.test.ts:21 asserts only `expect(notice).toContain("@mediapipe/tasks-vision")` — the package name, never the version — and the e2e (test/e2e/licenses.spec.ts:15) checks the same string. A grouped Dependabot PR silently falsified the one legally operative document on the published page, and every deploy since 14 August has served it.

**Reproduce skeptic: downgraded, severity medium.** public/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt:11 reads "1. MediaPipe Tasks Vision, @mediapipe/tasks-vision 1.0.0". package.json:45 pins ^1.0.1; package-lock.json:344 resolves 1.0.1; node_modules/@mediapipe/tasks-vision/package.json reports 1.0.1; MODEL_CARD.md:253 states the runtime is 1.0.1. `git show --stat 28cc0a1` = dependabot "chore(deps): bump the minor-and-patch group with 3 updates (#239)", Fri 14 Aug 2026, body "Updates @mediapipe/tasks-vision from 1.0.0 to 1.0.1". `git log -- public/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt` shows only 8aebffd (11 Aug, which `git log -S "tasks-vision 1.0.0"` confirms wrote the string) and 10e0c13 (16 Aug), so the notice was never corrected. test/tools/licenses.test.ts:20-24 asserts only toContain("@mediapipe/tasks-vision"); test/e2e/licenses.spec.ts:15 the same string. tools/modelProvenance.mjs:27 exports lockfileVision, declared at tools/modelProvenance.d.mts:12 and already used at test/tools/modelProvenance.test.ts:46 — the proposed fix compiles against code that exists.

_Note._ Every cited fact is exact, including the mechanism and the fix. Downgraded from high because the consequence is narrower than claimed: the Apache-2.0 obligation is substantively met on the served page — the work is identified, Google LLC's copyright is named, the licence is named and the full text ships (licenses.test.ts checks "END OF TERMS AND CONDITIONS"), and the served paths are correct. What is wrong is one version digit in an unguarded published line. Real claim-rot against the repo's own "published claims pinned to artefacts" standard, not a licence breach.

**Materiality skeptic: downgraded, severity medium.** Every fact checks out. public/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt:11 reads "MediaPipe Tasks Vision, @mediapipe/tasks-vision 1.0.0"; package.json:45 pins ^1.0.1 and package-lock.json:345 resolves tasks-vision-1.0.1.tgz; MODEL_CARD.md:253 states 1.0.1. `git show --stat 28cc0a1` confirms the Dependabot grouped PR #239 (2026-08-14) moved 1.0.0 to 1.0.1 touching only package.json and package-lock.json, and `git log -- public/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt` shows the notice written at 8aebffd (11 Aug) and last touched at 10e0c13 (16 Aug) without correction. The blind spot is exactly where the finding says: test/tools/licenses.test.ts:21 asserts only toContain("@mediapipe/tasks-vision") and test/e2e/licenses.spec.ts:15 the same string — package name, never version. The contrast with the guarded claim is real: tools/modelProvenance.mjs:27-31 recomputes the version from the lockfile, which is why MODEL_CARD.md:253 is right. The proposed fix compiles against code that already exists and is already typed (lockfileVision declared at tools/modelProvenance.d.mts:12).

_Note._ Downgraded from high to medium. The mechanism, the date, the cause and the fix are all correct and this should be fixed — it is a false sentence on the published page, unguarded, and the guard is two lines of existing code. But high overstates the harm: no measurement moves, no participant is misled about the instrument, and the Apache-2.0 obligation itself is substantively met — the notice names the right library, the right copyright holder, the right licence and carries the full licence text verbatim; only the version string is stale. Medium is the honest reading of "a published fact rotted because nothing recomputed it". The fix is proportionate and breaks nothing; do the test first and the line second, so the guard is what corrects the text.

#### G-Build, d-3. The corpus engine is Playwright's WebKit, and no guard pins it — Dependabot will move it inside a grouped chore PR

|                             |                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **medium**                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Category                    | missing-capability                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Raised by                   | Build, deploy and notice path — how code becomes the published page, and whether a reader of a published number can find the build that produced it                                                       |
| Files                       | `tools/measure_corpus.mjs:46`, `tools/measure_corpus.mjs:128`, `docs/eyeblink8-m5max.txt:247-254`, `tools/detectorRatchet.mjs:37-60`, `.github/dependabot.yml:16-24`, `docs/eyeblink8-result.txt:297-301` |

**Claim.** Half the instrument that produces the project's only externally validated number — the browser binary — is unpinned by any guard and is routed through the grouped dependency PR stream, so it can move with CI green and the ratchet quiet.

**Impact.** A routine grouped dependency PR swaps the browser that measures the benchmark, with nothing in the result file recording that the engine moved. The next corpus run — row 10.8's regression run, and 11.3/11.5's sibling-corpus reads on which the era's accuracy claims graduate — would then be measured on a different instrument than the published numbers describe, and the m5max elimination (code exonerated, files exonerated, model unchanged, runtime pinned, therefore the machine) would no longer apply to the tree it was written about. Given that re-encoding alone moved precision 12.4 points, an unrecorded engine change is not a small variable.

**Fix as proposed.** Surgical version: extend MODEL_CARD's "Model provenance" block and tools/modelProvenance.mjs to pin `@playwright/test` from the lockfile alongside tasks-vision — one more `lockfileVision`-shaped reader and one more card line — so a bump reddens CI until the card moves and the caveat gets written. Additionally split it out of the group in dependabot.yml (its own entry, or `ignore` inside minor-and-patch) so the corpus engine always arrives as its own reviewable PR. Doctrine-consistent alternative: add package-lock.json to DETECTOR_SOURCES — detectorRatchet.mjs:32-34 already argues the inclusive side ("a false staleness costs one honest caveat line, a false freshness costs silent rot"). And record the engine version in docs/eyeblink8-result.txt beside "Built from commit", since the file's own anchor is blind to half its instrument.

**Evidence as filed.** The published Eyeblink8 headline is produced by driving the real built app in WebKit: tools/measure_corpus.mjs:46 `import { webkit } from "@playwright/test"` and :128 `const browser = await webkit.launch()`. docs/eyeblink8-m5max.txt:247-250 makes that engine load-bearing in an argument: "package-lock.json is tracked and has not moved since the published run's commit — @mediapipe/tasks-vision 1.0.1 and @playwright/test 1.62.1, and a pinned Playwright version pins the WebKit build with it", from which :252-254 concludes "What is left is the MACHINE". But tools/detectorRatchet.mjs:37-60 watches 18 files and neither package.json nor package-lock.json is among them, and the ratchet anchor (docs/eyeblink8-result.txt:297-301) names a code commit and mentions WebKit only in prose — no engine version is recorded for the current run anywhere. Meanwhile .github/dependabot.yml:16-24 groups all npm minor-and-patch updates into one weekly `chore(deps)` PR, the exact vehicle that already moved MediaPipe 1.0.0→1.0.1 in 28cc0a1. @playwright/test sits at 1.62.1 in package-lock.json:360 behind a `^1.62.1` caret (package.json:30).

**Reproduce skeptic: downgraded, severity medium.** tools/measure_corpus.mjs:46 `import { webkit } from "@playwright/test";` and :128 `const browser = await webkit.launch();` (tools/diagnoseClip.mjs:29 is the only other webkit import). tools/detectorRatchet.mjs:37-59 lists 18 DETECTOR_SOURCES; neither package.json nor package-lock.json is among them. `grep -rn playwright tools/` returns only the two webkit imports — no guard reads the Playwright version. .github/dependabot.yml groups all npm minor+patch into one weekly chore(deps) PR (the vehicle of 28cc0a1); package.json:30 is `"@playwright/test": "^1.62.1"`, package-lock.json:360 resolves 1.62.1. docs/eyeblink8-m5max.txt:247-250 does lean on the pin ("package-lock.json is tracked and has not moved since the published run's commit — @mediapipe/tasks-vision 1.0.1 and @playwright/test 1.62.1, and a pinned Playwright version pins the WebKit build with it") before concluding at :252 "What is left is the MACHINE". BUT: `git log 65e8e7c..HEAD -- package-lock.json package.json` is empty, and `git show 65e8e7c:package-lock.json` gives @playwright/test 1.62.1 — the engine version for the published run IS recorded, in the tracked lockfile at the anchor commit docs/eyeblink8-result.txt:297 names.

_Note._ The unguarded-bump mechanism is real and confirmed: nothing reddens when the corpus engine moves, and the grouped Dependabot PR is the proven vehicle. Downgraded from high because the finding's evidence overstates the provenance half — "no engine version is recorded for the current run anywhere" is false; docs/eyeblink8-m5max.txt recovers it from the committed lockfile at the anchor, exactly the audit path the finding says is missing, and nothing has moved (1.62.1 at the anchor and at HEAD). The exposure is prospective (the next run measured on a silently different engine), not a broken record.

**Materiality skeptic: downgraded, severity medium.** The gap is real. tools/measure_corpus.mjs:46,128 drive the published benchmark through Playwright's WebKit (as does tools/diagnoseClip.mjs:29,41); DETECTOR_SOURCES (tools/detectorRatchet.mjs:37-60) lists 18 paths and neither package.json nor package-lock.json is among them; .github/dependabot.yml groups all npm minor and patch updates into one weekly chore(deps) PR, the vehicle that already moved MediaPipe in 28cc0a1; @playwright/test sits at ^1.62.1 (package.json:30) resolving to 1.62.1 (package-lock.json:361). No guard anywhere mentions playwright: grep over tools/_.mjs, test/tools/_.ts and MODEL_CARD.md returns only the two tool imports. But two facts soften it. The engine version for a published run IS recoverable, by the same route the m5max doc itself used: package-lock.json is committed, docs/eyeblink8-result.txt:297 names the built-from commit, and docs/eyeblink8-m5max.txt:247-250 reconstructs both @mediapipe/tasks-vision 1.0.1 and @playwright/test 1.62.1 from it. And README.md:45 records the corpus reproducing "digit for digit, across a different processor, operating system, browser binary and fifteen commits of instrument change" on 26 August, so the numbers are not known to be fragile to the browser binary.

_Note._ Downgraded from high to medium. This is a legitimate missing guard and it is inconsistent with the ratchet's own stated principle — 10.2 added the model file and src/io/landmarker.ts for precisely the reason that applies to the engine (ROADMAP.md:172), and the ratchet's comment argues the inclusive side. Doing it before 11.3/11.5 is right. It is not high: nothing is currently false, provenance is recoverable from the committed lockfile at the run's commit, and the one direct test of engine sensitivity reproduced digit for digit. Take the surgical variant only — extend tools/modelProvenance.mjs and MODEL_CARD's provenance block to pin @playwright/test from the lockfile, split it out of the dependabot group, and record the engine beside "Built from commit" in docs/eyeblink8-result.txt. Do NOT add package-lock.json to DETECTOR_SOURCES: every weekly grouped bump of eslint, prettier or fontsource would then demand a dated caveat in the Eyeblink8 result file, and caveat inflation would erode the ratchet's signal, which is a strength the fix would be trading away.

#### G-Guided b-1. The open phase measures the resting eye during the three seconds it is asking the person to read 26 words

|                             |                                                                                                                                                                      |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **medium**                                                                                                                                                           |
| Category                    | defect                                                                                                                                                               |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Raised by                   | Guided blink calibration as a measurement PROCEDURE: how the personal ruler is captured, cued, confirmed, and carried — not its arithmetic                           |
| Files                       | `src/main.ts:3450-3455`, `src/main.ts:3497`, `src/main.ts:3506`, `src/core/guidedCalibration.ts:232-239`, `src/core/constants.ts:20-23`, `src/core/constants.ts:172` |

**Claim.** The open phase begins sampling on the frame the instruction first appears, so the aperture it calls 'your open eye' is measured while the person is reading unfamiliar text in a downcast posture. Because the median is a cliff rather than a gradient, a person who spends more than half the phase reading gets a line up to 40 percent too low that passes every refusal check.

**Impact.** The open median is one of the two endpoints of the instrument's only personal ruler, and it is taken in the one posture the repo has documented as a droop. Unlike the closed-side failure, this one does not land in a refusal — it stores a plausible-looking wrong number, and a low line means missed blinks with no signal that anything went wrong. Precision is 'preparation-conditioned' by the repo's own account and this is the preparation step.

**Fix as proposed.** Introduce GUIDED_CALIBRATION_SETTLE_MS and discard samples taken in the first settle window of each phase (do not merely lengthen the phase). Better still, split the overlay into a read-then-measure sequence: show the instruction with an explicit 'Ready' affordance or a visible 3-2-1 countdown, and start sampling only after it. This is a pure-core change to calibrationSessionStep plus one constant, and it reuses the exact rationale already written at constants.ts:20-23.

**Evidence as filed.** The session starts and the overlay unhides in the same frame (main.ts:3450-3455), and calibrationSessionStep collects a sample BEFORE it checks elapsed time (guidedCalibration.ts:232-239), so frame one counts. What the person is doing on frame one is reading two freshly appeared strings totalling 26 words: 'Keep your eyes OPEN and look at the screen.' (main.ts:3497) plus 'Step 1 of 2 · N s left. Closing your eyes comes next. Click anywhere to cancel.' (main.ts:3506). At an unfamiliar-instruction reading rate of 200-250 wpm that is 6-8 s of reading inside a 3000 ms phase (constants.ts:172). Reading is done with a downcast lid posture — the same 'relaxed reading droop' this repo measured at 45-50 percent of baseline (src/core/longClosure.ts:29-33). The repo already knows this class of error: CALIBRATION_SETTLE_MS = 800 exists for the gaze capture because 'Samples taken while the eye is still travelling toward a fresh dot would poison the calibration' (constants.ts:20-23). The blink calibration has no settle at all. I simulated a 90-sample open phase (8.0 mm true open, 4.0 mm droop) front-loaded with droop: the median holds at 8.00 mm through 1200 ms and then flips to 4.00 mm at 1500 ms, giving a line of 3.00 mm instead of 5.00 mm — and closed/open = 0.5 passes the 0.7 separation gate (guidedCalibration.ts:101-106), so it stores silently.

**Reproduce skeptic: downgraded, severity medium.** Structural facts all confirmed. src/main.ts:3450-3455 creates the session and unhides the overlay in one frame; :3456-3461 calls calibrationSessionStep with the SAME nowMs, so startedAtMs === the first sampled frame — the first sample is taken before the instruction has even painted. src/core/guidedCalibration.ts:232-236 collects the sample, and only then (:237) checks elapsed time. Instruction strings verified at main.ts:3495-3499 (8 words) and :3504-3508 (18 words), 26 total. GUIDED_CALIBRATION_PHASE_MS = 3000 (constants.ts:172). The settle precedent is real: CALIBRATION_SETTLE_MS = 800 with the 'would poison the calibration' rationale (constants.ts:20-23), echoed in LEARNING.md:352; no settle exists for the blink calibration and no doc records the omission as accepted. The median cliff reproduces EXACTLY under the repo's own percentile (statistics.ts:30-40 is nearest-rank: rank = ceil(p/100 * n), sorted[rank-1]): with 90 samples, 8.0 mm open / 4.0 mm droop front-loaded, I ran it — 900 ms and 1200 ms droop both give median 8.00; 1500 ms flips to 4.00, line 3.00 instead of 5.00, ratio 0.50 which passes the 0.7 gate (GUIDED_CALIBRATION_MIN_SEPARATION_FRACTION = 0.3, constants.ts:167; guidedCalibration.ts:100-106). So it stores silently, as claimed.

_Note._ Downgraded from high because the mechanism that supplies the magnitude does not survive inspection. The finding leans on longClosure.ts:29-33's 'relaxed reading droop (45 to 50 percent)', but that number was measured for 'naturally low eyelids reading at the BOTTOM of a screen'; the calibration overlay's text is vertically centred (main.ts:1723-1726: inner element top 50%, translate(-50%,-50%)), so the downcast posture the 40%-error estimate depends on is not the posture this overlay creates. The other half of the premise is also weak for the OPEN phase specifically: the person's eyes are already open and looking at the screen when they click 'Calibrate blinks' (main.ts:1701-1703), so 'keep your eyes open' asks for no state change — unlike the closed phase, where the state mismatch is unambiguous. What remains and is fully confirmed: no settle window, sampling from frame one, and a nearest-rank median that flips as a cliff at exactly half the phase rather than degrading gracefully. Real gap, unproven magnitude — medium.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity high.** Mechanism verified end to end. src/main.ts:3450-3456 sets blinkCalibrationSession = startCalibrationSession(nowMs) and unhides the overlay in the same frame; the very next block (:3456-3460) calls calibrationSessionStep in that same frame, and src/core/guidedCalibration.ts:232-237 collects the sample BEFORE the elapsed-time check, so frame one counts. The instruction text is written afterwards, in the else branch at main.ts:3494-3508. There is no settle constant for this flow, while the gaze capture has CALIBRATION_SETTLE_MS = 800 (src/core/constants.ts:20-24) and LEARNING.md:352 states the principle in the repo's own words: "Nothing counts during the settle window after a dot moves, because sampled mid travel the eye is demonstrably NOT looking at the target yet, those samples would carry confident wrong labels, the worst kind of data." The droop is the repo's own measurement, not an assumption: src/core/longClosure.ts:21-33 records that "naturally low eyelids reading at the bottom of a screen sat below the blink line for five seconds while fully awake" and puts "their relaxed reading droop (45 to 50 percent)" of baseline. The bad line stores silently: resolveGuidedCalibration refuses only when closedMedian > openMedian x 0.7 (guidedCalibration.ts:98-106), which a proportionally depressed pair passes, and main.ts:3466-3487 then writes it to storage with a confident millimetre sentence. It drives the live detector from the next frame (main.ts:3538-3546, effectiveBlinkLineMm).

_Note._ Confirmed at high. This is the one finding in the batch that produces a plausible-looking wrong number with no refusal, in the instrument's only personal ruler — the exact failure class null-never-zero and refuse-rather-than-guess exist to prevent — and the repo already owns both the precedent constant and the measured droop that make it predictable. Scope note that does not reduce it: published corpus numbers are safe by construction (a corpus run never starts a session, main.ts:3447-3448, and storedBlinkCalibration is null in a fresh browser, main.ts:1689-1692), so the harm is confined to live sessions on laptop/tablet/phone — which is precisely the era's target. Two caveats. (1) Magnitude: the median only flips once droop exceeds half the phase, so "up to 40 percent too low" is the worst case, not the expected one; below half the phase the damage is modest. The mechanism and the silence are what justify high, not the 40 percent. (2) The fix is right to say "do not merely lengthen the phase" — constants.ts:168-172 chose 3000 ms "for the person, not fitted to data" — but a settle alone eats into GUIDED_CALIBRATION_MIN_SAMPLES = 30 (constants.ts:166): a 3000 ms phase yields ~90 samples at 30 fps and ~75 at 25 fps, so an 800 ms settle leaves ~55-66, still clear of the floor but with less headroom for dropped frames. Pair the settle with a small phase extension, or prefer the read-then-measure/countdown variant which costs no sampling time at all.

#### G-Guided b-2. The closed phase is a visual-only instruction to a person whose eyes are shut, and nothing marks its end

|                             |                                                                                                                                            |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Severity after verification | **medium**                                                                                                                                 |
| Category                    | ux                                                                                                                                         |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                                                          |
| Raised by                   | Guided blink calibration as a measurement PROCEDURE: how the personal ruler is captured, cued, confirmed, and carried — not its arithmetic |
| Files                       | `src/main.ts:3494-3507`, `src/main.ts:3465`, `src/main.ts:1709-1750`, `src/main.ts:2211`, `src/main.ts:2246-2248`, `test/MANUAL.md:66`     |

**Claim.** Every cue in the closed phase — the instruction to close, the countdown, and the signal that the hold is over — is delivered on the one channel the procedure has just asked the person to switch off. The person guesses when to reopen, and a screen-reader user cannot run the procedure at all.

**Impact.** The hold length is the sampling window for the closed endpoint of the ruler. A person who reopens early truncates it; one who holds long invites the long-closure detector (finding on contamination below). It also makes the instrument's only personal calibration inaccessible to blind and low-vision users, on a page that otherwise carries role=alert and aria-modal where they matter.

**Fix as proposed.** Add a short WebAudio tone at each phase boundary and at completion (three distinguishable beeps: open-start, close-now, done), plus navigator.vibrate([...]) guarded by a capability check for phones. Give the overlay role='dialog' aria-modal='true' and put the instruction node in an aria-live='assertive' region so the phase change is announced. Then rewrite test/MANUAL.md:66 as a procedure a person with closed eyes can actually perform.

**Evidence as filed.** During phase two the page writes 'Now gently CLOSE your eyes and hold them shut.' and 'Step 2 of 2 · N s left.' to the screen (main.ts:3498, :3507) — a countdown rendered for someone who cannot see it. When the phase ends the overlay simply hides (main.ts:3465); there is no other event. grep over src/ for AudioContext, speechSynthesis and navigator.vibrate returns nothing. The overlay div (main.ts:1709-1750) carries no role, no aria-modal and no aria-live, unlike the alert banner (setAttribute('role','alert'), main.ts:2211) and the KSS dialog (role/aria-modal/aria-labelledby, main.ts:2246-2248), so a screen reader announces neither the phase change nor the finish. test/MANUAL.md:66 instructs the checker to 'close them and hold until the overlay closes (another three seconds)' — an instruction that cannot be executed with the eyes closed, which is direct evidence the modality problem was never walked through.

**Reproduce skeptic: downgraded, severity medium.** Every code claim verified. main.ts:3494-3508: phase two writes 'Now gently CLOSE your eyes and hold them shut.' and 'Step 2 of 2 · N s left.' to the screen only. main.ts:3465 hides the overlay at completion; the only other completion signal is a visual status line (main.ts:3479-3492). `grep -rn 'AudioContext|speechSynthesis|navigator.vibrate|Audio(' src/` returns nothing at all. The overlay (main.ts:1709-1750) sets dataset.testid, styles and a click handler — no role, no aria-modal, no aria-live — while alertBanner has role='alert' (main.ts:2211) and kssDialog has role/aria-modal/aria-labelledby (main.ts:2246-2248), so the contrast is exactly as described. test/MANUAL.md:66 does instruct 'close them and hold until the overlay closes (another three seconds)', which cannot be executed with the eyes shut.

_Note._ Downgraded from high because one leg of the impact does not hold up. 'A person who reopens early truncates it' overstates the measurement harm: resolveGuidedCalibration takes a nearest-rank median (statistics.ts:30-40), so open frames appended to the TAIL of the closed phase sort above the median and do not move it until they exceed half the samples — I confirmed a 2500 ms reopen in a 3000 ms phase leaves the closed median untouched. What survives is the accessibility and cueing gap, which is genuine: no non-visual cue exists on any of the three boundaries, and a screen-reader user has no announcement of the phase change on a page that uses role='alert' and aria-modal where it matters. It is also a bounded harm — the calibration is optional, repeatable, and local-only — so medium rather than high.

**Materiality skeptic: downgraded, severity medium.** All three factual halves verified. The closed-phase instruction and countdown are visual only (src/main.ts:3494-3508), and the phase ends by hiding the overlay with no other event (main.ts:3464). Grepping src/ for AudioContext, speechSynthesis, navigator.vibrate and `new Audio` returns nothing — the whole app is silent. The overlay div (main.ts:1709-1750) is styled by Object.assign and carries no role, aria-modal or aria-live, while alertBanner.setAttribute("role", "alert") at main.ts:2211 and kssDialog's role/aria-modal/aria-labelledby at main.ts:2246-2248 show the project applying ARIA deliberately elsewhere. test/MANUAL.md:66 does read "close them and hold until the overlay closes (another three seconds)".

_Note._ Downgraded to medium. The defect is real and the accessibility gap stands against the repo's own ARIA practice, but the measurement consequence is weaker than "high" implies. An early reopen puts OPEN frames into the closed phase, which RAISES the closed median toward the 0.7 gate at guidedCalibration.ts:101-106 — the failure lands on a refusal, which is an honest result, not a fabricated number. And the person is not cueless: the open phase pre-announces the next step and its length for three full seconds ("Step 1 of 2 · N s left. Closing your eyes comes next", main.ts:3506), so they can count. The accessibility claim is also narrower than stated — the gaze calibration is "Follow the dot" (main.ts:3440) and is inherently visual, so fixing this buys one accessible procedure, not an accessible instrument. Worth adding to the fix's MANUAL.md rewrite: line 66 is stale on a second point the finding did not catch — it says the status "does NOT change detection yet", but main.ts:3538-3546 has the detector using the stored line immediately. The WebAudio/vibrate/ARIA fix is cheap, proportionate and breaks nothing; note only that a beep is a new capability for a deliberately silent page, so it should be gated the way navigator.vibrate is.

#### G-Guided b-3. The 'closure-not-registered' refusal blames the person's eyelids for what is most likely reading time

|                             |                                                                                                                                            |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Severity after verification | **medium**                                                                                                                                 |
| Category                    | overclaim                                                                                                                                  |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                                                          |
| Raised by                   | Guided blink calibration as a measurement PROCEDURE: how the personal ruler is captured, cued, confirmed, and carried — not its arithmetic |
| Files                       | `src/main.ts:1770`, `src/main.ts:1766`, `src/main.ts:1768`, `src/core/guidedCalibration.ts:101-106`, `src/core/constants.ts:199-203`       |

**Claim.** All three refusal messages misdiagnose their most probable cause. The separation refusal tells a person their closure is physiologically invisible to the instrument when the likeliest explanation is that they spent most of the phase reading the instruction; the two sample-floor refusals send a phone user to fix lighting when the real cause is holding the phone below eye level.

**Impact.** A refusal is supposed to be an honest result, and these ones are honest about the arithmetic but wrong about the cause. Telling a person 'this is the same limit the corpus showed' is the sentence most likely to make them conclude their eyes are unusual and stop trying — the opposite of the intended effect, and an overclaim about what the refusal actually evidenced.

**Fix as proposed.** Make the refusal text conditional on what the run actually saw. Report the sample counts and how many frames the pose gate rejected; when pose rejections dominate, say 'hold the camera closer to eye level'; when the closed phase's first second reads open, say 'the closure came late — try again and close as soon as the tone sounds' rather than invoking the corpus ceiling. The corpus-ceiling sentence should be reserved for a run whose closed samples are plentiful and still not separated.

**Evidence as filed.** The refusal text reads: 'Your closed eyes did not read far enough below your open ones for a line to be placed. This is the same limit the corpus showed, and rather than guess a line, the calibration refuses.' (main.ts:1770). It attributes the failure to the model's recall ceiling (docs/iris-occlusion.txt, cited in guidedCalibration.ts:40-43). But my simulation of the closed phase shows the same refusal fires from ordinary reading latency: with 1500 ms of open frames at the front of a 3000 ms phase, the closed median reads 6.50 mm against 8.00 mm open, ratio 0.81 > 0.7, refused. 'Now gently CLOSE your eyes and hold them shut.' is nine words; at 250 wpm that is ~2.2 s of a 3 s phase. The other two refusals (main.ts:1766, :1768) name light and steadiness but never head angle, even though POSE_LIMITS.maxPitchDeg = 20 (constants.ts:199-203) is the most likely cause of dropped frames on a hand-held phone, which is the era's target device.

**Reproduce skeptic: downgraded, severity medium.** The three messages are verbatim as quoted (main.ts:1766, :1768, :1770), including 'This is the same limit the corpus showed'. The pose link is real: stabilityMm is initialised null at main.ts:3054 and assigned only at :3168, inside the `if (gate.kind === "valid")` branch opened at :3088, so any frame the pose gate rejects (POSE_LIMITS.maxPitchDeg = 20, constants.ts:199-203) feeds collectCalibrationSample a null, which guidedCalibration.ts:63-65 drops — driving 'not-enough-open'/'not-enough-closed' with no mention of head angle. BUT the finding's quantitative evidence for the closure refusal does not reproduce. Under the repo's nearest-rank percentile (statistics.ts:30-40), a 3000 ms closed phase at 30 fps with 1500 ms of leading open frames gives a closed median of 2.00 mm (not 6.50), ratio 0.25, and it PASSES. I ran the real formula across lags: 1000/1400/1500 ms all yield median 2.00 and pass; the refusal only fires from 46 open samples (~1533 ms) upward, where the median jumps straight to 8.00 and the ratio to 1.00. There is no 0.81 anywhere — the behaviour is a cliff at exactly half the phase, and the finding computed it with an averaging median the code does not use.

_Note._ Downgraded from high: the conclusion survives with different arithmetic, but three supporting claims are wrong or overstated. (1) The 6.50 mm / 0.81 simulation is not what the code does; the correct statement is that a closure that starts later than half the phase flips the closed median to the open value and refuses. (2) 'The two sample-floor refusals name light' — only 'not-enough-open' mentions light; 'not-enough-closed' (main.ts:1768) says 'Try again, closing your eyes when the screen asks', which already names timing, the very cause the finding says is misattributed. (3) The page is not silent on head angle: validityGate.ts:43-51 writes 'Head turned too far: … Eye measurements paused until you face the camera again' to gateLabel — though it sits behind the opaque full-screen overlay (main.ts:1716-1722) during the run, so a person calibrating never sees it, which is the defensible version of the complaint. Also mitigating the closed-phase lag: main.ts:3506 pre-warns 'Closing your eyes comes next' during phase one, so the 2.2 s cold-read estimate is an upper bound. The core point — the corpus-ceiling sentence is asserted where the run's own sample counts and pose rejections were never consulted — is confirmed and worth fixing.

**Materiality skeptic: downgraded, severity medium.** The overclaim half is confirmed exactly as written. src/main.ts:1770 tells the person "This is the same limit the corpus showed" — an unconditional causal attribution to the model recall ceiling (docs/iris-occlusion.txt, cited at guidedCalibration.ts:38-42) that the run's own evidence cannot support: resolveGuidedCalibration (guidedCalibration.ts:98-106) sees only two medians and cannot distinguish a physiological ceiling from a late closure. The pose half is confirmed too, and is stronger than the finding argues: stabilityMm is computed only inside `if (gate.kind === "valid")` (main.ts:3088, assignment at :3168), so any frame beyond POSE_LIMITS.maxPitchDeg = 20 (constants.ts:196-203) contributes NO calibration sample at all, yet main.ts:1766 sends the person to "good light" and :1768 to closing on cue, neither naming head angle. The material for a truthful message already exists and is pure: poseValidityMessage (src/core/validityGate.ts:43-52) names the axis, the measured degrees and the limit — and the overlay's rgba(0,0,0,0.88) full-screen backdrop (main.ts:1714-1721) hides that on-page gate label for exactly the duration of the calibration.

_Note._ Downgraded to medium because the finding's headline premise is overstated. It argues the separation refusal most likely fires from reading the nine-word close instruction (~2.2 s of a 3 s phase), but the open phase has already told the person for three full seconds that "Closing your eyes comes next" (main.ts:3506) — at the transition they need only notice it, not read it, so reading latency is a much smaller share of the closed phase than of the open phase. (That asymmetry is exactly why G-Guided b-1, where the overlay appears cold, is the stronger finding.) What survives at medium is real and worth fixing: an in-product causal claim the code cannot evidence, in a project whose contract is that every claim carries its conditions, plus a refusal that never names the most likely cause on the era's target device. Severity does not reach high because nothing measured or published is corrupted — this is refusal text, and a refusal is already the honest outcome. The fix is proportionate and reuses existing pure code; the one thing it must not do is drop the corpus-ceiling sentence entirely — it is true and valuable for the case it was written for (plentiful closed samples, still unseparated), so make it conditional rather than delete it.

#### G-Guided b-5. Nothing verifies the stored line against a real blink, and the person is told 'your detector uses it now'

|                             |                                                                                                                                            |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Severity after verification | **medium**                                                                                                                                 |
| Category                    | missing-capability                                                                                                                         |
| Effort                      | M                                                                                                                                          |
| Raised by                   | Guided blink calibration as a measurement PROCEDURE: how the personal ruler is captured, cued, confirmed, and carried — not its arithmetic |
| Files                       | `src/main.ts:3480`, `src/main.ts:3462-3492`, `src/core/guidedCalibration.ts:240-243`, `test/MANUAL.md:66`                                  |

**Claim.** The procedure produces a threshold and announces it as in force without ever testing it on the event it exists to detect. A single 5-second verification step would catch every failure mode identified in this review — a line above the droop, a line built from a droopy open phase, a line ported to a different camera — and none of them are catchable any other way.

**Impact.** This is the highest-value missing capability on the path, and the cheapest. It is also the only check that tests the whole chain the way it will actually be used: geometry, ruler, line, hysteresis and refractory together, on this person, on this device, right now. Without it the person's only feedback is two numbers whose plausibility they cannot judge.

**Fix as proposed.** After a 'ready' resolve, keep the overlay up for a short verification phase: 'blink three times, normally' with the reducer's count shown live. Store the line only if it caught at least two of three; otherwise show the separation and offer a retry. Keep the refusal path intact — a failed verification is a refusal, not a fallback to a guessed line.

**Evidence as filed.** On resolve the session goes straight to done and freezes (guidedCalibration.ts:240-243), the line is written to memory and storage, and the person reads 'Blink line calibrated at X mm, the midpoint of your Y mm open and Z mm closed aperture. Your detector uses it now and on your next visit.' (main.ts:3480). There is no step in between: no 'blink three times' confirmation, no display of the blink counter incrementing, no accept/retry choice. The only quality gate the whole procedure has is the 0.7 separation ratio (guidedCalibration.ts:101-106), which is a check on the two held phases, not on the line's behaviour against a real blink. The manual script has no verification item either (test/MANUAL.md:66 ends at the stored-line reload check).

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity high.** calibrationSessionStep goes straight from the closed phase to `{kind:'done', result: resolveGuidedCalibration(samples)}` (guidedCalibration.ts:240-243) with no intermediate state. main.ts:3462-3492: on done the session is nulled (:3464), the overlay hidden (:3465), the line written to memory (:3477) and storage (:3478), and the status reads 'Your detector uses it now and on your next visit.' (:3480). No accept/retry branch exists. test/MANUAL.md is 66 lines; line 66 is item 62, the last line of the file, and it ends at the reload/'Recalibrate blinks' check plus the cancel and closure-not-registered refusals — no blink-verification step.

_Note._ Confirmed, and I found evidence that strengthens it: MANUAL.md item 55 (fix #126, the wide-eyed test) verifies the PASSIVE line against real blinks — 'blink normally ten times and check the log: durations should read near your usual 120 to 200 ms'. So the project's own standard already includes testing a line against blinks; the guided path is the asymmetry. Item 62 also still says the calibration 'does NOT change detection yet', which increment 3 (main.ts:3538-3541, effectiveBlinkLineMm) made false — the manual loop was never updated for adoption. One claim in the finding is false: a verification step would NOT catch 'every failure mode identified in this review' — b-6's export gap and b-7's silent cancel are untouched by it. The defect itself is exactly as described.

**Materiality skeptic: downgraded, severity medium.** Verified: calibrationSessionStep goes straight to {kind:'done'} (guidedCalibration.ts:243), main.ts:3462-3492 writes the line to memory and storage and prints 'Your detector uses it now and on your next visit' (main.ts:3480) with no intervening step; test/MANUAL.md has 66 lines and ends at item 62, whose text is also stale — it still says the line 'does NOT change detection yet', which increment 3 (main.ts:3538-3547) made false. The only gate is the 0.7 separation ratio, a check on the two held phases. A verification step is genuinely absent and genuinely cheap, and it is not circular by this repo's own standard: the marker rationale at main.ts:4197-4203 objects to using the instrument's output to LOCATE an event, whereas 'blink three times' makes the count ground truth from the person's action, which is exactly the discipline that rationale endorses.

_Note._ Downgraded from high to medium because the finding's load-bearing claim is overstated: 'a single 5-second verification step would catch every failure mode identified in this review'. It would not. The b-4 failure — a line above the droop band but below the resting aperture — still catches deliberate blinks (which plunge millimetres, per constants.ts:105-114) and would pass 3-of-3, so verification is not a substitute for the resolve-time ceiling. What it does catch is the gross case: a line above the resting eye stalls the re-arm (blink.ts:127-129) and the counter reads 0 of 3. It also inherits the instrument's own ~1-in-6 miss rate (CANNOT_SEE_CLAIMS, cannotSee.ts:18-21), so a 2-of-3 pass bar has a real false-fail rate on a sound line — the bar needs stating as a condition, not asserting as a verdict. No published number is wrong today: the path is opt-in, per-device, and unreachable from the corpus. STATE.md:806 and :845-849 already carry 'a real per-user verification of the personalisation benefit' as the acknowledged next step, which is a stronger check than this one; this is a useful in-session confidence step, not the missing evidence. Worth building, but it is second to b-4's ceiling and b-6's provenance, not first.

#### G-Guided b-8. The person is shown two medians but no evidence of the run's quality; the floors are tick counts a third of the phase can satisfy

|                             |                                                                                                                                              |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **medium**                                                                                                                                   |
| Category                    | ux                                                                                                                                           |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                                                            |
| Raised by                   | Guided blink calibration as a measurement PROCEDURE: how the personal ruler is captured, cued, confirmed, and carried — not its arithmetic   |
| Files                       | `src/main.ts:3480`, `src/core/constants.ts:166`, `src/core/constants.ts:172`, `src/main.ts:3457-3461`, `src/core/guidedCalibration.ts:87-92` |

**Claim.** A line built on the bare 30-sample minimum with 60 frames rejected reads exactly as confidently as a line built on 90 clean frames, and the separation ratio — the single number that says how good the ruler is — is left for the person to compute from two decimals.

**Impact.** It removes the person's ability to judge whether to keep the line or run it again, which is the only quality decision available to them. It also removes the owner's ability to spot a marginal calibration in support or in a pilot session, because the evidence was never displayed and (per the export finding) never recorded.

**Fix as proposed.** Extend the status to name n_open / n_closed and the separation as a percentage — 'from 88 open and 84 closed readings, closed 26 percent of open' — and colour or word a run that only just cleared the floors as 'thin, consider running it again'. Same three numbers into the export.

**Evidence as filed.** The completion status reports personalLineMm and the two medians (main.ts:3480) and nothing else — no sample counts, no separation ratio, no count of frames the pose gate dropped. GUIDED_CALIBRATION_MIN_SAMPLES = 30 (constants.ts:166) over a GUIDED_CALIBRATION_PHASE_MS = 3000 phase (constants.ts:172) is one third of the ~90 frames a 30 fps camera offers, and the floor is a bare length check (guidedCalibration.ts:87-92). The session is fed raw stabilityMm with no rate awareness (main.ts:3457-3461), so a run in which two thirds of frames were rejected produces a status sentence identical to a clean one.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** The completion status (main.ts:3479-3481) interpolates exactly personalLineMm, openMedianMm and closedMedianMm — no counts, no ratio, no drop count. constants.ts:166 GUIDED_CALIBRATION_MIN_SAMPLES = 30; :172 GUIDED_CALIBRATION_PHASE_MS = 3000 (its own comment at :168-171 says 'about ninety frames at 30 fps'), so the floor is one third of the phase. guidedCalibration.ts:87-92 is a bare `samples.open.length < MIN` / `samples.closed.length < MIN` pair. main.ts:3457-3461 passes raw stabilityMm straight into calibrationSessionStep, and collectCalibrationSample (:62-73) silently returns `samples` unchanged on null, so rejected frames leave no trace anywhere the person or the export can see.

_Note._ Confirmed exactly as described. The 30-of-90 arithmetic checks out against the constant's own stated frame budget, and the two-thirds-rejected run does produce a byte-identical status sentence to a clean one, because the drop happens inside a pure function that returns the same shape either way.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** Verified: main.ts:3480 reports only the line and the two medians; GUIDED_CALIBRATION_MIN_SAMPLES=30 (constants.ts:166) over GUIDED_CALIBRATION_PHASE_MS=3000 (constants.ts:172), and the floor is a bare length test (guidedCalibration.ts:87-92) with dropped nulls silently discarded (collectCalibrationSample, guidedCalibration.ts:67-69). One additional condition the finding missed and that strengthens it: the session is fed raw stabilityMm at main.ts:3459 with NO fps gate — blinkMeasurable (main.ts:3559) is applied to the blink reducer, PERCLOS and the long-closure detector, but not to the calibration. So a 10 fps device produces exactly 30 samples per phase and mints a line, and that line then lifts the passive refusal for every later session on that device.

_Note._ Confirmed at medium. The materiality argument is stronger than the finding makes it: roadmap 10.10b shipped on 5 September (ROADMAP.md:177, and commit 8ad1c06 'the conditions lines beside the numbers they scope') establishing as a live standard that a number on the page carries its conditions beside it. The guided status sentence is a number on the page with none — no n, no separation, no rejected-frame count, no delivered rate. It is also the one number a person is asked to accept or re-run, so withholding its conditions removes the only quality decision available to them. The 25 fps blink refusal is still honoured downstream (blinkStep is gated by blinkMeasurable at main.ts:3556-3566), so this does not fabricate a blink count and is not a re-find of that accepted limit — but the RULER can be built below the rate floor and carries no rate condition, which belongs in the same status line and in b-6's export rows. Fix is proportionate and additive: no behaviour change, three numbers the resolver already computes.

#### G-Guided b-9. The calibration contaminates the session it is preparing, and leaves no mark in the export

|                             |                                                                                                                                                      |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **medium**                                                                                                                                           |
| Category                    | defect                                                                                                                                               |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                                                                    |
| Raised by                   | Guided blink calibration as a measurement PROCEDURE: how the personal ruler is captured, cued, confirmed, and carried — not its arithmetic           |
| Files                       | `src/main.ts:3457-3461`, `src/main.ts:3688-3696`, `src/main.ts:3705-3714`, `src/main.ts:3755-3760`, `src/core/longClosure.ts:19`, `src/main.ts:4226` |

**Claim.** Running the preparation step injects a false drowsiness event into the session's own published metrics, raises PERCLOS to the threshold where the score starts penalising, and the export carries no evidence that it occurred.
