**Impact.** It corrupts the numbers of any pilot session in which a participant calibrates mid-run, in a direction that reads as sleepier, and it does so invisibly — the analysis track cannot exclude the span because nothing marks it. It also gives the person a spurious alert at the moment they are most likely to be forming an impression of whether the instrument works.

**Fix as proposed.** Suppress longClosureStep, perclosStep and the blink reducer while blinkCalibrationSession !== null (feeding them null, which every one of them already handles), and auto-write a marker at the calibration's start and end so the span is visible in the export. The suppression is one condition; the marker reuses existing machinery.

**Evidence as filed.** The calibration step is a pass-through: after it, the same frames continue into baselineStep (main.ts:3520), the blink reducer, longClosureStep (main.ts:3688-3696) and perclosStep (main.ts:3755-3760). Nothing gates on blinkCalibrationSession !== null. A deliberate 3 s closure exceeds the long-closure span of 500 ms (longClosure.ts:19), so once frozenShutBaselineMm exists it is counted as a long closure and fires the alert banner (main.ts:3705-3714); it also contributes about 3 s of closed time to the 60 s PERCLOS window, roughly 5 percent, which is exactly where the score's PERCLOS ramp begins. No marker is written — markers exist only when the person clicks (main.ts:4226) — so the exported PERCLOS, long-closure count and alertness score for a session containing a calibration are contaminated with no record that a calibration happened.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** The calibration block (main.ts:3456-3502) is a pass-through: baselineStep at :3520, blinkStep at :3564, longClosureStep at :3688-3696 and perclosStep at :3755-3760 all run on the same frames, and `grep -n blinkCalibrationSession src/main.ts` shows the variable is referenced ONLY at 1700, 1754, 3451, 3456-3464, 3494, 3499 — nothing downstream gates on it. LONG_CLOSURE_THRESHOLD_MS = MAX_BLINK_DURATION_MS = 500 (longClosure.ts:19, constants.ts:104), against a deliberate 3000 ms closed phase; the shut line is 0.4*baseline (longClosure.ts:35) and the repo records fully shut eyes at ~0.33*baseline (longClosure.ts:29-31), so the closure crosses it. alertStep fires (main.ts:3705-3714, ALERT_DEBOUNCE_MS 5000 does not suppress a first event). Markers exist only on the click handler at main.ts:4222-4234.

_Note._ Confirmed, and UNDERSTATED on the PERCLOS magnitude. perclos.ts:9 PERCLOS_WINDOW_MS = 60000 but :31 PERCLOS_MIN_OBSERVED_MS = 15000, so PERCLOS publishes from 15 s of observation — a 3 s calibration closure is up to 20% of the denominator, not 5%. score.ts:33-34 sets PERCLOS_RAMP_FLOOR 0.05 and PERCLOS_RAMP_CEIL 0.15 with PERCLOS_PENALTY_MAX 40, so a calibration run early in a session can drive the PERCLOS contribution to its full 40-point penalty, not merely to the foot of the ramp. One precondition the finding correctly states and I confirm: contamination needs frozenShutBaselineMm, set only once baselineState.kind === 'ready' (main.ts:3683-3685), so it requires calibrating after the 30 s passive window has frozen.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** Verified as a pure pass-through: nothing between main.ts:3452 and 3520 gates on blinkCalibrationSession, and the same frames continue into baselineStep (main.ts:3517), blinkStep (main.ts:3560), longClosureStep (main.ts:3688-3696) and perclosStep (main.ts:3755-3760). The 3 s held closure exceeds LONG_CLOSURE_THRESHOLD_MS = MAX_BLINK_DURATION_MS = 500 (longClosure.ts:19, constants.ts:104) and reaches below 0.40*baseline (the instrument's own shut floor is ~33% of baseline, longClosure.ts:29-31), so it fires a long closure and, via alertStep, the banner at main.ts:3705-3714. The PERCLOS arithmetic is exact, not 'roughly': 3 s in the 60 s window (PERCLOS_WINDOW_MS, perclos.ts:9) is 5.0%, and PERCLOS_RAMP_FLOOR is 0.05 (src/core/score.ts:33) — the closure lands precisely on the point where the 40-point PERCLOS penalty starts. Markers exist only on a click (main.ts:4225-4238), so the export carries no evidence the span happened.

_Note._ Confirmed at medium; correctly rated. It corrupts exported PERCLOS, longClosureCount and the alertness score of any session in which a calibration runs, in the direction that reads as sleepier, with no way for the analysis track to exclude the span — and test/MANUAL.md item 62 has the person calibrate right after starting the camera, so the pilot protocol produces exactly this. It is not yet in any committed published number (no calibrated dataset exists), which is why medium and not high, but validation round II (ROADMAP.md:189) would be the first to carry it. One further exposure the finding missed: blinkCalibrateButton is enabled the moment the camera runs (main.ts:889), so a calibration inside the 30 s learn also feeds 3 s of closed samples into the passive learning window; I worked the arithmetic and the p90/median shift is small (~10% of samples displaced moves the ratio only a point or two), so a spurious ceiling refusal is possible but unlikely — worth suppressing baselineStep for the same reason, not worth claiming as a second defect. Fix is proportionate and breaks no strength: every one of these reducers already handles a null aperture as its documented untrusted path. One caution on the auto-marker — marker indices are user-visible ('Marks: 1 at 12.3 s', main.ts:4213-4221) and are the ground-truth anchor the marker rationale exists for, so an auto-marker needs its own labelled kind rather than silently consuming a participant's numbering.

**Fix as proposed.** Three lines. (1) `return 0 if len(results) == len(tags_found) else 1` — refuse the run, not just the clip. (2) Print the skip/not-measured notices into the report body, not only stderr, so they travel with the number. Contrast analysis/tools/validation_report.py:559-561, `return 1 if refused else 0`, whose rationale is written out at analysis/README.md:41-42: "It exits non-zero when any participant was refused, so a run that could not read everybody cannot be mistaken for a clean one." tools/measure_corpus.mjs:150-157 catalogues three prior incidents of exactly this shape and calls the last "this project's fourth silent success".

(a) The report body is not silent about the denominator: its first line prints "N clips, M annotated blinks, K detected", so a seven-clip run prints "7 clips" against a published "8 clips, 408 annotated blinks" (docs/eyeblink8-result.txt:3), and the per-clip table loses a row. What genuinely remains unguarded is the machine-readable contract (exit 0 on a lost clip) and a human reading stdout directly. Take all three sub-fixes; they are cheap and doctrinally correct.

**Impact.** Benchmark conditions are incomplete; on narrow eyes the 4 mm line mints phantom closures for 30 s; the score's blink history inherits both regimes.

**Fix as proposed.** Withhold the count until a line exists (feed null while learning, matching the refusal rule) or label it provisional; write line source and mm per blink (shared with F-005/F-007); state the two-regime line in eyeblink8-result.txt and MODEL_CARD.

**Evidence as filed.** While learning, blinkLineMm is null and the reducer runs against BLINK_APERTURE_THRESHOLD_MM (4 mm, from the owner's fixture); the label prints 'Blinks: N' beside 'Learning your open eyes'; the comment at :3564-3567 says a line the instrument cannot vouch for must not count blinks. The 2026-08-09 finding measured the 4 mm line at or above the learned line in 6 of 8 Eyeblink8 clips. blinkState resets only in resetSession; the log has no line column. No published surface mentions the fixed-line regime.

**Reproduce skeptic: downgraded, severity medium.** src/main.ts:3569-3572: while learning, blinkLineMm is null and blinkStep is fed stabilityMm against BLINK_APERTURE_THRESHOLD_MM (4 mm, src/core/constants.ts:14-18, from the owner's fixture); src/main.ts:3551 prints 'Learning your open eyes' while src/main.ts:3655-3672 prints 'Blinks: N' in the same frame; src/main.ts:989 blinkState resets only in resetSession, so the learning-period count blends into the learned-line count. docs/evidence/2026-08-09/findings/issue-178-max-blink-duration.md:26 confirms the 4 mm fallback is at or above the learned line in 6 of 8 clips. grep of docs/eyeblink8-result.txt, MODEL_CARD.md, README.md finds no mention of the fixed-line regime; test/MANUAL.md:26 presents the 4 mm blind spot as retired by 4.2.

_Note._ Real disclosure gap and a real two-regime count, but overstated in two ways. The very row cited (issue-178 doc line 26) measured the warm-up regime's cost on Eyeblink8 as zero: learning time 0 gives 357 TP / 9 FP against 357 / 10, so 'every Eyeblink8 figure includes a foreign-ruler regime' is true as a conditions statement with no measured effect on the published figures. And the line is not unrecorded for clips: the per-frame trace writes blinkLineMm (the exact line handed to the reducer, 4 mm or learned) on every frame (src/main.ts:3578-3588, src/core/frameTrace.ts:32,76); only the blink log and the result doc lack it. The narrow-eye phantom-closure claim is arithmetic, not an observation.

**Materiality skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** Mechanism confirmed: src/main.ts:3572 hands the reducer blinkLineMm ?? BLINK_APERTURE_THRESHOLD_MM (4 mm, constants.ts:14-18) while baselineState is learning, and the label prints 'Blinks: N' (src/main.ts:3658-3671) beside the countdown (src/main.ts:3551); the comment at 3564-3567 applies the 'cannot vouch for' rule only to refused sessions. But the regime is measured and its cost is negligible: docs/evidence/2026-08-09/findings/issue-178-max-blink-duration.md:26 reports learning time 0 vs 30 s gives 357/9 vs 357/10 true/false positives on Eyeblink8 — one false alarm — and states the 4 mm line sits at or above the learned line in 6 of 8 clips. Published live numbers are unaffected: the validation protocol places mark 1 after the 30 s learning window (docs/validation-plan.md:43-46), so every scored 'in window' count (docs/validation-round.txt:38-45) is on the learned line, and PERCLOS/long closures are fed null until the shut baseline freezes (src/main.ts:3683-3697, 3755-3760). The fixed-line regime is disclosed to testers at test/MANUAL.md:22 and the learning window at MODEL_CARD.md:70-71, but not as a condition in docs/eyeblink8-result.txt (no mention found).

_Note._ Not an overclaim of any published number: the learning-period regime costs one false alarm on the benchmark and touches no scored live window. What remains is a small disclosure gap (one conditions sentence in eyeblink8-result.txt) and the shared line-column fix from F-005, which resolves this for free. The finding's primary fix would break a strength: feeding null while learning drops every Eyeblink8 blink in each clip's first 30 s, moving the ratcheted F1 and the 10.8 regression baseline for no accuracy gain — the replay showed the warm-up regime is the more sensitive state, not a phantom minter. 'Label provisional' is the proportionate half. Low.

#### F-033. Peak closing velocity and A/V are frame-rate biased 12-28% at 25-30 fps by the single finite difference, and nothing says so

|                             |                                                                                                                                |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Severity after verification | **low**                                                                                                                        |
| Category                    | science                                                                                                                        |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                                              |
| Raised by                   | oculometric                                                                                                                    |
| Files                       | `src/core/blinkShape.ts:1-6`, `src/core/blinkShape.ts:84-96`, `src/core/score.ts:50-56`, `test/MANUAL.md:30`, `ROADMAP.md:203` |

**Claim.** Independent of F-001, a finite difference over a 33-40 ms gap cannot see a 20 ms peak, so slower machines are charged more for the same blink.

**Impact.** Cross-device shape comparisons (DROZY, RLDD velocity, pending phone amplitude comparison) are confounded by rate.

**Fix as proposed.** State the bias in blinkShape.ts and MODEL_CARD; fit a quadratic through the three steepest samples; attach the sampling interval to each row; pin 12.8's check at 25, 30 and 60 fps.

**Evidence as filed.** Through analyzeClosing on a raised-cosine blink (80 ms close): peak velocity reads 83%/88%/97% of truth at 25/30/60 fps and A/V inflates x1.20/1.14/1.03; a 60 ms close gives 72%/80%/95% and x1.40/1.24/1.06. The A/V penalty above 150 ms was priced from one machine at one rate; 12.8 accepts 'within 5%' on a synthetic without naming the fps.

**Reproduce skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** The bias reproduces. Feeding a raised-cosine blink through the real analyzeClosing (src/core/blinkShape.ts:84-96), averaged over 20 sampling phases: 80 ms close -> peak/true 81%/86%/96% and A/V x1.19/1.12/1.03 at 25/30/60 fps; 60 ms close -> 69%/77%/94% and x1.37/1.25/1.05 (finding said 83/88/97, x1.20/1.14/1.03 and 72/80/95, x1.40/1.24/1.06). ROADMAP.md:203's '5%' check indeed names no fps and is only reachable near 60 fps.

_Note._ 'and nothing says so' is false, which is the finding's headline. AUDIT_REPORT_AUG_2026.md:187-192 and :360-382 already document this estimator's attenuation, measure its consequence ('moves the published Spearman correlations by about 0.04. No verdict changes'), state 'about 33 per cent faster at 60 fps than at 25', and explicitly flag the residue the finding claims as new ('What is not written down is the magnitude'); docs/audit/appendix-chunk-4-all-findings.md C4-04 and :200-210 carry the same adjudication. ROADMAP.md:203 already carries a 'within-device-only caveat until 10.9's gap is explained', so cross-device shape comparison is not unguarded either. What survives is placement (blinkShape.ts:3 still says frame rate 'cannot silently rescale it'; MODEL_CARD.md:31 says only 'unvalidated') and naming fps in 12.8's check — a documentation nit, not a medium science defect.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** Reproduced the bias almost digit for digit. Raised-cosine close through the analyzeClosing algorithm (src/core/blinkShape.ts:84-96, single adjacent-sample difference), phase swept 200 ways: 80 ms close reads 83%/88%/97% of true peak velocity at 25/30/60 fps with A/V inflated x1.20/1.14/1.03; 60 ms close reads 72%/80%/95% with A/V x1.40/1.26/1.06; a 150 ms close reads 95%/96%/99%, x1.05/1.04/1.01. The bias is real, monotone in fps, and unstated anywhere - blinkShape.ts:1-6 says peak velocity is 'in mm per second so frame rate cannot silently rescale it', which is true of the units and false of the estimate. MODEL_CARD.md:31 marks closing velocity 'unvalidated' but bounds nothing, and docs/blink-sample-rate.txt is entirely about COUNT catch-rates, never about shape.

_Note._ Confirmed at medium, with one impact claim corrected and one strengthened. CORRECTED: 'slower machines are charged more for the same blink' is essentially false as a score claim. The bias is largest exactly where A/V is smallest, and score.ts:52-55 does not start charging until A/V 150 ms, which for this shape means a ~236 ms close - where the 25 fps bias is ~2%, worth 0 or 1 point of a 15-point ramp. No score meaningfully moves. STRENGTHENED: the confound is not merely cross-device, it is plausibly INSIDE a published table. docs/drozy-result.txt publishes closing velocity rho -0.443 at raw p 0.0490 - the closest thing in the repo to a positive shape result - and the only frame-rate rule applied to that corpus was a floor ('excluded 16, below 25 fps'), so the surviving 20 sessions span the exact 25-to-60 fps band where the estimator's gain runs 83% to 97%. The published caveat stack on those three rows is already heavy (stale code, exclusion bias, 'suggestive and unconfirmed', ROADMAP 10.3 queuing them for re-measure or retirement) and rate is not in it. The forward point is sharper still: a 3.1-hour re-measure under 10.3 would NOT remove this confound, because it lives in the estimator, not in the PR #225 window bug the re-measure exists to correct - so this should be settled before 10.3 is spent, not after. Likewise 10.9's phone-vs-Mac gap: a 96 ms phone blink closes in roughly 32 ms, about one sample at 30 fps, so a velocity comparison there is close to meaningless as currently estimated. The fix is proportionate and sits squarely in the owner's own 10.10a/10.10b idiom - measure the bound, commit the table, print the condition beside the number - and the quadratic-through-three-samples refinement is optional; stating the bias and attaching the sampling interval to each row is the load-bearing half.

|                             |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **low**                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Category                    | science                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Raised by                   | oculometric, roadmap                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Files                       | `src/core/constants.ts:10-12`, `src/core/constants.ts:18`, `src/core/aperture.ts:5-6`, `src/core/blinkLog.ts:59-65`, `MODEL_CARD.md:30`, `AUDIT_REPORT_AUG_2026.md:413-415`, `docs/iris-occlusion.txt:47-50`, `ROADMAP.md:172-173` |

**Claim.** Every mm printed to two decimals is a person-level estimate with an unstated ~4% systematic error plus an unmeasured model chord bias; a 30-minute owner session with a printed scale bar would give the unit its first physical check.

**Impact.** 'Not validated against a physical measurement' is honest but bounds nothing; an oculometrics reviewer asks this first.

**Fix as proposed.** Cite MediaPipe Iris and one WTW study in constants.ts; add the +/-4% to MODEL_CARD:30; row 10.7d with a prediction (ruler within +/-5% of a scale bar at three distances); keep absolute-mm thresholds out of the measurement path.

**Evidence as filed.** 'close to 11.7 mm across in almost every adult', no source; MediaPipe Iris states 11.7 +/- 0.5 mm and WTW norms give SD ~0.42 mm (+/-4% per person at 1 SD). 'Cancels exactly' covers ratio decisions only; absolute-mm consumers remain (4 mm start line, FAINT_BLINK_MM 1.5, the '2.2 to 6.9 mm' range, pupilDiameterMm). The open-eye iris already reads vertically compressed (0.877-0.92), so the chord's own bias is unmeasured. 10.7b/c address cross-eye and scheme identity, not scale.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** src/core/constants.ts:10-12 states '11.7 mm across in almost every adult' with no citation; grep for 11.7 across the repo (ARCHITECTURE.md:56, aperture.ts:5-6, pupil.ts:6/51/90, videoCanvas.ts:69, ROADMAP 3.4/9.2) finds no source and no spread anywhere. AUDIT_REPORT_AUG_2026.md:411-415 defends it as 'one multiplier on the whole feed... It cancels exactly' because 'every decision is a ratio against the person's own baseline' — that premise is false in two live places: src/main.ts:3572 and :3585 feed blinkStep the absolute BLINK_APERTURE_THRESHOLD_MM=4 (constants.ts:18) whenever effectiveBlinkLineMm returns null (guidedCalibration.ts:144-148 — no stored calibration and no baseline yet, i.e. the first 30 s of every uncalibrated session), and src/core/blinkLog.ts:65,81 classifies rows faint against an absolute 1.5 mm. MODEL_CARD.md:30 says 'not validated against a physical measurement' and bounds nothing. docs/iris-occlusion.txt:47-50 and :106 confirm the model's own iris is not circular on an open eye (median 0.92; 0.877 baseline in the miss autopsy).

_Note._ Confirmed as written, with the scope worth keeping straight: ratio decisions (personal baseline, PERCLOS, RLDD/DROZY rank correlations) really do cancel the scale error; the exposure is the pre-baseline 4 mm line, the faint-row cut, and every absolute mm printed or exported.

**Materiality skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** The mechanism is real and the citation gap is real: src/core/constants.ts:10-12 asserts '11.7 mm across in almost every adult' with no source, in a repo that cites Salvucci and Goldberg 2000, Casiez et al 2012 and Massoz et al 2016 by name in code and docs. But the exposure is much narrower than claimed. Traced every consumer: src/core/aperture.ts:121 (openingPx * IRIS_DIAMETER_MM/rulerPx) and src/core/pupil.ts:192 are the only two. Every DECISION downstream is a ratio against the person's own baseline from the same feed - blink line 0.5*baseline, shut line 0.4*baseline (longClosure.ts:37-39), PERCLOS, the 1.25 ceiling - so the scale cancels exactly, which AUDIT_REPORT_AUG_2026.md:413-415 already established as measured, not assumed. Of the surviving absolute-mm consumers the finding lists: BLINK_APERTURE_THRESHOLD_MM (constants.ts:18) is live only as the pre-baseline fallback at src/main.ts:3572 and 3585, and MANUAL item 22 already discloses it ('the 4 mm threshold is tuned to the owner's eyes, not everyone's'); FAINT_BLINK_MM 1.5 (blinkLog.ts:59-65) only greys a table row; '2.2 to 6.9 mm' is prose in that docstring; pupilDiameterMm is on the repo's accepted-dead list. MODEL_CARD.md:30 already publishes 'not validated against a physical measurement'.

_Note._ Downgraded to low. It does not clear the materiality bar: no published conclusion moves, no reader is misled (the disclosure at MODEL_CARD:30 is explicit and correct), and it does not block accuracy of any decision the instrument makes, because every decision is a ratio that cancels the scale. What remains is a real but second-order gap - the exported absolute-mm columns (apertureMm, lastBlinkAmplitudeMm) carry an unstated person-level scale uncertainty, and the 11.7 has no citation in a repo that cites everything else. That is worth fixing precisely because it is cheap: the citation is a one-line edit and 10.7d is a 30-minute session, so the cost-benefit is good even though the severity is low. Two steers if it is done. First, priority order is inverted in the finding: the +/-4% biological spread is the smaller and less interesting term. The bigger unknown is the model's own chord bias, which docs/iris-occlusion.txt:47-50 already hints at - the open-eye iris reads a 0.92 vertical/horizontal aspect ratio, so at least one axis is systematically off, and only a physical scale bar can say which. That is the measurement worth taking. Second, 'keep absolute-mm thresholds out of the measurement path' is already essentially true; the single live one is disclosed, so do not spend a branch removing it.

#### F-035. I-DT thresholds are in eye-width units with no angular meaning (~3 deg vs 0.5-1 deg), merge reading-sized fixations, and the replay uses a different ruler

| Category                    | science                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

| Files                       | `src/core/fixation.ts:14`, `src/core/fixation.ts:18`, `src/core/gazeSmoothing.ts:14`, `src/core/gazeSmoothing.ts:28-31`, `src/main.ts:1936`, `src/main.ts:2104-2111`, `src/main.ts:3341-3349`, `test/MANUAL.md:41` |

**Claim.** The detector resolves quadrant-scale shifts, not reading-scale ones, its input is pre-lagged beyond the minimum fixation it seeks, and no geometry exists to state its resolution in degrees.

**Impact.** Fixation columns and the 'reading vs staring' story are coarser than presented; 12.13 turnover would under-count ~2x during reading.

**Fix as proposed.** State the box in degrees under an explicit geometry or derive it from the calibration slope; one ruler for live and replay; run I-DT on raw offsets or raise the minimum duration above tau; word the panel as 'gaze shifts' until 14.9.

**Evidence as filed.** 0.02 eye widths at ~0.007 units/degree is ~3 degrees summed dispersion; staged fixations with 0.01 hops detect as 2 of 5, 0.015 as 3, 0.02 as 4. MIN_CUTOFF_HZ 1 gives tau 159 ms at rest, longer than the 120 ms minimum fixation, and the detector consumes the smoothed buffer. The replay re-runs at 0.05 screen fractions (~0.01 offset units), so live and replay counts disagree on the same data. MANUAL 41 expects 15-30 reading fixations per 10 s, which ~2 degree word hops cannot produce.

**Reproduce skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** Structure confirmed: FIXATION_DISPERSION_THRESHOLD=0.02 summed over both axes (src/core/fixation.ts:14,33-49) on the SMOOTHED buffer (src/main.ts:3341-3349), while the replay re-runs the same detector at SCANPATH_SCREEN_DISPERSION=0.05 screen fractions (src/main.ts:1936, 2104-2111) — two rulers on the same data. My probe through the real gazeSmoothingStep + detectFixations reproduces the merge table exactly: staged 5 fixations at 30 fps, hops of 0.01/0.015/0.02 detect 2/3/4 of 5. tau=1/(2*pi*1)=159 ms > MIN_FIXATION_DURATION_MS=120 (gazeSmoothing.ts:14,28-31; fixation.ts:18) is arithmetically right. Nothing in core converts offsets to degrees (ROADMAP 14.9 is screen-fraction error only).

_Note._ Two sub-claims fail. (1) MANUAL 41 (item 37) is not unreachable: 10.7 s of 250 ms dwells with 2-degree (0.014 unit) hops yields 26 fixations through the real pipeline — inside its stated 15-30 band — with durations 333-400 ms against its 150-300 ms; under-count is 1.5x, not ~2x (at 1-degree hops it is 14 of 40 with 700-1000 ms durations, which the manual WOULD catch). (2) The 'input pre-lagged beyond the minimum fixation' harm does not reproduce: smoothing left the 0.01/0.015 cases unchanged and moved the 0.02 case from 3 to 4 of 5, i.e. it helped. The coarse box and the two rulers are real, on demo-only columns (fixationCount/fixationMedianMs, csv.ts:23-24; ROADMAP 12.13 unbuilt and 'permanently demo-only').

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** Reproduced the merging. Ran the real I-DT (src/core/fixation.ts:61-118, with dispersionOffset summing BOTH axis ranges at :49) on five staged 250 ms fixations at 30 fps: hops of 0.005/0.010/0.015 units detect 2/3/3 of 5; only at 0.020 do all five separate. The angular scale checks out physically - IrisOffset is iris displacement normalised by corner-to-corner eye width (gazeOffset.ts:41-54), eyeball radius ~12 mm over a ~30 mm fissure gives ~0.0070 units/degree, so FIXATION_DISPERSION_THRESHOLD 0.02 (fixation.ts:14) is ~2.9 degrees of summed dispersion against a literature I-DT box of 0.5-1 degree, and a ~2 degree reading saccade (0.014 units) sits inside the box. The lag claim also holds: smoothingFactor (gazeSmoothing.ts:28-31) with MIN_CUTOFF_HZ 1 (:14) gives tau = 1/(2*pi) = 159 ms, longer than MIN_FIXATION_DURATION_MS 120 (fixation.ts:18), and main.ts:3341-3349 feeds the detector smoothedGaze.smoothed, so the input filter's own lag exceeds the shortest event the detector is asked to resolve. The two rulers are real: live 0.02 offset units vs replay SCANPATH_SCREEN_DISPERSION 0.05 screen fractions (main.ts:1936, 2104-2111). test/MANUAL.md:41 (item 37) expects 'the count climbs toward maybe 15 to 30' reading fixations in 10 s, and unlike items 15, 18, 19 it carries no '(Observed ...)' note - it is an untested expectation.

_Note._ Confirmed at medium, with the honesty half trimmed and the engineering half kept. TRIMMED: the overclaim exposure is smaller than the finding implies. Fixations appear nowhere in MODEL_CARD's measurement table, no published correlation uses them (DROZY/RLDD run on rate, duration, velocity, amplitude, A/V, PERCLOS, long closures), and ROADMAP.md:208 already fixes 12.13 as 'permanently demo-only' with 'Playwright asserts the unvalidated wording'. The live/replay ruler split is also acknowledged in situ at main.ts:2101-2103 ('Structurally the same pair of numbers, only the ruler changes'). KEPT, and this is why it stays medium: two genuine design defects and a missing capability. (1) A detector whose input filter lags 159 ms cannot resolve the 120 ms event it is defined to find - that is self-defeating, not cosmetic. (2) fixation.ts:3-4 names Salvucci and Goldberg while running a box 3-6x their scale with the units never stated, in a repo that elsewhere insists thresholds be DERIVED not chosen (ROADMAP.md:172, 10.7b: 'threshold DERIVED from 10.7a's measured cross-eye distribution... not chosen'). (3) The gaze track has no angular geometry at all, and 14.9 adds screen-fraction error, not degrees - so no gaze number here can ever be compared to oculometry literature. For the owner's stated goal that is a real completeness gap. One caution on the fix: 'run I-DT on raw offsets' could break a working detector. 10.7a measured the APERTURE noise floor; gaze-offset noise has never been measured, and fixation.ts:11-13 justifies 0.02 on the untested assertion that 'smoothed jitter spreads well under this'. Measure the raw gaze noise floor first, in 10.7a's idiom - then the box can be derived instead of argued. Stating the box in degrees, unifying the two rulers, and re-wording the panel are all safe today; retuning it is not.

#### F-038. Re-crossing blinks report the first fragment's duration; slow reopeners are biased short

|                             |                                                                                                                   |
| --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **low**                                                                                                           |
| Category                    | science                                                                                                           |
| Effort                      | M                                                                                                                 |
| Raised by                   | blink-closure                                                                                                     |
| Files                       | `src/core/blink.ts:106-113`, `src/core/blink.ts:136-140`, `docs/blink-rearm.txt:11-14`, `src/core/score.ts:46-48` |

**Claim.** The drowsy slow-reopen blink reads as fast, the opposite of what the duration ramp and DROZY rows look for.

**Impact.** Systematic downward duration bias concentrated where duration should carry information; the score's ramp cannot fire for them.

**Fix as proposed.** Report first sub-line frame to the reopen that clears the re-arm line (or both fragment and envelope) with a 'fragmented' flag; pre-register on the dry run and Eyeblink8.

**Evidence as filed.** Count on the first reopen crossing records that fragment's closedDurationMs; the re-arm gate suppresses the second dip. Probe C: ~333 ms physical closure reports 133 ms. blink-rearm.txt documents this shape on P1.

**Reproduce skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** Probe C reproduces exactly: 133 ms deep, a single frame at 4.2 mm (above the 4.0 line, below the 4.4 re-arm line), 167 ms deep again, reopen — 'C count= 1 reported duration= 133 first-crossing-to-final-reopen = 333'. Same shape with the bounce at 4.5 mm (clearing the re-arm line) gives 'C2 count= 2 duration= 167', so the second fragment's duration is discarded at src/core/blink.ts:136-139 when completedBlink is false. score.ts:46-48 (floor 250 ms, ceil 450, max 15) confirmed, so 133 ms charges 0 where 333 ms would charge 6. docs/blink-rearm.txt:11-14 confirms the P1 shape (25 detections for 10 blinks, re-crossings 200-270 ms later).

_Note._ Mechanically true, but the framing overstates it two ways. First, the gate is not the cause: docs/blink-rearm.txt:79 pre-registered 'Durations: PREDICTION: byte-identical between the two designs on every trace, because the gate touches arming only', and that holds — before the gate the same closure yielded two counts, each still timed per fragment, never as an envelope. The fragment-not-envelope definition is the committed 4.3 definition (closed phase = time below the line), so 133 ms is the definitionally correct answer for a lid that rose to 0.525 of baseline mid-event. Second, 'the drowsy slow-reopen blink reads as fast' does not follow: a genuinely slow closure stays below the line and is timed in full; only a lid that re-crosses ABOVE the blink line — more than half open by the instrument's own ruler — fragments. No measurement of how often this happens is offered (the P1 citation is a count anomaly, not a duration one).

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** src/core/blink.ts:106-109 computes closedDurationMs from the CURRENT fragment only (nowMs - closedAtMs); :136-140 stores exactly that as lastBlinkDurationMs; :95-103 and :127-129 then suppress the second dip until the aperture clears thresholdMm*(1+0.1). I re-implemented blinkStep and ran the Probe C shape (line 4.0 mm; dip to 2.0 for 133 ms, partial reopen to 4.2 — inside the band, above the line, below the re-arm line — then a second dip to 2.5, then full reopen): blinkCount 1, lastBlinkDurationMs 133 for a ~333 ms physical closure. src/core/score.ts:46-48 sets BLINK_DURATION_RAMP_FLOOR_MS 250, so the ramp is unreachable for exactly these blinks. `grep -rn fragment docs/*.txt README.md MODEL_CARD.md src/core/` returns only false-alarm discussion (docs/eyeblink8-result.txt:191,198,221; README.md:152,410) — never duration.

_Note._ Undocumented and it biases a published quantity in the one direction that matters. docs/blink-rearm.txt:80-81 and :109-113 ('durations are untouched', 'every duration keeps its 4.3 definition') are true RELATIVE to the gate — the gate changed no duration — but they say nothing about fragment-versus-envelope, and a reader takes them as coverage. Prevalence is real and setup-dependent: the gate removed 13 Eyeblink8 false alarms of which 11 were fragments sitting on real blinks (~2.7% of 408), and P1 minted 25 detections for 10 blinks. Extra reason to raise its priority beyond what the finding claims: this is a live candidate mechanism for the open 10.9 device anomaly (phones ~96 ms vs Macs 149-166 ms) — a noisier phone reopen fragments more and reads shorter. FIX CAUTION, or it breaks a strength: take only the ADDITIVE variant (emit fragment AND envelope plus a 'fragmented' flag). The other variant in the fix text — report through to the reopen that clears the re-arm line — is the reopen latch that fix #114's review killed for corrupting durations with band time (src/core/blink.ts:19-23), and it would move every published duration, tripping tools/detectorRatchet.mjs against docs/eyeblink8-result.txt's commit anchor.

Consumers: grep shows onScreen reaches only analysis/blinklab/loader.py:37,69 as a column, no metric.

_Note._ Real but already recorded, and the honesty half of the complaint does not hold. src/main.ts:2142-2144 states the choice in a comment — "Off screen keeps its uncalibrated tag even with a profile: that boundary is still the guessed 5.3 threshold, only the quadrants are calibrated here" — and main.ts:2149-2150 prints "off screen (uncalibrated)" on the page. test/MANUAL.md:34 says the same to the operator verbatim and calls its calibration "a recorded follow-up issue", and src/core/gazeQuadrant.ts:11-13 documents the camera-above bias with "5.4's calibration is the cure". So this is a filed, disclosed limit the code still honours, not a defect, and the heatmap never labels anything for a user — it declines to bin. What survives as new is narrow: the exported `onScreen` column and its SPEC.md:37 entry carry no condition tag while neighbouring fields do (fps has "(D1)", baselineMm the freeze note), and no metadata row says a profile was active. That is a conditions gap on one boolean, with impact only on unbuilt rows 12.12 (ROADMAP.md:207) and 14.13 (:248). Low.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** Mechanism verified: src/main.ts:3220 sets frameOnScreen = isOnScreen(meanOffset) on the RAW mean unconditionally, and src/core/gazeQuadrant.ts:32-37 tests the raw offset against the fixed OFF_SCREEN_OFFSET_THRESHOLD = 0.18 (src/core/constants.ts:29). src/core/heatmap.ts:30 uses a different rule entirely (a CALIBRATED ScreenPoint outside the unit square accumulates nowhere). The raw box is zero-centred, and gazeQuadrant.ts:11-13 states the consequence itself: 'zero-centred boundaries assume neutral gaze reads zero. A camera above the screen biases vertical toward bottom.' Export path confirmed: src/main.ts:3837 writes frameOnScreen into the record, src/core/csv.ts:26 ships it as the onScreen column, and the full metadata block at src/main.ts:2342-2387 (source, coverage, device, blink-calibration window, delivery, session, KSS, provenance, pseudonym, light) contains NO gaze-profile row — calibrationMetadataRows (src/core/sessionMetadata.ts:201-214) is the blink/aperture window, not the gaze profile. SPEC.md:37 declares 'onScreen: boolean | null;' with no semantics, unlike its neighbours baselineMm/shutBaselineMm/perclos which all carry inline comments. No published number consumes it yet (analysis/blinklab/loader.py:37,69 only types it).

_Note._ Confirmed at medium, with the scope corrected. The 'two definitions' mechanism is NOT news: it is deliberate and tracked — main.ts:2142-2144 ('Off screen keeps its uncalibrated tag even with a profile'), test/MANUAL.md:38 ('its calibration is a recorded follow-up issue'), and STATE.md:3398 lists it as known issue #90 (calibrated off screen boundary). What survives as a finding is the part outside #90: the EXPORT carries neither the '(uncalibrated)' tag the page shows nor any row saying whether a gaze profile existed, and SPEC.md gives the column no definition — a conditions gap on a column shipped in every numbers-only dataset, against the repo's own 'a measurement without its conditions is not a measurement' rule (sessionMetadata.ts:20-21). The sequencing is the sharper half and the roadmap does not cover it: 12.12 (ROADMAP.md:207) will publish look-away events and an off-screen SHARE, and 14.13 (ROADMAP.md:248) will validate them, both on this box, while #90 sits in a known-issues list with no row — a direct collision with the era rule 'instrument rows land before their claim rows' (ROADMAP.md:41). Proportionality correction to the proposed fix: do NOT redefine the existing onScreen column to mean the calibrated notion when a profile exists. That would make one column mean two things across sessions and break the trailing-append CSV contract csv.ts:26-33 deliberately protects (older headers stay an exact prefix, files stay loadable). Add a new trailing column plus a gaze-profile metadata row, and give onScreen its definition in SPEC.md.

#### F-044. detectFixations is O(n^2) per tick on the 10 s buffer and dominates a per-tick core cost 60-120x the roadmap's quoted 42 microseconds

|                             |                                                                                                                                                                  |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **low**                                                                                                                                                          |
| Category                    | performance                                                                                                                                                      |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                                                                                |
| Raised by                   | gaze, core-numeric, performance                                                                                                                                  |
| Files                       | `src/core/fixation.ts:94-100`, `src/main.ts:3341-3349`, `src/main.ts:3904-3925`, `src/main.ts:2846`, `ROADMAP.md:40`, `ROADMAP.md:258`, `docs/latency.txt:43-58` |

**Claim.** Per-tick cost is quadratic in tick rate and fixation length; the roadmap's 'performance theater' dismissal rests on a subset.

**Impact.** On 120 Hz phones this drops ticks, which feed the processing readout, fps column and 25 fps gate.

**Fix as proposed.** Track running min/max while extending, or run once per photograph/at record cadence; replace spread+filter rebuilds with drop-from-front; add the work to the latency benchmark and amend ROADMAP:40/:258.

**Evidence as filed.** The extension loop re-slices and re-scans from start on every step; main.ts re-runs it every frame. Measured 0.48 ms at 300 samples, 1.46 at 600, 4.2-5.8 ms at 1200 (120 Hz x 10 s still gaze); with the other per-tick buffer rebuilds, ~5 ms per tick before inference or DOM at 120 Hz. latency.txt's 41.8 us timed only five reducers.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** The mechanism is exactly as described. src/core/fixation.ts:94-100: `while (end + 1 < samples.length) { const extended = dispersionOffset(samples.slice(start, end + 2)); ... }` re-slices and re-scans from `start` on every extension step, and dispersionOffset (fixation.ts:32-49) is a full linear scan — O(n²) in fixation length. src/main.ts:3341-3349 rebuilds the buffer with a spread+filter (`withinWindow([...gazeSamples, {...}], nowMs, SPARK_WINDOW_MS)`, SPARK_WINDOW_MS=10000 at main.ts:2846) and calls detectFixations every tick. The tick is requestAnimationFrame, not camera delivery: src/io/frameLoop.ts:8-21 startFrameLoop re-arms on rAF, and its own comment at :71-79 says the camera path "cannot tell a fresh photograph from the same one read again, and on a fast machine most of its ticks are the same one read again"; main.ts:2967 records the measured M5 Max case as "processing 120, reading 30". So 1200 samples in the 10 s buffer is a real configuration. I benchmarked a faithful JS port of fixation.ts on this container: still gaze 300→0.184 ms, 600→0.712, 900→1.490, 1200→2.591, 1800→5.429 ms per call — clean quadratic (4x per doubling). 2.591/0.042 = 62x the roadmap's figure. docs/latency.txt:44-46 does scope its number to five reducers: "baseline, blink, long closure, alert, PERCLOS", and its :59-66 not-included list names only inference, camera and display — not the gaze chain. ROADMAP.md:40 and :258 then generalise that to "the 42 µs core chain".

_Note._ Confirmed, with two corrections to the numbers. My figures run about half the finding's (0.18 vs 0.48 at 300; 2.59 vs 4.2-5.8 at 1200) — machine difference, the 60-120x ratio still holds at the low end. More important: those are the worst case, a single unbroken 10 s fixation. With realistic staged gaze the same port gives 0.101 ms (300 ms fixations), 0.273 (1 s) and 0.705 (3 s) at 1200 samples, and 0.012-0.047 ms at 300. The other per-tick rebuilds (main.ts:3304, :3341, :3511, :3904, :2944) are O(n) object copies, tens of microseconds — so "~5 ms per tick" is detectFixations' worst case plus rounding, not an independent total. Still medium: the quadratic is real, it is re-run every rAF tick, the still-stare case is the instrument's own intended posture, and ROADMAP:40/:258 do rest on a subset the latency doc scoped honestly and the roadmap did not.

**Materiality skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** Quadratic mechanism confirmed at src/core/fixation.ts:88-93: the extension loop calls dispersionOffset(samples.slice(start, end + 2)) inside while(end + 1 < samples.length), so each step re-allocates and re-scans the whole window from the start. Per-tick invocation confirmed: src/main.ts:3349 runs detectFixations(gazeSamples) on every measured frame, on a 10 s buffer (SPARK_WINDOW_MS = 10000, src/main.ts:2846). I measured it in-repo (vitest, temporary file since removed, repo verified clean): still gaze, 300 samples 0.356 ms, 600 samples 0.679 ms, 1200 samples 2.369 ms per call. On a REALISTIC mixed scanpath (300 ms fixations separated by 0.05 hops) the same sizes cost 0.292 / 0.072 / 0.185 ms. 120 Hz processing is real on this project's hardware (docs/blink-sample-rate.txt:603 records 'processing rate (median) 120.0'). Inference runs every tick too (src/main.ts:2993), at about 6 ms locally per docs/latency.txt:63-65. The doc-scope half is exactly as claimed: docs/latency.txt:43-46 scopes 41.8 us to 'the reducers the frame handler runs on the closure-to-alert path... baseline, blink, long closure, alert, PERCLOS', while ROADMAP.md:40 and :258 restate it as 'the core chain is 42 us'.

_Note._ Downgraded to low: the mechanism is real but the stated impact is not supported. Worst case is 2.4 ms, not the claimed 4.2-5.8, and 'with the other per-tick buffer rebuilds, ~5 ms per tick' did not reproduce — the spread+filter rebuilds (main.ts:3341-3348, 3904-3910) are O(n) on 1200-element arrays, microseconds. The 2.4 ms worst case needs 10 s of near-motionless gaze; realistic scanning costs under 0.3 ms. And it cannot reach the impact claimed: 120 Hz degrading to about 104 Hz never approaches the 25 fps blink gate, so no published number, no fps column value and no gate decision moves. What IS material and correctly found is the documentation half: latency.txt conditions its number honestly and ROADMAP:40/:258 strip the condition, turning a five-reducer subset into 'the core chain' — and that conditions-stripped number is the stated reason performance work is refused, in an era whose central lever (13.2, asking cameras for 60 fps) is about frame budget. Fix is proportionate and breaks nothing: tracking running min/max while extending is a pure-core change under the existing 98/95/100/98 floors and the existing dispersion tests pin the behaviour. Amend ROADMAP:40/:258 to say which reducers the 42 us covers; that is the load-bearing half, not the optimisation.

|                             |                                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **low**                                                                                                                             |
| Category                    | risk                                                                                                                                |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                                                   |

**Claim.** Any pursuit-lag or reading-rhythm number from the smoothed signal carries a filter lag comparable to the effect.

**Impact.** 14.10 as worded needs a tolerance wider than its effect or attributes filter lag to the eye.

**Fix as proposed.** Log raw offsets for 14.10/14.12; treat the filter as display-and-fixation only or pre-register its modelled lag per amplitude; add a 0.02-step test.

**Evidence as filed.** At 30 fps a 0.2 step reaches 90% in 100 ms but 0.02 takes 267 ms and 0.01 300 ms; the test asserts only 0.2. Pursuit sinusoids lag 64-89 ms; 300 ms staged fixations after 0.03 hops come out at 233 ms. Raw per-frame noise (|dh| median 0.0011) makes 14.12 feasible on raw offsets.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** The step-response numbers reproduce digit for digit. Simulating src/core/gazeSmoothing.ts:14-23 (MIN_CUTOFF_HZ=1, SPEED_COEFFICIENT=5, DERIVATIVE_CUTOFF_HZ=1) at 30 fps, time to 90% coverage: step 0.2 → 100 ms, 0.1 → 133, 0.05 → 167, 0.03 → 233, 0.02 → 267, 0.01 → 300 ms. Exactly the finding's 100/267/300/233. test/core/gazeSmoothing.test.ts:85-96 asserts the STEP_BUDGET_MS=150 / STEP_COVERAGE=0.9 ladder only for `for (const stepTo of [0.2, -0.2])` — no smaller amplitude is tested. And 0.2 is out of range by the instrument's own rule: OFF_SCREEN_OFFSET_THRESHOLD is 0.18 (src/core/constants.ts:29), so a 0-to-0.2 step lands off screen, and the session-01 fixture's whole horizontal excursion is -0.161 to +0.170. Sinusoids through the same filter: 0.2 Hz/amp 0.15 → 67 ms lag, gain 0.993; 0.2 Hz/amp 0.05 → 100 ms; 0.5 Hz/amp 0.05 → 67 ms — the same order as the 100 ms 14.10 wants to recover (ROADMAP.md:245). Raw per-frame noise on the fixture: median |dh| 0.00124, p90 0.0119 (finding said 0.0011).

_Note._ Confirmed. The sharpest verified point is one the finding only implies: the single amplitude the step test pins, ±0.2, is larger than the entire on-screen offset range the instrument admits, so the ladder is checked nowhere a real glance lives, and at the amplitudes that do occur the filter's own t90 is 233-300 ms at 30 fps. Partial mitigation, which keeps this a risk rather than a defect: ROADMAP.md:245 already words 14.10's check as recovering gain and lag "within tolerance THROUGH the smoothing filter", so the row has booked the concern — but nothing anywhere records the filter's lag-per-amplitude curve, so "within tolerance" is unbounded, and the measured 33-100 ms filter lag against a 100 ms target is precisely the collision the finding names. test/MANUAL.md:35's human check ("the orange lands within a frame or two of the gray, no visible lag") describes t50, not t90.

**Materiality skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** Lag confirmed by my own simulation of src/core/gazeSmoothing.ts:38-63 (temporary vitest file, removed; repo clean). At 30 fps, time to 90% of a step: 0.2 -> 67 ms, 0.05 -> 133 ms, 0.03 -> 200 ms, 0.02 -> 233 ms, 0.01 -> 267 ms. At 60 fps: 50 / 100 / 133 / 167 / 217 ms. Pursuit sinusoids at realistic amplitudes carry 33-100 ms lag with gain 0.90-0.99 (amp 0.03: 100 ms at 0.2 Hz, 67 ms at 0.33-1 Hz). Test coverage as claimed: test/core/gazeSmoothing.test.ts:85-96 exercises only the +/-0.2 step against STEP_BUDGET_MS/STEP_COVERAGE; no small-amplitude case exists. Present-tense reach is nil: the smoothed signal feeds only the live readouts, fixation detection and the heatmap. src/core/csv.ts:10-33 has no gaze column and src/core/frameTrace.ts:72-78 exports only frameIndex, mediaTimeSeconds, apertureMm, blinkLineMm, irisAspectRatio — no offsets are exported anywhere today, and all seven UTA-RLDD features are blink/PERCLOS (docs/uta-rldd-plan.md:88-96).

_Note._ Downgraded to low: this is a correct and well-quantified pre-implementation note, not a defect and not a risk to anything published. It changes no number today because no gaze quantity is exported or published. And the hazard is already named in the row it threatens: ROADMAP.md:245 requires 14.10's synthetics to 'recover gain 0.8 and lag 100 ms within tolerance THROUGH the smoothing filter' — the roadmap has pre-committed to validating through the filter rather than around it, which is the finding's own remedy. 14.10 and 14.12 are both unstarted. The residue worth keeping is the measured table above and one cheap, proportionate action that can land now without touching the filter: add a small-amplitude (0.02) step case to test/core/gazeSmoothing.test.ts so the pinned behaviour is the whole response curve, not just the easy end. Do not weaken the filter to shrink the lag — the adaptive smoothing is a strength (its counterfactual test at gazeSmoothing.test.ts:98-110 proves a fixed filter with the same calm smoothing misses the step budget), and it is what makes fixation dispersion tractable at all.

| Severity after verification | **low**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Category                    | overclaim                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Effort                      | M                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Raised by                   | statistics                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Files                       | `docs/eyeblink8-result.txt:5-7`, `README.md:45-48`, `MODEL_CARD.md:27`, `docs/uta-rldd-result.txt:45`, `docs/uta-rldd-result.txt:69`, `docs/alertness-score-result.txt:48-50`, `analysis/tools/evaluate_eyeblink8.py:115-123`, `analysis/tools/analyse_rldd.py:189-193`, `analysis/tools/compare_alertness.py:58-61` |

**Claim.** A reader cannot see that the three-class lower bound sits well under the 0.50 the README leads with or that the AUC could be 0.60.

**Impact.** 'Results at a glance' invites comparison with published F1s as if precise.

**Fix as proposed.** Add Wilson intervals and subject-level bootstrap CIs to the three tools, print beside the points, extend resultsBlock/resultGuard to carry them.

**Evidence as filed.** Recall 341/408 Wilson 95% CI [79.7%, 86.9%]; balanced accuracy 0.498 about [0.42, 0.57]; binary 0.732 about [0.65, 0.82]; heuristic AUC 0.701 about [0.60, 0.81]. No tool computes an interval; resultGuard and resultsBlock pin point strings.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** Every interval in the finding reproduces. Wilson 95% on 341/408 = [79.7%, 86.9%] — exact match to the finding. Three-class balanced accuracy from the published confusion matrix (docs/uta-rldd-result.txt:48-56: 40/53, 15/48, 20/47) is 0.498 with SE 0.0383 → [0.423, 0.573]; binary from :70-75 (46/53, 28/47) is 0.732 → [0.648, 0.815]; Hanley-McNeil on AUC 0.701 with n=53/47 → [0.599, 0.803]. All four match. No tool computes any of them: grep for wilson/bootstrap/confidence across analysis/ (excluding .venv) returns only `Interval` the frame-range class. The three cited print sites are point-only — evaluate_eyeblink8.py:115-123 emits `Recall {pct} ({tp} of {n} found)`, analyse_rldd.py:189-193 `balanced accuracy {:.3f} majority floor`, compare_alertness.py:58-61 `demo heuristic AUC {:.3f}`. tools/resultGuard.mjs:53-60 parses point strings by regex (`/Recall\s+([\d.]+)%\s+\((\d+) of (\d+) found\)/`) and tools/resultsBlock.mjs builds the README block from that parse, so the guard chain carries nothing but points.

_Note._ Confirmed, with the framing softened. Two mitigations the finding omits: the docs do publish an uncertainty statement of a different kind — permutation nulls with their 97.5th percentiles and p values (uta-rldd-result.txt:57-67, alertness-score-result.txt) — and every interval I computed still clears its chance floor (0.423 > 0.333; AUC 0.599 > 0.5), so no headline direction is overturned. The sentence "the three-class lower bound sits well under the 0.50 the README leads with" is muddled: the README's 0.498 IS the point estimate and it compares against 0.333, not 0.50. What holds up as a genuine overclaim is one the finding did not cite: MODEL_CARD.md:40-42 says published detectors report F1 "between about 82% and about 98%" and "blinklab sits inside that range" — with recall CI [79.7, 86.9] and precision CI [80.2, 87.3], the F1 interval's lower bound sits below that 82% floor, so "inside that range" is not supported at 95%. Medium stands.

**Materiality skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** The absence is real: no confidence interval, Wilson computation, or bootstrap exists anywhere in analysis/blinklab/, analysis/tools/ or the docs (grep for 'confidence interval|Wilson|bootstrap|binomial' returns only STATE.md's CI-bootstrap sense and docs/sampling-bounds.txt:40 discussing a boundary-limited, non-binomial error). analysis/tools/evaluate_eyeblink8.py:115-121 prints recall/precision/F1 as bare percentages; analyse_rldd.py:189-193 and compare_alertness.py:58-61 print bare balanced accuracies and AUCs. tools/resultGuard.mjs parses those exact point strings out of docs/eyeblink8-result.txt and reddens the build on drift. I recomputed the intervals: Wilson 95% on 341/408 = [79.8%, 87.0%], matching the finding; Hanley-McNeil on AUC 0.701 with 53/47 = [0.599, 0.803], also matching. MODEL_CARD.md:40-43 does make the point comparison the finding worries about: 'published detectors on those same eight clips report F1 between about 82% and about 98%. blinklab sits inside that range and below its top.'

_Note._ Downgraded to low, and the category 'overclaim' is wrong — this is a completeness gap, not a misleading claim. Two reasons. First, the finding's stated impact rests on a misreading: the README does not lead the three-class number with 0.50. README.md:45 and docs/uta-rldd-result.txt:45 both state 'balanced accuracy 0.498 where guessing scores 0.333' — the 0.500 belongs to the separate binary number. A three-class interval of roughly [0.42, 0.58] therefore undercuts nothing; its lower bound is comfortably above the 1/3 floor it is actually compared to. Second, the project already publishes a LARGER uncertainty statement and made it a roadmap row: MODEL_CARD.md's 'Measurement uncertainty' section (built by ROADMAP.md:165, row 10.1b, and held by resultGuard) reports that precision swings 12.4 F1 points with video preparation and that blink duration is device-conditioned — swings that dwarf the +/-3.6-point Wilson half-width — plus commit-binding via tools/detectorRatchet.mjs. Both drowsiness results also carry 1000-shuffle permutation p-values, which are the correct 'is it above chance' statement. So the reader is given a bigger and more relevant caveat than the missing interval. One sub-point is genuinely sharp and worth acting on cheaply: the AUC 0.701's lower bound (~0.60) sits essentially on the permutation null's own 97.5th percentile of 0.588 (docs/alertness-score-result.txt:56), which is informative about how marginal that effect is. Adding intervals is a real improvement; it is not a correction of a misleading number, and the M-effort of threading them through resultGuard/resultsBlock should queue behind F-047.

#### F-048. Label permutation ignores the one-video-per-state design; a within-subject contrast would answer the per-person question the docs call unanswerable

|                             |                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **low**                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Category                    | missing-capability                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Effort                      | M                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Raised by                   | statistics                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Files                       | `analysis/blinklab/rldd.py:539-543`, `analysis/blinklab/alertness.py:404-406`, `docs/uta-rldd-plan.md:189-192`, `docs/alertness-score-plan.md:163-170`, `MODEL_CARD.md:34`, `docs/alertness-score-result.txt:96-100` |

**Claim.** The control is valid for 'labels carry no information' but not the design-respecting null, and the cheapest route to the missing per-person evidence sits unused.

**Impact.** The project keeps stating 'per-person: unvalidated' while holding the data to test it.

**Fix as proposed.** Pre-register then run within-subject permutation as a second null and the paired share of subjects whose drowsy video scores drowsier, with sign-test p and CI, reported beside the cross-subject numbers.

**Evidence as filed.** rng.permutation(y) across all 148 videos produces assignments the design cannot generate; each subject has exactly one alert/low/drowsy video, so ~45 within-person pairs exist in already-measured CSVs.

**Reproduce skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** The code reads as described: analysis/blinklab/rldd.py:539-543 `shuffled = rng.permutation(y)` over the whole label vector, and analysis/blinklab/alertness.py:404-406 the same. With one video per state per subject, a global permutation can hand one subject three 'alert' labels, which the design cannot produce — that part is correct. But the decisive fact is that this is exactly what was pre-registered: docs/uta-rldd-plan.md:146 says the labels "are permuted **across videos** 1000 times from the fixed seed". The code implements the committed plan verbatim, so writing a restricted permutation instead would have been the contract violation. The proposed extra analysis is also barred by a standing rule: ROADMAP.md:39 — "The UTA-RLDD labels have been read twice and are read exactly ONCE more: one batched, pre-registered v2 read (12.18) carries every new signal family together. Per-feature dips into the same 148 videos are refused" — with ROADMAP.md:213 (12.18) and :255 naming the batched read as the only remaining route.

_Note._ The permutation observation is technically correct and the finding is careful to concede the control is valid for its stated H0, but 'missing-capability at medium' overstates it three ways. First, no defect: the null matches its pre-registration. Second, the fix as worded is a per-feature dip the era rule explicitly refuses; it would have to be folded into 12.18, which the finding does not mention. Third, the paired within-subject contrast would not answer the question the docs call unanswerable. docs/alertness-score-plan.md:163-170 defines that gap as "a live dial for one person over time", which two videos recorded on separate occasions cannot test, and docs/uta-rldd-result.txt:127-131 already names the confound a paired test inherits unchanged — "the alert and drowsy videos differ in more than drowsiness (time of day, session order, how the person sat)". Worth logging as a candidate rider for 12.18; not a medium finding today. (I could not verify the ~45 pairs directly — no RLDD CSVs are committed; the usable counts 53 alert / 47 drowsy at uta-rldd-result.txt:48 cap it at 47, so ~45 is plausible.)

**Materiality skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** Mechanism confirmed: analysis/blinklab/rldd.py:541 does rng.permutation(y) over all usable videos inside shuffle_control, and analysis/blinklab/alertness.py:405 does the same over the binary set — neither respects the one-alert/one-lowvigilant/one-drowsy-per-subject design (class balance 53/48/47 over 54 subjects, docs/uta-rldd-result.txt:34-35). The paired data does exist in already-measured CSVs. But the direction is conservative: breaking the one-of-each constraint lets a shuffled assignment correlate labels with subject identity, which can only raise the null, and the recorded null already sits at mean 0.310 against a 1/3 floor (docs/uta-rldd-result.txt:57-58), so the published verdict survives a stricter design-respecting null a fortiori. The collision is explicit: ROADMAP.md:39 — 'The UTA-RLDD labels have been read twice and are read exactly ONCE more: one batched, pre-registered v2 read (12.18) carries every new signal family together. Per-feature dips into the same 148 videos are refused; that drip is how evidentiary freshness dies' — and ROADMAP.md:255 records that a separate immediate read was already 'merged into 12.18, not killed'. The per-person gap is defined narrowly: docs/alertness-score-plan.md:163-170 and docs/alertness-score-result.txt:97-100 both define it as cross-subject classification versus 'a live dial for one person over time'.

_Note._ Downgraded to low. The methodological observation is correct and worth recording, but two of the finding's three legs do not hold. First, the invalid null is conservative, not permissive — it cannot have manufactured the published positive, so nothing already published is at risk. Second, the proposed fix runs straight into a documented, deliberate era rule: a new pre-registered paired sign test on the same 148 videos is exactly the 'per-feature dip' ROADMAP:39 refuses, and ROADMAP:255 shows the project has already declined one such standalone read on these labels. The right home is 12.18 (ROADMAP.md:213), as a named rider alongside the other families. Third, 'the missing per-person evidence' overstates what the paired test would deliver: one alert and one drowsy video per subject, recorded on different days, removes between-person variance but keeps every within-person confound the plan itself names (time of day, session order, how the person sat — docs/uta-rldd-plan.md:190-192), and the gap the docs call unanswerable is a LIVE dial over time, which a two-video pair does not close. What can be done now without touching the labels' read budget is the narrow half: replace the global permutation with a within-subject one as a robustness check on the ALREADY-published number, in the same spirit as the existing seed-robustness reseeds — it can only confirm or weaken the standing claim, it adds no new one. The paired directional test belongs in the 12.18 plan, pre-registered.

**Fix as proposed.** Append the chance rate to drozy-result.txt; require future within-subject bars with chance rate below 0.05.

**Reproduce skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** Arithmetic checks out. analyse_drozy.py:212-217: passes_p = c.p_holm < HOLM_ALPHA, passes_within = agree >= MIN_AGREEING_SUBJECTS (constants 0.05 and 3), and `elif passes_p or passes_within` emits "suggestive and unconfirmed". docs/drozy-result.txt:37-43 shows every Holm p >= 0.3427, so all three suggestive rows at :58,:60,:61 (closing velocity 3/5, amplitude/velocity 3/5, blink amplitude 4/5) are granted by the within-subject bar alone. `python3 -c "from math import comb; sum(comb(5,k) for k in (3,4,5))/32"` -> 0.5, so P(>=3 of 5) under no effect is exactly 16/32. _within_subject_agreement (analyse_drozy.py:66-94) compares only the lowest-KSS and highest-KSS session per subject, so each subject is a fair coin under the null. What F-049 genuinely adds is a correction to that audit's dismissal: chunk-4-measurement.md:156-157 says "No published text uses that label" on the basis of a grep over README/MODEL_CARD/STATE/ROADMAP (appendix-chunk-4-all-findings.md:359) that never looked at docs/drozy-result.txt, where the label appears three times and frames the re-measure decision. Harm is contained though: drozy-result.txt:65-68 states an unambiguous null ("Nothing cleared both bars"), and README.md:46 reports the DROZY result as a null with no mention of the suggestive rows, so no headline rests on a coin flip. Low, and the one-line fix (print the chance rate beside the bar) is right.

**Materiality skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** analysis/tools/analyse_drozy.py:42 MIN_AGREEING_SUBJECTS=3, applied at :212 as `agree >= 3` against the 5 multi-session subjects; the sign compared is derived from the observed rho (:210), so under no effect each subject is a fair coin and P(>=3 of 5)=16/32=0.5. Confirmed. But docs/drozy-result.txt prints the Holm p beside every label (0.3427 to 0.5275, :48-54), the label itself contains the word 'unconfirmed' (:58-61), and the document's own headline is a null: 'Nothing cleared both bars ... do not detectably track self-reported sleepiness' (:65-67). README.md:45 carries the DROZY result outward as 'no - a null result', so nothing suggestive is published upstream. The 10.3 decision (ROADMAP.md:167) has an independent and stronger motivation already in the file: docs/drozy-result.txt:20-31 states those three shape columns were produced by code carrying 'this project's one genuine arithmetic error', fixed in PR #225 and never recomputed.

_Note._ Mechanism real, materiality low. The verdict label's ~~50% null pass rate is a genuine unstated condition and the repo's own 'every number carries its conditions' rule makes appending the chance rate worth doing (effort S, no strength touched). It is not a medium: the reader sees p~~0.34-0.53 in the same table, the label says 'unconfirmed', the published headline is a null, and the 10.3 re-measure/retire decision rests on the acknowledged PR #225 arithmetic error, not on these labels - if anything the chance rate strengthens the cheaper 'retire' option. Fix must be an appended note, never an edit to the pre-registered rule or the scored verdicts (docs/drozy-analysis-plan.md:97-106), or it breaks the pre-registration strength.

**Claim.** The criterion was nearly unfalsifiable and the summaries read as a pass.

**Impact.** A reader takes 'generalises to live webcams' from a test that would have passed a detector missing two of three volunteers.

**Fix as proposed.** Add '0 of 3 sound sessions; 95% upper bound ~56%' to README and MODEL_CARD; express round-II criterion 1 as a proportion with a minimum sound count.

**Evidence as filed.** Exactly 3 of 6 sessions were sound, so the unchanged 'three or more missed' rule could only fail at 3/3; observed 0/3, Wilson 95% upper bound on the miss rate 0.56.

**Reproduce skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** Half confirmed, half refuted by the finding's own citations. Confirmed: docs/validation-plan.md:238-239 fixes an absolute threshold ("Three or more of the six sessions come back missed"); :420-433 later restricts criterion 1 to SOUND sessions and guards only against "more than half" being excluded; docs/validation-round.txt:57-59 shows exactly 3 excluded (P3, P4, P5), i.e. exactly half, so the guard did not trip and an unchanged threshold of 3 was applied to a pool of 3 — it could only fail at 3/3. Wilson 95% upper bound for 0/3 recomputed: (0 + 0.640266 + 0.640266)/2.28053 = 0.5615, so ~56% is right. _Note._ Downgraded to low. The structural point (an absolute miss threshold applied to a pool shrunk to that same size) is real and stated nowhere in those terms, and no uncertainty interval appears anywhere — the round-II fix (a proportion plus a minimum sound count) is good advice. But the headline charge collapses: the n IS published in the primary record and in README's own section, and the finding cites README.md:66-68 as evidence of the omission when that is precisely the sentence carrying the n. What actually lacks the n is the one-line README.md:47 bullet and MODEL_CARD.md:74-75 ("missed nothing on the sessions whose baseline worked"), neither of which claims a pass — both use the plan's own "criterion not met" wording.

**Materiality skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** The arithmetic holds: docs/validation-plan.md:238-242 fixes an absolute bar ('Three or more of the six sessions come back missed'), docs/validation-plan.md:420-433 later restricts it to sound sessions without rescaling the bar, and exactly 3 of 6 were sound, so it could only fail at 3/3. BUT the claim that 'criterion not met carries no n' is refuted by the files: docs/validation-round.txt:58-59 prints 'at 3 or more missed among the 3 sound sessions: 0 missed (none). not met', names all three exclusions, and :77-79 states the exclusion guard 'came within one session of refusing to evaluate the detector at all'; README.md:66-68 says 'Among the three sessions with a working baseline, zero of the scripted blinks were missed'; MODEL_CARD.md:69-75 gives the same with 'three of six ... unusable'. docs/validation-round.txt:200 says 'six people is six people: this round is a smoke test of generality, not a study.' The forward-looking half is moot: docs/validation-plan-round2.md:23-25 pre-registers NO detector-generalisation criterion at all ('a handful of people cannot establish a recall figure and none will be published'), so the unrescaled-bar error is not queued to repeat.

_Note._ Downgraded from medium to low. The unfalsifiability is real and is nowhere stated in those words, so adding '0 of 3 sound; 95% upper bound ~56%' to README/MODEL_CARD is a cheap honesty gain. But two load-bearing parts of the finding fail on the files: the n IS published in three places, and the summaries use the pre-registered words 'not met', not 'passed'. The round-II criterion redesign the fix proposes has no target, because round II deliberately makes no detector claim. Do not let this fix add a new absolute threshold to round II - that would import the defect the finding is about.

The missing track ended/mute listener is a re-find of published C5-12, whose surviving residue is stated in the same terms the finding uses — "the app never NAMES the cause... a missing diagnostic message... not a false measurement. Low." What IS new and not covered by that audit is the sentence: deliveryRate.ts postdates the audit (its comment cites an M5 Max measurement of 24 August 2026) and deliveryRateMessage does misattribute a stopped camera to browser incapability. That is a wrong sentence beside correctly-refused numbers, so the render fix ("no frames in the last 5 s") is worth doing; gating record writing on a delivered frame is not, since the records already read absence.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** src/core/deliveryRate.ts:119-124 documents null deliveredFps as 'no delivery callback in this browser, a session a frame old, or a camera that has stopped', and :167-170 renders all three as 'Camera delivery: this browser does not report it'. src/main.ts:2970 computes `evidenceFps = delivery?.sampledFps ?? fps`, so a stalled camera hands the risk gate the still-ticking rAF processing rate and the warning cannot fire (:2971-2977). No track lifecycle handling exists anywhere: a repo-wide grep for ended/mute/readyState on MediaStreamTrack finds only src/io/camera.ts:42 (stop) and src/main.ts:691, which is the video element's 'ended' and returns unless frameSource==='file'. processFrame keeps drawing and calling detectForVideo on whatever the element holds (:2983-2996), so records keep accruing from a frozen photograph, and the session's own conditions would report face seen 100% for that stretch.

_Note._ Confirmed at medium. The message half is a false statement about the viewer's browser; the serious half is the second one - a frozen frame keeps producing per-second rows, which is fabricated stillness (zero blinks, a static PERCLOS) in a file whose conditions positively assert good data, and that is the null-never-zero rule broken by omission rather than by a zero literal. It needs a hardware event (USB webcam unplugged, camera seized by another app, OS privacy toggle) so it is not routine, which is why medium and not high; but it is undetectable after the fact, which is why it is not low. Prioritise the track ended/mute handler and gating record writes on a delivered frame over the wording; ship the wording change together with F-053's misattribution so the sentence is corrected once. Do not weaken the honest null on deliveredFps to do it - 'no frames in the last 5 s' must stay distinct from 'this browser does not report it', or the fix trades one false fact for another.

**Claim.** The guard built after two wrong counts enforces a third; the same substring technique underlies the recall/precision checks.

**Impact.** A published number held wrong by a guard.

**Fix as proposed.** Count from the runner and assert static == runtime, or say 'about 950'; scope number checks to their section.
