**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** Ran `npx vitest run`: 94 files, 962 tests passed. Ran the guard: `actualUnitTestCount('.')` returns 952. tools/resultGuard.mjs:111-129 counts `/\b(?:it|test)\(/g` occurrences in source text, so the loop at test/core/rulerFit.test.ts:56-57 (6 published ratios) and the loop at test/core/blinkClosedForm.test.ts:112-113 (BLINKS has 6 entries, test/core/blinkClosedForm.test.ts:75-82) each contribute 1 statically and 6 at runtime: 952 + 5 + 5 = 962 exactly. test/tools/resultGuard.test.ts:145-158 asserts stated === actual for README.md, STATE.md and ARCHITECTURE.md, which is why all three publish 952 (README.md:595, STATE.md:18, ARCHITECTURE.md:18). Its own self-check (test/tools/resultGuard.test.ts:137-144) is only `toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(486)` under a comment claiming it 'counts this suite the way the runner does'.

_Note._ Confirmed, and the arithmetic closes exactly. I did not verify 'PR #403 reports 962' (no network check made), but that claim is not load-bearing: my own runner output is 962 against a guard-enforced 952. The extension that 'the same substring technique underlies the recall/precision checks' is weaker — those compare doc text against docs/eyeblink8-result.txt rather than recomputing, a different failure mode — so I would drop that clause and keep the count defect.

**Materiality skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** Ran both counts. `actualUnitTestCount('/home/user/blinklab')` (tools/resultGuard.mjs:112-129, `source.match(/\b(?:it|test)\(/g)`) returns 952; `npx vitest run` reports 'Tests 962 passed (962)' across 94 files. The 10-test gap comes from it( inside loops — test/core/rulerFit.test.ts:56-57 emits 6 from one token, test/core/blinkClosedForm.test.ts:112-113 emits 6 from one token. The guard forces README.md:595, STATE.md:18 and ARCHITECTURE.md:18 to state its own number (test/tools/resultGuard.test.ts:146-158). The self-check comment says 'counts this suite the way the runner does' and then asserts only toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(486) (test/tools/resultGuard.test.ts:137-144), so it never checks the property it claims.

_Note._ Mechanism confirmed, severity too high. Nothing here moves a scientific claim: it is suite size, the error understates rather than overstates (952 < 962), and no reader draws a wrong conclusion about the instrument. What deserves fixing is the false comment and the vacuous self-check, not the digits — 'about 950' or a runtime comparison both discharge it. One claim in the finding is only half right: the recall/precision checks do not inherit the wrong-number problem, because they parse the truth out of docs/eyeblink8-result.txt (tools/resultGuard.mjs:44-94); their weakness is toContain placing a right number in any sentence, which is a different and smaller defect.

**Claim.** Strangers are asked to email these files with the contents disclosed only in a planning document.

**Impact.** Health-adjacent self-report plus device fingerprint, undisclosed, against a checkable-privacy contract.

**Fix as proposed.** A tested constant beside the export buttons and in README derived from the metadata keys; offer a reduced user agent unless the full string is needed.

**Evidence as filed.** Full userAgent, core count, screen, DPR, camera label, pseudonym, KSS and clip filename are written; validation-plan.md admits 'together those identify a machine'; the export button is bare; the pilot's consent script does not list the fields.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** src/io/deviceInfo.ts:60-66 collects `navigator.userAgent` in full, `navigator.hardwareConcurrency`, screen w/h, viewport w/h, `devicePixelRatio`, orientation; :52-56 the camera label, resolution, declared fps and facingMode. src/core/sessionMetadata.ts:139-150 writes every one of them as `# camera:`, `# user_agent:`, `# hardware_concurrency:`, `# screen:`, `# device_pixel_ratio:` … rows into the export. src/core/sessionMetadata.ts:364-367 adds `# participant_pseudonym:`. src/core/kss.ts:61-68 adds `# kss_before:` / `# kss_after:` and always writes both lines. src/core/frameClock.ts:213-222 adds `# clip: <filename>`. The UI is bare: src/main.ts:2680-2683 `exportButton.textContent = "Export CSV"` and :2695-2699 `exportBlinksButton.textContent = "Export blink log"`, with no adjacent text listing contents. src/core/notice.ts:19-27 (DEMO_NOTICE) and README.md:587 say only that nothing is uploaded, never what the file holds. docs/validation-plan.md:293-295 concedes it in a planning document: 'They do carry the camera's name, the full user agent string, the screen and viewport size, and the core count. Together those identify a machine.'

_Note._ Two wording imprecisions that do not change the verdict. The plans never say 'email' — docs/validation-plan.md:293 says 'The two files a person sends', transport unspecified. And docs/assessment-pilot-plan.md:57-59 does put 'what the files contain' into the consent preamble read aloud, so it is not literally undisclosed to pilot participants; what is true is that no committed script or page string ENUMERATES the fields, so the disclosure depends on the moderator improvising. Partial mitigation the finding omits: the metadata is plain `# key: value` lines at the top of a CSV the participant downloads and can read. Medium still holds — this is a device fingerprint plus a health-adjacent self-report leaving the user's control on a repo whose stated dataset contract is numbers-only and pseudonymous, and the fix (a tested constant beside the buttons, derived from the metadata keys) is genuinely small.

**Materiality skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** The field inventory is accurate: src/io/deviceInfo.ts:52-66 collects full navigator.userAgent, hardwareConcurrency, screen, viewport, devicePixelRatio, orientation and camera label; src/core/sessionMetadata.ts:139-150 writes them as `# key: value` rows; :364-366 adds participant_pseudonym; KSS rows follow. The export button (src/main.ts:2680-2683) carries no disclosure text — I grepped main.ts and core/exportStatus.ts and found none — and README.md:22 and :587 do not mention the metadata. But the central claim, 'disclosed only in a planning document', is refuted. docs/UI.md:340-348 discloses it in full under the heading 'What the CSV export contains, since the person may send it to someone', naming in bold the camera's name, negotiated resolution and declared frame rate, the facing mode, the user agent, core count, viewport, screen, pixel ratio and orientation. docs/UI.md:356-357 goes further and records the line the project deliberately drew: 'deviceId is deliberately not collected: it is a stable per-origin identifier for one camera, which is a fingerprint rather than a measurement.'

_Note._ Downgraded because the repo reasoned about exactly this risk, drew a defensible line, and wrote it in the UI contract document — that is the opposite of undisclosed. What survives is a placement gap, not a disclosure gap: the text is not at the point of use (page) or in README, and assessment-pilot-plan.md:57-59's consent bullet says 'what the files contain' without enumerating, so the moderator improvises. Harm is bounded on every axis: the file lands on the exporter's own disk, the fingerprint is of their own machine, transfer is voluntary, and the pilot recipient is the maintainer who already holds the participant's email. The fix is right and cheap, and should follow src/core/notice.ts's own precedent — a tested constant so the sentence cannot drift between page, README and export — but derive it from the metadata key list so it cannot go stale, and skip the reduced-user-agent option: it would degrade the device-conditioning evidence the project's own open questions depend on (the 96 ms vs 149-166 ms phone/Mac gap, ROADMAP.md row 10.9), which is a strength, for a fingerprint the maintainer already has by email.

Over the last 60 commits: 3.47 doc files per commit (claimed 3.4); doc files are 208 of 335 total file touches = 62.1% (claimed ~60%); STATE.md appears in 50 of 60 (claimed 51). 30 of the last 120 commit messages contain "No LEARNING entry" (exact). 17 commits carry a 2026-09-05 date, running 02:09 to 09:48 — under 8 hours (exact). Independent corroboration the finding did not have: `npx vitest run` at HEAD reports "Tests 962 passed (962)", while README.md:595, STATE.md:18 and ARCHITECTURE.md:18 all state "952 unit tests" and PR #403's body — written for the same commit — states "962/962". Three prose documents carry the same stale number; the PR body carries the right one.

_Note._ One phrasing to soften: STATE.md:1-21 is a close paraphrase of PR #403's "What this changes", not a duplicate — same mechanism, same citations, reworded and extended with the phase tally. The thesis is otherwise better supported than the finding argued, since the 952-vs-962 drift is a live instance of exactly the failure the proposed fix ("any number in more than one document is generated", "PR body as canonical narrative") targets.

**Materiality skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** The measurements hold. Living prose: 13,327 .md lines excluding docs/audit, plus 4,975 lines across 25 docs/*.txt; docs/audit adds 8,049. STATE.md 3,432 lines, LEARNING.md 1,191 lines / 309 KB, README.md 648. Over the last 60 commits, 208 of 335 file touches are .md/.txt (62%), 3.47 doc files per commit, STATE.md in 50 of 60. 17 commits on 2026-09-05. But the LEARNING-waiver figure does not mean what the finding says: cross-tabulating the last 120 commits, 39 touch src/, of which 29 wrote an entry and 10 waived (26%); the other 20 waivers sit on commits that touch no src at all, where CONTRIBUTING.md:46-47 never required an entry. That is over-compliance noise, not a decaying rule. Meanwhile the guard layer the finding calls "the smallest part of the volume" is 13 modules in tools/ (detectorRatchet, claimGuard, resultGuard, drozyGuard, corpusGuard, exportGuard, modelProvenance, uiGuard, learningGuard, contrastGuard, bundleGuard, cannotSeeBlock, resultsBlock), and the pattern already works where it is applied (resultsBlock.mjs generates README's results block; resultGuard pins MODEL_CARD's figures to the result files).

_Note._ Downgraded to low. The diagnosis is correct and the numbers are real, but the severity and half the fix are not. (1) It double-counts: the demonstrated harms of prose drift are already F-068 and F-069; F-070's own stated impact ("the next audit finds the same drift class with new numbers") is a prediction, not an additional harm. (2) It names as a defect the discipline that is this repository's principal strength — pre-registration, bound-to-commit numbers, a written note per increment — and the audit's rule is that a recommendation breaking a strength is a net loss. (3) Two of the four fix items collide with the record or weaken durability: "STATE holds the STATUS block plus one line per PR" collides with STATE.md:271-274, where the append-only format was deliberately adopted and the snapshot rule retired in writing, and the finding does not acknowledge that; "PR body as canonical narrative" moves the project's record into GitHub's database and out of the clone, cutting against PROJECT.md:36 ("A stranger can clone and run it in under 5 minutes") and against the repo's whole self-contained-evidence posture. (4) The LEARNING-waiver evidence is misread, as measured above. What survives and is worth keeping is the non-colliding half — generate any number that appears in more than one document (the resultsBlock/resultGuard pattern already proven here), and archive docs/audit and the August trackers — and the second of those is already inside F-069's fix.

#### F-071. No cued ground-truth capture tool; every live claim rests on the count-ten-between-marks protocol the round already showed is contaminated

|                             |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **low**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Category                    | missing-capability                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Effort                      | M                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Raised by                   | roadmap                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Files                       | `docs/participant-instructions.md:55-59`, `docs/validation-round.txt:102-104`, `docs/validation-round.txt:181-200`, `ROADMAP.md:175`, `ROADMAP.md:188`, `ROADMAP.md:221`, `ROADMAP.md:240`, `ROADMAP.md:248`, `src/core/lightSchedule.ts:22-29` |

**Claim.** A cued schedule rendered by the existing overlay pattern yields per-event caught/missed/latency at zero privacy cost and is absent from Phases 10-13.

**Impact.** 10.9, 11.6 and 13.3 will produce compliance-contaminated counts.

**Fix as proposed.** Row 11.0a/b: pure cue schedule and scorer with refusals, then overlay and export rows; re-point 10.9, 11.6, 13.3, 14.5.

**Evidence as filed.** Three of six pressed Mark more than twice, one closed inside the blink window, markers stamp ~1 s early, a missed blink writes no row; 10.9, 11.6 and 13.3 repeat the protocol; lightSchedule already implements a timed logged schedule.

**Reproduce skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** The contamination evidence is real and correctly cited: docs/participant-instructions.md:54-62 is the two-marks/ten-blinks protocol; docs/validation-round.txt:181-188 records "Three of six pressed the mark button more than twice, one performed the closure inside the blink window"; :103-104 records "markers are stamped up to about a second early"; :193-195 records "a missed blink writes no row". src/core/lightSchedule.ts:19-50 plus 9.4b's overlay and export metadata are a shipped timed-logged-schedule precedent, as claimed. But three parts do not hold. (1) ROADMAP.md:175 (row 10.9) reads "the same clip stepped on phones and Macs" — a stepped recorded clip with no human protocol and no Mark presses; it does not repeat the protocol, so a third of the impact sentence is wrong. Only ROADMAP.md:188 (11.6) and :221 (13.3, "repeat the 10-deliberate-blinks protocol") actually do. (2) "No cued ground-truth capture tool" is not the state of the ladder: ROADMAP.md:240 (14.5) commits "a per-blink caught/not-caught tally", :245 (14.10) is "schedule, overlay, bounded offset log", :246 (14.11) is task-block schedule machinery, and :248 (14.13) is a "cue schedule and metadata pure and tested" with an ignore-the-cues adversarial synthetic that must fail. (3) The compliance problem already has a committed remedy: docs/validation-plan-round2.md:85-90 rule 6 makes round II moderated, quoting round I's exact three failures, and docs/validation-round.txt:205-212 queues four rules; ROADMAP.md:189 (11.7) is that frozen plan.

_Note._ Real but overstated. What survives is a sequencing preference — the cue machinery lands in Phase 14, after the 11.6 and 13.3 claims that would benefit from it, and an in-app cue schedule may well beat moderation as the fix — which is a roadmap suggestion, not a missing capability or a defect. The headline ("every live claim rests on the ... protocol", "absent from Phases 10-13") reads as a gap in the record when the gap is an ordering choice with a different remedy already frozen.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** The protocol: docs/participant-instructions.md:54-66 (two Mark presses, ten counted blinks between them). The measured contamination: docs/validation-round.txt:181-184 ("Three of six pressed the mark button more than twice, one performed the closure inside the blink window"), :103-104 ("markers are stamped up to about a second early, so the table refuses to call a count that a marker shift could change"), :193-195 ("The blink log is censored: a missed blink writes no row"). The pattern already exists and is proven end-to-end: src/core/lightSchedule.ts:22-29 is a pure fixed schedule, and ROADMAP.md:156-157 (rows 9.4a/9.4b, done 4 Sep) wired it to a fullscreen overlay with the schedule and its moment-zero written into the export, so per-row phase is recoverable by subtraction. The claim rows that reuse the human protocol: ROADMAP.md:188 (11.6, "formalizing the dry run") and ROADMAP.md:221 (13.3, "repeat the 10-deliberate-blinks protocol").

_Note._ Confirmed at medium — running the era's per-device accuracy claims on a protocol the project has already measured as compliance-contaminated puts human compliance, not the instrument, in the error bar, which blocks the audit's stated goal. Three corrections. (1) 10.9 is not contaminated: ROADMAP.md:175 defines it as "the same clip stepped on phones and Macs", a stepped-clip run with no Mark button and no participant; drop it from the affected set, which is 11.6 and 13.3. (2) "Absent from Phases 10-13" is literally true but the capability is not missing from the ladder — ROADMAP.md:240 (14.5) already specifies a cued script with a per-blink caught/not-caught tally and a pre-specified empty-stream case, :245 (14.10) a schedule plus overlay plus bounded offset log, and :248 (14.13) a pure tested cue schedule with an adversarial ignore-the-cues synthetic. So this is an ORDERING defect: the instrument sits two phases after the claim rows that need it. (3) That framing is stronger than the finding's, because it makes this a breach of the repo's own era rule at ROADMAP.md:41 — "instrument rows land before their claim rows" — rather than an outside opinion. Adjust the fix accordingly: pull 14.5/14.13's cue-schedule-and-scorer core forward as the 9.4a/9.4b core-then-io split (the repo's own proven shape) and re-point 11.6, 13.3, 14.5 and 14.13 at it, rather than opening a parallel 11.0 family that would build cue machinery twice.

#### F-072. Blendshape witness (12.2/12.3) is scheduled after the sibling corpora are read, risking a second read

|                             |                                                                                                                                                 |
| --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **low**                                                                                                                                         |
| Category                    | wrong-priority                                                                                                                                  |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                                                               |
| Raised by                   | roadmap                                                                                                                                         |
| Files                       | `ROADMAP.md:35`, `ROADMAP.md:185-186`, `ROADMAP.md:197-198`, `docs/iris-occlusion.txt:121-129`, `STATE.md:217-220`, `src/io/landmarker.ts:9-17` |

**Claim.** If 12.3 succeeds, a fused detector must graduate on corpora already spent.

**Impact.** The never-scored corpora are read twice, the freshness loss amendment 16 refuses.

**Fix as proposed.** Reorder 12.2 -> 12.3 -> 11.1-11.4 once.

**Evidence as filed.** 11.3/11.4 spend TalkingFace/Silesian5 on the landmark-only detector; 12.3 is the only remaining route past the ~49-miss ceiling; STATE named 12.2 a starter row but it sits ~28 rows down.

**Reproduce skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** The mechanics check out: src/io/landmarker.ts:9-17 sets only outputFacialTransformationMatrixes, so 12.2 is genuinely unstarted; ROADMAP.md:185-186 (11.3/11.4) precede :197-198 (12.2/12.3); ROADMAP.md:198 itself says "any fusion signal routes through Phase 11's corpora"; ROADMAP.md:181 says Phase 11 corpora are ones "no version of the detector ever saw"; STATE.md:217-220 names 12.2 among the five starter rows; docs/iris-occlusion.txt:121-129 closes the iris route. But the premise fails on its own citations. ROADMAP.md:39 (the amendment-16 bullet the finding invokes) scopes once-only reading to UTA-RLDD alone — "The UTA-RLDD labels have been read twice and are read exactly ONCE more ... Per-feature dips into the same 148 videos are refused" — and says nothing about TalkingFace or Silesian5, so "the freshness loss amendment 16 refuses" is a misattribution. Worse for the finding, ROADMAP.md:187 (row 11.5) already schedules "a second pre-registered sibling read with the 10.8 fix's delta predicted": a second read of those corpora is the ladder's own accepted mechanism, not a violation of it. And 12.3's own corpus run is against Eyeblink8's 67 misses (the regression harness, ROADMAP.md:35), not the siblings — only a downstream fusion touches them, and only if 12.2 survives its own kill criterion (ROADMAP.md:197, "ships disabled by default if the 30 fps budget breaks on the slowest tier"). Counting the ladder, 23 rows precede 12.2 (16 of them unchecked), not "~28"; and ROADMAP.md:164 (10.2, done) already pins the flag as "blendshapes stated `false` explicitly, the pin 12.2 flips", so the row is anticipated rather than forgotten.

_Note._ Real observation, wrong frame. The dependency at ROADMAP.md:198 is genuine and reordering 12.2 before 11.3/11.4 is defensible on cost. But calling it wrong-priority rests on a once-only rule that does not apply to these corpora and ignores that the roadmap already books a second pre-registered sibling read at 11.5. That makes this a scheduling preference costing one extra pre-registered run in a branch that may not survive 12.2's kill criterion — not a freshness loss the project's rules refuse.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** ROADMAP.md:181 declares the siblings the graduation ground ("Eyeblink8 ... is exhausted as evidence. Every accuracy claim from here graduates on corpora and people no version of the detector ever saw"), and ROADMAP.md:35 repeats it for the era. ROADMAP.md:185-186 spend TalkingFace (11.3) and Silesian5 (11.4) on the landmark-only detector. ROADMAP.md:198 (12.3) is the only remaining route past the ceiling docs/iris-occlusion.txt:121-129 establishes ("The ~49 shallow-aperture misses are a recall CEILING, not a tunable defect ... neither moving the blink line nor fusing the iris signal can recover them"), and 12.3's own text says "any fusion signal routes through Phase 11's corpora". STATE.md:219-220 names 12.2 among the five starter rows, yet ROADMAP.md:197 places it after 11.1-11.8. The reorder is unblocked: src/io/landmarker.ts:9-17 shows outputFaceBlendshapes simply absent from the options (12.2 flips one flag), and 12.3 runs on Eyeblink8, already prepared and designated a regression harness by ROADMAP.md:35.

_Note._ Confirmed at medium — the reorder is S-effort, breaks nothing, and protects the era's single most valuable evidentiary asset, so the wrong-priority call is right. Two corrections to the reasoning, both of which make the case sharper rather than weaker. (1) "The freshness loss amendment 16 refuses" is imprecise: ROADMAP.md:39's refusal is scoped to the UTA-RLDD labels ("the same 148 videos"), and ROADMAP.md:187 (11.5) already schedules a SECOND pre-registered sibling read for the 10.8 fix — so the ladder already accepts more than one sibling read, and the cost of 12.3 landing late is a third read, not a stated-rule violation. (2) The stronger internal argument the finding under-uses is consistency: the ladder ALREADY applies exactly this logic to the other detector-changing route by sequencing 10.8 before 11.5, and it also breaks the era rule at ROADMAP.md:41 ("instrument rows land before their claim rows") — the same rule F-071 breaks, which is worth reporting to the owner as one systemic ordering slip rather than two unrelated ones. One adjustment to the fix: keep 11.1 first. It is a download-verification gate that reads no corpus (ROADMAP.md:183), costs nothing, and if the GPL3 downloads turn out to contain no video the whole ordering question is moot; the sequence should be 11.1 → 12.2 → 12.3 → 11.2-11.4.

**Claim.** The one action that clears the caveat and scores a committed prediction has no row.

**Impact.** Evidentiary freshness erodes on the one externally validated number.

**Fix as proposed.** Row 10.8a 'regression run at HEAD' before any detector change: re-measure Eyeblink8, move the anchor, score the prediction.

**Evidence as filed.** The adoption doc's outcome section is missing; the caveat lists four un-remeasured commits and points at 10.8, which is a fix-then-measure row; 10.11, 12.3 and 10.8's fix each add to the caveat.

**Reproduce skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** Two of three sub-claims hold. The prediction is unscored: docs/blink-line-adoption.txt is 122 lines and ends at 121-122 with "This prediction is not edited after the fact; the outcome becomes a new dated section below it" — no such section exists. The caveat is open: docs/eyeblink8-result.txt:312-327 lists 1a6c88f, dce2b87, bf5bfca, fab006c as "DETECTOR CHANGED, not yet re-measured". The third fails. The caveat's own last lines (docs/eyeblink8-result.txt:326-327) read "row 10.8's regression run is already committed to do exactly that", and ROADMAP.md:174 (10.8) does commit it: "Eyeblink8 regression prediction committed (5 recovered, no false-alarm identity churn, other 62 misses unchanged) with an adopt-or-revert rule". ROADMAP.md:187 (11.5) adds "the ratchet (10.1) forces the dated re-measure anyway". Separately, `grep -rn '10\.11'` over the repo returns nothing and `grep -n '^- \[.\] 10\.'` lists 10.1a through 10.10b with no 10.11 — the cited row does not exist.

_Note._ "No regression-run row exists" is refuted: 10.8 is that row and the caveat names it by number. What survives is narrower — the run is bundled behind a re-arm fix, so the adoption doc's neutrality branch ("with no stored calibration, any committed Eyeblink8 number changed at all") cannot be attributed cleanly to the guided line versus the fix. That is a sequencing refinement to an existing row, not a missing one, and the fabricated 10.11 citation weakens the "grows with every detector commit" arithmetic (the real future contributors are 10.7b, which touches aperture.ts, and 12.3, which touches landmarker.ts — both on the DETECTOR_SOURCES watch at tools/detectorRatchet.mjs:37-59).

**Materiality skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** docs/blink-line-adoption.txt ends at its "WHAT WOULD REFUTE THIS" section with "the outcome becomes a new dated section below it" and no such section exists — the prediction (commit 5359764, 2026-09-02) is unscored. docs/eyeblink8-result.txt:312-327 carries the DETECTOR CHANGED caveat naming four commits (1a6c88f, dce2b87, bf5bfca, fab006c, all dated 2026-09-02) and says "row 10.8's regression run is already committed to do exactly that". ROADMAP.md:174 (10.8) is fix-then-measure. STATE.md:14-18 lists 10.8's regression run among the rows waiting on the maintainer's data. There is no row 10.11 anywhere in ROADMAP.md or STATE.md (`grep -n "10\.11"` returns nothing), so one third of the finding's escalation evidence does not exist.

_Note._ Downgraded because the load-bearing premise is wrong. "The one action that clears the caveat has no row" is refuted: 10.8's regression run IS that row, and docs/eyeblink8-result.txt:325-327 names it explicitly as the thing that will move the built-from line. The caveat mechanism is working exactly as designed — it found real staleness in its first hour (ROADMAP.md:164) and CI reddens both ways. And the erosion is four days old, not chronic: the commits are 2 September, the caveat 5 September, today 6 September. What genuinely survives, and is worth acting on, is narrower than filed: 10.8 changes the detector AND re-measures in one run, so a moved number cannot be attributed between the guided line and the re-arm fix, and the adoption doc's own refutation condition ("if, with no stored calibration, any committed Eyeblink8 number changed at all") becomes unscoreable. That confound is real, the fix is a one-line roadmap split, and it matches the neutrality discipline 12.3 already demands (ROADMAP.md:198). Low, not medium: nothing published is wrong, the caveat is honest and machine-enforced, and the prediction being scored is one the doc itself labels a HYPOTHESIS whose default is today's behaviour. One adjacent observation the finding missed and that is worth more than the filed version: README.md:45 publishes the recall/precision/F1 numbers without the staleness caveat, which lives only in the linked result file — the freshness note does not travel with the number where it is most read.

#### F-076. Blink taxonomy is duration-only; completeness (depth relative to baseline) is absent though the detector's own misses are defined by depth

|                             |                                                                                                                        |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **low**                                                                                                                |
| Category                    | missing-capability                                                                                                     |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                                      |
| Raised by                   | roadmap                                                                                                                |
| Files                       | `ROADMAP.md:201`, `docs/miss-character.txt:263-264`, `docs/validation-dry-run.txt:85-87`, `src/core/blinkLog.ts:89-97` |

**Claim.** Complete-vs-incomplete is the standard distinction the instrument already makes at its arm line and does not export; 1.5 mm absolute is a different ruler per face.

**Impact.** Per-person amplitude comparability and 12.14/12.18 riders are weaker for one missing column.

**Fix as proposed.** 12.6b: closureFraction = amplitude / frozen baseline plus a complete/incomplete label at the arm line; retire the absolute grey line.

**Evidence as filed.** 12.6 classifies by 0.8/3/20 s; never_armed misses sit at 0.91-0.996 of the line; the on-page table greys out under an absolute 1.5 mm line; amplitudeMm is exported absolute only.

**Reproduce skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** All four citations are accurate. ROADMAP.md:201 (12.6) classifies on 0.8/3/20 s only. docs/miss-character.txt:263-264 gives never_armed min_ratio 0.91-0.996 (15 of 20) against an arm line at 0.9 * line, so the misses are indeed defined by relative depth. docs/validation-dry-run.txt:86-87 describes "one detection of 1.26 mm amplitude, below the 1.5 mm line the on-screen table greys out", and that line is absolute: src/core/blinkLog.ts:65 `FAINT_BLINK_MM = 1.5`, applied at :81 as `shape.amplitudeMm < FAINT_BLINK_MM`. BLINK_CSV_COLUMNS (src/core/blinkLog.ts:89-97) carries amplitudeMm and no fraction. But the inputs for the fraction are both already committed to disk: baselineMm is a per-second export column (src/core/csv.ts:15; SPEC.md:26 "the 4.2 baseline, frozen at birth since 2026-08-20"), and it is the open-eye median, with the blink line derived from it at src/core/baseline.ts:107-110 (`state.baselineMm * BASELINE_THRESHOLD_FRACTION`).

_Note._ Real but overstated as a missing capability. amplitudeMm / baselineMm is computable offline today from two committed exports, so what is absent is a derived column and an on-page label, not a measurement the instrument cannot make — the 12.14/12.18 riders can be built from the existing files. The absolute 1.5 mm grey line is a genuine per-face inconsistency, but src/core/blinkLog.ts:58-64 documents it as an empirical choice ("real blinks ran 2.2 to 6.9 mm and the phantoms sat under 1 mm") and it greys a panel row only; the export keeps the row regardless.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** ROADMAP.md:201 (12.6) classifies closures by duration only (0.8/3/20 s), no depth term. docs/miss-character.txt:255-264 defines the detector's own misses by depth: never_armed sits at min_ratio 0.91-0.996 of the line, armed_then_dropped at 0.26-0.45, with the arm line at 0.9 * line. src/core/blinkLog.ts:89-97 exports amplitudeMm absolute with no baseline-relative column, and src/core/blinkLog.ts:58-65 greys rows under an absolute FAINT_BLINK_MM = 1.5. docs/validation-dry-run.txt:85-87 records that line mislabelling a real detection (1.26 mm) in the macbookair session whose baseline was born 1.41x resting.

_Note._ Confirmed, and the impact argument is stronger than the finding states. The decisive point is the freeze: ROADMAP.md:212 (12.17) is a column-freeze manifest and ROADMAP.md:213 (12.18) is the ONE remaining read of the UTA-RLDD labels, carrying "taxonomy" as a named rider. A completeness column absent at 12.17 is permanently absent from the last label read this project may take. Two corrections. (1) "Absent" is slightly strong: baselineMm and lastBlinkAmplitudeMm are both in the per-second export (src/core/csv.ts:10-37), so the fraction is derivable offline today — what is missing is the event-level column, the on-page label, and the shared vocabulary with the miss taxonomy. And ROADMAP.md:202 (12.7, lid openness ratio over the frozen shut baseline) already schedules the baseline-relative ruler this needs, so the fix should be built on 12.7 rather than inventing a second ruler. (2) The "retire the absolute grey line" half is the risky part and I would not adopt it as written: FAINT_BLINK_MM is evidence-derived (src/core/blinkLog.ts:58-64, real blinks 2.2-6.9 mm, phantoms under 1 mm), documented at docs/UI.md:260, display-only, and never touches the export — while a fraction-of-baseline line would couple the display to a ruler the repo has already caught being born wrong (docs/validation-dry-run.txt:81-84). Add the fraction alongside the absolute line; retiring it trades a stable heuristic for one with a known failure mode.

The one figure I could not reproduce is the specific "2769 ms" — that is the finding author's observed cold-start sample, not a repo constant; the label format and the 30 ms budget (src/core/constants.ts:8) are as stated. Worth noting F-077 and F-078 are the same defect inverted: the page says "measuring..." when nothing is running, and says nothing when a measurement is actually being waited for.

**Materiality skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** Every mechanism verified. src/main.ts:1227 shows the clip path is the only one that announces the wait ("Loading the model before the clip starts...", awaited); the camera path at src/main.ts:1125-1141 sets state running and fires ensureLandmarker() unawaited with no status write, and cameraStateMessage returns "" for running (src/core/cameraState.ts:59). src/main.ts:981 blanks scoreLabel in resetSession, and the only rewrite is inside the per-second block at src/main.ts:3875-3883, which cannot run before the model exists — so the headline stays empty for the whole download. src/core/timing.ts:30 produces "Inference time: N ms, over the 30 ms budget". The baseline countdown "Learning your open eyes: N s left" is written to baselineLabel (src/main.ts:3551), which lives in blinksBox, appended last in column B (src/main.ts:4409). src/main.ts:1505-1522 confirms there is no load timeout at all.

_Note._ Downgraded to low. Nothing false is asserted here — the blank headline is honest silence, and the mitigation the finding omits is that the camera preview paints immediately: drawVideoFrame at src/main.ts:2984-2986 sits OUTSIDE the landmarker guard, so the visitor sees their own face throughout the wait, which is fairly strong evidence the page is alive. No measurement, export or published number is touched. And the worst version of this — a fetch that hangs rather than fails, leaving the page silent forever — is already disclosed roadmap work at ROADMAP.md:228 (13.10: "a load-timeout state machine test (timeout plus no model is a visible stuck state, never healthy idle)"), so the severe case is tracked, not hidden. Low is the severity; the priority is nonetheless high for effort, and I would ship the copy half with F-077 in one small PR rather than parking it behind 13.10, since 13.10 is a measurement row and will not by itself produce a loading indicator. One caution on the fix as written: "keep 'measuring...' in resetSession" pushes in the opposite direction from F-077 — the right string during a model download is a loading sentence, not a measurement sentence, or you fix the idle overclaim and reintroduce it one state later.

#### F-080. No link from the page to the repository, README, model card or any doc the page cites by path
