#### F-081. No facingMode, no wake lock, no orientation handling: phones may open the rear camera mirrored, and hands-off sessions stop at the screen timeout

|                             |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Severity after verification | **low**                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Category                    | missing-capability                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Raised by                   | demo-ux, performance                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Files                       | `src/io/camera.ts:28-32`, `src/main.ts:1084-1085`, `src/main.ts:1151-1154`, `src/main.ts:1336-1341`, `src/main.ts:4238-4247`, `src/io/deviceInfo.ts:59`, `src/core/lightSchedule.ts:22-29`, `ROADMAP.md:219`, `ROADMAP.md:227` |

**Claim.** First-impression failure on phones for a one-line constraint, and any protocol longer than auto-lock ends in a gap the instrument can only count.

**Impact.** Lost minutes in exactly the long sessions the drowsiness rows need.

**Fix as proposed.** facingMode ideal 'user' and untick Mirror on environment; navigator.wakeLock('screen') on start with re-request on visibilitychange; record grant/refusal and orientation flips; scope 13.1 to laptops too.

**Evidence as filed.** Constraints are resolution plus optional deviceId; mirror is forced; the picker appears only after start with raw device strings; no wakeLock or orientationchange in src/; a hidden document stops rAF and is only counted afterwards; the light protocol runs 260 s 'keep still' and 13.9 plans 30-minute runs; dry-run phone sessions survived because they were ~2 minutes.

**Reproduce skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** Code facts hold: src/io/camera.ts:28-32 constrains only `width/height ideal` plus optional `deviceId` — no facingMode; `grep -rn 'wakeLock' src/` returns nothing; the only orientation read is a one-shot src/io/deviceInfo.ts:45 `screen.orientation?.type`, with no orientationchange listener; main.ts:1084-1085 forces `mirrored = true` on every beginCamera, and main.ts:1567-1569 re-runs beginCamera on picker change, so the mirror resets on every camera switch. But the predicted failures are contradicted by the project's own record. docs/validation-dry-run.txt:55-60 CONDITIONS table: all three iPhone sessions opened "Front Camera"/"Front Ultra Wide Camera" with no facingMode constraint, ran 111.5-121.8 s, and report `tab hidden 0` with `face seen 100.0%` — i.e. no rear camera was ever selected and no screen timeout interrupted a ~2-minute hands-off capture, past iOS's 30 s default auto-lock. Mirror is display-only: `grep -n '\bmirrored\b' src/main.ts` shows it is consumed solely by frameTransform() at :728 and :2984 for the canvas draw, never by any measurement, and a user-facing Mirror checkbox exists at :713-717.

_Note._ Downgraded, not refuted: the three gaps are real in code and a 30-minute run (ROADMAP.md:227, row 13.9) or the 260 s light protocol (src/core/lightSchedule.ts:22-29) would be genuinely exposed by the missing wake lock. What does not hold is the impact framing — 'phones may open the rear camera mirrored' has not happened in any of the six recorded sessions, and 'mirrored' is cosmetic since no measurement reads the flag. The finding's supporting claim that phone sessions 'survived because they were ~2 minutes' is backwards: surviving 122 s with tab_hidden=0 is evidence the timeout does not fire during capture. It also restates ROADMAP.md:219 (13.1) almost verbatim — 'facingMode fallback, a wake lock, and orientation re-reads with a flip count in the export' — so it is a planned row, not a discovery.

**Materiality skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** Mechanism holds: src/io/camera.ts:28-32 constrains width/height/deviceId only, no facingMode; no wakeLock or orientationchange anywhere in src/ (grep returns only the visibilitychange listener at src/main.ts:4241). But ROADMAP.md:219 already commits row 13.1 'Phone session survival kit... facingMode fallback, a wake lock, and orientation re-reads with a flip count in the export' behind a scoping ADR. The mirror half is display-only: detection runs on the video element, not the mirrored canvas (src/main.ts:2993 detectForVideo(video,...), and 3134 'Measured against the VIDEO, not the canvas'), while mirroring only reaches frameTransform on the drawn canvas (src/main.ts:2984). An interruption is already recorded rather than fabricated: visibilityChanges is counted and stamped at the last live record (src/main.ts:4238-4247), and a stepped clip refuses outright on suspension (src/main.ts:1330-1342).

_Note._ Downgraded because almost all of it is a committed roadmap row, not news, and because the harm is lost minutes, never wrong numbers — the gap machinery keeps a suspended session honest. The mirror-on-rear-camera claim is cosmetic by construction, since no measurement reads the mirrored frame. What survives and is worth keeping is the scoping note, which is genuinely new: 13.1 is written phones-only, but the wake lock is equally needed on laptops for 13.9's pre-registered 30-minute runs (ROADMAP.md:226) and the 260 s light protocol (src/core/lightSchedule.ts:22-29, LIGHT_TOTAL_MS), so 13.1 should be scoped to laptops and ordered before 13.9. File that as a scope amendment to 13.1, not as a defect.

#### F-082. Unguarded DOM rewrites every tick: ~14 readouts rebuilt as fresh spans and the status-strip MutationObserver fires per tick

|                             |                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **low**                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Category                    | performance                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Raised by                   | performance                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Files                       | `src/main.ts:4505-4528`, `src/main.ts:2961-2981`, `src/main.ts:3066`, `src/main.ts:3099-3104`, `src/main.ts:3211-3221`, `src/main.ts:3543-3552`, `src/main.ts:3714`, `src/main.ts:3920-3925`, `src/main.ts:4564-4570` |

**Claim.** At 120 Hz ~1,700 replaceChildren and 5,000 element creations per second for text that changes at most 30 times.

**Impact.** Avoidable layout cost worst on phones; makes per-tick timing noisy, which the fps window reports as the instrument's rate.

**Fix as proposed.** Cache last text per element and early-return; set hidden only on change; write modelStatus only on kind change.

**Evidence as filed.** writeReadout creates two or three elements and replaceChildren's every call with no equality check; ~14 sites fire unconditionally per face frame; alertBanner.hidden and modelStatus.textContent are re-set per tick so refreshBanner runs every tick; rateWarningLabel shows the guarded pattern the rest lacks.

**Reproduce skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** Mechanism confirmed exactly. src/main.ts:4505-4528 writeReadout() creates label+separator+value spans and calls replaceChildren unconditionally, with no equality check. 36 writeReadout call sites sit inside processFrame (main.ts:2933-3998, counted with awk), and the camera path runs on requestAnimationFrame at display rate (src/io/frameLoop.ts:14-21; main.ts:2969 records the M5 Max measurement 'processing 120, reading 30'). The guarded counter-example is real: main.ts:2978-2981 `if (rateWarningLabel.textContent !== riskText)`. The observer at main.ts:4564-4570 watches statusBanner subtree for childList/characterData/hidden, and main.ts:3714 `alertBanner.hidden = !alertVisible(...)` re-sets hidden=true on every measured frame — a boolean-attribute set to an identical value still runs 'change an attribute', which queues an attributes mutation record — so refreshBanner does run per tick.

_Note._ One cited half is wrong: main.ts:3066 `modelStatus.textContent = landmarkValidationMessage(validation)` returns "" for a valid face (src/core/landmarkGuard.ts:20-21), and a textContent='' assignment on an already-empty element queues no mutation record (replace-all with both addedNodes and removedNodes empty). The per-tick observer firing comes from alertBanner alone. Impact is overstated: browsers coalesce layout to at most one pass per animation frame, so ~1,700 replaceChildren/s is not ~1,700 layouts/s — the real cost is style recalc and GC on ~14 tiny text nodes inside an 8.3 ms budget the fastest recorded device already meets at 120 processed fps with all this churn present. No measurement in the repo supports 'makes per-tick timing noisy'; the claim is unmeasured. Real, cheap to fix, but low.

**Materiality skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** Mechanism holds: writeReadout always builds label/sep/value spans and replaceChildren's with no equality check (src/main.ts:4505-4527); 48 call sites, ~14 of them on the per-frame path (3066, 3099-3104, 3211-3221, 3543-3552, 3920-3925 and kin); modelStatus.textContent (3066) and alertBanner.hidden (3714) are written unconditionally inside the observed strip (statusBanner.append at 4529, observer at 4564-4570 with attributeFilter ['hidden']), so refreshBanner is delivered every tick. The camera path is rAF-driven at display rate (src/io/frameLoop.ts:8-21). But refreshBanner reads only textContent/hidden and forces no layout (src/main.ts:4547-4562), and the repo has already ruled this class of work out: ROADMAP's 'Deliberately not taken up' rejects core-chain optimization as 'performance theater' against a ~30 ms inference budget, with the chain measured at 41.8 µs/frame (docs/latency.txt:52).

_Note._ Downgraded: the cost is real but unmeasured and of the same order the project has explicitly ruled theater, and the claimed impact on the published rate does not survive — the fps figure is whatever the loop actually achieved, so it stays honest under any render cost, and the cold-start phantom-frame problem was already fixed by remediation B1 (frames_measured counted after the model call, src/main.ts:3006-3016). The one part worth doing anyway is fragility, not speed: the guard comment at src/main.ts:4550-4557 records that an unguarded write inside this same observed subtree once re-triggered the observer forever, hung page.goto in every browser on CI and a laptop, and made an overnight corpus run silently produce nothing for an hour — so guarding modelStatus and alertBanner.hidden costs almost nothing and closes the door that incident came through. Do that as hygiene; do not open a render-optimization row ahead of claim rows, and if speed is ever the question, measure the per-tick render cost first the way docs/latency.txt did.

#### F-083. Stepped corpus runs are seek-bound (hours per dataset), which is what gates the open owner rows; a WebCodecs decode path would make them inference-bound

|                             |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **low**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Category                    | missing-capability                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Effort                      | L                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Raised by                   | performance                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Files                       | `src/io/videoStepper.ts:41`, `src/io/videoStepper.ts:63`, `src/io/videoStepper.ts:301-359`, `src/core/frameClock.ts:76-78`, `src/core/frameTrace.ts:48-49`, `docs/drozy-result.txt:28-33`, `docs/latency.txt:61-62`, `ROADMAP.md:167`, `ROADMAP.md:174` |

**Claim.** Turnaround is set by HTMLVideoElement seeking, not the model, and that is the stated reason two evidence rows are stalled.

**Impact.** Every detector change costs hours to re-measure, pushing toward not re-measuring.

**Fix as proposed.** A VideoDecoder driver with a demuxer feeding the same processFrame; keep the seek stepper as reference; accept only on digit-for-digit Eyeblink8 parity.

**Evidence as filed.** Each frame is a seek waiting on rVFC, 200 ms grace or 2 s timeout; DROZY's three shape rows need ~3.1 h (why 10.3 is parked); inference is ~6 ms per frame so the longest Eyeblink8 clip would take ~95 s decode-bound.

**Reproduce skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** The mechanism is exactly as described: src/io/videoStepper.ts:301-359 drives one seekTo() per frame index, and seekTo (:78-118) races requestVideoFrameCallback against a `seeked` + FRAME_GRACE_MS=200 (:63) fallback and a SEEK_TIMEOUT_MS=2000 (:41) ceiling. The arithmetic also checks: docs/eyeblink8-m5max.txt:87-88 gives the real per-clip measured-frames counts (15784, 11182, 9216, 5405, 10663, 5134, 9077, 4895) and 15,784 x 6 ms (docs/latency.txt:61-62, '~6 ms recorded locally under roadmap 8.7') is ~95 s. But the magnitude claim is contradicted by the repo's own measured throughput: STATE.md:3255-3269, 'About 58 frames per second. A full corpus run takes about 20 minutes, not 2.4 hours' — measured from run file timestamps, 55,572 frames in 954 s = 58.25 fps. The 71,356-frame Eyeblink8 corpus is therefore ~20 minutes, not hours. The 3.1 h figure (docs/drozy-result.txt:31) is a DROZY-only projection, and STATE.md:3424-3426 flags it: 'Both figures assume DROZY runs at the same speed as Eyeblink8... Nobody has measured either one.' The DROZY run that actually happened took 31 minutes (docs/drozy-result.txt:19, 22:10 to 22:41).

_Note._ Downgraded on two counts. (1) 'Every detector change costs hours to re-measure' is false for Eyeblink8, the corpus every detector change actually re-runs (~20 min at the measured 58 fps) — and STATE.md:3258-3264 records that the 'corpus is an overnight job' belief was a past error that nearly caused the owner to cut the evaluation plan, so this finding re-commits a mistake the project already corrected in writing. (2) 'Seek-bound, not the model' is unattributed: 17.2 ms/frame total minus ~6 ms inference leaves ~11 ms shared by seek, canvas draw, the per-tick DOM churn of F-082 and readback; nothing in the repo profiles the split, so the best case for a WebCodecs path is ~2.9x, not hours-to-minutes. Of the two 'stalled rows' cited, only ROADMAP.md:167 (10.3) names a ~3-hour cost; ROADMAP.md:174 (10.8) is gated on failing trace-harness tests and a committed prediction, not on run time.

**Materiality skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** The repo's own committed measurement contradicts the headline: tools/measure_corpus.mjs:32-38 records 'about 58 frames per second, so the eight clip Eyeblink8 corpus of roughly 71,000 frames takes about 20 minutes', and that comment exists precisely because an earlier estimate said 'hours' and was never re-measured ('Time it again rather than trusting this line'). At ~17 ms/frame against ~6 ms inference (docs/latency.txt:61-62) seeking is roughly 11 ms/frame, i.e. a 2-3x ceiling, not orders. The 200 ms grace and 2 s timeout are fallbacks, not per-frame costs: seekTo resolves the moment rVFC answers (src/io/videoStepper.ts:80-118). The DROZY gate is not purely time: 'Recomputing needs a re-extract from DROZY.zip and about 3.1 hours, and it would recreate the derived video DATASETS.md requires destroyed' (docs/drozy-result.txt:30-33) — a safeguard cost no decoder removes. Cost side: videoStepper.ts is in src/io and reachable from the shipped app's video-file mode, so a demuxer lands against the 268,000-byte bundle budget (tools/bundleBudget.mjs:28), and the stepper's comments record five separate browser-specific correctness fixes (origin search 128-145, double-counted final frame 345-352, WebKit 200 ms grace 56-62, duration revision 290-293, index-driven schedule 295-300) a second driver would have to re-earn.

_Note._ Downgraded, and the impact claim is the part that fails: 'hours per dataset' is true only of DROZY, whose re-measure a faster decoder shortens by perhaps a third while leaving the derived-video safeguard untouched, and it is false of the regression harness the era actually depends on (Eyeblink8 is 20 minutes, and row 10.1a's ratchet already forces a caveat rather than silent staleness when it is not re-run). So 'every detector change costs hours' does not hold, and the finding repeats the exact over-estimate the corpus runner's comment was written to kill. Real but small: this belongs on the ideas list next to 'Researcher's Night corpus scoring: deferred, the stepping-time sink', with a measured seek-versus-inference split committed first, not as an L-effort row competing with claim rows. If it is ever taken up, the finding's own guard rails are the right ones — keep the seek stepper as reference and accept only on digit-for-digit Eyeblink8 parity — plus a dev-only entry point so the bundle budget is not the thing that pays.

#### F-084. Cold load fetches 15.8 MB only after 'Start camera', with no prefetch, no timeout and no cache

|                             |                                                                                                                                                                       |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **low**                                                                                                                                                               |
| Category                    | risk                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Effort                      | M                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Raised by                   | performance                                                                                                                                                           |
| Files                       | `src/main.ts:1130`, `src/main.ts:1228`, `src/main.ts:1505-1522`, `src/io/landmarker.ts:5-18`, `tools/bundleBudget.mjs:28`, `REMEDIATION.md:104-105`, `ROADMAP.md:226` |

**Claim.** The first seconds to a minute of every cold session are preview-only, unrecoverable on stall, and impossible on poor connectivity.

**Impact.** Time-to-first-measurement is unbounded and not overlapped with the permission prompt and KSS question.

**Fix as proposed.** ensureLandmarker at page idle; a load timeout landing in modelFailed; consider Cache API after first load; write docs/cold-load.txt as 13.10 asks.

**Evidence as filed.** wasm 11.76 MB + glue 0.32 MB + model 3.76 MB per cold client against a 268 kB JS budget; ensureLandmarker is first called from beginCamera/beginVideoFile; a hanging load still looks healthy; no Cache API use.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** Sizes verified on disk: public/mediapipe-wasm/vision_wasm_internal.wasm 11,756,954 B + vision_wasm_internal.js 323,377 B + public/models/face_landmarker.task 3,758,596 B = 15,838,927 B (15.84 MB) per cold client, against tools/bundleBudget.mjs:28 BUNDLE_BUDGET_BYTES = 268_000. src/io/landmarker.ts:5-18 fetches both from BASE_URL at first call. ensureLandmarker (main.ts:1505-1527) is first invoked only from beginCamera (main.ts:1130, fired not awaited) and beginVideoFile (main.ts:1228, awaited) — grep confirms those are the only entry points besides retryModel at :1540; nothing runs at page idle. No timeout exists: the promise has .then/.catch/.finally but no race, and REMEDIATION.md:103-104 states it outright — 'Known residue, deliberate: a load that HANGS forever still looks healthy, no timeout was added.' `grep -rn 'caches\.|serviceWorker|prefetch|preload' src/ index.html` returns nothing, so there is no Cache API or preload path.

_Note._ Every technical claim holds; the only error is the roadmap citation — the cold-load row is ROADMAP.md:228 (13.10), while :226 is 13.8 (rVFC-gated inference). Kept at medium rather than downgraded because the failure mode is an honesty failure by this repo's own contract, not just slowness: a hung load leaves a session that looks healthy and can never produce a measurement, which is the one shape REMEDIATION.md B2 was written to remove and explicitly did not finish. Note it is a documented, deliberately-accepted residue with a planned row, so it is a known gap rather than a discovery.

**Materiality skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** Sizes check out: 11,756,954 + 323,377 + 3,758,596 bytes on disk in public/ = 15.8 MB, and ensureLandmarker is first called from beginCamera (src/main.ts:1130). But the hang half is documented as an accepted deliberate residue in the very lines the finding cites — REMEDIATION.md:104-105, 'Known residue, deliberate: a load that HANGS forever still looks healthy, no timeout was added' — and the timeout state machine plus docs/cold-load.txt are already committed as row 13.10 (ROADMAP.md:227, 'a load-timeout state machine test (timeout plus no model is a visible stuck state, never healthy idle)'). One evidence claim is simply wrong: the load IS overlapped with the KSS question — askKss returns immediately and ensureLandmarker is fired on the next statement (src/main.ts:1119-1130), so the download runs while the person answers. And the wait is honest, not fabricated: frames_measured ticks only after the model call returns (src/main.ts:3006-3016, remediation B1), so a cold start writes no phantom frames.

_Note._ Downgraded: an accepted, written-down residue plus a planned row is not a finding, and the finding cites the acceptance itself as its evidence. Two overstatements to correct if this is carried forward: the load is already overlapped with the KSS question, and 'no cache' means no Cache API only — the ordinary HTTP cache serves repeat visits, and offline caching is 14.8's held PWA row, which the repo deliberately gates because 'offline caching can demo a stale instrument'. What survives is one cheap idea not named in 13.10's text: kick ensureLandmarker at page idle so the download overlaps the permission prompt as well as the KSS question. Add it as a line under 13.10 rather than as its own row, and let 13.10 keep the timeout, since that row already writes the stuck state the finding wants.

#### F-086. Aperture-in-mm is not pose-invariant inside the gate: pitch foreshortens the lid chord but not the ruler, gaze rotation the reverse

|                             |                                                                                                               |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **low**                                                                                                       |
| Category                    | science                                                                                                       |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                             |
| Raised by                   | oculometric                                                                                                   |
| Files                       | `src/core/constants.ts:196-203`, `src/core/aperture.ts:109-122`, `src/core/validityGate.ts:31`, `SPEC.md:137` |

**Claim.** The same eyelid can read +/-6% (up to ~12% combined) within a valid pose, comparable to the 10% arm band.

**Impact.** Feeds the ruler-fit ratio and shut line unnamed.

**Fix as proposed.** State the bound; optionally divide the chord by cos(pitch) from the corrected pose or gate pitch tighter.

**Evidence as filed.** With eyes on screen the lid chord scales by cos(pitch) (-6% at 20 deg) while the ruler does not; a 20 deg eye rotation shrinks the horizontal iris chord (+6%); only roll is invariant.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity low.** I ran the repo's own synthetic generator through apertureMm in the square space its tests use (W=H=1000, matching test/core/aperture.test.ts:18-19), true aperture 10 mm at 500 mm: roll 15 and 30 deg -> 10.0000 mm (0.00%, SPEC.md:137's invariance holds exactly); pitch 20 deg -> 9.3996 mm (-6.00%, exactly cos(20 deg)=0.9397); yaw 25 deg -> 11.3275 mm (+13.27%). src/core/constants.ts:199-203 sets maxPitch 20 / maxYaw 25 / maxRoll 25 and src/core/validityGate.ts:31 rejects only `Math.abs(value) > limit`, so exactly 20 and exactly 25 are admitted as valid. src/core/aperture.ts:109-122 divides the lid chord by the horizontal iris chord with no pose term.

_Note._ The pitch mechanism and its -6% number are exact. Two caveats. (1) It is a re-find of the repo's own committed C4-09 (docs/audit/appendix-chunk-4-all-findings.md:280-288), which reports the identical measurements and files them HIGH — and shows the finding UNDERSTATES the band: the dominant term inside the gate is yaw (+13.27% per eye), not pitch, so '+/-6%, up to ~12% combined' is below the repo's own measured +13.3%. (2) The gaze-rotation half is geometrically sound but cannot be checked in-repo: syntheticFace's irisShiftMm is a translation, not an eyeball rotation, so the ruler is unchanged (23.400 px at shifts of 0/2/4/6 mm) and no fixture models a foreshortened iris. Confirmed at low as filed, but the filed bound is the wrong (smaller) one.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** Reproduced exactly, and larger than filed. Synthetic face at 500 mm, true aperture 10.000 mm, re-projected 16:9 the way test/core/tiltInvariance.test.ts:28-32 does: roll 25 deg -> 10.0000 (0.00%, the documented invariance holds); pitch 20 -> 9.3996 (-6.00%); yaw 10 -> 10.2653 (+2.65%); yaw 25 -> 11.3275 (+13.27%) per eye, +10.34% on the two-eye mean. src/core/validityGate.ts:31 admits all of these (POSE_LIMITS maxPitchDeg 20, maxYawDeg 25, src/core/constants.ts:199-201, rejecting only strictly beyond). So the admissible band is -6.0% to +10.3% on the mean and -6.0% to +13.3% per eye. That is roughly 4x the published aperture noise floor p95 of 0.286 mm (~4% of a 7 mm aperture, docs/aperture-noise-floor.txt via ROADMAP.md:171), and it exceeds the 10-percentage-point gap between the blink line at 50% of baseline and the shut line at 40% (src/core/longClosure.ts:35), so a pose change between the 30 s learning window and the reading can move a frame across a classification boundary and therefore change PERCLOS - a number the page publishes.

_Note._ Confirmed and raised from low to medium for three reasons the finding does not state. (1) It is not new: docs/audit/appendix-chunk-4-all-findings.md:286-288 filed the identical mechanism in August 2026, VERIFIED, severity HIGH, verdict 'violation', with the same numbers I just reproduced - and it was never closed. It appears in no roadmap row, no REMEDIATION item and no NEEDS-REVIEW entry, and the chunk summary at docs/audit/chunk-4-measurement.md:243-254 presents 'The ruler' as sound without mentioning it. So this is an unremediated prior high, not a nit. (2) It is undisclosed where a reader looks: MODEL_CARD.md has no pose or head-angle line at all (grepped), README.md:18 scopes the invariance claim to distance only ('survives moving closer to or further from the camera'), and SPEC.md:137 correctly scopes its proof to roll - so nothing overclaims, but the repo's contract that every published number carries its conditions is unmet for this one. (3) The finding under-scopes it: yaw is the larger term (+13.3% per eye) and F-086 omits it in favour of gaze rotation. On the fix, the finding's FIRST clause is right and the second two would cost strengths: dividing the chord by cos(pitch) would put a pose-derived correction inside a module whose whole architectural claim is that it is distances only and needs no correction (SPEC.md:137), it would leave yaw untouched, and a cos(yaw) ruler correction would double-count a genuine off-axis glance; tightening the gate destroys data, and the August audit measured that the existing gate already costs 4 true positives on Eyeblink8 (docs/audit/appendix-chunk-4-all-findings.md:619-621). The proportionate move is to state the measured band in MODEL_CARD.md and beside the aperture readout, and pin -6.0%/+13.3% with a test so it cannot drift.

#### F-087. Refusal sentence is hidden behind the guided-line label

|                             |                                                                                                    |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **low**                                                                                            |
| Category                    | ux                                                                                                 |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                  |
| Raised by                   | blink-closure                                                                                      |
| Files                       | `src/main.ts:3543-3552`, `src/main.ts:3718-3721`, `src/main.ts:3764-3768`, `src/main.ts:3877-3878` |

**Claim.** The user sees three withheld lines and no sentence saying what was refused or that a restart fixes it.

**Impact.** The promised remedy is unreachable from the page.

**Fix as proposed.** Render the refusal sentence under the guided-line label whenever calibrationRefused is true.

**Evidence as filed.** With a stored guided line the label shows the personal threshold and CALIBRATION_REFUSED_SENTENCE is never rendered while three readouts say 'withheld, calibration was refused'.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity low.** src/main.ts:3529 `const calibrationRefused = baselineState.kind === "refused"`. src/main.ts:3543-3552: the baselineLabel ternary tests `storedBlinkCalibration !== null` FIRST, so with a stored guided line CALIBRATION_REFUSED_SENTENCE (its only render site, src/main.ts:3548) is unreachable. The withheld readouts consult only calibrationRefused, never hasGuidedLine: src/main.ts:3653-3654 (Blinks), :3715-3720 (Long closures), :3764-3765 (PERCLOS), :3877-3878 (Alertness score) — FOUR lines, one more than filed. The combination is reachable: src/main.ts:3569 and :3584 run blink metrics on `blinkMeasurable && (hasGuidedLine || !calibrationRefused)`, i.e. the code explicitly anticipates guided-line-plus-refusal.

_Note._ Substance confirmed and slightly understated (four withheld lines, and line 3654 withholds the blink COUNT while the guided line is driving a live detector two dozen lines earlier). One correction to the impact wording: the sentence is not unreachable from the page outright — assessSession (src/main.ts:2587 -> src/core/sessionVerdict.ts:87, pinned by test/core/participantReport.test.ts:148) puts it in the 'Show the report' panel. But that panel is deliberately gated until the camera stops (src/main.ts:2628-2637), and the promised remedy is 'restart the camera', so during the session the remedy really is unreachable. Stays low.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** Real and wider than filed. src/main.ts:3536-3542 and STATE.md:834-836 both state the design: 'A stored guided line becomes the detector's line, overrides the passive baseline, and lifts the refusal, so a calibrated person counts blinks from the first frame'. The reducer honours it - src/main.ts:3569 and :3584 gate on `blinkMeasurable && (hasGuidedLine || !calibrationRefused)`. Four consumers do not, and test bare `calibrationRefused`: src/main.ts:3653 writes 'Blinks: withheld, calibration was refused', :3715 the same for long closures, :3764 for PERCLOS, :3877 for the alertness score, and src/main.ts:3825 nulls the exported `blinkRatePerMin`. Meanwhile src/main.ts:3543-3548 shows the guided line first, so CALIBRATION_REFUSED_SENTENCE (src/core/baseline.ts:52) is never rendered. Net effect for a guided-calibrated user whose passive window refuses: blinks are being counted in blinkState.blinkCount, the page says 'Personal blink threshold: X mm (from your guided calibration)' and 'Blinks: withheld' at the same time, the CSV drops blinkRatePerMin, and the only stated remedy ('Restart the camera...') never appears on screen.

_Note._ Raised from low to medium, and the fix should be redirected. Not a cosmetic missing sentence: a documented capability silently does not work, and it fails for exactly the population it was built to serve - STATE.md:820 records that guided calibration exists because passive baselines fail, and README.md:50 records that three of six volunteer machines produced no usable baseline, so the intersection (stored guided line + refused passive window) is the main use case, not an edge. Corpus results are unaffected: src/main.ts:3538-3542 notes storedBlinkCalibration is null in a fresh corpus browser, so Eyeblink8 numbers are byte-for-byte unchanged. It withholds rather than fabricates, which is why this is medium and not high - null-never-zero is honoured throughout. The proposed fix is the wrong direction: rendering CALIBRATION_REFUSED_SENTENCE under a valid guided line would tell a person with a measured ruler that their numbers are withheld, contradicting the design in STATE.md:835. The right fix is to make src/main.ts:3653 and :3825 use the same `hasGuidedLine || !calibrationRefused` predicate the reducer already uses. Note the split: the PERCLOS and long-closure refusals at :3715 and :3764 are substantively CORRECT as they stand, because frozenShutBaselineMm only exists when baselineState.kind === 'ready' (src/main.ts:3683-3685) and the guided record carries openMedianMm/closedMedianMm but is never consulted for a shut line - so those two should be reworded ('no shut line', not 'calibration was refused') rather than unblocked.

#### F-088. The per-eye 'Iris offset' readout is dominated by a ~0.07 anatomical bias the synthetic tests cannot see

|                             |                                                                                                                 |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **low**                                                                                                         |
| Category                    | science                                                                                                         |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                               |
| Raised by                   | gaze                                                                                                            |
| Files                       | `src/gazeOffset.ts:47-48`, `test/fixtures/syntheticFace.ts:36-39`, `test/MANUAL.md:34`, `src/main.ts:3211-3216` |

**Claim.** Per-eye numbers carry a constant offset larger than a corner glance; only the mean is near zero.

**Impact.** A single-eye fallback, asymmetry or vergence feature would inherit it.

**Fix as proposed.** Pin the fixture numbers; show per-eye offsets relative to calibration medians; give the synthetic face a bias option.

**Evidence as filed.** On the fixture the right eye reads -0.073 and the left +0.065 because the iris does not sit at the corner midpoint; the synthetic face places it exactly there; MANUAL expects pairs near 0.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity low.** My own run of the src/core/gazeOffset.ts:39-55 math over all 300 frames of test/fixtures/session-01.json at 1280x720: right horizontal mean -0.0726 (median -0.0769), left +0.0647 (median +0.0789) — matching the filed -0.073 / +0.065 to three decimals; the per-frame mean of the two is -0.0007. That it is anatomy and not gaze is provable from the repo's own convention: test/core/gazeOffset.test.ts:44-45 shows a conjugate iris shift gives the SAME sign on both eyes, whereas both fixture eyes read temporal (opposite signs), which no vergence can produce. test/fixtures/syntheticFace.ts:96-112 puts the iris exactly at the corner midpoint, so the synthetic tests assert exactly 0 (test/core/gazeOffset.test.ts:71-74) and the only fixture test is a +/-0.5 sanity range (test/core/gazeOffset.test.ts:124-146). test/MANUAL.md:34 expects 'hovering near +0.00' per eye; src/main.ts:3211-3216 prints both eyes raw.

_Note._ Path citation is wrong (src/gazeOffset.ts does not exist; it is src/core/gazeOffset.ts:47-48) but the lines and numbers are right. Two mild overstatements: 'larger than a corner glance' — test/MANUAL.md:34 quotes a glance swing of 0.05 to 0.15, so 0.077 is comparable to the low end, not larger than a glance; and 'only the mean is near zero' holds for the HORIZONTAL only — the mean vertical carries about -0.059 (right -0.063, left -0.056), the camera-above bias already documented at src/core/gazeQuadrant.ts:11-13. Display-only today, since every consumer (isOnScreen, screenQuadrant) takes the mean. Stays low.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity low.** Mechanism reproduces on real data. Running src/core/gazeOffset.ts:15-55 over the 300 recorded frames of test/fixtures/session-01.json: right-eye horizontal median -0.0769, left-eye +0.0789, mean of the two +0.0010; vertical medians -0.0626 and -0.0561, mean -0.0594. So the horizontal per-eye bias is +/-0.077 eye-widths - the size of a deliberate corner glance by test/MANUAL.md:30's own scale ('should swing roughly plus and minus 0.05 to 0.15') - and it cancels only because the two eyes are symmetric. The synthetic fixture reads exactly 0.0 for both eyes (I ran it), confirming test/fixtures/syntheticFace.ts places the iris at the corner midpoint and cannot see this. test/MANUAL.md:30 expects the pairs 'hovering near +0.00' and 'near zero again' at screen centre; both are wrong for the horizontal pair.

_Note._ Confirmed at low, but the impact is narrower than the finding implies and one half of the fix would cost a strength. The single-eye fallback the finding worries about does not exist: src/core/gazeQuadrant.ts:17-27 returns null when either eye is null, so no consumer ever reads one eye alone, and every downstream user (isOnScreen, screenQuadrant, the calibration profile) takes the mean where horizontal cancels to +0.001. The vertical bias that does NOT cancel (-0.059 on the mean) is already documented in three places as a known limit with a stated cure: src/core/gazeQuadrant.ts:11-13 ('A camera above the screen biases vertical toward bottom, known, documented, and 5.4's calibration is the cure'), test/MANUAL.md:31 and :34. So no published number is wrong today; what is real is (a) the MANUAL's per-eye expectation is unattainable, and (b) nothing pins these values, so a sign or axis regression in one eye would pass the suite silently. The 'pin the fixture numbers' half of the fix is proportionate and cheap and I would keep it. Drop the 'show per-eye offsets relative to calibration medians' half: the raw per-eye display is the only instrument that can catch the swapped-sign bug test/MANUAL.md:31 explicitly asks the reader to watch for ('If left and right ever read systematically SWAPPED, that is a sign bug, report it'), and subtracting calibration medians would hide exactly that.

#### F-090. The PERCLOS sampling-bound generator excludes ordinary blinks that the 40% shut line counts as closed, so the on-page 'at most +/-0.002 even at 15 fps' is understated ~2x

|                             |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **low**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Category                    | science                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Raised by                   | statistics, core-numeric                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Files                       | `src/core/samplingBounds.ts:25-28`, `src/core/samplingBounds.ts:63-68`, `src/core/samplingBounds.ts:142-149`, `docs/sampling-bounds.txt:25-27`, `docs/sampling-bounds.txt:81-88`, `src/core/perclos.ts:27`, `src/core/longClosure.ts:29-31` |

**Claim.** The bound is right for its generator and roughly double for a realistic window; the 'even at 15 fps' clause is false with blinks.

**Impact.** Practically nil (PERCLOS is refused below 25) but a pinned conditions sentence is incomplete.

**Fix as proposed.** Add a pre-registered blink term or scope the sentence to closures of 0.3 s and longer; do not edit the existing table.

**Evidence as filed.** Closures are drawn in [0.5, 6) s; a full blink dips to ~0.33 x baseline so every blink adds two edges; re-running the sweep with 15 extra 120 ms closures: 15 fps 0.0022 -> 0.0044, 30 fps 0.0011 -> 0.0022, 25 fps unchanged.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity low.** I re-ran the sweep from src/core/samplingBounds.ts in isolation. Committed table reproduces exactly (15 fps 0.0022, 25 fps 0.0013, 30 fps 0.0011, 60 fps 0.0006). Adding 15 non-overlapping 120 ms closures per window and recomputing the truth from the union reproduces the filed numbers exactly: 15 fps 0.0022 -> 0.0044 (0.0033 at P=0.05), 30 fps 0.0011 -> 0.0022, 25 fps unchanged at 0.0013. The odd '25 fps unchanged' is real and explained: 120 ms is exactly three 25-fps periods, so those closures quantise without error. Break the resonance and 25 fps also exceeds the sentence — 15 blinks of 50/60/100/140 ms give 0.0025/0.0030/0.0030/0.0030 — and a count sweep at 60 ms gives 0.0013 (n=0) -> 0.0027 (n=10) -> 0.0033 (n=20) -> 0.0040 (n=30). The premise checks out on real data: the shut line is 0.4 x baseline (src/core/longClosure.ts:35, aliased by src/core/perclos.ts:27), and in test/fixtures/session-01.json the mean aperture falls below 0.4 x its own median on 7 of 300 frames, minimum 31% — ordinary blinks really do register as closed samples. So perclosConditionsSentence()'s 'at most +/-0.002 of the share even at 15 frames per second' (src/core/samplingBounds.ts:144-145, rendered at src/main.ts:2188) is false for a blink-laden minute.

_Note._ Confirmed and, in one respect, understated: the sentence is also exceeded at 25 and 30 fps — inside the operating range — not only at the 15 fps the finding concedes is unreachable (below 25 fps blinkMeasurable is false, so src/main.ts:3757 feeds perclosStep null and src/core/perclos.ts:80-82 records nothing). One imprecision in the stated reason: samplingBounds.ts:67-68 rescales the drawn set, so the generator does NOT exclude short closures — at P=0.05 actual durations run 0.040 to 2.689 s, median 0.423, with 30.7% under 0.3 s. What it lacks is the blink COUNT (2-10 closures per minute against a realistic 15-20 blinks), which is why the proposed 'scope the sentence to closures of 0.3 s and longer' would not describe the existing table. docs/sampling-bounds.txt:25-27 does disclose the generator shape honestly; the on-page sentence is the part carrying no conditions.

**Materiality skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** I re-ran the committed sweep (src/core/samplingBounds.ts, same seed 20260905, same 2000 draws) with 15 extra 120 ms closures injected into the open gaps. The finding's numbers reproduce to the digit: 15 fps 0.0022 -> 0.0033-0.0044, 25 fps 0.0013 -> 0.0013 (unchanged at all three fractions), 30 fps 0.0011 -> 0.0022, 60 fps 0.0006 -> 0.0011. But PERCLOS is not computed below 25 fps: src/main.ts:3752-3754 feeds perclosStep `blinkMeasurable ? stabilityMm : null`, and blinkMeasurable is measurableAtFps(fps) with MIN_BLINK_FPS = 25 (src/core/fpsGate.ts:12, src/core/constants.ts:123). At every rate PERCLOS actually runs, the blink-augmented p95 is at most 0.0022 - which is what '+/-0.002 of the share' says. So the on-page bound in perclosConditionsSentence() (src/core/samplingBounds.ts:135-143) is NOT understated at any reachable operating point.

_Note._ Downgraded because the headline is wrong in the direction that matters: 'the on-page +/-0.002 is understated ~2x' is false at 25, 30 and 60 fps, and true only at 15 fps, a rate at which the instrument refuses to produce the number at all. What survives is one clause - 'even at 15 frames per second' - describing an unreachable operating point, so no reader can ever obtain a PERCLOS value whose sampling term exceeds the published bound. It is also close to already-documented: docs/sampling-bounds.txt:24-27 states the generator shape verbatim ('each duration drawn uniformly between 0.5 and 6 seconds') and says explicitly 'The generator shape, stated because the bound inherits it', and :81-88 names the exact mechanism the finding extends ('each closure edge can miscount at most about one sample', 'the error should scale with closure COUNT'). The blink term is also generous to the finding: at 25 fps a 120 ms blink spends far less than 120 ms below the 40%-of-baseline shut line (src/core/longClosure.ts:35), so 15 full 120 ms closures per minute overstates the real edge count. Keep the finding only as the scope edit its own fix names second - bound the sentence to closures of 0.3 s and longer, or add a pre-registered blink term - and do not touch the committed table.

#### F-091. light_response one-sided p can print exactly zero; it drops the +1 convention used elsewhere

|                             |                                                                                                                        |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **low**                                                                                                                |
| Category                    | defect                                                                                                                 |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                                      |
| Raised by                   | statistics                                                                                                             |
| Files                       | `analysis/blinklab/light_response.py:231-233`, `analysis/blinklab/stats.py:91-94`, `analysis/blinklab/rldd.py:471-476` |

**Claim.** A future large effect would publish p = 0.0000, which 1000 shuffles cannot establish.

**Impact.** Cosmetic today; an impossible number the repo's own comments forbid.

**Fix as proposed.** (at_least + 1) / (PERMUTATIONS + 1) with a never-zero test.

**Evidence as filed.** at_least / PERMUTATIONS versus (hits + 1) / (iterations + 1) two modules over.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity low.** analysis/blinklab/light_response.py:232-233 returns `at_least / PERMUTATIONS` with PERMUTATIONS=1000 (line 46). Ran the real function through the project venv (/home/user/blinklab/analysis/.venv) on a maximally separated pair (dark=100..119, bright=0..19): `_permutation_control` returned p = 0.0. analysis/tools/pupil_light.py:51 formats it `{result.p_one_sided:.3f}` -> prints "0.000". The +1 convention is used two modules over with comments that name a zero p impossible: analysis/blinklab/stats.py:91-94 ("A p of exactly zero would claim the observed value is impossible by chance, which ten thousand shuffles cannot establish") and analysis/blinklab/rldd.py:471-476 ("the +1 that keeps a zero-count from reading as an impossible p of exactly zero").

_Note._ Confirmed, with two small corrections to the write-up: the printed form is 0.000 (3 decimals via :.3f), not 0.0000; and nothing in docs/ currently publishes a light-response p at all (grep for "one-sided permutation p" over docs/*.txt returns nothing), so this is entirely prospective, exactly as the finding's own 'cosmetic today' says. Low is right.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity low.** analysis/blinklab/light_response.py:232-233 returns `at_least / PERMUTATIONS` (PERMUTATIONS=1000, line 47). The +1 convention holds at every other permutation site: analysis/blinklab/stats.py:91-94 with the explicit comment "A p of exactly zero would claim the observed value is impossible by chance, which ten thousand shuffles cannot establish"; analysis/blinklab/rldd.py:471-476 ("the +1 that keeps a zero-count from reading as an impossible p of exactly zero"); and a fourth site the finding missed, analysis/blinklab/alertness.py:272-273. Cosmetic today is exactly right: analysis/tools/pupil_light.py:41-51 prints p only inside the `if result.gate_cleared` branch, and the published run never cleared the gate (docs/pupil-light-result.txt:10, verdict INCONCLUSIVE), so no p is in print anywhere.

_Note._ Material as a latent honesty defect, not as a live one, and low is correct. One point of priority the finding does not make: the detection rule is `observed > percentile` (light_response.py:190), NOT p < 0.025, so the +1 cannot move any verdict — which is why this is safe to fix despite docs/pupil-light-result.txt:82 declaring the analysis method fixed, and why it must be fixed BEFORE the invited re-run. Making a permutation-p more conservative after a re-run's data is read would be the post-hoc edit the pre-registration discipline exists to forbid; making it now, while the only committed result is inconclusive, is free. The fix should say so in its commit message or it will read as method-tampering to a later reader.

#### F-093. PERCLOS minimum observation is a span rule, so it speaks from almost no evidence

|                             |                                                           |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **low**                                                   |
| Category                    | defect                                                    |
| Effort                      | S                                                         |
| Raised by                   | core-numeric                                              |
| Files                       | `src/core/perclos.ts:29-31`, `src/core/perclos.ts:95-118` |

**Claim.** The mirror image of F-004: one over-refuses, this under-refuses, and the heaviest score penalty rides it.

**Impact.** Bounded; the estimator is honest for the samples it has.

**Fix as proposed.** Require a minimum valid-sample count or observed fraction; export the fraction.

**Evidence as filed.** Readiness checks last - first >= 15 s and staleness only; one closed sample at t=0, face lost until 15 s, 31 open samples 15-16 s gives 3.1%.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity low.** src/core/perclos.ts:103 gates only on span (`last.timestampMs - first.timestampMs < PERCLOS_MIN_OBSERVED_MS`, 15000 at :31) plus staleness at :108; nothing counts samples or observed fraction. I compiled src/core/perclos.ts with the repo's tsc and ran it: one closed sample at t=0, nothing until 15 s, then 31 open samples over 15.0-16.0 s -> 32 samples, value 0.03125 (3.1%), exactly the finding's number; the same with nulls pushed through the gap -> identical, since null apertures append nothing (:79-81). Two samples 15 s apart -> value 0.5 from two frames. The repo's own test blesses this: test/core/perclos.test.ts 'runs the boundary trio at exactly the minimum span' expects perclosValue == 0 from two samples 15 s apart. Heaviest penalty confirmed: src/core/score.ts:32 PERCLOS_PENALTY_MAX = 40 against 30 (:39), 15 (:46), 15 (:54), and scoreRecords returns null without a PERCLOS value (:96).

_Note._ Mechanism, arithmetic and the 'heaviest penalty' claim all hold. Real-world reach is bounded by the 2 s staleness rule (the newest sample must be fresh) and by src/main.ts:3755-3760 only pushing samples while blinkMeasurable, so the sparse case needs a genuine mid-window gap — which is precisely the face-lost / fps-drop case. Low is right.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** src/core/perclos.ts:98-111 gates only on span (`last.timestampMs - first.timestampMs < PERCLOS_MIN_OBSERVED_MS`, 15000 at :31) and staleness (2000 at :45), then divides by inWindow.length at :112-118. Nothing counts samples or measures coverage of the 60 s window (:9), so the sparse case the finding describes returns a number. Two things make it matter more than 'bounded'. (1) The most recent commit publishes an on-page conditions line beside the value: src/main.ts:2187-2188 renders perclosConditionsSentence(), src/core/samplingBounds.ts:142-149 "the sampling term is at most ±0.002 of the share even at 15 frames per second" — a bound measured by src/core/samplingBounds.ts:108-127, which steps `for (let t = phaseS; t < windowS; t += period)`, i.e. a FULLY sampled window. That bound does not hold for a window that is 95% empty, and the sentence carries no coverage condition. (2) The value is not display-only: src/main.ts:3761-3768 labels it "PERCLOS (eyes closed share, last 60 s)", :3832 writes it into featureRecords (exported, src/core/csv.ts:21), and src/core/score.ts:32,96,108-114 rides the score's heaviest penalty (PERCLOS_PENALTY_MAX = 40) on it. README.md:20 and :5 describe it to readers as "the eyes closed share of the last minute". Face loss does not lower the frame rate, so the upstream fps gate the module's own comment leans on (perclos.ts:87-90) cannot catch this.

_Note._ Upgraded from low to medium. The mechanism is as filed, but 'the estimator is honest for the samples it has' understates it: the number is LABELLED as a minute and now carries a precision claim derived under an assumption the readiness rule does not enforce. On the fix, split it and do the non-refusing half first — export an observed-sample-count or coverage-fraction column and add the coverage condition to perclosConditionsSentence(). That cannot over-refuse and it repairs the conditions claim immediately. The refusal threshold is the part that risks becoming the F-004 mirror the finding names, so it needs its own committed prediction and a number derived from real sessions, not a round constant. Note the export already lets a careful analyst reconstruct gaps from the per-second faceDetected column, so the export path is only half-blind; the on-page number and the 40-point penalty are the blind ones.

#### F-094. Noise-floor median sits at two rounding quanta of the fixture's storage precision

|                             |                                                                                                                                                              |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Severity after verification | **low**                                                                                                                                                      |
| Category                    | science                                                                                                                                                      |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                                                                            |
| Raised by                   | core-numeric                                                                                                                                                 |
| Files                       | `src/core/fixtureRecording.ts:35-39`, `docs/aperture-noise-floor.txt:49-50`, `docs/aperture-noise-floor.txt:66-67`, `test/core/apertureNoise.test.ts:82-107` |

**Claim.** The lower half of the distribution 10.7b would derive a threshold from is quantisation.

**Impact.** A refusal derived from it would be mis-placed.

**Fix as proposed.** Add the precision to the conditions block; record an unrounded fixture for 10.7b.

**Evidence as filed.** Landmarks are stored at 1e-4 (0.072 px at 720p); one single-chord step is 0.0100 mm after the two-chord mean; published medians 0.020/0.019 mm are 1.95 quanta and 40% of deltas are within 1.5 quanta; conditions omit storage precision. p95 values are unaffected.

**Reproduce skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** Every number reproduces. src/core/fixtureRecording.ts:35-39 rounds landmarks to 1e-4 (0.072 px of y at 720p). Recomputing the committed pipeline over test/fixtures/session-01.json at 1280x720: kept 270/300, left median 0.019776, right 0.019344, p95 0.2864/0.2419, cross-eye median 0.2005 — digit for digit docs/aperture-noise-floor.txt:65-68. Median iris ruler 42.00/42.17 px -> 0.2786/0.2775 mm per px, so one endpoint moving one quantum, halved by the two-chord mean (src/core/aperture.ts:38-64), is 0.01003/0.00999 mm. Medians are 1.97 and 1.95 quanta; 38.3% / 40.2% of deltas fall within 1.5 quanta. p95 is 28.3 / 22.7 quanta, unaffected. docs/aperture-noise-floor.txt:49-50 lists 'ONE face, ONE camera, ONE lighting, at the fixture's frame rate' and never the storage precision.

_Note._ Downgraded on impact, not on arithmetic. The threshold row it names does not ride the quantised half of the distribution: ROADMAP.md:172 and docs/aperture-noise-floor.txt:84-88 both say 10.7b derives the cross-iris refusal from the CROSS-EYE distribution 'not from the temporal one'. I measured that distribution: median 0.2005 mm = 20.0 quanta, p5 = 3.1 quanta, only 2.6% of values within 1.5 quanta — not quantisation-dominated. Also, rounding adds noise to small deltas rather than removing it, so the published medians are a conservative upper bound and the conclusion they support ('temporal noise an order of magnitude under the 0.4 mm shallow-blink band') only strengthens on an unrounded fixture. What survives is the smaller claim: the conditions block omits the fixture's storage precision, and a reader cannot tell that the median sits ~2 quanta above the floor.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity low.** Arithmetic reproduced from the fixture. src/core/fixtureRecording.ts:35-38 rounds every stored landmark to 1e-4. Recomputing the committed pipeline over test/fixtures/session-01.json at 1280x720: iris ruler median 42.00 px, so 0.2786 mm/px; one y quantum is 1e-4 * 720 * 0.2786 = 0.02006 mm on a single chord, halved to 0.01003 mm by the two-chord mean at src/core/aperture.ts:37-64. The published medians (docs/aperture-noise-floor.txt:49-50, left 0.020 / right 0.019) are 1.97 and 2.00 quanta; my per-eye reconstruction returns left median 0.0198 (matching the published 0.020) with 38.3% of left and 38.9% of right deltas at or under 1.5 quanta. The p95s are unaffected as filed: 0.286 and 0.242 mm are 28 to 34 quanta. The conditions paragraph (docs/aperture-noise-floor.txt:44-48) names one face, one camera, one lighting, one frame rate — not storage precision. The live path does not round: round4 is only reached through serializeFixture, so this is a property of the fixture, not the instrument.

_Note._ Mechanism confirmed exactly; the impact line is what needs correcting. The finding says the lower half of "the distribution 10.7b would derive a threshold from" is quantisation, but the doc's own closing paragraph (docs/aperture-noise-floor.txt:78-84) states that 10.7b's cross-eye refusal "must be derived from that distribution, not from the temporal one" — and the cross-eye median is 0.200 mm, about 20 quanta, nowhere near the rounding scale. So no refusal currently planned is mis-placed by this. The residue is a conditions omission on one published number, and it errs conservatively: rounding ADDS variance, so 0.020 mm is an upper bound on the true temporal wobble and the doc's conclusion (temporal noise is not what hides shallow blinks) is if anything strengthened. Low is right. On proportionality: add the precision to the conditions block, yes. But do NOT re-record session-01.json in place — it is the committed fixture behind test/core/frameTrace, sessionFixture and calibrationWindow tests and the noise-floor numbers are pinned to three decimals by test/core/apertureNoise.test.ts; replacing it silently rewrites a scored prediction. A separate unrounded fixture, with its own dated prediction, is the version of this fix that keeps the ratchet honest.

#### F-095. Reset residue: in-flight guided calibration, inference samples and post-stop buttons survive a session boundary

|                             |                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **low**                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Category                    | defect                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Raised by                   | wiring                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Files                       | `src/main.ts:950-1039`, `src/main.ts:1699-1700`, `src/main.ts:2912`, `src/main.ts:4109-4110`, `src/main.ts:4144-4150`, `src/main.ts:4175-4178`, `src/main.ts:4210-4211`, `src/core/guidedCalibration.ts:229-231` |

**Claim.** One session's controls or readouts act on another's clock.

**Impact.** A stuck overlay over a clip and a stimulus on a stopped camera look like broken controls.

**Fix as proposed.** Null calibration state and clear inference samples in resetSession; gate mark/light on running; refuse or export every stimulus start.

**Evidence as filed.** resetSession does not touch the calibration session or overlay; inferenceSamplesMs is never reset; sessionStartedAtEpochMs persists after Stop so Mark and Light response stay enabled; a second stimulus overwrites the first's start.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity low.** All four legs hold. (1) resetSession (src/main.ts:950-1039) clears the GAZE calibration (captureState/calibrationRequested/calibrationOverlay at :993-995) but never blinkCalibrationSession / blinkCalibrationRequested / blinkCalibrationOverlay (declared :1699-1700, cleared only by the click-to-cancel handler at :1753-1756 and on 'done' at :3464-3465). Carried into a clip run this sticks permanently: src/core/guidedCalibration.ts:227-231 returns state unchanged when nowMs < startedAtMs, and a file source restarts the pipeline clock at the clip's media time (src/main.ts:2915-2925), so a session started on performance.now() can never advance and the overlay stays up until clicked. (2) inferenceSamplesMs (:2912) is assigned only at :3026 and never in resetSession. (3) The stop handler (:2667-2678) only calls setState({kind:'idle'}); render() (:860-934) touches neither markButton nor lightResponseButton, and neither sessionStartedAtEpochMs (:2805, set at :3846) nor frameSource is cleared, so refreshLightResponseButton's condition (:4176-4178) and markButton.disabled (:4211) both stay satisfied — startLightStimulus (:4145-4150) will run a fullscreen dark/bright stimulus on a stopped camera, and a post-stop Mark stamps `lastRecordAtMs ?? 0` (:4225), frozen at the last live record. (4) lightStimulusStartMs is overwritten unconditionally at :4150 while the export writes one row set from it (:2388).

_Note._ Confirmed as filed. Two calibrations of degree worth passing on: the inference-samples leg is the weakest — pushSample caps the array at 60 (:3026-3030) and the mean is display-only (no export consumer for meanDurationMs), so contamination is ~2 s of one readout; and the stuck guided-calibration overlay has a documented escape hatch (click anywhere, :1752-1757). The load-bearing residue is the honesty one: a light stimulus can start, and land in the export's stimulus metadata rows, on a camera that is no longer measuring.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity low.** Verified, with the sub-claims unequal in weight. The stop handler at src/main.ts:2667-2678 bumps sourceRunToken, sets state idle and releases the camera; it does not clear sessionStartedAtEpochMs and does not call refreshMarkButton or refreshLightResponseButton, and render() (src/main.ts:880-933) never touches either button. So after Stop, src/main.ts:4210-4211 (`markButton.disabled = sessionStartedAtEpochMs === null`) and :4175-4177 both still read enabled. That matters most for Mark: the handler at :4224-4234 stamps the marker at lastRecordAtMs (not reset on stop, only in resetSession at :966), markers are exported (:2363 sessionMetadataRows) and marker 1 and marker 2 define the participant report's marked window (:2415-2426) — the pilot protocol's ground-truth device. Light response is real but self-limiting: startLightStimulus (:4144-4150) will run a full-screen stimulus over a stopped camera and set lightStimulusStartMs, but the export then carries a start with no rows in window and analysis/blinklab/light_response.py's usable-data gate returns INCONCLUSIVE rather than a fabricated result. Second-stimulus overwrite at :4151 is data loss (the first run's seconds fall outside the recorded window), not mislabelling. Two sub-claims are weaker than filed: the guided calibration overlay has a click-anywhere-to-cancel handler at :1753-1757 that nulls the session and hides the overlay, and it covers the viewport at z-index 10, so a source change mid-calibration is barely reachable and one click recovers; inferenceSamplesMs (:2912, :3026-3033) is a rolling 60-sample display readout that is exported nowhere, and :4366-4368 already says it is not a measurement of the eyes.

_Note._ Confirmed at low, but the bundle should not be fixed as one unit. The material item is the mark/light gate on a stopped session — one condition, and it protects the instrument's own validation apparatus from a silent bad marker; do that. Refusing or exporting every stimulus start is the second-best item. Nulling the calibration session in resetSession is cheap and correct as defence in depth but fixes a path the overlay's cancel handler already covers, and clearing inferenceSamplesMs is cosmetic. Sizing the whole finding by its worst sub-claim would overstate it; sizing it by its weakest would lose the marker path, which is the one that can quietly corrupt a ground truth this project relies on.

#### F-096. The telemetry block comment overclaims install order: ES imports evaluate the MediaPipe bundle before line 285 runs

|                             |                                                                                                                                                |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **low**                                                                                                                                        |
| Category                    | overclaim                                                                                                                                      |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                                                              |
| Raised by                   | wiring                                                                                                                                         |
| Files                       | `src/main.ts:268`, `src/main.ts:279-285`, `src/io/landmarker.ts:1`, `src/io/telemetryBlock.ts:22-23`, `test/e2e/telemetryBlock.spec.ts:81-110` |

**Claim.** The protection rests on an unstated bundle property; a future maintainer could reorder or lazy-load without knowing what the order protects.

**Impact.** A privacy claim guarded by an inaccurate comment.

**Fix as proposed.** State the true reason; optionally install from a side-effect module imported first; note the bundle sha in the ratchet rationale.

**Evidence as filed.** The bundle's top-level code runs before installTelemetryBlock; the block works only because the bundle resolves fetch at call time, pinned by the 150 s e2e alone.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity low.** src/main.ts:268 statically imports ./io/landmarker, whose line 1 statically imports @mediapipe/tasks-vision; installTelemetryBlock() is called in main.ts's own body at :285, so the bundle's top level is evaluated first (I reproduced the ordering with a three-module ESM chain in node: bundle -> landmarker -> main body, printed in that order). The comment at src/main.ts:279-285 nonetheless says the call 'puts the guard up before anything else runs'. The unstated property is real and I checked it against the vendored bundle: node_modules/@mediapipe/tasks-vision/vision_bundle.mjs contains three bare `fetch(` call sites (model fetch, graph fetch, and the XHR-less POST helper) and zero `new XMLHttpRequest` / `sendBeacon` occurrences, with no module-scope capture such as `const f = fetch` — so patching globalThis after evaluation still catches them. Only test/e2e/telemetryBlock.spec.ts:81-110 (test.setTimeout(150_000)) exercises that against the real bundle; the deterministic spec above it calls the three transports directly and never loads the model.

_Note._ Confirmed as a comment-accuracy defect, with one mitigation the write-up misses: every published statement of the guarantee is already the accurate one — README.md:591 and src/io/telemetryBlock.ts:22-23 say 'before the model is loaded / before the model is ever created', as do STATE.md:227-234 and decisions/ADR-0004-model-telemetry.md:85. So the privacy claim itself is not wrong; what is wrong is the local 'before anything else runs' rationale at src/main.ts:281, which is what a future maintainer would reorder against.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity low.** The mechanism is right, verified in the bundle itself. src/main.ts:268 imports ./io/landmarker, whose first line imports @mediapipe/tasks-vision, so the bundle's top level evaluates before installTelemetryBlock() at :285 and before the comment at :279-284 claiming it runs "before anything else". The unstated property is real and load-bearing: in node_modules/@mediapipe/tasks-vision/vision_bundle.mjs the logger class does `this.m.send({url:"https://odml.pa.googleapis.com/v1/log",...})` on a `setInterval(...,6e4)`, and that transport's send is `async send(t,e,r){ ... await fetch(t.url,{...}) }` — a bare `fetch` identifier resolved through the scope chain at CALL time, which is the only reason wrapping globalThis.fetch (src/io/telemetryBlock.ts:85-99) intercepts it. Note it uses fetch only; the XHR and sendBeacon wraps are the net, not the catch, and prototype patching (:102-146) would survive early capture anyway. Two things blunt the impact as filed. The PUBLISHED claim is accurate as written: README.md:591 says the guard goes up "before the model is loaded", which is true (loadLandmarker is called from the Start handler, long after :285), so no reader-facing statement is wrong. And the property is not pinned by an untested test — .github/workflows/ci.yml runs `npm run e2e` (Chromium) on every PR and push to main, including the 150 s live case in test/e2e/telemetryBlock.spec.ts:81-110 that drives a real session past the 60 s mark and fails loudly if the model never ran.

_Note._ Confirmed, but reclassify: this is a comment-precision fix, not an overclaim. Its stated impact — "a privacy claim guarded by an inaccurate comment" — is the part I would not repeat to the owner, because the privacy claim readers actually see is correct and a live CI test would go red on the exact regression the finding fears (a dependency bump to a bundle that captures fetch early, or a reordering that moves installation after model creation). What survives is worth doing and costs three sentences: say in the comment that ES imports have already evaluated the bundle by this line, that what the install must precede is model CREATION not module evaluation, and that interception depends on the bundle resolving fetch at call time. The optional half of the fix — installing from a side-effect module imported first — is worth taking too, since it makes the true invariant structural instead of positional. Noting the bundle sha in the ratchet rationale is the least valuable third; the e2e already carries that duty empirically.

#### F-097. The dev recorder's 478-point face-mesh download is the one export .gitignore does not refuse, and exportGuard cannot see it

|                             |                                                                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **low**                                                                                                                                                             |
| Category                    | risk                                                                                                                                                                |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                                                                                   |
