| Files                       | `src/main.ts:816`, `src/main.ts:825`, `.gitignore:47-51`, `tools/exportGuard.mjs:27`, `test/tools/exportsAreIgnored.test.ts:63-68`, `test/fixtures/README.md:40-48` |

**Claim.** The highest-sensitivity artefact the app produces is the only one outside the gitignore net, and the guard's claim is wrong.

**Impact.** Bounded (dev-only) but git history cannot be un-published.

**Fix as proposed.** Match both quote styles; add session-*.json with a negation for the consented fixture.

**Evidence as filed.** downloadTextFile("session-01.json", ...) uses a plain string the template-literal regex misses; git check-ignore reports the name not ignored; the test claims to cover every download.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity low.** src/main.ts:816 is `downloadTextFile("session-01.json", serializeFixture(recording));` — a double-quoted literal, inside the DEV-only recorder gated at src/main.ts:825. tools/exportGuard.mjs:27 uses `/downloadTextFile\(\s*`([^`]+)`/g`, backticks only. I ran the guard's own parser over src/main.ts: it returns exactly ['blinklab-session-STAMP.csv','blinklab-report-STAMP.txt','blinklab-blinks-STAMP.csv','blinklab-frames-STAMP.csv'] — 4 of the 5 literal first arguments; 'session-01.json' is invisible to it. `git check-ignore --quiet --no-index`returns IGNORED for all four blinklab-* names and NOT IGNORED for session-01.json (the export patterns are .gitignore:51-54, not :47-51 as cited — :47-50 are the video extensions).`npx vitest run test/tools/exportsAreIgnored.test.ts` = 8 passed, including the test named "refuses every download main.ts can produce, including any added later" (test/tools/exportsAreIgnored.test.ts:63-68), which is green while blind to the one download it misses. The artefact is 478-point face mesh (src/main.ts:812) and the committed sibling test/fixtures/session-01.json is 4.9 MB of the author's own face (test/fixtures/README.md:38-48).

_Note._ Holds exactly as described, including the guard's over-claim. Two cosmetic corrections: the gitignore export block is :51-54, and the risk is bounded further than the finding says — the file lands in the browser's download directory, so it only reaches history if a developer moves it into the tree and runs `git add .`. Low is right.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity low.** src/main.ts:816 is `downloadTextFile("session-01.json", serializeFixture(recording));` — double quotes. tools/exportGuard.mjs:27 matches only /downloadTextFile\(\s*`([^`]+)`/g, so this call is invisible to the guard. `git check-ignore --no-index session-01.json`exits 1 (not ignored). test/tools/exportsAreIgnored.test.ts:63-68 nevertheless asserts it "refuses every download main.ts can produce, including any added later", and its self-guard at :72-80 tests gitRefusesToTrack, not the regex, so the blind spot is uncovered. I also bounded the exposure:`grep -c "Record fixture" dist/assets/*.js`→ 0, so the recorder is genuinely dead-code-eliminated from the production build (src/main.ts:825`import.meta.env.DEV ? createRecorder() : null`), and test/fixtures/README.md:38-45 records session-01.json as the author's own face, consented 2026-08-15, deliberately tracked.

_Note._ The material half is the guard-honesty defect, not the privacy one. The repo's own rule (CONTRIBUTING.md:50-52) is that "a test that passes against the bug it claims to catch is worse than no test, because it certifies" — exportGuard's test certifies coverage it does not have, and the very next export written with a plain-quoted string escapes silently. That is exactly the failure exportGuard.mjs:9-13 was built to prevent the third time. The privacy framing is overstated: the artefact is dev-only and absent from prod, and session-01.json MUST stay trackable because test/fixtures/session-01.json is a deliberately committed, consented fixture (NEEDS-REVIEW.md:90-114 closed this on 2026-08-15). Fix the regex to match both quote styles; note that doing so turns the :63-68 test RED until session-01.json is handled, so the .gitignore negation must be precise (`session-*.json` plus `!test/fixtures/session-01.json`) or the exemption must be stated explicitly in the test. Do not let this land as a regex fix alone.

#### F-098. Every repository guard is armed only by its sibling test file; deleting one silently disarms it

|                             |                                                                    |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Severity after verification | **low**                                                            |
| Category                    | risk                                                               |
| Effort                      | S                                                                  |
| Raised by                   | test-quality                                                       |
| Files                       | `.github/workflows/ci.yml:78`, `vitest.config.ts:9`, `test/tools/` |

**Claim.** A tidy-up removing one guard test removes the guard with a green build.

**Impact.** Low likelihood, high consequence for the ratchet and claim guards.

**Fix as proposed.** guardsArmed.test.ts asserting a sibling test per tools/*Guard|Block|Ratchet.mjs with a consciously bumped literal count.

**Evidence as filed.** Fourteen guards are enforced solely by test/tools/*.test.ts; nothing asserts those files exist or counts them.

**Reproduce skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** The structural half is true: no test enumerates test/tools (no readdirSync/existsSync over it anywhere in test/), and 7 tools — claimGuard, contrastGuard, detectorRatchet, drozyGuard, exportGuard, modelProvenance, uiGuard — are referenced by nothing but their own test file. But the consequence claim is false. tools/resultGuard.mjs:113-130 `actualUnitTestCount` walks test/**/*.test.ts counting `it(`/`test(`, and test/tools/resultGuard.test.ts:146 asserts every document stating a count states the real one. Actual today = 952; README.md:595 and STATE.md:18 both say "952 unit tests". I simulated the finding's scenario in the scratchpad (copied test/ + README.md, deleted claimGuard.test.ts, 5 `it(` calls): actual 947 vs stated 952 → the guard FAILS, red build. Two of the fourteen are also not test-only: bundleBudget runs via tools/checkBundleBudget.mjs (ci.yml:88 `npm run bundle:budget`) and learningGuard via tools/checkLearningEntry.mjs (ci.yml:75).

_Note._ Real gap, wrong failure mode. "A tidy-up removing one guard test removes the guard with a green build" does not happen — an existing coarse cross-check reddens on the test-count drop. The residual, narrower truth: the red message says a doc's test count is stale, not which guard vanished, so someone who deletes the test AND edits the count in README/STATE gets green; and deleting resultGuard.test.ts itself removes the counter along with it. "Fourteen guards enforced solely by test/tools" is also two too many.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity low.** 14 library guards in tools/ carry a hand-written .d.mts sibling (bundleBudget, bundleGuard, cannotSeeBlock, claimGuard, contrastGuard, corpusGuard, detectorRatchet, drozyGuard, exportGuard, learningGuard, modelProvenance, resultGuard, resultsBlock, uiGuard); the executables (checkBundleBudget, checkLearningEntry, mutationCheck, measure_corpus, write*) have none. CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml:75-85) invokes only checkLearningEntry.mjs and `npm run bundle:budget`; every other guard reaches CI solely through `npm test`. vitest.config.ts:9 globs test/**/*.test.ts with no minimum count and no manifest. `grep -rln readdirSync test/ tools/` returns nothing that enumerates tools/. tools/detectorRatchet.mjs:25 states the arrangement in its own words: "the test file is what CI runs."

_Note._ Real and low. It moves no published number and misleads no reader today, and the failure needs a deleted file that shows as a diff line under branch protection. But the asymmetry is what makes it worth the S: the .mjs survives deletion of its test and keeps _looking_ enforcing, so a future reader counts 14 mechanisms and gets fewer — and this repo has direct precedent for a discipline held on intent lapsing unnoticed (ci.yml:69-73, CONTRIBUTING.md:46-49: "held for 130 pull requests on intent alone, lapsed at #134"). Two corrections to the proposed fix, or it will misfire. (1) Drop the "consciously bumped literal count" — it adds friction on every new guard and is the weakest part. (2) Do not key on the name pattern `tools/*Guard|Block|Ratchet.mjs`: it misses modelProvenance.mjs and bundleBudget.mjs, and exportGuard.mjs's test is named exportsAreIgnored.test.ts, so a filename-sibling check false-alarms. The crisp predicate is: every tools/*.mjs that has a .d.mts sibling must be imported by at least one file under test/.

#### F-099. Model provenance pin proves the file equals itself, not that it is Google's

|                             |                                                                                                                                         |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **low**                                                                                                                                 |
| Category                    | process                                                                                                                                 |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                                                       |
| Raised by                   | security-privacy                                                                                                                        |
| Files                       | `MODEL_CARD.md:250-255`, `decisions/ADR-0002-model-hosting.md`, `tools/modelProvenance.mjs:21-24`, `public/models/face_landmarker.task` |

**Claim.** A change detector, not a provenance statement.

**Impact.** 'Which model' is the first question a replicator asks.

**Fix as proposed.** Add origin URL, variant, fetch date and matched upstream hash to MODEL_CARD and ADR-0002; optionally assert the URL in the tool.

**Evidence as filed.** No download URL or upstream hash anywhere; the fetched float16/1 model's sha256 matches, but nothing in the repo lets a reader check.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity low.** MODEL_CARD.md:249-255 pins the model by the sha256 of the file already in the repo (`64184e22…bc9ff`), and tools/modelProvenance.mjs:21-24 `modelHash` recomputes that same committed file — the tool can only ever prove the file equals itself. ADR-0002-model-hosting.md:18 says the model is committed and served from our own origin, and its Context says it is "not published on npm", but never says where it was fetched from. Grepping every .md/.ts/.mjs/.json/.yml outside node_modules for a download host turns up no fetch URL, no upstream hash, no fetch date and no variant name (float16 vs float32); MODEL_CARD.md:217 identifies it only as "Google's MediaPipe Face Landmarker".

_Note._ Confirmed as a provenance gap. One correction to the evidence line: there IS an origin pointer, in public/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt item 2 — https://developers.google.com/mediapipe/solutions/vision/face_landmarker — but that is a documentation landing page, not a download URL, and it carries no hash, variant or date, so a replicator still cannot check that the committed 3.7 MB binary is the one Google publishes.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity low.** MODEL_CARD.md:244-255 pins the committed file's own sha256 (64184e22...bc9ff), the lockfile integrity prefix and the landmarker options. Grepping every .md/.ts/.mjs outside node_modules for a model origin returns nothing: ADR-0002 says only "committed at public/models/face_landmarker.task", never where it came from; tools/modelProvenance.mjs:21-24 recomputes the hash of the same file the card describes. AUDIT_PLAN.md:120-122 puts the model's weights out of scope but says "Where it comes from and how it is loaded is IN scope", so this is not an accepted limit. I resolved it: `curl https://storage.googleapis.com/mediapipe-models/face_landmarker/face_landmarker/float16/1/face_landmarker.task` returns 3,758,596 bytes, sha256 64184e229b263107bc2b804c6625db1341ff2bb731874b0bcc2fe6544e0bc9ff — byte-identical to the committed file (`ls -l` shows the same 3758596).

_Note._ Confirmed, and the highest value-per-effort of the six after F-101. The section heading says "Model provenance" and delivers a change detector; nothing in the repo lets a third party establish that the 3.7 MB blob is Google's published float16/1 model rather than a modified one, and "which model" is the first question a replicator asks of an instrument whose every published number is conditioned on it. The card's prose does not itself overclaim (it says the pins stop a swap from leaving the card stale, which is true), so this is an omission, not a false sentence — hence low. The fix is now free: add the origin URL, the `float16/1` variant, the fetch date and the matched upstream sha256 to MODEL_CARD.md and ADR-0002. Do NOT take the "optionally assert the URL in the tool" half — a guard that fetches from storage.googleapis.com puts a third-party network dependency into CI and contradicts ADR-0002's own "offline development works" consequence. Record the matched hash as text; the existing local-hash test already catches drift.

| Files                       | `.github/workflows/ci.yml:67`, `.github/workflows/deploy.yml:32`, `package.json:24-26`, `package-lock.json` |

**Claim.** --ignore-scripts changes nothing today and stops the first postinstall a dependency acquires.

**Impact.** Bounded; one flag.

**Fix as proposed.** npm ci --ignore-scripts in both workflows; note in CONTRIBUTING; verify wasm assets still populate.

**Evidence as filed.** Bare npm ci, no .npmrc; only fsevents carries an install script today; 181 packages; Dependabot grouped bumps weekly with 0 required reviews; the project's own pre-scripts run under npm run.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity low.** .github/workflows/ci.yml:67 and .github/workflows/deploy.yml:32 are both bare `- run: npm ci`; there is no .npmrc anywhere in the repo (`ls .npmrc` → no such file; no match under any non-node_modules directory). Parsing package-lock.json: 182 package entries (181 plus the root ""), and exactly two carry hasInstallScript — node_modules/fsevents and node_modules/playwright/node_modules/fsevents. .github/dependabot.yml sets npm to weekly Monday with a grouped minor-and-patch update type. package.json:24-26 are prepare-assets/predev/prebuild, which run under `npm run build`, not under `npm ci`, so a flag on `npm ci` alone does not disable them.

_Note._ Accurate, including the reason the flag is free today: fsevents is darwin-only and never installs on ubuntu-latest. Minor caveat the finding does not mention — on a developer Mac, --ignore-scripts would also skip fsevents' own install step, so the "verify wasm assets still populate" check should extend to a macOS `npm ci` before it goes in CONTRIBUTING.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity low.** ci.yml:67 and deploy.yml:32 both run bare `npm ci`; no .npmrc exists anywhere in the repo. Parsing package-lock.json: 181 packages, and `hasInstallScript` is true for exactly two entries, both fsevents (macOS-only, inert on ubuntu-latest runners). package.json:24-26 has predev/prebuild → prepare-assets, and there is no `prepare` lifecycle script. .github/dependabot.yml runs weekly grouped minor+patch npm bumps. deploy.yml's job builds dist/ and hands it to upload-pages-artifact, so a postinstall in that job reaches the published site.

_Note._ Confirmed low, and the effort claim holds: one flag, zero behaviour change today. It fits the posture the repo already pays for elsewhere (SHA-pinned actions, vendored model, blocked telemetry POST, license test). One trap the fix must avoid, because it would break a strength: put `--ignore-scripts` on the two `npm ci` invocations ONLY. Setting `ignore-scripts=true` in an .npmrc would also suppress pre/post hooks for `npm run`, which kills `prebuild` → `prepare-assets` and ships a build with no MediaPipe WASM — the same silent-model-missing failure mode documented at docs/audit/appendix-chunk-5-all-findings.md:146. With the CLI flag on `npm ci` only, `npm run build` still fires prebuild, so the finding's "verify wasm assets still populate" check is the right acceptance test.

#### F-105. 'Camera delivery: 3 frames per second, of which this instrument read 5' — the page can print an impossibility

|                             |                                                                                                            |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **low**                                                                                                    |
| Category                    | defect                                                                                                     |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                          |
| Raised by                   | demo-ux                                                                                                    |
| Files                       | `src/core/deliveryRate.ts:100-116`, `src/core/deliveryRate.ts:126-147`, `src/core/deliveryRate.ts:167-179` |

**Claim.** Two rates over different spans are printed as part-of-whole.

**Impact.** One impossible sentence discounts every other number for a skeptical reader.

**Fix as proposed.** Measure both over one common span; say 'read all N' when sampled >= delivered; unit test sampled <= delivered.

**Evidence as filed.** deliveredFps and sampledFps are measured over different spans in the same window; the type comment says sampled can never exceed delivered; reproduced ratio 1.67 on the built page; readFraction > 1 reaches the export.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity low.** src/core/deliveryRate.ts:130-143 measures the two rates over different spans: deliveredFps = measureFps(delivered) over the delivered timestamps' own first-to-last span, sampledFps = (distinct-1)*1000/(reads[last].atMs - reads[0].atMs). I ran the repo's own module unmodified (copied to scratchpad, `node --experimental-strip-types`). Steady state is fine (3/5/10/15/24/30 fps all give readFraction 0.94-0.997). A transient reproduces the impossibility: deliveries at t=0 then a gap to t=1000 then 30 fps, with reads starting at t=1000, yields {deliveredFps: 20.22, sampledFps: 29.50, readFraction: 1.459} and deliveryRateMessage prints "Camera delivery: 20 frames per second, of which this instrument read 30". A sparser delivery gap gives readFraction 3.06 and "2 frames per second, of which this instrument read 5". That transient is the normal cold start: main.ts:1100-1105 attaches the delivery observer the moment the camera starts, main.ts:1129 loads the model "Fired, not awaited", and main.ts:2987/3024 only counts a read after the model returns — so deliveries are recorded during a stretch where no read is. The type comment at deliveryRate.ts:101-105 asserts sampledFps "can never exceed deliveredFps, however fast the machine runs", which the same file contradicts at 107-114. `npx vitest run test/core/deliveryRate.test.ts test/core/deliveryReadout.test.ts` passes (14 tests): the <=1 assertion at test/core/deliveryRate.test.ts:84 only covers the steady 30fps/126.7fps case.

_Note._ Confirmed with my own reproduction, at low severity. Two fair mitigations the finding omits: the readFraction doc at deliveryRate.ts:107-114 already anticipates "a value a shade over one" and refuses to clamp on purpose ("hiding that behind a clamp would turn a measurement artefact into a claim") — so the module knows about the artefact; and the export exposure is smaller than stated, because main.ts:590-596 freezes settledDeliveryRates() once with `??=` at report/export time (main.ts:2359 -> sessionMetadata.ts:182-184), typically long after the cold-start transient, whereas the readout at main.ts:2960-2962 recomputes live every frame and is where the impossible sentence actually shows. The real defects are the wording of deliveryRateMessage (a part-of-whole sentence for two rates that are not part-of-whole) and the false "can never exceed" comment.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity low.** Reproduced, and larger than filed. I ported src/core/deliveryRate.ts + src/core/fps.ts to JS unchanged and validated the port against the repo's own committed expectations (test/core/deliveryRate.test.ts: 30/126.7 gives fraction 0.9941, within the test's >0.98 and <=1; 30/29.2 gives 0.9733, below 1). Deliveries start when the stream goes live (src/main.ts:1099-1103) but a read is only counted AFTER the model call returns (src/main.ts:3018-3025), and the model's first inference is seconds later (LEARNING.md:579). At the first instant two distinct reads exist, spanMs is one display period, so deliveryRate.ts:142-143 returns the PROCESSING rate: 30 fps delivery prints 'Camera delivery: 30 frames per second, of which this instrument read 60' (fraction 2.003) for ~80 ms; a 15 fps camera prints 'read 60' (fraction 3.999). The filed 1.67 is inside that range. deliveryRate.ts:101-105 asserts sampled 'can never exceed deliveredFps'; deliveryRate.ts:107-114 says it can. No test pins the relation.

_Note._ Material in the honesty register, not the number register — this is the one module built to stop the page crediting the processing rate as observations of an eye (deliveryRate.ts:12-24), and at read-start it prints exactly that error. Exposure to exports is bounded: settledDeliveryRates() snapshots once (main.ts:589-596) and its three consumers are export and report, and the report is gated to after the session stops (main.ts:2628-2637), so a normal session snapshots a steady window. The residual risk is a degenerate few-hundred-millisecond session freezing a warm-up artefact into sampled_fps, which is the evidence rate for the 25 fps refusal (sessionVerdict.ts:100-121, main.ts:2970) and for the Python re-derivation (STATE.md:1504). Two corrections to the fix. Do NOT clamp readFraction: 1.002 is a real measured value in the record (docs/blink-sample-rate.txt:602) and deliveryRate.ts:108-113 refuses the clamp on honesty grounds — that refusal is a strength. And 'unit test sampled <= delivered' as literally proposed would fail on that legitimate 1.002; the invariant to pin is a warm-up guard (no sampled rate until the read span covers a stated fraction of the delivered span) plus a message that says 'read all N' rather than an impossible N. deliveryRate.ts is not ratchet-watched (tools/detectorRatchet.mjs:37-59), so no corpus re-measure is owed.
