#### F-108. GPU delegate is hard-coded with no CPU retry; the runtime throws without WebGL, so 'falls back to CPU silently' is not the whole story

|                             |                                                                                                                          |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Severity after verification | **low**                                                                                                                  |
| Category                    | risk                                                                                                                     |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                                        |
| Raised by                   | performance                                                                                                              |
| Files                       | `src/io/landmarker.ts:9-17`, `src/main.ts:1505-1522`, `src/main.ts:1532-1548`, `MODEL_CARD.md:262-266`, `ROADMAP.md:223` |

**Claim.** Without WebGL the page lands in modelFailed with a retry that fails identically; the successful delegate and a webgl2 probe are observable and unrecorded.

**Impact.** A recoverable platform reported as a broken model; the card misdescribes the mode.

**Fix as proposed.** Retry once with CPU; record delegate and webgl2 probe in export and readout (13.5); correct the MODEL_CARD sentence.

**Evidence as filed.** delegate 'GPU' unconditionally; any rejection maps to modelFailed and retry repeats the same request; the bundle throws 'Failed to obtain WebGL context' with no catch switching delegate; the wasm's fallbacks are per-operation.

**Reproduce skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** True parts: src/io/landmarker.ts:12 sets `delegate: "GPU"` unconditionally with no catch and no CPU variant; src/main.ts:1509-1521 maps ANY load rejection to `false`, main.ts:1136-1141 turns that into modelFailed, and retryModel (main.ts:1532-1548) calls the identical ensureLandmarker(), so a load-time failure does retry identically. The string exists: `grep -o "Failed to obtain WebGL context..."` hits node_modules/@mediapipe/tasks-vision/vision_bundle.mjs. But it is thrown inside function `Gh`, and tracing its callers in vision_bundle.mjs shows only two: `addGpuBufferToStream` and `Da` (`_addBoundTextureAsImageToStream`) — the PER-FRAME image-upload path, which the vision runner uses for every frame (`t.g.Da(e, t.Ba, n ?? performance.now())`) regardless of delegate. So without WebGL the failure surfaces on detectForVideo (src/main.ts:2993), not on load, and lands in the frame-loop crash handler at src/main.ts:4613-4617 => `measurementFailed` (remediation B3) carrying the raw library sentence as its reason (src/core/cameraState.ts:66) — a state with no retry button. Also, the wasm carries a graph-level fallback string, not only per-operation ones: `strings public/mediapipe-wasm/vision_wasm_internal.wasm` yields "Missing InferenceCalculator registration for %s. Falling back to %s." alongside "Following operations are not supported by GPU delegate:" and "Fall back on WebGL 1."

_Note._ Real core, wrong mechanism and wrong fix. (1) The stated failure path is wrong: a no-WebGL browser does not land in modelFailed with an identical retry; it runs, then dies on the first inference into measurementFailed with a raw MediaPipe string and NO retry control — which is a different (and arguably worse) defect than the one written. (2) The fix would not work: because the frame upload goes through the WebGL texture path for every delegate, retrying with delegate CPU cannot rescue a browser that has no WebGL. (3) The MODEL_CARD.md:263-264 sentence is defensible, not a misdescription — the wasm's own "Missing InferenceCalculator registration... Falling back to" string is exactly a silent CPU fallback, and the card already says GPU is "a request, not an observation". (4) The recording half is not an unrecorded gap: ROADMAP.md:223 (row 13.5) already commits the request, a webgl2 probe and p50/p95 inference to the export, and the finding cites that row itself. What survives at low severity: no delegate fallback is attempted anywhere, and a WebGL-side failure is presented to the user as an untranslated library sentence in a dead-end state.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity low.** Verified end to end. src/io/landmarker.ts:12 hard-codes delegate 'GPU' with no alternative; ensureLandmarker maps any rejection to false (src/main.ts:1505-1521) and setState modelFailed (main.ts:1140,1235); retryModel calls the identical loadLandmarker (main.ts:1532-1548). The vendored runtime does throw: node_modules/@mediapipe/tasks-vision/vision_bundle.mjs contains 'if(!(r=t.i.canvas.getContext("webgl2")||t.i.canvas.getContext("webgl")))throw Error("Failed to obtain WebGL context from the provided canvas.")' in the texture-bind path. Sharper than the finding filed: the state's user-facing sentence is 'The measuring model could not be loaded ... This is often a network problem. Check your connection, then click "Retry loading the model"' (src/core/cameraState.ts:75) — a false diagnosis plus a retry that cannot succeed. MODEL_CARD.md:262-266 and ROADMAP.md:223 both carry 'falls back to CPU silently'.

_Note._ Confirmed at low: nothing published moves, and the affected population (no obtainable WebGL context, after Chrome/Firefox software-GL fallbacks) is small and unmeasured. But it is a page sentence that is untrue on the devices where it fires, which is this project's own sorest register. Split the fix by cost, because the halves are not alike. Free and correct now: hedge cameraState.ts:75 so it does not diagnose the network as the cause, and amend the two 'falls back to CPU silently' sentences (MODEL_CARD.md:262-266, ROADMAP.md:223) to say the fallback is per-operation and a missing WebGL context is a hard failure — neither file is ratchet-watched. The webgl2-probe half is already row 13.5 (ROADMAP.md:223) and needs no new row. Only the CPU retry is expensive: src/io/landmarker.ts IS a watched detector source (tools/detectorRatchet.mjs:59), so touching it turns the build red until a corpus re-measure or a dated caveat lands — correctly, since delegate choice can move numbers. Weigh it knowing the payoff is modest: CPU inference on this chain would likely land under the 25 fps evidence floor and be refused anyway, so the win is an honest gated session instead of a dead end. The compensating prize is that a GPU rejection followed by a CPU success is the first DISCRIMINATING evidence of the executed delegate the vendored API otherwise denies — the exact observability 13.5 is chasing.

#### F-109. The 1 Hz pupil read redraws the full 1920x1080 frame into a non-readback canvas to sample a box a few dozen pixels wide

|                             |                                                                                                              |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Severity after verification | **low**                                                                                                      |
| Category                    | performance                                                                                                  |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                            |
| Raised by                   | performance                                                                                                  |
| Files                       | `src/io/videoCanvas.ts:130-137`, `src/main.ts:502-503`, `src/main.ts:3798-3803`, `src/core/pupil.ts:268-298` |

**Claim.** A periodic full-frame draw plus synchronous readback for a measurement that is dead in practice.

**Impact.** A once-per-second hitch, worst on phones; pure waste.

**Fix as proposed.** willReadFrequently: true; draw only the source rect; skip when iris width is below the measured floor.

**Evidence as filed.** The offscreen canvas is sized to the full video and drawn whole before getImageData; the context lacks willReadFrequently so each read is a GPU-to-CPU stall; the box is ~120 px; the estimator returns null at the project's iris sizes.

**Reproduce skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** Mechanism confirmed, all four cited sites read as described. src/io/videoCanvas.ts:130-137: `if (canvas.width !== width || canvas.height !== height) { canvas.width = width; canvas.height = height; }` then `context.drawImage(video, 0, 0, width, height)` then `return context.getImageData(box.x, box.y, box.width, box.height)` -- the whole frame is drawn, only the box is read. src/main.ts:502-503: `const pupilCanvas = document.createElement("canvas"); const pupilContext = pupilCanvas.getContext("2d");` -- no willReadFrequently option, confirmed. src/io/camera.ts:28-32 requests `width: {ideal: 1920}, height: {ideal: 1080}`, while the visible canvas is capped at 640 (src/main.ts:1042-1045, `displaySize(widthPx, heightPx, 640)`), so the pupil canvas really is a second, full-resolution surface, not a re-use of the display one. Cadence confirmed: main.ts:3774 `if (lastRecordAtMs === null || nowMs - lastRecordAtMs >= 1000)` gates the call at main.ts:3803, and the enclosing block runs whenever `state.kind === "running"`, i.e. every live camera session, not only while exporting. Single call site: grep for readVideoPixels/pupilContext returns only src/main.ts:539 and the definition. Estimator's real-world yield confirmed from the project's own committed result, docs/pupil-light-result.txt:11,35 -- 1 of 239 in-window seconds, 0.4%, against a >=50% gate -- with the limit localised to the 43 px median iris (docs/pupil-light-result.txt:32). Waste ratio computed with node: at the documented 43 px median iris and marginFactor 1.4 (src/core/pupil.ts:273,286,290-293) the box is 62x62 = 3844 px, 0.18% of a 1920x1080 frame -- the draw is ~540x larger than the region sampled, and the canvas holds an 8.3 MB backing store for it.

_Note._ Real and correctly located, but three of the finding's own claims do not survive checking, and a third of its fix is barred by the repo's contract. (1) Wrong number: the evidence says "the box is ~120 px"; marginFactor multiplies the RADIUS (src/core/pupil.ts:286, `const half = irisRadiusPx * marginFactor`), so the box is 1.4x the DIAMETER = 62 px at the documented 43 px iris, not 120. Off by 2x; the title's "a few dozen pixels" is the correct figure, the evidence line contradicts it. (2) "A once-per-second hitch" is unmeasured and overstated. The readback is 62x62 (~15 KB) off a private canvas whose only pending work is the one blit, so the sync flushes one draw, not the page pipeline -- a few ms once per second against a 33-40 ms frame budget is a cost, not a hitch, and neither the finding nor the repo has a timing to support the stronger word. (3) "Pure waste" mischaracterises the column: the null-heavy pupilDiameterMm column IS the evidence base for the project's published refusal (ROADMAP.md:157, docs/pupil-light-result.txt), which under null-never-zero is a measurement, and ROADMAP.md:230 keeps 13.12 dormant-but-armed rather than removed. Low-yield, not waste. (4) The prescribed fix's third leg -- "skip when iris width is below the measured floor" -- has no floor to use: ROADMAP.md:229 row 13.11 is UNTICKED and explicitly requires "the 43 px anchor committed as a one-line prediction BEFORE the sweep". Gating live code on a floor nobody has measured would pre-empt an unrun pre-registered experiment, which is the one thing this repo does not permit. (5) The first leg is also unsafe alone: willReadFrequently:true forces a CPU-backed canvas, making a 1920x1080 video drawImage more expensive, so it is a win only together with the source-rect draw. What survives is the middle leg and it is worth doing on its own merits: `context.drawImage(video, box.x, box.y, box.width, box.height, 0, 0, box.width, box.height)` in src/io/videoCanvas.ts with getImageData at 0,0 removes ~540x of per-second draw and the 8.3 MB surface, is behaviour-preserving, and needs no new number from anyone. Severity stays low (already the floor) -- the honest framing is a small, cheap cleanup, not a performance defect.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity low.** Mechanism verified end to end. src/io/videoCanvas.ts:130-137 sizes the offscreen canvas to the FULL source frame (`canvas.width = width` where `width = video.videoWidth`) and draws the whole frame (`context.drawImage(video, 0, 0, width, height)`) before `getImageData(box.x, box.y, box.width, box.height)` at line 137. src/io/camera.ts:29-30 requests `width: {ideal: 1920}, height: {ideal: 1080}`, so the drawn frame really is ~2M pixels. src/main.ts:502-503 creates the context with no options (`pupilCanvas.getContext("2d")`), so `willReadFrequently` is indeed absent. src/main.ts:539 is the only caller (`readVideoPixels(pupilContext, video, region.box)`), reached from `measurePupilMm` (src/main.ts:510-557), which is invoked only inside the ~1 Hz record gate at src/main.ts:3774 / 3801-3802 — inside the same synchronous frame callback that runs `landmarker.detectForVideo` (src/main.ts:2993), so a readback stall does sit in the detection path. Box size: src/core/pupil.ts:286 uses `marginFactor = 1.4` on the iris RADIUS, so at the repo's own 43 px iris (ROADMAP.md:157, STATE.md:297) the box is ~60x60 px, not the ~120 px the finding states — the waste ratio is worse than claimed, not better. Deadness confirmed: ROADMAP.md:152 says the estimator 'resolved the pupil in under 1% of webcam seconds' and ROADMAP.md:157 records 1 of 239 in-window seconds (0.4%).

_Note._ Confirmed at low, with the fix trimmed. Materiality: this changes no published number (a source-rect draw at 1:1 scale is pixel-identical, so nothing under tools/detectorRatchet.mjs moves), misleads no reader, and fabricates nothing — null-never-zero is intact (src/main.ts:3802-3806 prints 'no valid measurement' and featureRecord.ts:120 gates the column through nonNegativeOrNull). It is not cosmetic either, because frame budget is this instrument's binding constraint (the 25 fps gate, src/core/fpsGate.ts:25; the resolution-versus-rate probe ROADMAP.md:225; 'inference once per photograph' ROADMAP.md:227), and the cost sits in the detect callback. But the cost is once per second against a per-frame MediaPipe inference that dominates it, and the finding offers no measurement of the hitch it asserts — 'worst on phones' is exactly the kind of unconditioned claim this repo does not accept. Low is right; it does not reach medium. Not an accepted limit: main.ts:3798-3800 and STATE.md:369-370 document the 1 Hz gate as the mitigation for 'getImageData is not free', but nothing anywhere accepts drawing the FULL frame to sample a 60 px box, so this survives as news. Fix proportionality — only one of the three parts should ship. (1) 'draw only the source rect' is correct, contained, and number-neutral: readVideoPixels already returns box-local pixels that main.ts:546-553 re-crops at {x:0,y:0}, so sizing the canvas to the box and using the 9-arg drawImage at 1:1 is a local change, and it PRESERVES the strength LEARNING.md:1159 was written to protect (clean, unmirrored, full-camera-resolution, overlay-free source — 'display and measurement are different consumers of the same frame'). (2) 'willReadFrequently: true' is misguided here: it forces a CPU-backed canvas, which penalises the drawImage of a GPU-resident video frame, and 1 Hz is not 'frequently' — this part would likely cost more than it saves and should be dropped absent a measurement. (3) 'skip when iris width is below the measured floor' should NOT be done now: there is no measured floor, and ROADMAP.md:229 (13.11, unticked) exists to derive it and explicitly requires 'the 43 px anchor committed as a one-line prediction BEFORE the sweep'. Coding a guessed floor into the instrument would bake an unmeasured constant into a shipped gate and contaminate 13.11's pre-registration — the repo's own pre-registration rule forbids it. Finally, 'pure waste' overstates: the estimator is deliberately kept alive for 13.11 and the dormant, owner-gated 13.12 (ROADMAP.md:230), so this is a live-but-idle instrument, not dead code to delete.

#### G-Browser--1. Headline results say the corpus reproduced across a different "browser binary"; the source says "WebKit binary"

|                             |                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **low**                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Category                    | overclaim                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Raised by                   | Browser-engine conditioning of the published detection numbers                                                                                                                                                             |
| Files                       | `README.md:45`, `MODEL_CARD.md:29`, `tools/resultsBlock.mjs:233`, `docs/eyeblink8-result.txt:170`, `tools/measure_corpus.mjs:46`, `tools/measure_corpus.mjs:128`, `tools/diagnoseClip.mjs:29`, `tools/diagnoseClip.mjs:41` |

**Claim.** The two most-read statements of the Eyeblink8 result generalise a two-WebKit-build reproduction into a claim about 'a different browser binary', which an ordinary reader takes as engine-independence. No blink-detection number in this repository has ever been measured on a second engine.

**Impact.** This is the repo's own failure mode — correct numbers, rotten sentence — in the one block the results guard regenerates and therefore treats as authoritative. It matters more than usual because the engine is the single dimension the deployed page varies on: the corpus is measured in WebKit and the page ships to Chrome and Android. A reader deciding whether the 83.6/84.0 figures describe what their visitors will get is being answered with evidence that does not address the question.

**Fix as proposed.** One word, in two places. Change 'browser binary' to 'WebKit binary' in the template string at tools/resultsBlock.mjs:233 and regenerate with `npm run results:write` (the test will hold README.md:45 to it), and make the same edit at MODEL_CARD.md:29. Then add one clause naming what remains unmeasured: 'both runs were WebKit; no engine other than WebKit has measured this corpus.'

**Evidence as filed.** The source record says the reproduction spanned 'a different processor generation, operating system and WebKit binary' (docs/eyeblink8-result.txt:170). The generated README bullet drops the qualifier: 'across a different processor, operating system, browser binary and fifteen commits of instrument change' (README.md:45, hard-coded in the template at tools/resultsBlock.mjs:233). MODEL_CARD.md:29 repeats 'browser binary' by hand and adds 'the measurements that eliminated the code, the files, the model and the runtime as causes' — an elimination list from which the engine is absent as a candidate. Meanwhile every corpus and diagnostic run in the repo launches one engine: `import { webkit } from "@playwright/test"` (tools/measure_corpus.mjs:46) and `await webkit.launch()` (:128), same at tools/diagnoseClip.mjs:29,41. There is no Chromium, Firefox or Safari-proper corpus run anywhere in the repository.

**Reproduce skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** The cited strings are all real: docs/eyeblink8-result.txt:170 "a different processor generation, operating system and WebKit binary"; README.md:45 and the template at tools/resultsBlock.mjs:233 both say "browser binary"; MODEL_CARD.md:29 says "browser binary". Corpus and diagnostic runs are WebKit-only — tools/measure_corpus.mjs:46,128 and tools/diagnoseClip.mjs:29,41 — and there is no non-WebKit corpus run in the repo. But two supporting claims fail. (1) "an elimination list from which the engine is absent as a candidate" is wrong: docs/eyeblink8-m5max.txt:245-250 enumerates "The model runtime and the browser: package-lock.json is tracked and has not moved... a pinned Playwright version pins the WebKit build with it", and "the runtime" in MODEL_CARD.md:29 is the repo's word for exactly that. (2) "browser binary" is the repo's own settled phrase for the per-machine WebKit build, used unambiguously at docs/eyeblink8-m5max.txt:253 and STATE.md:2001 ("the browser binary built for them"), and is literally true — the two runs did use different binaries. README.md:595 also states plainly that e2e runs in Chromium and WebKit, so the repo is not concealing engines.

_Note._ Real but overstated. What survives is a one-word precision loss in the generated block (source says WebKit binary, README/card say browser binary) and the genuine, unstated fact that no blink-detection number here has been measured on a second engine — worth the one-word fix at tools/resultsBlock.mjs:233 and MODEL_CARD.md:29. What does not survive is the framing as a misleading generalisation into engine-independence: no number changes, both statements are true, and the elimination-list omission the finding alleges is not an omission.

**Materiality skeptic: downgraded, severity medium.** Verified the substitution: docs/eyeblink8-result.txt:170 says "different processor generation, operating system and WebKit binary"; README.md:45 and its generator tools/resultsBlock.mjs:233 say "browser binary", as does MODEL_CARD.md:29. STATE.md:1894 keeps "WebKit binary". And the engine claim is genuinely single-engine: tools/measure_corpus.mjs:46,128 and tools/diagnoseClip.mjs:29,41 launch only `webkit`; playwright.config.ts:18,51 runs e2e in Chromium plus WebKit, but no corpus or diagnostic run uses any engine but WebKit. Neither README nor MODEL_CARD ever states the corpus was WebKit-measured (`grep -n browser MODEL_CARD.md` → :14,:29,:99,:315 only), and MODEL_CARD's "Measurement uncertainty" section, whose opening line is "The published numbers carry conditions, and the conditions are part of the numbers" (MODEL_CARD.md:271-272), lists preparation, device-conditioned duration and the commit binding — never the engine.

_Note._ The material half is confirmed: the engine is an unstated condition on the headline in the section whose declared job is conditions, and the app ships to Chrome/Android while every corpus number is WebKit-only. Add the clause. But the wording half is overstated, which is why this is medium not high. "Browser binary" is not a dropped qualifier invented by the generator — it is the repo's own sourced phrase from docs/eyeblink8-m5max.txt:252-253 ("the MACHINE: its processor, its operating system, and the browser binary built for them"), and both sentences say "the same pinned runtime" three clauses earlier, which forecloses the engine-independence reading. The finding's sub-claim that MODEL_CARD.md:29's elimination list omits the engine is also wrong: m5max:247-250 files the browser under "the model runtime and the browser ... a pinned Playwright version pins the WebKit build with it", so "the runtime" is the engine in this repo's vocabulary. Fix stands, severity does not.

#### G-Browser--3. The executed delegate is unrecorded for every published corpus run, and the repo's own test says CI runs on the CPU

|                             |                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **low**                                                                                                                                                     |
| Category                    | risk                                                                                                                                                        |
| Effort                      | M                                                                                                                                                           |
| Raised by                   | Browser-engine conditioning of the published detection numbers                                                                                              |
| Files                       | `src/io/landmarker.ts:12`, `MODEL_CARD.md:263-266`, `test/e2e/videoFile.spec.ts:106-107`, `tools/measure_corpus.mjs:128`, `ROADMAP.md:223`, `ROADMAP.md:40` |

**Claim.** Whether the published Eyeblink8 numbers were produced by GPU-as-WebGL2 or by the silent CPU fallback is unknown and unrecorded, and headless browsers are precisely where that fallback happens. This is a larger unstated condition on the headline number than the engine question itself, because it can differ between the measuring environment and every visitor's browser even when the engine is the same.

**Impact.** The card pins four landmarker options to prevent 'this card describing an instrument that no longer exists' (MODEL_CARD.md:244-248), but the option most likely to differ between the bench and the page is the one it cannot state. If the corpus ran on CPU and visitors run GPU-as-WebGL2, the 83.6/84.0 figures describe an instrument nobody in the field is using — and the project would have no way to notice, since nothing records it on either side.

**Fix as proposed.** Pull row 13.5's webgl2 probe forward and make it unconditional rather than camera-only: record the delegate request and the probe result as export rows, so every clip measurement — corpus runs included — states which delegate was available. Amend 13.5's Check line (ROADMAP.md:223) to require the probe row in a clip-mode export, not only a live one. Then add one line to the run header of docs/eyeblink8-result.txt recording the probe result for the anchor run, or 'unknown, probe added after this run' if it cannot be recovered.

**Evidence as filed.** The landmarker requests `delegate: "GPU"` (src/io/landmarker.ts:12), pinned into the card as configuration (MODEL_CARD.md:257). The card then admits the request is unverifiable: 'the vendored API cannot report which delegate actually executed and falls back to CPU silently' (MODEL_CARD.md:263-266), with the probe deferred to row 13.5 (ROADMAP.md:223). ROADMAP.md:40 fixes the option space: 'the delegate is CPU or GPU-as-WebGL2, nothing else'. The suite already knows the fallback is real in at least one headless context: 'On a CI machine the model runs on the CPU and takes seconds per frame' (test/e2e/videoFile.spec.ts:106-107). Every corpus number was produced by `await webkit.launch()` (tools/measure_corpus.mjs:128) — headless, Playwright's default, with no launch options and no WebGL2 probe anywhere in src/ (grep for webgl returns nothing).

**Reproduce skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** Facts check out: src/io/landmarker.ts:12 `delegate: "GPU"`; ROADMAP.md:40 "the delegate is CPU or GPU-as-WebGL2, nothing else"; ROADMAP.md:223 is row 13.5; test/e2e/videoFile.spec.ts:106-107 "On a CI machine the model runs on the / CPU and takes seconds per frame"; tools/measure_corpus.mjs:128 `await webkit.launch()` with no options; `grep -rni webgl src/` returns nothing; docs/eyeblink8-result.txt contains no delegate line. But the load-bearing claim — that this is a LARGER UNSTATED condition than the engine question — is refuted by the card itself: MODEL_CARD.md:263-266 states plainly that "'GPU' is a request, not an observation: the vendored API cannot report which delegate actually executed and falls back to CPU silently", and names row 13.5 as the fix. It is stated, not unstated. The finding's premise that 13.5 is camera-only is not in the text of ROADMAP.md:223, which says only "null-in/unknown-out tests; the doc states the observability limit plainly". And the CPU-fallback worry is contradicted by the corpus runner's own measured throughput: tools/measure_corpus.mjs:31-37 records ~58 frames per second, ~71,000 frames in about 20 minutes — three orders of magnitude off the "seconds per frame" CPU path the finding cites as evidence the fallback happens headless.

_Note._ True that the executed delegate is unrecorded for the published runs, and pulling 13.5's probe into clip mode is worth doing. Downgraded because the finding's severity rests on this being a hidden condition (it is disclosed at MODEL_CARD.md:263-266 and scheduled at ROADMAP.md:223), on 13.5 being camera-scoped (unsupported by the row's text), and on the headless-CPU-fallback inference (contradicted by the runner's own 58 fps figure). The corpus is also stepped frame-by-frame, so delegate speed cannot change which blinks are found — only numerical float differences could, and nothing here evidences those.

**Materiality skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** src/io/landmarker.ts:12 requests `delegate: "GPU"`; MODEL_CARD.md:263-266 already says plainly that "'GPU' is a request, not an observation: the vendored API cannot report which delegate actually executed and falls back to CPU silently", naming row 13.5; STATE.md:109 repeats it; ROADMAP.md:217 opens Phase 13 with "never recorded which delegate actually ran"; ROADMAP.md:223 is 13.5 with a Check line, and ROADMAP.md:258 records the deliberate refusal of WebGPU work. test/e2e/videoFile.spec.ts:105-107 does say CI runs the model on CPU, and measure_corpus.mjs:128 is headless. Counter-evidence on impact: the corpus reproduced digit-for-digit on a second machine (docs/eyeblink8-result.txt:163-170) and the awake autopsy reproduced the same 67 misses blink-for-blink on different CPU/OS (docs/evidence/2026-09-02-awake-autopsy/README.md:11-18); test/MANUAL.md:12 records the XNNPACK (CPU) boot chatter as expected, and docs/log.md:25 already closed the delegate question on cost grounds.

_Note._ This collides with a limit the repo documents and has scheduled: the observability gap is stated in the model card, in STATE, and as roadmap row 13.5 with its own Check line — it is not news, and the audit brief says a documented accepted limit is not a finding. The impact claim ("the numbers may describe an instrument nobody is using") is unsupported: the corpus is frame-stepped, so the delegate cannot act through timing, and two hardware stacks reproduced every count and every miss identically, which is what you would not see if the delegate were moving results. What survives is small and worth keeping: the anchor run's delegate is not recorded in docs/eyeblink8-result.txt, and 13.5's Check line is camera-shaped. Amending 13.5 to require the probe row in a clip-mode export is a cheap, correct scheduling nudge; pulling the row forward is an opinion, not a defect. Low.

#### G-Browser--6. ROADMAP has no engine row, and Phase 13's phone rows will confound engine with device without one

|                             |                                                                                                                                                      |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **low**                                                                                                                                              |
| Category                    | wrong-priority                                                                                                                                       |
| Effort                      | M                                                                                                                                                    |
| Raised by                   | Browser-engine conditioning of the published detection numbers                                                                                       |
| Files                       | `ROADMAP.md:215-217`, `ROADMAP.md:219`, `ROADMAP.md:221`, `ROADMAP.md:223`, `docs/validation-dry-run.txt:138-150`, `docs/validation-round.txt:25-26` |

**Claim.** The era's platform-truth phase omits the platform variable that every existing result is already confounded on. 13.1 and 13.3 will produce phone numbers on iOS/WebKit and Android/Chrome with no engine baseline, repeating the dry run's exact ambiguity at greater cost.

**Impact.** The unexplained 96 ms phone versus 149-166 ms Mac blink duration (row 10.9) is the flagship open mechanism, and 'browser engine' is one of the four things that moved together. Without an engine-agreement measurement on a fixed clip, 10.9 and 13.3 cannot attribute their findings, and any phone result will inherit the same 'no explanation has yet survived' status.

**Fix as proposed.** Add one row before 13.1, in Phase 13 or as 10.11: 'Engine agreement on a fixed clip — one commit, one machine, one prepared corpus clip, two engines, paired run.' Its Check should follow the m5max template exactly (docs/eyeblink8-m5max.txt:27-40): the prediction and its three outcome classes committed before the run — identical counts confirm engine-independence for this corpus; a few blinks moving with coverage identical is a cross-engine numeric bound, a number the project does not have; coverage differing at all is a defect that stops the line. Scope it as an instrument measurement, no accuracy claim, and make it a precondition of 13.1 the way 10.3 precedes 12.8.

**Evidence as filed.** Grepping ROADMAP.md for webkit/chromium/safari/firefox/engine returns only prose (ROADMAP.md:9, :34-40, :157, :249) — not one checkbox row. Phase 13 is titled 'Capture chain and platform truth' and opens 'The app has never asked its cameras for more than the default, never recorded which delegate actually ran, and never measured its own first load' (ROADMAP.md:215-217); its rows cover phone survival (13.1, :219), rate negotiation (13.2, :220), the capture-rate claim (13.3, :221), delegate truth (13.5, :223), thermal and cold load. The engine is not among them. The record already shows the confound biting: the dry run's device gap is explicitly unresolvable because 'device, browser engine, camera, orientation and mounting all moved together' (docs/validation-dry-run.txt:138), and the six-person round is stratified by device-plus-browser pairs — 'a Mac in Safari, a Windows laptop in Chrome, an Android phone, an iPhone' (docs/validation-round.txt:25-26) — with no way to separate the two.

**Reproduce skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** The absence is real: Grep for /(?i)webkit|chromium|safari|firefox|engine|browser/ over ROADMAP.md returns lines 9, 34, 37, 157, 227, 249 — all prose or unrelated rows (227 is 13.9, matching only on 'no browser thermal API exists'); no engine-agreement checkbox row exists anywhere. Phase 13 line numbers check out exactly: :215 title, :217 opening, :219 (13.1), :221 (13.3), :223 (13.5). But the central supporting evidence is misread. docs/validation-dry-run.txt:138 ('device, browser engine, camera, orientation and mounting all moved together') is describing the state BEFORE a pre-registered test, not a standing ambiguity: :140-152 record the prediction committed before `iphone17promax` was recorded ('If it is something about iOS, WebKit or the front camera, it will miss roughly 3 of ten REGARDLESS of how fast it runs'), and :150-153 record the outcome — 'It ran at 55.0 frames per second and caught 10 of 10... The second hypothesis is refuted by the same session, which holds iOS, WebKit, the front-facing camera, portrait orientation and propped mounting constant against `iphone2`. The phone was never the problem. The rate was.' docs/validation-round.txt:25-26 does stratify by device-plus-browser as quoted.

_Note._ The finding presents a confound the record explicitly resolved as still unresolvable, which is the load-bearing half of its argument. With that removed, 'the platform variable that every existing result is already confounded on' and 'repeating the dry run's exact ambiguity at greater cost' do not hold — the dry run held the engine constant and refuted the engine explanation by a pre-registered rule. What survives is a reasonable roadmap suggestion (a paired fixed-clip engine run would be cheap and the project does not have that number), not a wrong-priority risk of medium size. Downgraded to low.

**Materiality skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** Stronger than filed on the fact: `grep -ci engine ROADMAP.md` returns 0 — not "only prose", but zero occurrences of engine/webkit/chromium/safari/firefox anywhere in the file, and no engine entry in the "Deliberately not taken up in this era" list (ROADMAP.md:252-259). Phase 13's rows are as cited (13.1 :219, 13.2 :220, 13.3 :221, 13.5 :223). The confound is on the record (docs/validation-dry-run.txt:137, "device, browser engine, camera, orientation and mounting all moved together"; docs/validation-round.txt:25-26 stratifies by device-plus-browser). BUT the roadmap is not blind here: row 10.9 (ROADMAP.md:175) already reads "Blink-duration device anomaly: the same clip stepped on phones and Macs... Check: prediction committed before the phone run; disagreement beyond one frame period falsifies the camera-side hypothesis AND NAMES THE NEXT INSTRUMENT ROW" — a fixed-clip paired design with a falsification rule that schedules exactly the follow-up this finding asks for. And the dry run did not stay ambiguous: docs/validation-dry-run.txt:139-152 records a pre-registered two-branch prediction that broke the device/engine confound by measurement ("It ran at 55.0 frames per second and caught 10 of 10... The phone was never the problem. The rate was."). Phase 13's rows are likewise pre-committed to device-scoped claims (13.3's empty-set branch at :221; 13.9 "device-scoped, never a fleet claim" at :227).

_Note._ The omission is real and the row is worth adding — an engine-paired run on one prepared clip is nearly free, since the corpus runner is already WebKit and CI is already Chromium — but this is a planning enhancement, not a defect, a risk to a number, or a misleading claim. It fails every materiality test except 'omission': nothing published depends on it, and the roadmap already carries a fixed-clip cross-device row with a falsification rule that names the next instrument row. Two corrections to the fix. First, gating 13.1 on it is disproportionate and would be a net loss: 13.1 is facingMode fallback, wake lock and orientation re-reads — session SURVIVAL, not attribution — and blocking it buys no accuracy. Gate 13.3 and 10.9's attribution instead. Second, the finding's impact sentence ("repeating the dry run's exact ambiguity at greater cost") overstates: the dry run resolved its confound by pre-registered prediction, which is the method this project has already demonstrated.

#### G-Browser--7. Coverage inversion: CI exercises the engine that publishes nothing, and the engine that publishes everything runs two local tests

|                             |                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **low**                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Category                    | risk                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Raised by                   | Browser-engine conditioning of the published detection numbers                                                                                                                                      |
| Files                       | `playwright.config.ts:17-27`, `playwright.config.ts:47-60`, `playwright.config.ts:53`, `playwright.config.ts:57-59`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml:92`, `tools/measure_corpus.mjs:128`, `README.md:595` |

**Claim.** The measuring engine and the tested engine are disjoint. Two of 27 e2e tests protect the engine that produced 100% of the published detection numbers, and 27 of 27 protect an engine that has produced none — while the config itself records that these two engines genuinely differ on seeking, the mechanism the benchmark rests on.

**Impact.** A WebKit-side seek regression of the kind that already shipped once ('a stepped clip measured zero frames there while Chromium measured every one', playwright.config.ts:29-31) would reach a corpus run before it reached a test, and the corpus runner's success check is a prefix match on 'Measured' (tools/measure_corpus.mjs:161-169) that a partial measurement would satisfy. The asymmetry also means the Chromium suite's green cannot be read as evidence about the published numbers, which is how a reader will naturally read it.

**Fix as proposed.** Two moves, neither expensive. Make the stepped-frame-count assertion (test/e2e/videoFile.spec.ts:147-190) the WebKit project's mandatory local test and state in the config comment that it is the corpus runner's only automated protection. Then, once the engine falsifier below has run, decide from data whether the corpus runner should stay WebKit or move to the engine CI already covers — at that point the coverage and the measurement would point the same way.

**Evidence as filed.** CI runs Chromium only (playwright.config.ts:17-27 is the sole project when `process.env.CI` is set, :47-48; `npm run e2e` at .github/workflows/ci.yml:92). The WebKit project exists locally only and is narrowed to one file — `testMatch: /videoFile\.spec\.ts/` (playwright.config.ts:53) with the watched path excluded (:60) — which README.md:595 counts as '27 end to end tests of which all run on every pull request in Chromium and 2 rerun locally in WebKit'. Every published corpus number, by contrast, comes from `await webkit.launch()` (tools/measure_corpus.mjs:128), which CI never runs at all. The config states the reason WebKit is kept: 'What WebKit is here to check is SEEKING, which is where the engines genuinely differ and where the zero-frame bug lived' (:57-59) — and seeking is exactly what stepped corpus measurement does, frame by frame.

**Reproduce skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** Every code fact checks out. playwright.config.ts:17-28 is the sole project under CI (:47-48 `...(process.env.CI ? [] : [...])`); .github/workflows/ci.yml:91-92 installs chromium only, then `npm run e2e`. WebKit is local-only, testMatch /videoFile\.spec\.ts/ (:53) with grepInvert /@chromium-only/ (:60); videoFile.spec.ts has three tests (:30 tagged @chromium-only, :115, :147), so exactly 2 run in WebKit, and `grep -rc '^\s*test('` over test/e2e/*.spec.ts sums to 27 — README.md:595 is accurate. tools/measure_corpus.mjs:128 is `const browser = await webkit.launch();`. But the finding omits the documented rationale in the same file it quotes (playwright.config.ts:31-46: 'WebKit on a Linux runner is not Safari on a Mac... three failures in a row that were about the platform, not the code... `npm run e2e` on a Mac covers both engines and is where this protection actually lives. Safari proper is manual check 58'). Its proposed fix is already in place: test/e2e/videoFile.spec.ts:147-187 'stepping measures every frame of a fast clip' IS one of the two WebKit tests, and asserts the count within ±1 of FIXTURE_FRAMES (:185-186). The 'Measured' prefix-match risk was already remediated: the runner's own comment at tools/measure_corpus.mjs:151-159 records it, and src/main.ts:1383-1389 refuses a zero-measurement by name before the summary line.

_Note._ Real observation, overstated as a risk. The asymmetry exists and 'CI green says nothing about the published numbers' is fair, but the arrangement is a documented deliberate retreat rather than an oversight, the seek regression test the finding asks for already runs in WebKit locally where the corpus is measured, and the silent-success path it cites was closed. Note the fixture is CFR (test/fixtures/clip-60fps-60frames.mp4, 60 frames), so that test would not catch G-Stepped--1 — but that is a different gap than the one claimed. Downgraded to low.

**Materiality skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** The asymmetry is real: CI runs Chromium only (.github/workflows/ci.yml:91-92 installs and runs chromium; playwright.config.ts:46-48 returns [] for the WebKit project under CI), while 100% of published corpus numbers come from `await webkit.launch()` (tools/measure_corpus.mjs:128), and README.md:595 counts "27 end to end tests of which all run on every pull request in Chromium and 2 rerun locally in WebKit". But the finding's own first fix is ALREADY IN PLACE: the WebKit project's testMatch is /videoFile\.spec\.ts/ with grepInvert /@chromium-only/ (playwright.config.ts:53-60), and the stepped-frame-count regression test is NOT tagged — test/e2e/videoFile.spec.ts:147 "stepping measures every frame of a fast clip", asserting FIXTURE_FRAMES ±1 at :185-186 — so the corpus runner's engine is already covered by exactly the test proposed, and only the watched path (:30, tagged @chromium-only) is excluded. The local-only choice is a dated, reasoned, written decision in the config itself (playwright.config.ts:28-45: WebKit on a Linux runner is not Safari; three consecutive platform failures; "a test that fails for reasons unrelated to the change under review teaches people to ignore red").

_Note._ Downgraded because the load-bearing remedy already exists and the remaining premise collides with a limit the repo documents and justifies in place. What survives is worth one sentence, not a medium finding: CI green cannot speak for the measuring engine, so the README's test-count sentence (:595) reads stronger than it is. The one genuinely unprotected seam the finding touches is the corpus runner's success check — a prefix match on "Measured" (tools/measure_corpus.mjs:165, :184) that a partial or inflated measurement satisfies, with the status line truncated to 62 characters at :210 — but that seam belongs to G-Stepped--2/-3, where the fix actually lands. Do not act on the hint about moving the corpus runner to Chromium without evidence: the WebKit seeking path is where the zero-frame bug lived (playwright.config.ts:29-31, :57-59), and every published corpus number and the m5max reproduction are WebKit-to-WebKit, so an engine switch would break the digit-for-digit comparability that is currently a strength.

#### G-Build, d-1. GitHub Pages publishes 4 minutes before CI finishes, and would publish a red merge

|                             |                                                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **low**                                                                                                                                             |
| Category                    | risk                                                                                                                                                |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                                                                   |
| Raised by                   | Build, deploy and notice path — how code becomes the published page, and whether a reader of a published number can find the build that produced it |
| Files                       | `.github/workflows/deploy.yml:3-6`, `.github/workflows/deploy.yml:23-36`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml:50-92`, `package.json:12`, `README.md:11`       |

**Claim.** Every guard the project relies on to keep the published page honest — the Apache-2.0 notice e2e, claimGuard's retired-phrase ban, resultGuard, the detector ratchet, modelProvenance, the bundle budget — runs in a workflow that has no power to stop the publish. The page goes live roughly four minutes before the first of them reports.

**Impact.** The repo's whole honesty architecture assumes a red build stops something. On the publish path it stops nothing. A merge that deletes public/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt still builds green and ships an unattributed redistribution of Google's Apache-2.0 model; a merge reintroducing a retired privacy phrase ships it; a type error ships. For a page people are asked to run a measurement protocol on, the deployed artefact is the product, and it is the one artefact nothing gates.

**Fix as proposed.** Change deploy.yml's trigger to `on: workflow_run: {workflows: [CI], types: [completed], branches: [main]}` plus `workflow_dispatch`, and guard the build job with `if: github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'`. No repository-settings change and no reviewer, so the one-row-one-PR self-merge ritual is untouched; cost is ~4 minutes of publish latency. One trap must be handled or the E2 provenance stamp starts lying: under `workflow_run`, `github.sha` is the default-branch tip at run time, not the triggering commit, so pass `ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}` to actions/checkout and set `GITHUB_SHA: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}` in the build step's env, since vite.config.ts:18 reads `process.env.GITHUB_SHA`.

**Evidence as filed.** deploy.yml:3-6 triggers on `push: branches: [main]`; its `build` job (deploy.yml:23-36) runs only `npm ci` and `npm run build`, and `deploy` (:38-51) has `needs: build` only. There is no `needs`, `workflow_run`, or status dependency on ci.yml anywhere in the file. Measured on the current tip: for 8ad1c06 the Deploy run started 2026-09-05T09:52:56Z and completed 09:53:29Z (33 s), while the CI run for the same head_sha started 09:52:56Z and completed 09:57:16Z — the page was live and public for 3 min 47 s before any check concluded. `npm run build` is `vite build` (package.json:12), which does not typecheck: `lint`, `typecheck`, `test`, `coverage`, `bundle:budget`, `format:check` and `e2e` (ci.yml:76-92) all sit downstream of publication. GitHub reports 300 Deploy runs; none has yet shipped a red merge, so the risk is latent, not fired. No ROADMAP or REMEDIATION row covers the deploy gate — REMEDIATION.md:317-325 (E5) reasons only about required reviews, NEEDS-REVIEW.md:169 only about response headers. gh CLI is unavailable in this environment, so branch-protection/ruleset state could not be read directly; the workflow files establish the gap regardless, since protection gates merges, not this publish.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity high.** .github/workflows/deploy.yml:3-6 is `on: push: branches: [main]` plus workflow_dispatch; build (:23-36) runs only checkout, setup-node, `npm ci`, `npm run build`, upload-pages-artifact; deploy (:38-51) has `needs: build` only. `grep -n 'needs: build|workflow_run' deploy.yml` finds no CI dependency anywhere. package.json:12 `"build": "vite build"` — no typecheck. Timing on the tip commit 8ad1c06: Deploy run 300 created 2026-09-05T09:52:56Z, completed 09:53:29Z; CI run 678 same head_sha created 09:52:56Z, completed 09:57:16Z — 3 min 47 s of public page before any check concluded. THE RISK HAS ALREADY FIRED, contrary to the finding's own hedge: three pushes to main failed CI (runs 451/455/457, 2026-08-23, shas 89658cb, d52f6f0, 937e358 — all still on main per git log), and their Deploy runs 197, 199 and 200 all concluded SUCCESS (200: 19:06:11Z) while CI concluded FAILURE (19:06:26Z). On 937e358 the `checks` job failed at step 9 `npm run coverage`, and steps 10-14 — build, bundle:budget, format:check, playwright install, `npm run e2e` (which carries the Apache-2.0 notice test) — were all SKIPPED, yet the page published.

_Note._ Confirmed and understated. The finding says "none has yet shipped a red merge, so the risk is latent, not fired"; that sub-claim is refuted — three red-CI commits were published on 23 August 2026, and on at least one of them the licence e2e and the bundle budget never ran at all. The proposed workflow_run fix and its GITHUB_SHA trap (vite.config.ts:18 reads process.env.GITHUB_SHA) are correct as stated.

**Materiality skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** The mechanism is exactly as filed. .github/workflows/deploy.yml:3-6 triggers on push to main; build runs only npm ci + npm run build (deploy.yml:29-31); deploy has `needs: build` alone; there is no workflow_run or status dependency. Timing re-measured through the API for head_sha 8ad1c06: Deploy run 33959164276 created 2026-09-05T09:52:56Z, updated 09:53:29Z; CI run 33959164317 for the same sha created 09:52:56Z, updated 09:57:16Z — 3 min 47 s of public page before any check concluded. `npm run build` is `vite build` (package.json:12), which does not typecheck. What the finding could not check, the repo can: main is protected (list_branches reports main protected:true at 8ad1c06), and the repo's own verification records required contexts ["checks","analysis"] with strict:true, enforce_admins enabled, force-push and deletion off (docs/audit/appendix-chunk-1-all-findings.md:950, restated at :1001). Every guard the finding names — licences e2e, claimGuard, resultGuard, ratchet, modelProvenance, bundle budget — runs inside the `checks` job (.github/workflows/ci.yml:76-92), which is a required context; with strict:true the merged tree is the tree that passed. And this exact item is already on the record: docs/audit/appendix-chunk-1-all-findings.md:665-673, C1-46, filed at severity low, verdict partial, for the same reason ("the exposure is small in practice because branch protection requires the `checks` and `analysis` contexts with strict mode before a merge").

_Note._ Downgraded from high. The publish path really is ungated, and the fix is cheap and correct — the github.sha trap it catches (workflow_run sets github.sha to the branch tip, so actions/checkout needs ref: workflow_run.head_sha and the build step needs GITHUB_SHA set, since vite.config.ts:18 reads it) is the most valuable line in the finding and would otherwise silently falsify the E2 build stamp. But the impact story overstates: it is not true that nothing gates the deployed artefact. Branch protection gates the content that can reach main, the required `checks` context runs every guard named, and the residual exposure is a manual workflow_dispatch or a future protection change — i.e. the owner bypassing his own gate. 300 Deploy runs, none red. It also lands on ground the August audit already walked and filed at low. Keep the fix, at low priority and behind the measurement rows; and if it ships, note that the `secrets` job is not a required context, so the belt-and-braces version is worth a glance at the required-contexts list too.

#### G-Build, d-4. A published app_commit names a build nobody can get back, including runs already measured on the deployed page

|                             |                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **low**                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Category                    | missing-capability                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Effort                      | M                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Raised by                   | Build, deploy and notice path — how code becomes the published page, and whether a reader of a published number can find the build that produced it                                           |
| Files                       | `src/core/sessionMetadata.ts:354-355`, `src/core/participantReport.ts:259`, `vite.config.ts:18`, `STATE.md:1298-1299`, `STATE.md:1342`, `ROADMAP.md:185`, `ROADMAP.md:190`, `CHANGELOG.md:15` |

**Claim.** The project can say which build produced a number but cannot hand anyone that build, and two planned rows — the frozen-instrument sibling-corpus run and the three-week n-of-1 — assume an instrument that stays still while the publish path guarantees it does not.

**Impact.** Reproduction is the project's core standard, and here it silently degrades to "rebuild it yourself from the commit, and hope". A reviewer holding a CSV stamped `app_commit: d8f0dcd` has no page to compare against; a three-week within-subject series would span a hundred instrument versions with no record of which session met which build, turning a test-retest bound into a measurement of the release cadence.

**Fix as proposed.** Do not cut a version tag — ROADMAP.md:141 already declines that ceremony and the decline is sound. Instead: (a) tag and GitHub-release the exact commit of any run that becomes evidence, attaching the built `dist` as a release asset so the measured page is downloadable and openable offline; (b) add a short "reproduce the exact page" section to README naming `git checkout <app_commit> && npm ci && npm run build && npm run preview`, stating that the committed lockfile makes it deterministic; (c) for 11.8, freeze the instrument for the protocol's duration by branching, and record in the plan which build each session ran. Until (a) exists, drop "frozen" from ROADMAP.md:185 or say what freezes it.

**Evidence as filed.** The forward direction is solved: vite.config.ts:18 stamps the commit, sessionMetadata.ts:354-355 writes `app_commit`, participantReport.ts:259 prints it. The reverse direction has no answer. GitHub reports the newest release is v0.7.0 (2026-08-07); CHANGELOG.md:15 is "Unreleased" for everything since; package.json:4 is version 0.0.1; Pages serves one build, the newest. Not hypothetical: STATE.md:1342 records "The owner ran the full protocol once on the deployed page at commit 7041010" and STATE.md:1298-1299 "ran the full protocol again on the deployed page at commit d8f0dcd" — the pilot dry-run evidence was measured on pages that no longer exist at any URL. ROADMAP.md:185 calls row 11.3 a "pre-registered frozen-instrument run" and ROADMAP.md:190 (11.8) plans "~3 weeks of sessions" with "same setup, same protocol", against a page that redeployed 17 times on 5 September alone (Deploy run numbers 291-300 that day).

**Reproduce skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** Forward chain verified: vite.config.ts:18 `const commit = (process.env.GITHUB_SHA ?? "dev").slice(0, 7);`, src/core/sessionMetadata.ts:354-355 writes app_commit, src/core/participantReport.ts:259 prints "App commit:". CHANGELOG.md:15 is "## Unreleased", package.json:4 is 0.0.1, and the newest GitHub release is v0.7.0 (2026-08-07). STATE.md:1341-1342 and :1297-1298 do record protocol runs on the deployed page at 7041010 and d8f0dcd. BUT three parts fail inspection: (1) tools/measure_corpus.mjs:57 `const URL = "http://localhost:4173/blinklab/"` with the header usage `npm run build; npm run preview` — the corpus runs drive a LOCAL build, never the deployed page, so ROADMAP.md:185's "frozen-instrument run" does not depend on the Pages cadence at all; (2) "a build nobody can get back" is overstated — source, package-lock.json and public/models/face_landmarker.task are all committed, so `git checkout <app_commit> && npm ci && npm run build` reconstructs it (the finding's own fix (b) concedes this); (3) the deploy count is wrong — 5 September 2026 carried 13 Deploy runs (numbers 288-300, 02:19Z to 09:52Z), not 17, and the parenthetical "291-300" is 10.

_Note._ What survives is narrow and real: no tag, release or archived dist exists for the commits that produced evidence, so a reviewer holding a CSV stamped d8f0dcd cannot open the page it was measured on, and ROADMAP.md:190's three-week n-of-1 has no instrument-freeze plan. Downgraded to low because the headline ("nobody can get back") is refuted by the committed lockfile and model, the flagship affected row (11.3) runs on localhost rather than Pages, and one supporting number is wrong.

**Materiality skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** The forward stamp is as described (vite.config.ts:18; src/core/sessionMetadata.ts:354-355), and the STATE.md dry-run entries do cite pages at commits that Pages no longer serves (STATE.md:1342, :1298-1299). Two of the impact claims are refuted by the repo. First, 11.3 does not run against the deployed page: tools/measure_corpus.mjs:9-11 and :57 drive `npm run preview` at http://localhost:4173/blinklab/ from a local build, with tools/bundleGuard.mjs refusing if the served bundle is not the one just built — so "frozen instrument" at ROADMAP.md:185 is frozen by git and the committed lockfile, and the Pages redeploy cadence is irrelevant to it. Second, "no record of which session met which build" is false: provenanceMetadataRows writes app_commit into every export (sessionMetadata.ts:354-355, printed at participantReport.ts:259), and docs/pupil-light-result.txt:5 shows it used in practice ("app_commit 57c60e2"). What survives is that a historical hosted build is not retrievable as a URL — though it is rebuildable from a public commit plus a committed lockfile — and that ROADMAP.md:190's ~3-week n-of-1 names no instrument freeze.

_Note._ Downgraded from medium to low. The genuinely useful residue is one line of the fix: for 11.8, say what freezes the instrument for the protocol's duration, since a within-subject test-retest bound measured across a moving build measures the release cadence too. That is worth writing into the plan before the row starts. The rest is over-built. Tagging every evidence commit and attaching dist as a release asset is ceremony the repo has already declined with reasons (ROADMAP.md:141, 8.3: "a version number is not worth a ceremony"), and it buys little when npm ci from a committed lockfile at a public commit reproduces the page. The advice to drop "frozen" from ROADMAP.md:185 is wrong and would remove an accurate word. A README "reproduce the exact page" line is cheap and fine. Note also the strength this must not disturb: app_commit in every export, plus the bundle guard's refusal to measure a page it did not just build, is already better provenance than most instruments have.
