But the defect stands on the project's own terms: tools/resultGuard.mjs:11-18 states the fix is explicitly NOT "update the prose" because "every one of those sentences was written correctly and then the run changed underneath it", which is precisely this file's condition; and `## Unreleased` is a present-tense heading with no per-entry date, unlike docs/log.md:82 which carries "2026-08-09" on the same 87.7% figure. Severity held at medium.

**Materiality skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** The mechanism is real. CHANGELOG.md:24-27 under "## Unreleased" prints 87.7% / 83.3% / 85.4%, while the current run at /home/user/blinklab/docs/eyeblink8-result.txt:5-7 is 83.6% / 84.0% / 83.8%; 87.7% now sits in the superseded block at docs/eyeblink8-result.txt:250-253 ("the 9 August run, superseded 20 August"). resultGuard's doc and stamp arrays are [readme, state, modelCard] at test/tools/resultGuard.test.ts:106-112 and :175-180 — CHANGELOG.md is in neither, and `git log -- CHANGELOG.md` returns exactly one commit, 29b571d, 2026-08-15. The "Six checks" sentence (CHANGELOG.md:71-75) is against 11 guard .mjs files in tools/ today (bundleGuard, claimGuard, contrastGuard, corpusGuard, detectorRatchet, drozyGuard, exportGuard, learningGuard, modelProvenance, resultGuard, uiGuard; 35 files total, not 21 as the finding states).

But three checks cut against the severity. (1) CHANGELOG.md:3 reads "Written 15 August 2026, against the state of `main` on that date" — precisely the defence the repo has adopted and enforces: tools/resultGuard.mjs:143-149 records that MODEL_CARD's stamp "converted what would have been a contradiction finding into a correctly scoped snapshot, the cheapest defence in the repository", and the rule is "when a stamped file changes, its stamp must change with it". CHANGELOG has not changed since its stamp date, so it satisfies that rule. (2) The bullet was factually correct on 15 August: `git log --diff-filter=A` dates the guards, and on that date the current figure WAS 87.7% (README.md:96-100 columns: 69.6, 82.8, 87.7, then the two later corrections) with exactly two earlier figures beside it; seven guard files existed and the six-check list matches them. (3) Nothing bound by tools/detectorRatchet.mjs moves, no measurement is fabricated, and the guarded README results block (README.md:96-100, generated by tools/resultsBlock.mjs) is correct. claimGuard does cover CHANGELOG — it is a repo-wide `git grep` (tools/claimGuard.mjs:44-58) — so "outside every guard" is imprecise.

_Note._ Downgraded medium -> low: this is stale-but-correctly-stamped prose in a secondary historical document, not an overclaim on a published number. The finding's own header paragraph concedes the stamp and then scores it as if it were absent. It stays a finding (not refuted) for one narrow reason the repo has genuinely not resolved: "## Unreleased" is a heading that claims the present tense, and a 15-August stamp three screens above does not neutralise it — the two fight each other, and no rule in the repo covers that collision.

The proposed fix is disproportionate and would damage a strength. The assertion at test/tools/resultGuard.test.ts:106-112 is `expect(doc).toContain(run.recallPercent)` — a containment check. Adding CHANGELOG.md to that array would force a historical record to restate the newest headline on every ratchet move while STILL leaving 87.7% on the page (containment does not forbid stale numbers), and it churns a document whose whole value is that each entry says what was true at that release — directly against README.md:107-112, "Every column stays. A project that shows you only its final answer tells you less than one that also shows you the road there."

The proportionate fix is the cheap half only: add ["CHANGELOG.md", changelog] to the STAMP array at test/tools/resultGuard.test.ts:175-180 (so the stamp must move whenever the file is edited — a rule the changelog can honour without rewriting history), and scope the Unreleased section itself: either rename it so it does not claim the present tense, or replace its quoted figures with a pointer to the README results block that tools/resultsBlock.mjs generates. Leave the released-version entries alone. The "Six checks" sentence is covered by the same stamp and needs no derived count.

#### G-Build, d-6. The font licences are paraphrased where the Apache licence is verbatim, and no test reads that half of the notice

|                             |                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Severity after verification | **low**                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Category                    | defect                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Raised by                   | Build, deploy and notice path — how code becomes the published page, and whether a reader of a published number can find the build that produced it                                  |
| Files                       | `public/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt:90-92`, `public/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt:94-139`, `public/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt:22`, `src/styles.css:21-27`, `test/tools/licenses.test.ts:20-40` |

**Claim.** Half the published attribution is a summary of a licence rather than the licence, in a file whose stated purpose is that the terms travel with the work, and no test covers that half.

**Impact.** Small legal exposure, larger consistency cost: the project's argument for shipping the notice is that a pointer rots and an offline reader cannot follow it (test/tools/licenses.test.ts:26-31), and the OFL block is a pointer wearing a licence's clothes. It is also the untested half of the file, which is how the MediaPipe version came to be wrong in the same document.

**Fix as proposed.** Paste the three upstream LICENSE files verbatim from node_modules/@fontsource/{inter,space-grotesk,ibm-plex-mono}/LICENSE (one copy of the OFL text plus the three upstream copyright lines suffices), and extend test/tools/licenses.test.ts with the same shape as the Apache assertions: the notice must contain "SIL OPEN FONT LICENSE Version 1.1", "PREAMBLE", and each family's upstream copyright line, plus each family name that src/styles.css imports.

**Evidence as filed.** The notice's Apache block is introduced as "The Apache License 2.0, verbatim" (:22) and is. The OFL block is not: :94-139 reproduces only "PERMISSION & CONDITIONS" through "DISCLAIMER", omitting the PREAMBLE and DEFINITIONS sections that node_modules/@fontsource/inter/LICENSE carries in full, and the copyright lines are rewritten rather than copied — :91 says "Space Grotesk: Copyright (c) 2020 Florian Karsten." where upstream reads "Copyright 2020 The Space Grotesk Project Authors (https://github.com/floriankarsten/space-grotesk)"; :90 similarly drops Inter's upstream URL. OFL clause 2, quoted in the notice itself at :106-111, requires each copy to contain "the above copyright notice and this license". test/tools/licenses.test.ts:20-40 asserts only on the MediaPipe and Apache strings — nothing in the suite reads lines 82-139 at all. Two adjacent questions check out clean and are worth recording as such: the fonts named (:82, :90-92) exactly match what src/styles.css:21-27 imports (Inter, IBM Plex Mono, Space Grotesk, all self-hosted via @fontsource, no CDN fetch), and the served WASM directory needs no NOTICE of its own — the upstream package ships none (node_modules/@mediapipe/tasks-vision contains only README.md, package.json, the bundles and wasm/), so Apache §4(d) is not triggered and the root notice covers /mediapipe-wasm/.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** public/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt:22 reads "The Apache License 2.0, verbatim:" and the block through :78 ("END OF TERMS AND CONDITIONS") is. The font block is not: :90-92 read "Inter: Copyright (c) 2016 The Inter Project Authors." / "Space Grotesk: Copyright (c) 2020 Florian Karsten." / "IBM Plex Mono: Copyright (c) 2017 IBM Corp.", against upstream node_modules/@fontsource/space-grotesk/LICENSE:1 "Copyright 2020 The Space Grotesk Project Authors (https://github.com/floriankarsten/space-grotesk)" and @fontsource/inter/LICENSE:1 "Copyright 2016 The Inter Project Authors (https://github.com/rsms/inter)". The licence body runs :96-139, starting at "PERMISSION & CONDITIONS" — the upstream header line "SIL OPEN FONT LICENSE Version 1.1 - 26 February 2007", PREAMBLE, and DEFINITIONS (@fontsource/inter/LICENSE:28) are all absent. I diffed :96-139 against `awk '/^PERMISSION & CONDITIONS/,0'` of the upstream file: beyond re-wrapping, TWO CLAUSES ARE SUBSTANTIVELY ALTERED. Clause 4 upstream: "...shall not be used to promote, endorse or advertise any Modified Version, except to acknowledge the contribution(s) of the Copyright Holder(s) and the Author(s) or with their explicit written permission." Notice (:129-131): "...shall not be used to promote, support or sell modified versions of the Font Software." Clause 5 upstream ends "...must not be distributed under any other license. The requirement for fonts to remain under this license does not apply to any document created using the Font Software." Notice (:133-135) deletes that final sentence. All three upstream LICENSE files (inter, space-grotesk, ibm-plex-mono) carry identical clause 4/5 text, so this is not a per-family variant. Clause 2 as quoted in the notice itself (:106-111) requires each copy to contain "the above copyright notice and this license". Test coverage: test/tools/licenses.test.ts is 41 lines total and asserts only "@mediapipe/tasks-vision", "face_landmarker.task", "Google LLC", "Apache License", "END OF TERMS AND CONDITIONS", "/models/face_landmarker.task" (:21-39); test/e2e/licenses.spec.ts:14-16 asserts the same three MediaPipe/Apache strings. `grep -rn "SIL|OFL|Font Software|fontsource" test/` returns nothing — lines 82-139 are read by no test at all. The finding's two clean side-checks also hold: src/styles.css:21-27 imports exactly @fontsource/{inter,ibm-plex-mono,space-grotesk} latin CSS, matching the three families named at :82/:90-92, and `ls -a node_modules/@mediapipe/tasks-vision/` shows README.md, package.json, vision.d.ts, the four bundles + maps and wasm/ — no NOTICE file, so Apache §4(d) is not triggered.

_Note._ Confirmed and understated, so raised low → medium. The finding characterises the OFL block as truncated-and-paraphrased (missing PREAMBLE/DEFINITIONS, rewritten copyright lines); all of that is true, but the diff shows the operative terms themselves are altered. Clause 4 in the notice states a different, narrower restriction and drops the acknowledgement carve-out; clause 5 deletes the sentence exempting documents created with the font from the licence. That is a published legal notice misstating the licence it purports to reproduce, not a formatting shortfall — and it sits in the one document whose stated rationale (test/tools/licenses.test.ts:26-31, "A pointer rots and a reader offline cannot follow it") is that the terms travel intact with the work. The fix as written is correct and sufficient: paste the upstream files verbatim and extend the test with the same shape as the Apache assertions.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity low.** Every element checks out. public/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt:22 introduces "The Apache License 2.0, verbatim:" and delivers it ("END OF TERMS AND CONDITIONS" at :78). The font block does not match that standard: grep for "PREAMBLE", "DEFINITIONS" and "SIL OPEN FONT LICENSE" over the notice returns ZERO hits — the file jumps straight from prose at :96 ("All three are licensed under the SIL Open Font License, Version 1.1.") to "PERMISSION & CONDITIONS" at :98, omitting the licence's own title block, PREAMBLE and DEFINITIONS, all of which node_modules/@fontsource/inter/LICENSE:8-28 carries in full. The copyright lines are rewritten, not copied: notice :91 "Space Grotesk: Copyright (c) 2020 Florian Karsten." against upstream node_modules/@fontsource/space-grotesk/LICENSE:1 "Copyright 2020 The Space Grotesk Project Authors (https://github.com/floriankarsten/space-grotesk)" — a different named holder, not just a dropped URL; :90 likewise drops Inter's upstream URL. OFL clause 2, quoted in the notice itself at :106-111, requires each copy to contain "the above copyright notice and this license".

The obligation is live, not theoretical: /home/user/blinklab/dist/assets/ contains 14 font binaries (woff/woff2 for Inter 400/500/600/700, IBM Plex Mono 400/500, Space Grotesk 700), so the published page really does redistribute the Font Software. test/tools/licenses.test.ts:20-40 asserts only on "@mediapipe/tasks-vision", "face_landmarker.task", "Google LLC", "Apache License", "END OF TERMS AND CONDITIONS" and the model path — nothing in the suite reads notice lines 82-139. The finding's supporting claim about the untested half is also true: the notice says "@mediapipe/tasks-vision 1.0.0" (:11) while node_modules/@mediapipe/tasks-vision/package.json:3 is "1.0.1", and the test asserts the package name without the version. The two adjacent clean results the finding records are correct as well: the families named at :90-92 exactly match the @fontsource imports at src/styles.css:21-27 (self-hosted, no CDN), and @mediapipe/tasks-vision ships no NOTICE file of its own, so Apache 4(d) is not triggered. Not documented anywhere as an accepted limit — grep for OFL/"Open Font"/fontsource across all .md and .txt outside node_modules hits only the notice itself and its dist copy.

_Note._ Confirmed at low, which is the right level: no published number moves, no measurement is fabricated, and the exposure is small. It earns its place because it is a consistency defect against the project's own stated reason for shipping the file — test/tools/licenses.test.ts:26-31, "A pointer rots and a reader offline cannot follow it" — and the misattributed Space Grotesk holder is a factual error on a published page, which is exactly the class of thing this repo guards elsewhere.

The fix is proportionate and breaks nothing. Pasting the OFL verbatim once plus the three upstream copyright lines from node_modules/@fontsource/{inter,space-grotesk,ibm-plex-mono}/LICENSE adds roughly 90 lines to a static file in public/ that vite copies to dist — no bundle-budget impact (tools/bundleGuard.mjs budgets the JS bundle, not public/ copies) and no runtime cost. Extending test/tools/licenses.test.ts with assertions in the same shape as the Apache ones puts the untested half under the same discipline as the tested half, which is the repo's own pattern rather than a new one. Worth folding in while there: assert the MediaPipe version string against node_modules/@mediapipe/tasks-vision/package.json so :11 cannot drift again.

#### G-Guided b-10. The pending regression run cannot measure the procedure, yet it is the gate the ratchet caveat is waiting on

**Claim.** The run that is expected to clear the guided-line ratchet caveat can only establish that the guided path was not reached. **Impact.** This is the priority error that matters most for the era's goal. The guided line is now the instrument's primary personal ruler and the thing that lifts the passive refusal, and the only planned evidence about it answers a question about its absence. A per-person measurement is available cheaply and is not scheduled.

**Fix as proposed.** Add a roadmap row that measures the procedure on live subjects, and put it before or alongside the regression run. The smallest honest version needs no corpus: log the verification blink of the earlier finding as an outcome (caught / missed, per calibrated person) together with the separation ratio and the sample counts, and pre-register a bar. Ship the export fields and the settle window first, so the run measures the procedure people will actually use. Correct test/MANUAL.md:66 in the same change — it is now wrong about the shipped behaviour.

**Evidence as filed.** The prediction doc states plainly that 'Eyeblink8 cannot test it: its subjects are pre-recorded and cannot perform a two-phase guided calibration' (blink-line-adoption.txt:95-103). Of its three pre-registered falsifiers (:107-123), only the third — that no committed number changes when there is no stored calibration — is reachable by a corpus run. The first two, including the precision/droop falsifier this review finds most likely, have no instrument, no corpus and no roadmap row. Meanwhile ROADMAP.md:164 records that the ratchet caveat 'now stands in the result file until 10.8's regression run re-measures', and 10.8 (ROADMAP.md:174) is about armed_then_dropped misses, not about the guided line. Separately, test/MANUAL.md:66 — the only human script for this procedure — still tells the checker the line 'does NOT change detection yet', written at eecc3da which git confirms is an ancestor of the adoption commit 1a6c88f.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** docs/blink-line-adoption.txt:96-97 reads "Eyeblink8 cannot test it: its subjects are pre-recorded and cannot perform a two-phase guided calibration"; the three falsifiers sit at :107-110, :112-115, :117-119, and only the third (no stored calibration, no committed number moves) is reachable by a corpus run. ROADMAP.md:164 verbatim: "the honest caveat now stands in the result file until 10.8's regression run re-measures"; ROADMAP.md:174 is the armed_then_dropped row, no mention of the guided line. docs/eyeblink8-result.txt:312-329 carries the caveat and states "row 10.8's regression run is already committed to do exactly that". test/MANUAL.md:66 still says the status line "was saved for your next visit and does NOT change detection yet"; `git blame -L 66,66` attributes it to eecc3da, and `git merge-base --is-ancestor eecc3da 1a6c88f` returns 0 — while 1a6c88f's message reads "a stored guided line becomes the detector's line, overrides the passive baseline, and lifts the refusal" and src/main.ts:3538-3546 confirms it (hasGuidedLine gates the readout). `grep -n guided ROADMAP.md` returns exactly one line (164): no row schedules a per-person measurement, though STATE.md:806 records "Next: a real per-user verification of the guided line's personalisation benefit needs the owner".

_Note._ All five cited locations check out and the MANUAL staleness is a hard documentation defect about shipped behaviour. One framing nuance, not enough to downgrade: the ratchet caveat's own text scopes itself to corpus neutrality ("Argued corpus-neutral... argued is not measured"), so the regression run answers precisely the question the caveat asks. The misalignment is between the caveat's narrow job and the absent procedure-validation row, not inside the ratchet.

**Materiality skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** The headline framing does not survive the caveat's own text. docs/eyeblink8-result.txt:312-327 is the caveat, and what it claims is exactly and only corpus-neutrality: "Argued corpus-neutral: the personal line engages only when a stored guided calibration exists, and a corpus clip run starts with none... But argued is not measured, and this caveat stands until the next corpus run moves the built-from line." 10.8's regression run therefore answers precisely the question the caveat poses; clearing it with that run asserts neutrality, not efficacy, and nothing in the file or ROADMAP.md:164 reads otherwise. The neutrality mechanism is real in code: src/main.ts:3539 calls effectiveBlinkLineMm(storedBlinkCalibration, personalMm) and src/main.ts:1692-1693 loads from localStorage, null in a corpus run's fresh browser (tools/measure_corpus.mjs:128 launches a fresh webkit). Two residual claims DO hold. (2) `grep -n guided ROADMAP.md` returns exactly one line (164): no row measures the procedure on people. 11.7's plan (docs/validation-plan-round2.md:1-10, frozen 27 August) predates the guided line and is about the passive baseline fixes; 11.6 is a per-device blink matrix, not a calibrated-subject read.

_Note._ Downgraded from medium because the priority error it names is not there: the ratchet caveat's claim is corpus-neutrality and 10.8 measures corpus-neutrality, so clearing it misrepresents nothing. The gap it correctly identifies — no scheduled per-person verification of a detector-touching personalisation — is real but is already named as the next thing to measure by the repo itself (docs/blink-line-adoption.txt:100-104, "Whether it helps a real atypical user is the next thing to actually measure"), so it is an unscheduled known, not an overclaim; nothing published asserts an accuracy benefit. What is worth acting on now is the cheap half of the fix: correct test/MANUAL.md:66, which is the only human script for this procedure and is currently wrong about shipped behaviour, and add the roadmap row so the measurement has a home. #### G-Guided b-11. A stored line is reapplied across cameras with no record of where it was measured

|                             |                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Severity after verification | **low**                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Category                    | risk                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Raised by                   | Guided blink calibration as a measurement PROCEDURE: how the personal ruler is captured, cued, confirmed, and carried — not its arithmetic                                           |
| Files                       | `src/main.ts:1692-1693`, `src/io/calibrationStore.ts:199-212`, `src/core/guidedCalibration.ts:118-122`, `src/main.ts:470`, `src/core/cannotSee.ts:24-27`, `src/core/constants.ts:12` |

**Claim.** A line measured on a built-in webcam at 40 cm stays in force when an external webcam or a different resolution takes over, resting on an uncited iris constant, and nothing stored allows the reuse to be audited afterwards.

**Impact.** Lower severity than the rest because the mm normalisation is a real defence and localStorage does not cross devices — but it is an unmeasured assumption sitting underneath the instrument's primary ruler, in exactly the area (cross-device disagreement) the repo has publicly declared unexplained. The missing provenance is what makes it uninvestigable rather than merely unknown.

**Fix as proposed.** Store the camera label, resolution and an ISO timestamp alongside the three numbers (parseBlinkCalibration already validates strictly, so extend the shape and keep unknown-shape entries refused), and name the source camera in the status line when a stored line is reused on a different one.

**Evidence as filed.** The stored calibration is read once at module init (main.ts:1692-1693) and is not cleared by resetSession — only the erase button clears it (main.ts:1893, :1900). The camera picker (main.ts:470) can switch to an external webcam mid-session with the mm line still in force. StoredBlinkCalibration holds three numbers and nothing else (guidedCalibration.ts:118-122; calibrationStore.ts:199-212): no camera label, no timestamp, no session. The mm normalisation via IRIS_DIAMETER_MM = 11.7 is what makes cross-camera reuse defensible, and that constant carries no citation (constants.ts:12) — while the report's own honesty block says 'Two phones measured at the same evidence rate found different blinks, and that difference is unexplained' (cannotSee.ts:24-27).

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity low.** src/main.ts:1692-1693 `let storedBlinkCalibration: StoredBlinkCalibration | null = loadBlinkCalibration();` at module init. `grep -n storedBlinkCalibration src/main.ts` gives every assignment: 1692 (init), 1900 (erase handler), 3477 (calibration resolved) — resetSession (src/main.ts:950) never touches it, so a session reset keeps the line. The camera picker is created at src/main.ts:469-471 and its handler at :1567-1569 calls beginCamera(picker.value) mid-session with the line still live. src/core/guidedCalibration.ts:118-122 is the whole stored shape: personalLineMm, openMedianMm, closedMedianMm — no camera, no timestamp; src/io/calibrationStore.ts:199-212 serializes exactly that. src/core/constants.ts:12 `export const IRIS_DIAMETER_MM = 11.7;` with a prose comment at :10-11 and no citation; it is the mm normaliser at src/core/aperture.ts:121. src/core/cannotSee.ts:24 states the two-phones disagreement is unexplained.

_Note._ Accurate as written, including the finding's own defence of why it is low (mm normalisation is a real invariance argument and localStorage does not cross devices). The cited main.ts:470 is one line off the picker's creation at :469 and its change handler is at :1567; immaterial.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity low.** StoredBlinkCalibration is three numbers and nothing else (src/core/guidedCalibration.ts:118-122), serialized verbatim (calibrationStore.ts:199-212). It is read once at module init (src/main.ts:1692-1693), set live on a resolved run (main.ts:3467-3478) and cleared only by the erase handler (main.ts:1900) — no camera-change or session-reset path touches it, while the picker at main.ts:470 can switch cameras mid-session. The line does more than adjust a threshold: main.ts:3546 makes it the printed "Personal blink threshold" and main.ts:3567 notes it lifts the calibration refusal, so a calibrated person never sees the passive no-ruler refusal regardless of the camera in front of them. The mm defence is real (IRIS_DIAMETER_MM, src/core/constants.ts:12, feeding ROADMAP.md:78's normalisation whose test holds mm stable across synthetic distances) and localStorage is per-origin per-browser, so this cannot cross devices — only cameras or resolutions on one machine. A related gap strengthens it: the export writes the PASSIVE window's certificate only (src/core/sessionMetadata.ts:202-214, calibration_samples / spread_ratio / ceiling_bound / calibration_refused) and nothing anywhere records that a guided line was in force or what it was, so a session's own file cannot say which ruler measured it.

_Note._ Confirmed at the filed severity. Low is right: the mm normalisation is a genuine defence, no published number moves, and nothing crosses devices. Two calibrations on the citation: the 11.7 mm constant is not undocumented — ARCHITECTURE.md:56, ROADMAP.md:78 and AUDIT_REPORT_AUG_2026.md:413 ("A wrong iris size is one multiplier on...") already name it and its risk, so treat that clause as colour, not as the finding. The load-bearing part is provenance: three numbers with no timestamp, camera or resolution make an unmeasured reuse uninvestigable in exactly the area (docs cross-device disagreement, src/core/cannotSee.ts:24-27) the page publicly calls unexplained. The proposed fix is proportionate and does not weaken parseBlinkCalibration's strict refusal, which is a strength worth keeping (calibrationStore.ts:213-221). Worth adding to the fix: put the same fact in the export, so a file says which ruler produced it — that is the conditions-carrying rule, and it is currently silent for every guided session.

#### G-Guided b-7. On a phone the most likely gesture silently cancels the calibration and says nothing at all

|                             |                                                                                                                                            |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Severity after verification | **low**                                                                                                                                    |
| Category                    | ux                                                                                                                                         |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                                                          |
| Raised by                   | Guided blink calibration as a measurement PROCEDURE: how the personal ruler is captured, cued, confirmed, and carried — not its arithmetic |
| Files                       | `src/main.ts:1716-1722`, `src/main.ts:1753-1757`, `src/main.ts:3454`, `src/main.ts:3492`, `src/main.ts:4183-4184`                          |

**Claim.** A stray touch during the closed phase ends the calibration with no cue of any kind, and because the person's eyes are shut they cannot see the overlay vanish. They open their eyes to an unchanged page, unable to distinguish a cancelled run from one that finished. A keyboard-only user can neither perceive nor cancel the overlay at all.

**Impact.** This lands hardest on the era's declared target device. The person's model of what happened is simply wrong, and the natural next action — assuming it worked — leaves them measuring on the passive line while believing they are calibrated. It is also the second half of the accessibility gap in the cueing finding.

**Fix as proposed.** Replace full-surface click-to-cancel with an explicit Cancel button inside the overlay (keeping the gaze overlay's hatch on the gaze overlay, where eyes are open), always write a status line on cancel ('Calibration cancelled, nothing was stored'), and add an Escape handler for this overlay alongside the existing one.

**Evidence as filed.** The overlay is position:fixed, inset:0, cursor:pointer (main.ts:1716-1722) and any click on it cancels: the handler nulls the session, clears the request and hides the overlay (main.ts:1753-1757) and writes NO status text. blinkCalibrationStatus was hidden when the run started (main.ts:3454) and is unhidden only on completion (main.ts:3492), so a cancelled run leaves the page exactly as it was. There is no Escape handler for this overlay — the only keydown listener is gated on the light overlay (main.ts:4183-4184) — and the div has no tabindex and no focus management. On a hand-held phone the person is gripping the device with their eyes shut; a thumb, a palm or a steadying touch is the cancel gesture.

**Reproduce skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** main.ts:1716-1722 sets position fixed, inset 0, background rgba(0,0,0,0.88), zIndex 10, cursor pointer. The listener at :1753-1757 is the whole cancel path — `blinkCalibrationSession = null; blinkCalibrationRequested = false; blinkCalibrationOverlay.hidden = true;` — and writes no status. blinkCalibrationStatus.hidden = true at :3454 when the run starts; hidden = false only at :3492, inside the `kind === 'done'` branch. `grep -n 'keydown|Escape' src/main.ts` returns only :4183-4184, gated on `!lightOverlay.hidden`. `grep -n 'tabIndex|tabindex|role|aria-'` shows no attribute on blinkCalibrationOverlay or its inner div (aria appears on alertBanner:2211, kssDialog:2246-2248, etc., but not here).

_Note._ Confirmed. Worth noting the design is deliberate and documented — the comment at main.ts:1751-1752 says 'the same escape hatch as the gaze overlay', and MANUAL.md item 62 makes the cancel-by-click a scripted check — so this is a considered choice being challenged, not an oversight. That does not touch the two verified gaps: no status is written on cancel, and there is no keyboard path in or out. Medium is right.

**Materiality skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** Mechanism verified exactly as described: the overlay is position:fixed/inset:0/cursor:pointer (main.ts:1709-1721), the click handler nulls the session and hides the overlay with no status write (main.ts:1751-1756), blinkCalibrationStatus is hidden at start (main.ts:3454) and unhidden only on completion (main.ts:3492), and the only Escape listener is gated on the light overlay (main.ts:4182-4187). No tabindex, no aria-modal, no focus move — against a repo that does exactly that elsewhere (kssDialog aria-modal plus focus, main.ts:2247-2248 and 4174-4178; the alert banner as an assertive live region, main.ts:3712-3714). Also verified: main.ts:3510 never writes 'Click anywhere to cancel' in step 2, only step 1.

_Note._ Downgraded from medium to low because the claim it rests on is partly refuted by the page itself. After a cancel the person is NOT left without information: main.ts:3543-3550 continuously names the line in force ('(from your guided calibration)' vs '(half of your X mm baseline)'), and the button label at main.ts:3483 is left unchanged, so a first-time calibrator has two visible signals that nothing was stored. The misleading case narrows to a RE-calibration, where the old line's label is still true and reads as the new one. The cancel-anywhere hatch is also not an oversight — it is an established pattern shared with the gaze overlay and documented as an intended check in test/MANUAL.md item 62 ('click the overlay to cancel, nothing is stored'). No number moves. What remains genuinely material is the half the severity should hang on: a full-surface cancel target on a hand-held phone, the declared target device, while the person's eyes are shut, and a keyboard/screen-reader user who can neither cancel nor perceive the phase change. Both fixes are cheap and I would still make them — an explicit Cancel button, a status line on cancel, an Escape handler and focus management — but this is a usability and accessibility defect, not an honesty or accuracy one.

#### G-Reproduc-4. Frame alignment between the stepper's origin-relative index and the annotation's frameID has never been measured; the coverage columns are cited as if they establish it and structurally cannot

|                             |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **low**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Category                    | risk                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Effort                      | M                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Raised by                   | Reproducibility of the headline: the published run's inputs live outside the repository and the evaluator that turns them into 83.6% has no test                                                                                             |
| Files                       | `src/io/videoStepper.ts:286-359`, `analysis/blinklab/eyeblink8.py:198`, `analysis/blinklab/blink_match.py:29-33`, `analysis/blinklab/blink_match.py:50-59`, `analysis/tools/miss_autopsy.py:111-120`, `docs/eyeblink8-preparation.txt:60-64` |

**Claim.** The whole benchmark rests on annotation frame k being the same picture as stepper index k, and that has only ever been argued, never measured. A constant offset of up to ~8-12 frames (270-400 ms at 30 fps) is invisible to recall, precision and coverage alike.

**Impact.** Worse than the headline: analysis/tools/miss_autopsy.py:111-120 reads trace rows strictly inside the annotation's [startFrame, endFrame], so the ~49-of-67 "face-model ceiling" and the `above_line` bucket (min_ratio median 1.24) are exactly what a small misalignment would also produce — sampling open-eye frames inside a window that has drifted off the closure. The strongest counter-evidence in the repo is incidental: 29 of 67 misses are `crossed_line` (docs/evidence/2026-09-02-awake-autopsy/README.md:33-36), i.e. the aperture really does dip below the line inside the annotated window, which would be unlikely under a large offset. That is reassuring and it is not a test.

**Fix as proposed.** Measure it once, directly, and pin it. Over the MATCHED blinks of the anchor run, cross-correlate the committed frame trace's per-frame aperture minimum against the annotation windows and report the argmax lag; commit the lag histogram under docs/evidence/ and a pytest asserting modal lag 0 with a stated tolerance. Separately, harden the reader: make load_annotation refuse (or record) an annotation whose lowest frameID is not 0, so `frame_count = highest + 1` stops being an unchecked assumption. Both become possible offline the moment finding 1's inputs are committed.

**Evidence as filed.** The stepper numbers frames `index = 0, 1, 2...` from a SEARCHED origin (`const origin = found.firstFrameSeconds` … `const target = origin + (index + 0.5) * step`, videoStepper.ts:257-296, with the inexact-landing fallback `origin + index * step` at :328 and its own comment warning the symptom would be "a benchmark indexed by frame number, shifted against its own annotations"). analysis/blinklab/eyeblink8.py:198 computes `frame_count=highest_frame + 1`, assuming frameIDs start at 0; load_annotation never checks the LOWEST frame id or contiguity — `seen_frames` (:123, :149-154) is used only for duplicate detection. I searched docs/ and analysis/ for any direct alignment measurement (`off-by-one`, `index offset`, `frameID`, `zero-based`, `alignment`): the only hit is the comment at analysis/tests/test_eyeblink8.py:87-92, which pins the arithmetic against a synthetic fixture that itself starts at frame 0. I measured what the ±4 tolerance hides by feeding the real evaluator detections shifted by a constant k over 5-frame annotated blinks: k=0, 4 and 8 all give recall 100.0%; k=9 gives 0.0%. Real Eyeblink8 blinks are longer (from the committed miss table: median 7, mean 9.4 frames), so the invisible window is wider still. Coverage cannot detect this: it compares total counts (evaluate_eyeblink8.py:166-179), and a constant offset changes no count. Yet docs/eyeblink8-preparation.txt:60-64 reasons "what a transcode CANNOT change is the frame count the stepper visits, so the evaluator's coverage columns must still match the annotations exactly" — a count check offered where an alignment check is needed.

**Reproduce skeptic: downgraded, severity medium.** The code claims hold. videoStepper.ts:314 `const target = origin + (index + 0.5) * step`, :335 fallback `origin + index * step`, and the comment at :328-334 warns the symptom would be 'a benchmark indexed by frame number, shifted against its own annotations'. eyeblink8.py:198 is `frame_count=highest_frame + 1` with `seen_frames` (:123, :149-154) used only for duplicate detection — the lowest frameID and contiguity are never checked. Grepping docs/ and analysis/ for off-by-one/alignment/frameID/zero-based finds no direct alignment measurement. I confirmed the blindness empirically against the real evaluator: 5-frame annotated blinks with detections shifted by a constant k give recall 100.0% at k=0, 4 and 8, and 0.0% at k=9; miss durations in the committed table are median 7, mean 9.37 frames, so the window is wider on real data. BUT the magnitude claim does not survive: analysis/tools/prepare_eyeblink8.py:92-107 normalises the output timeline to zero (`-avoid_negative_ts make_zero -muxpreload 0 -muxdelay 0`) with the reason written out, and :112-113/:131-137 decode-count both sides and print 'FRAME COUNT CHANGED, DO NOT USE' on any difference; the committed log header reads `# frames_measured: 4895` matching that clip's annotated 4895 (result:32), and docs/audit/appendix-chunk-4-all-findings.md:913 and :985 record MP4 stsz sample counts parsed from the containers (15784/11182/9216/5405/10663/5134/9077/4895 = 71,356) identical to the AVI idx1 chunk counts and to every exported header. framesMeasured is pure origin/step/end arithmetic (videoStepper.ts:301-360), so an origin displaced by k frames would visit ~k fewer frames; the exact per-clip agreement bounds any constant offset to well under one frame.

_Note._ Real but overstated. The gap is genuine — no direct index↔frameID measurement exists, and docs/eyeblink8-preparation.txt:61-64 does offer a count check where an alignment check is needed. The impact paragraph is what fails: an offset large enough to fake the 49-of-67 'face-model ceiling' would need ~5+ frames, and the remux's verified frame counts plus the stepper's framesMeasured matching the container sample counts exactly leave room for at most about one frame. The fix (measure the lag once, harden load_annotation on the lowest frameID) is still worth doing; the risk it guards is smaller than filed.

**Materiality skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** The impact claim is contradicted by a committed artefact the finding did not consult. docs/evidence/2026-08-09/tables-current-run/eyeblink8_false_positives.csv carries a `framesToNearestAnnotatedBlink` column computed as the frame gap from each unmatched detection to the nearest annotated blink, 0 when they overlap with ZERO tolerance (docs/evidence/2026-08-09/scripts/tables/autopsy.py:163-173). Its histogram over the 72 false alarms is {0: 45, 1: 18, 2: 1, 20: 1, 44: 1, 65: 1, 79: 1, 82: 1, 145: 1, 161: 1, 224: 1} — a hard mode at 0, a secondary at 1, and nothing at all between 2 and 19. These are the 2-3 frame re-fire fragments; a constant index offset of k frames would displace them to ~k and empty the zero bin. Any constant offset of two frames or more is refuted by this table. The 0-indexing assumption behind `frame_count = highest_frame + 1` (analysis/blinklab/eyeblink8.py:198) is also settled empirically by the coverage columns themselves: a 1-indexed annotation would give annotated = measured + 1 on every clip, and docs/eyeblink8-result.txt:24-31 shows six clips exactly equal and two with measured one HIGHER, so 1-indexing is impossible. Independently, the corpus preparation is a byte-for-byte H.264 remux with the frame count verified on both sides (analysis/tools/prepare_eyeblink8.py:7-14, :79, :142), so frame k of the MP4 is frame k of the AVI, and docs/audit/appendix-chunk-4-all-findings.md:913 records MP4 stsz sample counts parsed directly from the containers (15784, 11182, 9216, 5405, 10663, 5134, 9077, 4895) matching the AVI idx1 chunk counts one for one. The origin-relative fallback the finding quotes carries its own note (src/io/videoStepper.ts:324-334) that the committed preparation tool normalises every corpus clip's timeline to zero, so origin = 0 on this corpus.

_Note._ Downgraded from high to low, and the load-bearing half is refuted. The claim that a constant 8-12 frame offset is invisible is true of the tolerance and the coverage columns in isolation, but the repository is not relying on those alone: the nearest-distance histogram bounds any offset at one frame or less, the remux guarantees frame identity, and the coverage columns rule out 1-indexing. That kills the impact claim outright — a residual offset of at most one frame samples six of seven frames of a median-7-frame annotated blink, so it cannot manufacture the `above_line` bucket (min_ratio median 1.24) or the ~49-miss face-model ceiling. Do NOT let this reopen the ceiling question; the ceiling stands on the evidence at docs/evidence/2026-09-02-awake-autopsy/README.md:33-45. What survives is small and worth doing cheaply once finding 1's logs are committed: there is no dedicated alignment regression test, and load_annotation checks duplicates and per-blink contiguity (eyeblink8.py:147-154, :180-190) but never the lowest frameID, so the 0-indexing that the coverage columns happen to prove today is an unchecked precondition for any future corpus. Add the lowest-frameID check; treat the cross-correlation lag histogram as optional confirmation of something three lines of committed evidence already bound.

I demonstrated it — a clip measuring 600 of 1000 annotated frames printed `<-- MISMATCH` under a full recall/precision table with EXIT=0. The threshold `max(5, r.frames_annotated * 0.01)` (:174) means the largest clip could lose 157 frames (5.2 s) with no flag at all. What is left is the enforcement gap — advisory flag, 1% tolerance, fail-open on a missing header — which is real, verified, and almost entirely the same fix as finding 3 (make the run refuse rather than print). #### G-Stepped--5. Duplicated frames inflate peak closing velocity by exactly the duplication factor, corrupting three of the seven pre-registered features

|                             |                                                                                                   |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Severity after verification | **low**                                                                                           |
| Category                    | science                                                                                           |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                 |
| Raised by                   | Stepped-clip CFR assumption and the corpus exclusion mechanism                                    |
| Files                       | `src/core/blinkShape.ts:83-95`, `docs/uta-rldd-result.txt:112-120`, `docs/drozy-result.txt:19-33` |

**Claim.** A duplication artefact does not average out in the shape features: it scales velocity and A/V by the duplication factor, and it does so per-video, so it becomes a between-video covariate that a leave-one-subject-out classifier can read.

**Impact.** It is a plausible non-drowsiness route into the surprising positive at docs/uta-rldd-result.txt:10-13, and it is not one of the four leakage checks run (:83-120), which test subject leakage rather than recording-artefact leakage. These are also exactly the three columns DROZY already declares unrecomputed (docs/drozy-result.txt:24-33), so the same three rows carry two unresolved caveats at once.

**Fix as proposed.** Add a fifth verification to the RLDD record: refit with the three shape features dropped and report whether the verdict survives. That is a re-fit over numbers already on disk, minutes of compute, and it converts this from a doubt into a scored answer whichever way it lands.

**Evidence as filed.** src/core/blinkShape.ts:83-95 takes peak velocity as the largest adjacent drop divided by the dt of the REPORTED timestamps. In my run F the reported sequence is (real frame k, duplicate of k, real frame k+1, duplicate of k+1) at schedule times 0, 25, 50, 75 ms with apertures a0, a0, a1, a1. The whole a0->a1 drop therefore lands on a 25 ms dt instead of the true 50 ms: velocity exactly doubled, and amplitude/velocity exactly halved. Amplitude itself (:78) and blink duration (media-time spans) survive. Those are three of the seven columns in analysis/blinklab/rldd.py's FEATURE_NAMES, and docs/uta-rldd-result.txt:112-120 reports that the model leans partly on "slower lid-closing velocity toward drowsy".

**Reproduce skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** Arithmetic verified by running the real module (vitest, scratch config, repo root): analyzeClosing([{0,8mm},{50ms,2mm}]) = {amplitudeMm 6, peakClosingVelocityMmPerS 120, amplitudeOverVelocityMs 50}; analyzeClosing([{0,8},{25,8},{50,2},{75,2}]) = {amplitudeMm 6, peak 240, A/V 25}. Exactly 2x on velocity, amplitude unchanged, A/V halved — src/core/blinkShape.ts:84-96 divides each adjacent drop by the REPORTED dt, and :79 takes amplitude from max-min. Run F reproduces on current code: stepping a 200-frame true-20.05 fps clip with one 25 ms gap near the start gives summary {framesMeasured 399, frameIntervalSeconds 0.025, stoppedEarly false}, 399 distinct fabricated media times at 25 ms, measured/span 40.10 fps (src/io/videoStepper.ts:335-337 falls back to `origin + index*step` on an inexact landing, which is what a repeat seek produces). But the corrupted columns are TWO of the seven in analysis/blinklab/drozy.py:81-89, not three: closing_velocity_mm_s and amplitude_over_velocity_ms. blink_amplitude_mm survives — the finding says so itself — and rate/duration/PERCLOS/long-closures survive because the fabricated timeline spans the same total media time.

_Note._ Mechanism confirmed and reproducible on current code; the headline overstates it twice. (1) 'three of the seven' is two — amplitude, the third of DROZY's unrecomputed trio (docs/drozy-result.txt:24-27), is untouched by duplication, so the 'two unresolved caveats on the same three rows' overlap is two rows, not three. (2) Nothing establishes the artefact happened in the RLDD corpus: duplication INFLATES measured fps (40.1 for a 20 fps clip), so it cannot be the cause of the 30 sub-25 fps exclusions, and no per-video rate is published to check the retained 148 (finding G-Stepped--4). The repo also has two live defences the finding never mentions — src/io/videoStepper.ts:348-353 breaks the run on an exact repeat landing, and src/core/frameClock.ts:47-58 rejects a non-advancing timestamp (the path that produced the recorded DROZY 3600-sought/1800-measured case at frameClock.ts:236-241). The proposed drop-three-features refit is still a cheap and worthwhile robustness check.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** src/core/blinkShape.ts:83-95 takes the peak as max adjacent drop over the dt of the REPORTED timestamps, so a duplicated series a0,a0,a1,a1 puts the whole a0->a1 drop on one step: velocity exactly doubled, A/V halved; amplitude (:78, max-min) and duration are untouched. The route is narrower than the finding states, and checking it strengthened rather than weakened the case: src/core/frameClock.ts:47-57 (acceptFrame) rejects a repeated timestamp, and src/io/videoStepper.ts:348-354 BREAKS the run on an exact repeat, so duplication reaches the shape features only when landings are inexact and the schedule fallback at videoStepper.ts:335-337 fabricates monotone times. That is precisely the case src/core/frameClock.ts:262-276 (checkStepping) cannot see, because sought == measured there and the operator is told 'ok'. A stronger sibling of the same worry is already measured in this repo: docs/audit/appendix-chunk-4-all-findings.md:200-204 puts the finite-difference peak-velocity under-read at 22-38% at 30 fps and rising as the rate falls, and docs/uta-rldd-result.txt:111-112 reports the model leaning on 'slower lid-closing velocity toward drowsy'.

_Note._ Confirmed at medium, and the proposed fix is the right one for a reason larger than duplication. The prior audit's defence of this estimator ('monotone, so Spearman only moves ~0.04') is scoped to DROZY's RANK correlations and does not transfer: analysis/blinklab/rldd.py fits standardised logistic regression on VALUES, so any label-correlated rate difference — drowsy videos recorded later, darker, at a lower phone frame rate — lands directly on velocity and A/V and reads as 'slower closing toward drowsy'. The four verifications at docs/uta-rldd-result.txt:83-115 test subject leakage, not recording-rate confounding, and verification 4's 'the weights match the physiology' argument is the one this would defeat. Two constraints on the fix so it does not break a strength: report the refit as a fifth post-hoc robustness check beside 1-4, never as a re-run of the primary (analyse_rldd.py:1-12 forbids editing the plan's cut), and add the cheaper companion check first — measured_fps by label, computable from numbers already in hand, which would settle the confound directly rather than by ablation.

#### G-Stepped--7. The export carries no witness of how a clip was stepped, so a duplicated run is indistinguishable from a clean one after the fact

|                             |                                                                                                  |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Severity after verification | **low**                                                                                          |
| Category                    | missing-capability                                                                               |
| Effort                      | S                                                                                                |
| Raised by                   | Stepped-clip CFR assumption and the corpus exclusion mechanism                                   |
| Files                       | `src/core/frameClock.ts:160-179`, `src/io/videoStepper.ts:31-36`, `src/core/frameTrace.ts:71-77` |

**Claim.** A stepped session's export cannot answer 'was this clip stepped at the right interval', even though the run knew the answer and threw it away.

**Impact.** Every corpus result — Eyeblink8 included — is therefore unauditable on this axis after the derived video is destroyed per DATASETS.md:104. The retained numbers cannot settle a question the retained numbers created.

**Fix as proposed.** Three header rows, written once at src/main.ts's stepped branch: `frame_interval_s`, `frames_sought`, `inexact_landings`. Plus a five-line post-hoc check over any retained *.frames.csv — a histogram of consecutive mediaTimeSeconds differences separates exact (irregular) from schedule-fabricated (perfectly regular) landings, so the existing UTA-RLDD traces, if kept, can be audited today with no re-measurement.

**Evidence as filed.** `grep -rn "stoppedEarly|frameIntervalSeconds|sought" src/` finds them only inside src/io/videoStepper.ts and src/main.ts's status line (:1344-1346, :1417): none reaches any exported file. The session header writes measurement_mode, frames_measured, clip_duration_s and measured_fps (src/core/frameClock.ts:174-178), and measured_fps is framesMeasured/duration — inflated by the duplication itself, so it CORROBORATES the wrong rate rather than contradicting it (run F: header would read 40.1 for a 20 fps file). The one place the truth survives is the frame trace (src/core/frameTrace.ts:71-77), where duplicated rows carry repeated apertureMm at perfectly regular mediaTimeSeconds while genuine frames carry irregular ones.

**Reproduce skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** The grep holds: `grep -rn "stoppedEarly|frameIntervalSeconds|sought" src/` returns only src/io/videoStepper.ts, src/core/frameClock.ts (checkStepping's own types) and src/main.ts:1344-1347/1391-1419 (the status line) — no export path. The three export headers are sourceMetadataRows + coverageMetadataRows only (src/main.ts:2342-2348 session CSV, :2704-2708 blink log, :2734-2740 frame trace), and coverageMetadataRows writes measurement_mode/frames_measured/clip_duration_s/measured_fps (src/core/frameClock.ts:159-180). In the fabricated-timestamp duplication path I reproduced, measured_fps really does corroborate the wrong rate: 399 frames over a 9.95 s span = 40.10 for a true 20.05 fps clip.

_Note._ Real but overstated. The export is not witness-free in the other duplication mode: coverageMetadataRows is handed the PIPELINE count after duplicate rejection (src/main.ts:2344-2347), which is exactly the `trueRate = measured/duration` checkStepping uses to diagnose a wrong interval (src/core/frameClock.ts:262-277), and the operator already gets steppingWarning's 'stepped at the wrong interval' sentence live (:280-292). So 'the export cannot answer whether the clip was stepped at the right interval' is true only where landings are inexact and the timestamps are fabricated. Two further corrections to the proposed audit route: the frame-trace columns are frameTrace.ts:72-78, not 71-77, and the trace caps at FRAME_TRACE_RECORD_CAP = 20,000 rows (frameTrace.ts:50), so a ten-minute RLDD trace only witnesses its first ~20k frames. The three header rows remain a cheap, sensible addition.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** grep over src/ puts stoppedEarly and frameIntervalSeconds only in src/io/videoStepper.ts (10 hits) and src/main.ts (4 hits, all at 1344-1347 and 1417 in the status branch); neither reaches any export. The header is src/core/frameClock.ts:174-178, and measured_fps at :172 is framesMeasured/durationSeconds — in the inexact-landing case the duplicates are accepted, so the header corroborates the wrong rate. Stronger than the finding states: checkStepping's own duplicateVisits diagnosis, the app literally concluding 'This clip was stepped at the wrong interval' (frameClock.ts:280-291), is written to status.textContent at src/main.ts:1397-1403 and to nothing else — the instrument's own verdict that a run is corrupt never reaches the file the analysis reads. The frame trace is the one survivor: src/main.ts:3579-3588 writes mediaTimeSeconds and apertureMm per frame, capped at 20000 rows (frameTrace.ts:50), which covers a 6-minute 30 fps clip.

_Note._ Confirmed at medium. This is the finding that makes the other four un-answerable after the fact: DATASETS.md:103-105 requires the source video destroyed, so the retained numbers are the only witness, and they were written without the three facts that would settle how they were produced. Fix is three header rows and is proportionate. One correction to the post-hoc check: keying it on regularity of consecutive mediaTimeSeconds will not separate the cases, because a correctly stepped CFR clip is perfectly regular too. The discriminating signature is the one the finding's own evidence names — consecutive rows with byte-identical apertureMm (and irisAspectRatio) at regular spacing. Write the check that way.

#### G-Stepped--8. ROADMAP 12.18's v1-parity gate would lock the artefact in, whichever way the stepper is fixed

**Claim.** If the CFR instrument lands first, a corrected stepper will legitimately FAIL the parity gate and be read as a regression against numbers that were wrong. If it lands second, v2 inherits v1's exclusion set and the re-download is spent reproducing the artefact at higher resolution.

**Impact.** 12.18 is the biggest single-shot commitment on the roadmap (a re-download plus ten predicted riders). Ordering it wrong wastes the shot and, worse, gives a parity gate the authority to reject a genuine correction.

**Fix as proposed.** Insert the CFR instrument (ffprobe manifest + coverage check + inexact-landing witness) as a row before 12.18, and rewrite the parity gate as conditional: parity is required on videos whose container coverage check passes, and a coverage failure explains a mismatch rather than condemning it. This is the same ordering discipline already applied at ROADMAP.md:194 (the column freeze before the one-shot label read).

**Evidence as filed.** ROADMAP.md:213 makes 12.18 (the one-shot UTA-RLDD v2 re-measure) conditional on "a v1-parity gate (the seven original features reproduce within a pre-stated tolerance) before any new number is read". The v1 numbers were produced by the stepper as it stands, on 178 phone-recorded videos, with 30 excluded on an unverified rate (docs/uta-rldd-result.txt:29-34).

**Reproduce skeptic: downgraded, severity low.** Both quotations are accurate: ROADMAP.md:213 (12.18) reads 'a v1-parity gate (the seven original features reproduce within a pre-stated tolerance) before any new number is read', and ROADMAP.md:194 is the Phase 12 preamble that orders the column freeze before the one-shot label read. But `ls docs/uta-rldd-plan-2.md` → No such file: the v2 plan does not exist yet, the tolerance is 'pre-stated' and as yet unstated, and the roadmap nowhere says what a parity failure means — so no semantics exist that could 'condemn' a corrected stepper. The repo's established practice for exactly this situation is to annotate rather than condemn: docs/drozy-result.txt:19-33's MEASURING COMMIT block explains three features changed by a later code fix and says to read those rows as produced by superseded code.

_Note._ The ordering advice is reasonable and cheap, but the stated harm is a prediction about an unstarted row whose failure semantics are unwritten, and it is contingent on G-Stepped--5/--7 being material on real corpus clips, which is not established. Nothing is locked in today, so this is a planning suggestion, not a defect of medium severity.

**Materiality skeptic: confirmed, severity medium.** ROADMAP.md:213 gates 12.18 on 'a v1-parity gate (the seven original features reproduce within a pre-stated tolerance) before any new number is read', and names 12.18 as the one-shot re-measure carrying ten predicted riders. The v1 numbers it would be judged against are docs/uta-rldd-result.txt's, produced by the stepper as it stands with 30 exclusions whose per-video rates are nowhere on record (:29-34). ROADMAP.md:194 states the same ordering discipline the fix asks for ('Every per-second field that wants a validation path must exist and freeze before 12.17; then UTA-RLDD's labels are read once'). docs/uta-rldd-plan-2.md does not exist yet.

_Note._ Confirmed at medium, and the timing is the whole point: because plan-2 is not written, amending the row now is roadmap sequencing, not editing a scored prediction — so the fix does not touch the pre-registration strength, and it is the last moment where that stays true. Once plan-2 is committed with the gate as written, a corrected stepper either fails a gate it should never have been judged by, or the re-download is spent reproducing v1's exclusion set at higher fidelity. Its force is contingent on G-Stepped--4/5/7 being real, which they are; if the CFR instrument is judged not worth building, this row's amendment collapses to a one-line clarification that a parity mismatch is diagnostic rather than disqualifying — still worth making.
